description:
# Senior review: epoch — time travel (capture, history, restore, replay, tool-pair injection)

Reviewer persona: senior devtools / time-travel-debugging engineer (Redux DevTools, re-frame-10x, Replay-class): bounded epoch capture, snapshot restore with preconditions, deterministic strict replay, wire protocol for an external pair tool.
Tree: review-sep16 worktree, trunk d89a41e057
Scope read: implementation/epoch/src in full — epoch.cljc (880), epoch/tool_pair.cljc (2314), epoch/state.cljc (2099), epoch/capture.cljc (776), epoch/listeners.cljc (519), epoch/assembly.cljc (383); ~6,970 lines. Tests skimmed by grep for what is pinned (ring retention, restore preconditions, incarnation tokens, no-run-start harvest skip, halted records, restore-must-not-revive-host-work). Core seams read where the slice calls into them: router.cljc 3290-3530 + 3686-3702 + 3932-3987 + 4505-4574 (depth halt, settle, drain-block, dispatch-sync reentrancy), views.cljs 196-357 (render cap), frame.cljc 2226-2335 (drain-lock serialization), core_epoch.cljc, machines.cljc 425-465, machines/timer.cljc 1240-1292.
Owning specs consulted: spec/Tool-Pair.md §Time-travel (Bounded history, Restore failure modes, Restore caveat, Replay, replay-epoch!), §Pair-tool writes, §Surface behaviour against destroyed frames, §Silencing under same-id churn; spec/009-Instrumentation.md §The :epoch stream, §What is NOT / IS available in production; spec/Spec-Schemas.md §:rf/epoch-record + §Outcomes; spec/Security.md §Epoch privacy posture; spec/Ownership.md rows 50-78 (Tool-Pair row 68, data-classification row 62); spec/005-StateMachines.md §Restore semantics.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. Post-settle render/sub-run back-fill has no cap and re-fans the growing record on every render  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs:303-329 (cap read), implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/capture.cljc:372-430 (`run-cause` reads only the in-flight buffer), implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/listeners.cljc:171-186 (`record-render!` de-dup condition), :204-214 (`record-sub-run!`, no de-dup), implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:832-913 (`back-fill-event!` appends unboundedly)
- What: the 100-per-run `:rf.view/rendered` cap is enforced from `run-cause`'s `:rendered-so-far`, which counts the IN-FLIGHT buffer only; every post-settle render reads `n-so-far 0`, emits, and is back-filled into the anchor record — de-dup applies only when the resolved target differs from the anchor — so a substrate-driven re-render loop with no dispatch (a ratom/rAF animation, a controlled input with local state, a parent re-render) grows one record's `:renders` and `:trace-events` (two render rows plus one `:rf.sub/skip` per deref'd sub per render) without bound and re-fans the whole record to every epoch listener on each splice.
- Evidence: views.cljs:305 `n-so-far (long (or (:rendered-so-far cause) 0))`; capture.cljc:373 reads `buffer-for`, empty post-settle by construction (`settle!` harvested it). listeners.cljc:171-174 skips only when `(not= target-epoch-id default-epoch-id)` AND the row exists — a view whose inputs changed in the anchor epoch (`value-changed-epoch-for` returns the anchor: the common case right after the dispatch that changed it) or whose mount epoch IS the anchor is never de-duped; `record-sub-run!` never de-dups. `back-fill-event!` conj's unconditionally; both back-fills call `notify-listeners!` per splice, so an Xray re-sync costs O(record) per render — quadratic over an animation. Control for "no test pins a bound": `rendered-cap-reached` under implementation/epoch/test hits only epoch_run_cause_test.clj (3 hits, in-flight counting); the same needle over core/src finds the emit site, so the instrument reads both trees.
- Action: bound the back-fill path with the cap the in-flight path already has — in `record-render!` read `(count (:renders target-record))` (or let `run-cause` fall back to the anchor record's count when the buffer is empty), and past `view-rendered-cap` splice one `:rf.view/rendered-cap-reached` and stop re-fanning; give `record-sub-run!` the same bound. ~15 lines; the constant already exists in views.cljs.

### 2. Off-box egress applies two policies to the same fx args: `:effects[*].:args` fails closed, the `:trace-events` twin rides raw  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:2125-2154 (`elide-effect-row`), :2046-2088 (`elide-trace-events-slot` — no arm for `:rf.fx/args` / `:rf.event/fx` beyond the resources-hook one at :1899-1943), :1761-1796 (`omit-off-box-event-args`, the precedent that aligned event args across both carriers)
- What: the structured `:effects` row redacts `:args` off-box by default under `:rf.egress/include-fx-args?`, but the identical payload rides `[:trace-events i :tags :rf.fx/args]` (every `:rf.fx/handled` / `:rf.fx/skipped-on-platform` / `:rf.error/*` fx row) and `[:trace-events i :tags :rf.event/fx]` (`:rf.fx/do-fx`), where only emit-time REGISTRATION classification applies — an unmarked `[:http {:body {:password …}}]` or `[:dispatch [:login "pw"]]` egresses raw three rows above its redacted structured twin, and `:rf.egress/include-fx-args? false` protects nothing.
- Evidence: Security.md:107 states the MUST for the structured row and gives as its reason that the value is "captured verbatim from the `:rf.fx/args` trace tag … NOT routed through the marks-projection chokepoint … NOT rooted at the frame's app-db" — the reason names the tag it leaves unredacted, and neither it nor Spec-Schemas §:rf/epoch-record `:effects` nor Tool-Pair mentions the `:trace-events` carriers. The bulk walk at tool_pair.cljc:2088 roots at app-db paths so `[i :tags :rf.fx/args …]` never matches (control: projection.cljc has 16 hits for `rf.event/db|:trace-events|:rf/epoch-record` and 0 for `rf.fx/args|rf.event/fx`, so the door has no fx-args arm). The asymmetry is PINNED as current behaviour by epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj:1715-1720 and :1889 ("the row's NON-key payload is untouched … `{:method :get :url "/secret"}` rides verbatim"), while :772-784 of the same file calls this "the sharpest form of the two-carrier shape rf2-irwsq named" and rf2-1kiuj fixed only the resource-KEY case through a resources hook. Event args were aligned the other way: `omit-off-box-event-args` extends `:trigger-event`'s fail-closed rule to `:rf.event/v` under one switch.
- Action: decide: A) add an `omit-off-box-fx-args` step to `elide-trace-events-slot` that redacts the `:rf.fx/args` / `:rf.event/fx` tag slots under `:rf.egress/include-fx-args?` (mirror of `omit-off-box-event-args`, ~25 lines) and re-pin the two conformance assertions; or B) rule the structured-row redaction cosmetic, drop `elide-effect-row`, and amend Security.md:107 to say fx args egress under registration classification only (fail-open, consistent with Ownership row 62's "hygiene helper"). Trade-off: A closes an actual off-box leak at the cost of MCP tools seeing `:rf/redacted` fx args unless they opt in; B is honest but retires a documented MUST.

### 3. The `:halted-depth` record committed for an event that ran `:ok` moves the back-fill anchor and blocks restore of the newest epoch  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:3695 (depth check is the first `cond` arm, before `take-event!`), :3370-3379 (`halting-event (or (:event halting-envelope) last-event)`, `halting-time-ms` nil on that fallback), implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:363-412 (`commit-halt-record!`), implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:2057-2065 (`commit-frame-owner-record!` anchors EVERY record), tool_pair.cljc:446-452 (restore refuses non-`:ok`), :554 (replay refuses `:halted`)
- What: the sibling review's router bug (a drain of exactly `:drain-depth` events halts with an EMPTY queue) reaches the epoch side as a `:halted-depth` record whose `:trigger-event` is the `last-event` fallback — the event that just settled `:ok` — with `:committed-at nil`; the epoch side then treats it as authoritative in three places: the last-settled ANCHOR moves to the phantom (the real last event's post-settle renders / sub-runs / unmounts back-fill into it and Xray shows them on a `:blocked` row, `:rf.epoch/outcome :blocked` fires for a clean drain), `restore-epoch!` of `(last history)` is refused with `:rf.epoch/restore-non-ok-record` although its `:frame-state-after` IS the live state, and `replay-epoch!` of it is refused with `:cause :halted`.
- Evidence: router.cljc:3363-3371 calls the fallback "defensive" but it is reachable on every exactly-N drain (common with test frames at `:drain-depth 3-5` and `:initial-events`); epoch.cljc:398 full-harvests the empty buffer and :410 commits with the fallback trigger pinned; state.cljc:2063 `set-last-settled-epoch!` runs for halt records with no outcome gate. epoch_test.clj:1932-1968 pins the runaway case (depth 5, `:loop` re-dispatching, queue never empty); nothing pins the exactly-N / empty-queue case. Router bug not re-derived here.
- Action: two epoch-side hardenings that stand whether or not the router is fixed: (a) `commit-halt-record!` should commit nothing when there is no halting envelope (nil `committed-at` is the tell) rather than pin the last-run event as "never ran"; (b) `commit-frame-owner-record!` should not move `last-settled-epoch` for a non-`:ok` record — a halt adds no state, so anchoring post-settle attribution to it is always wrong. ~5 lines each.

### 4. `restore-epoch!` leaves no evidence in the ring; the timeline is not self-describing across a rewind  [PLAUSIBLE] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics]
- Where: implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1161-1190 (`perform-restore!` emits a trace and re-anchors, records nothing), implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:540-585 (`replace-frame-state!` records a synthetic epoch "so it can be undone"), state.cljc:700-770 (anchor-bounded scan that exists because the ring is left non-monotonic)
- What: after a restore to E the ring reads `… E, E+1 … R` with the frame at E's state and the next real record N carrying `:frame-state-before` = E's after ≠ R's after — a tool walking `epoch-history` sees a discontinuity with no marker unless it also consumed the `:rf.epoch/restored` trace, and "undo the restore" is "find R yourself" rather than a record; the other write surface (`replace-frame-state!`) records a synthetic epoch for exactly this reason.
- Evidence: epoch_attribution_test.clj:1705-1717 and :1855-1879 document the two-layer compensation (re-anchor to E, then bound `value-changed-epoch-for` at the anchor index) whose stated cause is "`perform-restore!` re-anchors WITHOUT truncating the ring". Tool-Pair §Restore says only "Emits `:rf.epoch/restored`"; §Pair-tool writes:250 spells out the synthetic record for replace. Would confirm: an Xray/pair-tool cursor after restore — does it read the trace or the ring? (Not traced into tools/; out of slice.)
- Action: decide: A) keep as is and add one sentence to Tool-Pair §Restore that the ring is not self-describing across a restore (the trace is the only marker; consumers must not expect `:frame-state-before` continuity); B) record a synthetic `:rf.epoch/restored` epoch (before = pre-restore state, after = E's after, empty projections) mirroring replace — undo-of-restore becomes a first-class target and the anchor is the ring-newest again, but the anchor-bounded scan must then stop at the synthetic boundary instead, so this reshapes that machinery rather than removing it.

### 5. rf2-9nlg1 has two siblings of the same class: restore cancels machine `:after` timers and never re-arms them, and aborts non-resource in-flight HTTP whose reply the restored app-db is waiting for  [PLAUSIBLE] [severity: low] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:963-1025 (`quiesce-orphaned-async-host-work!` chain), implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:441-465 (`:machines/on-frame-restored!` cancels; `:machines/rearm-after-hydration!` exists and is explicitly "NOT the epoch-restore hook"), implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc:1257-1291
- What: a restored snapshot that is IN a state with an `:after` transition has its host timer cancelled by the quiesce and nothing re-arms it from the restored snapshot, so the machine sits in that state until some other event re-enters it; likewise a restored app-db captured mid-request (`:loading`) waits for a reply that `:http/abort-in-flight-for-frame!` suppresses — both are "durable state expects a host transient that restore cleared", the shape rf2-9nlg1 records for resource GC timers.
- Evidence (premise check the brief asked for, done here): `restore-epoch!` / `replay-epoch!` / `replace-frame-state!` each gate on `rf.interop/debug-enabled?` (epoch.cljc:452, :524, :711); the only production-source callers of `perform-restore!` / `perform-replay!` are those gated facades (grep over the tree: every other `perform-restore!` hit is a comment or a test; 40+ test hits as the control); the only callers of core's `rf.frame/replace-frame-state!` are epoch.cljc:669, tool_pair.cljc:1155 (both under the gate) and ssr/render_state.cljc:425 (hydration, a different door); no `tools/` file requires `re-frame.epoch.tool-pair` and the http hits are comments (content checked). So the dev-only disposition rests on a sound premise, and it covers these two seams by the same argument. machines.cljc:453-462 shows the framework already separates "cancel the old timeline's handles" from "arm the handles the snapshot implies" — for hydration.
- Action: decide: A) record on rf2-9nlg1 that the accepted dev-only disposition also covers machine `:after` timers and non-resource HTTP (Tool-Pair §Restore caveat:137 already discloses the HTTP half; add the timer half there); or B) wire `rf.machines.hydrate/rearm-after-timers!`'s shape into `perform-restore!`'s tail after the quiesce, which keeps "MUST NOT revive host work" (old handles stay cancelled) while giving the restored snapshot the timers it declares.

### 6. `harvest-buffer-for-event!` / `harvest-buffer!` are read-then-swap, not the atomic split their docstrings claim  [PLAUSIBLE] [severity: low] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:963-968 (`harvest-buffer!`: `get` then `dissoc`), :1013-1061 (`harvest-buffer-for-event!`: deref at :1014, partition, then `swap! assoc remaining-events` at :1037/:1055)
- What: on the JVM a `buffer-event!` from another thread that lands between the deref and the `swap!` is overwritten by the stale `remaining-events` — and the slice's own account (state.cljc:309-315) says an async `dispatch!` from another thread emits `:rf.event/dispatched` at enqueue with its own `:dispatch-id`, which `capture-event!` buffers; that child's later record then lacks its `:rf.event/dispatched` row, so its `:rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id` lineage is silently missing from the epoch (Xray's causality popover reads it off that row).
- Evidence: the swap at :1037 writes a value computed from a prior deref; nothing re-partitions on CAS retry. Control: epoch_concurrency_stress_test.clj has 20 hits for `dispatch-sync|buffer-event!|capture-event!` and 0 for `harvest`, so the split is not exercised under concurrency. Would confirm: a two-thread test enqueuing an async dispatch during a sync drain's settle and asserting the child record carries its `:rf.event/dispatched` row. CLJS is unaffected.
- Action: partition inside one `swap!` (compute both halves from the value being swapped, stash the settling half in a volatile, return the remainder) — ~10 lines, same shape `back-fill-event!` already uses for its index.

### 7. Tool-Pair spells the `restore-non-ok-record` outcome tag `:rf.epoch/outcome`; the code emits `:outcome`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: spec/Tool-Pair.md:131 (`{… :rf.epoch/outcome <kw>, :halt-reason <any>}`); implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:447-452 (`:outcome (:outcome epoch-record)`)
- What: a tool routing the refusal by the spec'd tag reads nil.
- Evidence: Spec-Schemas.md:4560 endorses the bare `:outcome` tag on `:rf.epoch/snapshotted` and Spec-Schemas carries no tags schema for `restore-non-ok-record` (1 prose hit at :4562); epoch_test.clj:2004-2028 asserts only that the op fired. The code is internally consistent (bare `:outcome` on both ops); the Tool-Pair table cell is the odd one out.
- Action: change the Tool-Pair.md:131 cell to `:outcome`. (If the qualified-tag rule of §Identity spellings is meant to win instead, `:rf.epoch/snapshotted`'s tag and Spec-Schemas:4560 drift too — a bigger change for no consumer.)

## Considered, left alone

Only an ordering oddity remains (epoch listeners inline, trace listeners deferred to the boundary).

- Lowering `:trace-events-keep` at runtime leaves older records holding raw traces until they evict (state.cljc:178-205, one elision per append) — documented as an append-time rule; dev heap only.

- Restore does not truncate the ring (rf2-arzb9o, deliberate) and `check-restore-preconditions!` runs outside the drain lock — the resolved `epoch` value is fixed before the lock, so an interleaved drain cannot change the install target. See finding 4 for the design-level question only.

- ripgrep `harvest` in epoch_concurrency_stress_test.clj: 0; control: 20 hits for `dispatch-sync|buffer-event!|capture-event!`.
- ripgrep `halted-depth` under implementation/epoch/test (content): epoch_test.clj:1932-2110, epoch_replay_cljs_test.cljc:308-324, epoch_attribution_test.clj:1140-1164 — every case has a non-empty queue at the halt.

title: review(resources): senior-developer findings, 6 ranked, trunk d89a41e057 (2026-09-16)
description:
# Senior review: resources

Reviewer persona: senior engineer who has built and maintained a server-state cache library (React Query / SWR / Apollo class) — dedupe, staleness, GC, owners vs causes, optimistic rollback, invalidation fan-out, SSR hydration.
Tree: review-sep16 worktree, trunk d89a41e057
Scope read: implementation/resources/src — events.cljc (3434), state.cljc (1732), mutation_events.cljc (2203), mutation_runtime.cljc (1194), work_ledger.cljc (909), timers.cljc (522), reply_handlers.cljc (203) in full; ssr.cljc 1470-2538 (hydrate / restore / refetch-plan / rearm seams); route.cljc adopt seam (270-330, 1140-1250); registry.cljc scope resolution + gc default. ~11.5K of the ~22K source lines. Not read: classification / trace_egress / tooling / subs / scope_registry (projection and tooling surfaces outside the leak / race classes named in the brief). Tests skimmed by deftest roster: optimistic_apply, optimistic_settle, reply_to_reads, work_ledger, invalidation_gc, mutation, time_ms_cofx.
Owning specs consulted: spec/016-Resources.md §Active owners and causes, §Status semantics, §Frame work ledger / §Ledger row retention, §Read completion continuations, §Populate is an authoritative load, §Optimistic mutations / §Optimistic settle, §Race and in-flight semantics, §Stale and GC scheduling, §Polling, §Invalidation, §Restore and replay, §Resource cache retention defaults; docs/EP/EP-0019 (R6 / Open Issue 6).

Not re-derived (per brief): PR #9857 hydration GC arming, rf2-9nlg1 epoch-restore GC, the hydrated-poll claim.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. An invalidation-driven refetch that fails or is aborted erases the invalidation; the entry then reads FRESH with pre-mutation data  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: correctness / spec-drift]
- Where: implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc:972 (`entry-start-load` writes `:invalidated-at nil`); state.cljc:1034-1046 (`entry-failed` does not restore it); implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:2556-2559 (`entry-abort-settled` neither); events.cljc:436-439 (fresh-skip gate reads `entry-stale?`); events.cljc:1332-1334 (focus / reconnect scan only picks STALE entries).
- What: the stale mark is cleared when the refetch STARTS, not when it SUCCEEDS, so a 5xx or an owner-release abort on that refetch leaves `:loaded` + `:invalidated-at nil`; with the default (no `:stale-after-ms`) the entry is never stale again — the next route `ensure` fresh-skips it (`:rf.resource/cache-hit`) and the focus scan skips it, so a mutation's effect is never seen until the cache is cleared.
- Evidence: trace — `invalidate-tags-handler` → `entry-invalidate` (events.cljc:1793-1797) → `[:dispatch [:rf.resource/refetch …]]` (:1810-1818) → `ensure-load` `:else` → `entry-start-load` clears the mark (state.cljc:972) → `failed-handler` `:else` → `entry-failed` → `:loaded` + `:refresh-error`, mark still nil → `entry-stale?` false. Abort twin: owner released mid-refetch → `:abort-requested` → `entry-abort-settled` → `:loaded`, mark nil. Spec 016:403 "a `:fetching` entry may be refreshing STALE data" and 016:1199 "its SUCCESS may satisfy the invalidation" — the code satisfies it at start. Control: every SUCCESS settle already clears the mark itself (`entry-succeeded` state.cljc:1004, `entry-append-page` :1199, `entry-replace-page` :1274, `patch-entry` / `populate-entry` in mutation_runtime.cljc:281/321), so the start-time clear does no work on the happy path. Grep `invalidated-at` over implementation/resources/test: no test asserts the mark is nil right after start-load; two test COMMENTS call the clear "correct framework behaviour" (resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc:563, resources_time_ms_cofx_cljs_test.cljc:163) and `background-refresh-failure-does-not-rearm-gc` (resources_invalidation_gc_cljs_test.cljc:761) never invalidates first — the failure-after-invalidation path is unpinned.
- Action: delete the `:invalidated-at nil` write at state.cljc:972 (the success settles own the clear). Accept the visible consequence: the `:stale?` sub reads true while a refetch is in flight after an invalidation, which is the stale-while-revalidate the spec describes. Pin two tests: invalidate owned entry → refetch fails → `entry-stale?` true and the next `ensure` does NOT fresh-skip; and the release-mid-refetch abort twin. Update the two test comments.

### 2. Optimistic REMOVE + owner release mid-flight + failed reply resurrects the departed owner — the entry is pinned for the frame's life  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:510-512 (optimistic remove DISSOCs the entry) and :1412-1413 (`reindex-keys` drops the owner-index membership); events.cljc:1970 + 1874-1886 (`release-owner` walks the owner-index → the removed key is never visited, no `:revision` bump); implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_runtime.cljc:508-510 (`optimistic-conflict?` for `:remove` = `(some? current-entry)` → nil → NO conflict); mutation_runtime.cljc:583-584, 620 (`reconcile-restored-entry` with `current` nil seats `before` unchanged — `:active-owners` included).
- What: delete a card optimistically, navigate away before the DELETE reply, reply fails → the rollback restores the full pre-apply entry with the route owner `[:route … nav-token]` that already released; nothing will ever release it again, so the entry never GCs, refetches on every focus / reconnect, and polls forever if the resource declares `:poll-interval-ms`.
- Evidence: the PATCH twin of this exact leak is fixed and pinned (`release-mid-flight-does-not-resurrect-the-owner-on-rollback`, implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_optimistic_settle_cljs_test.cljc:416) through the `detach-owner` revision bump (state.cljc:934-938) — a mechanism that needs an entry to bump, and the REMOVE form has none. `optimistic-remove-vanishes-entry-and-records-before` (resources_optimistic_apply_cljs_test.cljc:201) pins the dissoc and the full-entry `:before` (owners included). Spec 016:395 names this hazard verbatim ("resurrect the departed owner … so the entry never GCs"). Spec 016:1053 / EP-0019 R6 bless the remove form.
- Action: decide A or B. A (recommended): tombstone instead of dissoc — the optimistic remove writes `:data nil :status :idle` in place (keep `:active-owners` / `:current-work` / index), `has-data?` already reads it as empty, and the ordinary `detach-owner` / `attach-owner` revision bumps then protect it exactly like the patch form; the `:absent` / `applied-removed-revision` special cases collapse. B (one-liner, known cost): in `restore-before` when `current` is nil, seat `before` with `:active-owners` filtered to owners the owner-index still lists anywhere — a fully-released owner is dropped, but a still-live owner whose ONLY key this was is dropped too (its entry then GCs under an open route; views are passive and will not re-ensure). Either way add the remove-form twin of the settle test at :416.

### 3. The work ledger is not bounded: failed / suppressed / cancelled rows are pruned only by a later SUCCESS, mutation rows are never pruned, and an entry's rows outlive the entry  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness / spec-drift]
- Where: implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc:530-582 (`prune-terminal-for-key`); its only src callers are events.cljc:2481 and :2921 (scalar / page SUCCESS). Absent from `failed-handler` (events.cljc:2666-2673, 2732-2739), `page-failed-handler` (:3091-3095, 3169-3173, 3225-3229, 3256-3260), `gc-fired-handler` (:3382-3386), `remove-handler` (:2221-2232), `clear-scope-handler*` (:2122-2135), mutation `apply-removes` (mutation_events.cljc:297-301), mutation `succeeded-handler` (:1819-1821 marks `:completed`, no prune), `clear-handler` (:1500-1507).
- What: `:rf.runtime/work-ledger` lives in runtime-db (every frame-state value, every epoch snapshot) and grows without bound under three ordinary workloads: a polled resource against a failing endpoint (one `:failed` row per tick — 720/hour at 5s, until a success lands), a form submitted N times (N `:completed` mutation rows, never pruned by any path), and any key that is GC'd / removed / cleared (its ≤3 terminal tail plus every un-pruned failure, and its `:rf.runtime/work-ledger-by-key` bucket, survive until frame destroy).
- Evidence: ripgrep `prune-terminal-for-key` over implementation/ → work_ledger.cljc (def) + events.cljc:2481, :2921 + tests only; control: `mark-terminal` over the same tree → 26 sites, so the two-hit answer is real. Spec 016:554 promises "the ledger is bounded" but its stated rule ("pruned on the linked entry's next successful transition") is precisely what leaves these holes; the mutation work-kind has no prune at all.
- Action: (a) prune after EVERY terminal settle (failure, abort, page failure, mutation success/failure) — the newest-3 tail still serves Xray; (b) on entry removal (`remove`, `clear-scope`, `gc-fired`, mutation `:removes`) drop all of that key's rows (`prune-terminal-for-key rdb key 0` — the in-flight row is already `:cancelled` on those paths) and the index bucket; (c) amend 016 §Ledger row retention to "pruned on the linked entry's next TERMINAL transition; all rows dropped when the entry is removed; mutation rows pruned per instance id". One sentence each in three handlers plus a shared helper.

### 4. An optimistic SEED of an absent key never arms a GC timer  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]
- Where: mutation_events.cljc:492-530 (`apply-optimistic` emits no `:rf.resource/schedule-timers`), :1454-1459 (execute fx = commit-generation / record-work-handle / before-fxs / lower-fx); success re-arms ONLY `timer-policies` from `:patches` / `:populates` (:1708, :1836-1849); mutation_runtime.cljc:381-404 (`apply-optimistic-patch` seeds `:loaded` with `:active-owners #{}`).
- What: a create-mutation that optimistically seeds the new detail key and settles by `:invalidates` (the common shape — populate the list, invalidate the tag) leaves an owner-free `:loaded` entry with no stale / GC / poll timer; `invalidate-tags-handler` then classes it `:left-stale` "GC-eligible" (events.cljc:1806-1807) but no timer will ever fire. It is collected only if some later owned `ensure` happens to fresh-skip onto it (events.cljc:510-518). Same class as rf2-ar9pcx / rf2-kz5op1 / PR #9857 — a settle that yields an owner-free entry without arming GC.
- Evidence: control — `apply-populates` DOES arm via `timer-delays` (mutation_events.cljc:97-107, :242), so the seed path is the odd one out. resources_optimistic_apply_cljs_test.cljc:72 stubs `schedule-timers` to a no-op, so no test can observe a seed's timer (grep `schedule-timers|gc-scheduled` over test/**/*optimistic*: 1 hit, the stub).
- Action: in `succeeded-handler` add each `:seed` key from `(:rollback opt-summary)` that is not in `authoritative-keys` to `timer-policies` with its resource's `timer-delays` (~8 lines); or arm stale+GC at apply time for a `:seed` forward. Test: optimistic seed + invalidates-only success → `:rf.resource/gc-scheduled` for the seeded key.

### 5. A read `:reply-to` is silently voided when a poll / focus / invalidation / manual refetch supersedes the in-flight attempt  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: ergonomics / spec question]
- Where: events.cljc:702-707 and :739-745 (supersession marks the prior record `:suppressed` and builds the new record with `:reply-targets (when reply-to' [reply-to'])` — the prior record's targets are not carried over); events.cljc:2409-2429 (stale branch delivers nothing). Spec 016:725 says exactly this; `reply-to-stale-superseded-never-delivered` (implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_reply_to_reads_cljs_test.cljc:273) pins it.
- What: a machine that `ensure`s with `:reply-to` on a resource with `:poll-interval-ms`, or while a focus scan or a mutation invalidation can fire, may never receive its continuation — a fresher attempt settles the SAME key and delivers to nobody, so the workflow hangs with no trace naming the dropped target beyond a generic `:rf.resource/stale-suppressed`. Code matches spec; the question is whether the spec is right — "inherits suppression for free" (016:725) inherits the mechanism, but from the caller's side the read it caused WAS answered, by a fresher generation.
- Evidence: the superseding branch has the prior record in hand (`prior-work`, events.cljc:743-745) and `add-reply-target` (work_ledger.cljc:336-351) already dedupes, so migration is a three-line change; `fetchQuery` in TanStack never silently hangs.
- Action: decide A or B. A (recommended): on supersession fold the prior record's `:reply-targets` onto the superseding record (still exactly-once, never stale data) and amend 016:725 to "a superseded attempt hands its continuation to its successor; only a vanished / cross-frame / restored-dangling reply delivers nothing". B: keep, and say at the `:reply-to` doc site that polling / focus / invalidation can void it, so a workflow must not block on a read that way.

### 6. Mutation-driven cancellations lack the causal `:completed-at` every other cancellation carries  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics]
- Where: mutation_events.cljc:299-301 (`:cancelled {:reason :mutation-remove}`), :1503-1506 (`:cancelled {:reason :mutation-clear}`).
- What: rf2-x76af2.14 ruled a cancellation is a completion and stamps the event's `:rf/time-ms` (events.cljc:2126-2132, :2225-2230; pinned by `remove-cancelled-row-carries-causal-completed-at`, resources_work_ledger_cljs_test.cljc:573); the two mutation paths were missed, so epoch / Xray correlation of a mutation-removed or cleared in-flight read has no completion time.
- Evidence: grep `:completed-at` in mutation_events.cljc → only the reply-token sites (:87, :1659, :1989, :2109); the two `mark-terminal :cancelled` calls carry none.
- Action: pass `clock-ms` into `apply-removes` and declare/consume `:rf/time-ms` in `clear-handler`; two lines each.

## Considered, left alone
- `:patches` keys are not exempt from the same mutation's `:invalidates` pass (only `:populates` are — mutation_events.cljc:1737), so a patched-and-tagged owned key is refetched right after the patch; 016:1005 exempts populate only, so this is spec-conformant (a patch is a client transform, not authoritative) — the handler docstring at :1621-1626 merely overstates.
- `apply-optimistic-patch` writes `:status :loaded` over an in-flight entry (mutation_runtime.cljc:381-404) so `:fetching?` reads false until the reply; view-only — fresh-skip / poll / focus all gate on `live-work?`, and `reconcile-restored-entry` repairs status on rollback.
- The GC timer is re-armed every `:gc-after-ms` for as long as an entry is owned (events.cljc:3398-3419, rf2-07693y) — deliberate, one timer per owned entry, trivial.
- An ownerless in-flight load whose entry is invalidated mid-flight clears the mark on success (state.cljc:1004) with a possibly pre-invalidation payload; 016:1199 leaves "did the request cover the invalidated identity" to policy, and finding 1's fix does not touch it.
- `resource-meta` returning nil after `clear-resource` makes `gc-fired` skip without rescheduling (events.cljc:3404-3405) — hot-reload edge.

## Instruments and controls
- All findings are end-to-end code traces of the frozen tree; no test lane or REPL was run (only `git rev-parse --short HEAD`).
- ripgrep `prune-terminal-for-key` over implementation/: 2 src call sites (events.cljc:2481, :2921) + the def + tests; control `mark-terminal` over the same tree → 26 sites.
- ripgrep `invalidated-at` over implementation/resources/test (≈80 hits): none asserts nil immediately after `entry-start-load`; the two comment mentions are cited in finding 1. Control over src: state.cljc:972 (start clear) and :1004 (success clear) both found.
- ripgrep `deftest` in resources_optimistic_settle / _optimistic_apply / _reply_to_reads / _work_ledger / _invalidation_gc test files — the roster of what is pinned; the PATCH-form owner-resurrection test (settle :416) exists, the REMOVE-form twin does not.
- ripgrep `release-owner|active-owners|gc-scheduled|schedule-timers` over test/**/*optimistic*: 23 hits (settle 21, apply 1 = the `schedule-timers` no-op stub at apply:72, validation 1).
- ripgrep `:completed-at` in mutation_events.cljc: reply-token sites only; the two `:cancelled` outcomes carry none.
- ripgrep `defn resolve-scope-for-event` in registry.cljc (payload scope has highest precedence) — confirms the poll / focus / invalidation refetch dispatches, which pass the entry's concrete scope back, resolve to the same key.

title: Incomplete: effect override edits can leave snapshot identity and watch results stale
description:
PR #9862 (810506544b10c8d088bb51fe6d088fd7060f3832) extends snapshot identity to inherited render inputs, but the shared render-input-keys omits the authored :fx-overrides map. This map is a first-class variant/fragment world input under Story spec 017 and is inherited through :extends. It is therefore absent from the own, composed and inherited identity slices. A direct variant override edit also misses the watch hash, which combines identity, judged slots and referenced registrations.

Independent exact-merge JVM reproduction through the real Story runner, using stable keyword override references rather than changing function code: register two fixed effects :audit/one and :audit/two that dispatch app-db :n=1 and :n=2. A :test variant sets up [:audit/start], which emits :audit/resolve, and asserts :n=1. Change only :fx-overrides {:audit/resolve :audit/one} to {:audit/resolve :audit/two}. The run changes PASS with n1 to FAIL with n2, but both snapshot identity and its watch hash stay identical. Watch mode therefore keeps the old verdict until another trigger or a manual run.

Repeat with the map on an :extends parent and on a :compose fragment: both child runs again change PASS/n1 to FAIL/n2 while identity stays identical. Their watch hashes DO change, which is the positive control for the reference tracking in #9860; the missed-watch claim applies to the directly authored map.

A temporary one-key correction adding :fx-overrides to the existing render-input-keys makes all three identities and watch hashes change while preserving the actual PASS/n1 to FAIL/n2 behavior. This was an audit experiment only; source bytes were restored and git diff is clean. Use the existing canonical fingerprint and shared slices to include this declared input, with focused own/composed/inherited regressions. No new API, plan compilation or baseline mechanism is needed.

Evidence: audit-sep15-b gate-9862 attempt3 (original reproduction,exit0), attempt5 (one-key correction,exit0), attempt4 (the PRs inherited-slot control,6 failures), attempt6 (restored runtime suite103 tests/338 assertions,0 failures,exit0). Probe: C:/Users/miket/.codex/tmp/audit-sep15-b/9862-probe.clj. Gate root and source restoration verified. No exact separately tracked open Bead records this override-input defect.
acceptance_criteria: Changing only an authored :fx-overrides reference changes snapshot identity for direct, composed and inherited inputs when the settled world changes. Watch detects a direct variant override edit and reruns it; preserve existing inherited/composed watch behavior. title: Initialize the Fresco login JVM host before serving SSR requests
description:
Add explicit JVM adapter initialization to the Fresco login's documented SSR application startup. Keep initialization at the application boundary: a short host boot function or concrete README startup snippet should call `(rf/init! ssr/adapter)` before the Ring server accepts requests. Do not initialize the generic SSR library implicitly or reinstall its process-global adapter on each request.

Ownership and revision

- Slice: examples_substrates. Own the startup wiring in `examples/substrates/fresco/login/host.clj:45-52,74-112` and the launch recipe in `examples/substrates/fresco/login/README.md:231-254` (particularly the instruction at 251-254 to serve `host/handler` from any Ring adapter).
- Reviewed baseline: `9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261`; observed HEAD: `9291090725fa3ebcad67ea81a74946fc3aac96a4`. All 21 owned files are unchanged between those revisions (`git diff --exit-code`, exit 0).
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- Remediation fence inherited from the first finding in `rf2-fzbj.36`: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj. This issue records review evidence only; no fixer is dispatched.

Concrete trigger and behavior

Start a fresh JVM with the example's declared dependencies and source roots, require `fresco.login.host`, and serve its exported handler as the README instructs. Neither the host namespace nor the documented launch installs a state-container adapter in that JVM. `re-frame.ssr` exports `adapter` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:72`), without installing it. The Node bundle's boot and browser's run install adapters only in their respective processes.

Expected: the first GET / creates its request frame, reaches the configured renderer, and returns the rendered login document.

Actual: request setup calls `rf/make-frame` in `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:313-335`, which fails without an installed adapter. The exception is projected to HTTP 500, body `Internal error`, before the renderer is called. This occurs even with a correct sidecar configuration.

Fresh-process witness (re-run for this review): replace only `node/renderer` with a synchronous body renderer and construct the current `host/make-handler`. The installed adapter is initially absent. GET / returns 500 and the renderer call count stays 0. Call `(rf/init! ssr/adapter)` in the same JVM, invoke the SAME constructed handler again, and it returns 200 with renderer count 1. `implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/login_host_crossing_test.clj:75-90,184-185` runs requests under its reset fixture. `test_support.clj:83-96` installs `rf.ssr/adapter` on the fixture's behalf. Those tests check the initialized handler and model crossing, but cannot prove that the example's documented application startup is complete. The general Ring API example already shows the needed startup call (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:267-277`).

Suggested repair and acceptance

1. Supply an explicit application boot that initializes the JVM with `ssr/adapter` once and then serves the example handler, or give the complete equivalent REPL/launch snippet in the README.
2. Make the README's instruction to serve `host/handler` point at that complete startup sequence. Keep the independent Node and browser adapter installs.

title: Give the Reagent async Form-3 recipe request-owned cleanup
description:
Correct the Reagent README's Form-3 async widget recipe so every embed result has a live owner and stale results are finalized. A compact synchronous-library example plus an explicit async ownership note is an acceptable simpler replacement; avoid adding framework machinery to solve an example's Promise ownership.

Remediation fence: [FENCE: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj]. This dedicated documentation finding is split from rf2-fzbj.29 F2. The new review authorizes evidence and issue creation, not dispatching implementation; preserve the original report and status.

Scope/revision
- Owned path: implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md:65-82, especially unconditional Promise completions at 68-69 and 75-76, and the cleanup guarantee at 97.
- Source baseline: 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261. Revalidated 2026-09-13 at HEAD 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879; adapter source/docs are unchanged from baseline.

Concrete triggers
1. vegaEmbed returns a controlled Promise during component-did-mount. Unmount before it resolves. Unmount sees no vega-instance, clears both atoms, then the late .then writes the resulting view back into vega-instance. No future lifecycle callback owns or finalizes that result.
2. Mount starts request A; update starts request B. Resolve B first, then A, then unmount. The older A overwrites accepted B without finalizing B. Unmount finalizes only A.

Expected versus actual
Every returned instance is either the currently owned live instance or is finalized as obsolete; late work cannot resurrect a disposed owner or replace newer state. Actual controlled-Promise observations were:
- completion-after-unmount: held="pending-at-unmount", finalized=[], hasElement=false;
- out-of-order completions then unmount: finalized=["older"] only; the newer instance was overwritten and leaked.
These are normal navigation and overlapping async updates, not malformed application input. The canonical recipe specifically teaches release of library resources/listeners, so copying it defeats its own cleanup guidance. This is an executable-documentation defect, not a promise that the adapter can cancel arbitrary user async work.

Suggested repair
Keep each embed request tied to a per-mount/request generation token. Invalidate before teardown or superseding a request. Accept a completion only if it still owns the live mount/request; finalize obsolete completions immediately, and retire the previous accepted instance exactly once. Preserve the per-mounted-instance frame capture and closure state already taught by the surrounding example. If demonstrating an async embed API which may mutate the target before resolution, serialize calls or use an isolated target; guarding only the final assignment does not by itself control external DOM writes. Alternatively use a genuinely synchronous widget lifecycle example and state the async ownership requirement separately.

Acceptance
- Controlled completion after unmount finalizes the late result and retains no widget.
- Two overlapping requests resolved in reverse order keep only the newest live result; stale results finalize once, and final unmount finalizes the retained result once.
- Normal mount/update/unmount works and accepted instances are retired once, including teardown while an update is pending.
- Check the executable ownership sequence explicitly. A Markdown link gate cannot validate Promise ownership.

Validation performed and limits
Ran node C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/ai/surface-review-20260913/adapter_reagent/probe-adapter_reagent-1.cjs with its own ignored .log/.exit artifacts; captured exit 0 asserts that both defects and controls were reproduced. The README handlers' ownership algorithm is expressed in process-local JS using controlled Promises; the recipe itself and corresponding lifecycle tests were inspected. This does not mount React or load Vega, and does not verify Vega's internal DOM scheduling. The late-DOM-write possibility is a repair-design limit, not a third confirmed defect. No installs, shared builds, browser/advanced gate, source edits or persistent processes.

Deduplication/history
Current all-status vegaEmbed search returned only rf2-fzbj.29. Exact identity and newest three history entries were read; the report remains open/fenced and contains two independent defects, with no later corrective notes. This issue isolates its F2 for independent remediation. The shared derived-listener defect is filed separately by the same reviewer and is not part of this task.

title: Incomplete inspector ref lifecycle in PR #9577: width updates stop after reattachment
description:
Audit of PR #9577 (676439530302ba3df09eebe0858d440953f8edc7), discovered during rf2-k97c.3. container-ref-for in tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs returns a memoized callback. A nil call releases the mount entry, including its dispatcher. Reusing that same callback with an element restores measurements/observer state without restoring the dispatcher, so width dispatch stops. React StrictMode's callback-ref setup/cleanup/setup cycle is a real trigger: https://react.dev/reference/react/StrictMode.

Measured on the exact landed lifecycle functions with ClojureScript 1.12.145: element width 100 -> nil -> same element -> width 200 emits only set-width 100 and clear-width, leaving state with no dispatcher. Existing tests request a new callback or mount a new root and miss retained-callback reuse. This was previously appended to the broad migration owner; the user clarified that such updates are ignored as actionable work, so this issue is the visible owner of the correction. Original notes remain the evidence record.
acceptance_criteria: The same returned callback supports element -> nil -> element and subsequent width changes, dispatching into the captured frame. Final detach still disconnects the observer and removes the full mount/width state. A focused retained-ref or StrictMode regression witness proves reattachment works and final cleanup returns to baseline; use the existing API.

CLOSED ON PR #9591, merged as c255a4c3d7, alongside rf2-vw80.

THE DEFECT, as the bead had it: `release-mount!` drops the whole entry, so a RETAINED callback re-attaching
rebuilt measurement and observer state around a store carrying no `:dispatch-fn` and no `:ref`. Width
dispatch then stopped silently. React StrictMode's setup/cleanup/setup cycle on a callback ref is a real
trigger, so this is not a synthetic case.

THE FIX: the mount branch reinstates both BEFORE `measure-and-dispatch!`, which reads the dispatcher out of
the store.

WHY THE EXISTING ROWS COULD NOT CATCH IT, and this is the part worth keeping: they miss it BY CONSTRUCTION —
one asks for a NEW callback, the other never re-attaches. Neither exercises reuse of a retained callback
across a nil call, which is the whole defect. The new rows do exactly that. A control that cannot reach the
case it exists to catch is the class named in the method's own defect catalogue, and this is a clean instance.

A SECOND-ORDER FINDING BEYOND THE BEAD, reported rather than absorbed: the MEMO was lost too, so the next
render would mint a fresh closure — the same defect by a route the original row cannot see. Filed by the
worker as its own row rather than carried as a passenger.

description:
GOAL: rename the product Hicasso to FRESCO, everywhere, in one atomic sweep, BEFORE first
publish. Namespace `re-frame.fresco`, artifact `io.github.day8/re-frame2-fresco`.

Ruled by Mike, 2026-09-09. THIS DESCRIPTION IS THE DURABLE RECORD — the discussion behind it
is not in any tracked file. Everything load-bearing is restated here. Verify at source; line
numbers drift.

== WHY, AND WHY NOW ==

The existing name is argued at docs/design/hicasso/charter.md:14 and ruled at
docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md:23 (HD-001): "Hicasso — Hiccup + Picasso, one letter apart",
alias `h`, "Reopens never — names are permanent after first publish."

THE WINDOW IS OPEN AND CLOSES AT FIRST PUBLISH. docs/skills/reagent-migration.md:11: "Hicasso
is PRE-PUBLICATION. There is no released Maven coordinate; a project can adopt it only from
source." Measured 2026-09-09: `git ls-remote --tags origin` returns 0 tags against a control
of 2 heads. So HD-001's own "never" clause has not yet bound.

THREE REASONS, in descending weight:
 1. THE DERIVATION IS A DOCUMENTED ONE-LETTER MISS ON A LIVING TRADEMARK. The charter and the
    ruling both state the Picasso derivation as the rationale. The availability check that was
    run (charter.md:26 — "Verified unclaimed on Clojars, GitHub, and npm") checks REGISTRIES,
    not marks. This is the only non-taste reason and it is the one that decided it.
 2. PRONUNCIATION FORKS. From the Picasso half, hi-CASS-oh; from the Hiccup half, HICK-asso.
    Single-c is canonical, so double-c is the predictable misspelling of a name mostly heard
    before it is read.
 3. IT NEEDS A PARAGRAPH. charter.md:24 spends one on Cubism and single-line drawing.

WHY FRESCO. It keeps the painting lineage the charter wanted and sharpens the product claim
rather than merely surviving it: a fresco MUST be completed in one continuous pass, before the
plaster dries. That is one-pass interpreted rendering, stated by the medium instead of by a
person's name. Short, one pronunciation, no celebrity mark.
KNOWN COLLISION, and child .1 exists to price it: Facebook Fresco is a well-known Android image
library on Maven (com.facebook.fresco). Different ecosystem, same package universe Clojars
lives in.

== THE DECISIONS, ALREADY MADE — DO NOT RE-LITIGATE ==

Mike delegated the mechanical choices. These are settled; implement them.

 * PRODUCT: Fresco. NAMESPACE ROOT: `re-frame.fresco`. COORDINATE:
   `io.github.day8/re-frame2-fresco`. Directory: `implementation/fresco/`, sources under
   `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/` (underscore, per CLJS munging).
 * ALIAS STAYS `h`. It was never an abbreviation of Hicasso — `h` is the universal
   hiccup/hyperscript alias, and interpreted hiccup is still exactly what the product is
   (charter.md:3). Keeping it means `(:require [re-frame.fresco :as h :refer [defview sub]])`
   and EVERY `h/defview` and `h/...` call site is untouched. The authoring surface does not
   move. `f` was considered and rejected: `f` is the commonest local binding for a function,
   and `:f>` already means React-interop in this tree.
 * `:rf.adapter/hicasso` BECOMES `:rf.adapter/fresco`, AND THE OLD VALUE IS **NOT** RESERVED.
   This is the one place the rename differs from the ui/freehand retirements. Those two stay
   permanently rostered in spec/006, spec/Conventions.md and spec/API.md because tooling must
   keep refusing them defensively against a stale CO-LOADED BUILD. No such build can exist for
   Hicasso — it has never been published and has no released coordinate. So this is a TOTAL
   rename with no reserved residue. Do not add a reserved-kind row for `:rf.adapter/hicasso`.
   (42 sites measured; controls `:rf.adapter/ui` 44, `:rf.adapter/freehand` 18,
   `:rf.adapter/uix` 27.)
 * HD-001 IS SUPERSEDED, NOT DELETED. decisions.md keeps HD-001 with a superseding block
   naming this epic and the date, in the house style of HD-002's supersession. The rationale
   paragraph is rewritten, not sed-replaced (see child .3).

== MEASURED SURFACE (2026-09-09, over 4,920 tracked files EXCLUDING .beads/) ==

  hicasso            24,312 occurrences / 911 files
  Hicasso             2,995 occurrences / 579 files
  HICASSO               391 occurrences /  86 files
  hicasso_ (munged)     174 occurrences /  53 files
  re-frame2-hicasso     116 occurrences /  62 files
  paths carrying the name: 741
  `fresco` anywhere today: 0 files      NEGATIVE CONTROL `zzqqxx`: 0

FOUR CASE FORMS, NOT ONE. A sweep that handles only lowercase leaves 3,386 occurrences
standing. The munged `hicasso_` form appears in CLJS namespace file paths and generated names.
`.beads/issues.jsonl` is EXCLUDED from all of the above and from the sweep — it is a database
export, the mayor's to commit, and bead prose is history, not source.

MACHINE-READABLE SURFACES A PROSE SWEEP WILL MISS OR BREAK:
 * shadow-cljs build ids (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn): :hicasso, :hicasso-bench,
   :hicasso-bench-node, :hicasso-compile, :hicasso-modules-compile, :hicasso-release,
   :hicasso/hmr-testbed, :hicasso/testbed, :node-test-hicasso. These are the roster
   `implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list` reads.
 * npm scripts in implementation/package.json (build:hicasso-release, and four
   run/serve scripts naming hicasso in their FILENAMES as well as their keys).
 * 9 files under .github/ — workflows test.yml, lint.yml, docs.yml, expensive-tests.yml,
   release.yml, release-xray.yml plus preflight-xray-package.sh, report-changed-surfaces.sh,
   verify-version-lockstep.sh.
 * ~45 files under scripts/ and implementation/scripts/, including check_provenance_pins.py
   (whose docs.yml job validates changed pages under docs/design/hicasso/ BY PATH),
   check_retired_spellings.py, check_architecture_census.py, require-alias-baseline.edn,
   and a bundle-isolation positive-control source file literally named hicasso.cljs.
 * clj-kondo exports directory:
   implementation/hicasso/resources/clj-kondo.exports/day8/re-frame2-hicasso
 * scripts/_test_fixtures/ contains hicasso-named FIXTURES for check_doc_slugs and
   check_retired_spellings. Fixtures pin behaviour; changing them changes what is tested.

== THE HOT-ZONE FACT THAT DETERMINES THE SHAPE OF THE WORK ==

This change touches nearly every file CLAUDE.md lists as a sequential-never-parallel hot zone:
spec/API.md AND BOTH spec/api-manifest*.edn sidecars (one holding — hand-edit API.md and the
metadata sidecar, then REGENERATE spec/api-manifest.edn, which carries a do-not-hand-edit
header), spec/Conventions.md, spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md, spec/009-Instrumentation.md,
implementation/deps.edn, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, .github/workflows/*, and
.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh together with its mirror
implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs — a pair that must move in ONE commit or the
suite contradicts the script.

THEREFORE: ONE WORKER, ONE BRANCH, ONE PR. No fan-out, no parallel children on the sweep.
A rename split across two PRs leaves the tree in a state where nothing builds.
AND: run it when the tree is QUIET. This is the largest conflict generator the repo can
produce; every worker worktree in flight will conflict with it.

== SEQUENCING AGAINST THE XRAY EPIC rf2-k97c ==

rf2-k97c ("Xray must work on every browser adapter") is the other live programme touching
these paths. THE RENAME SHOULD LAND FIRST, and there is no hard dependency in either
direction. Reasoning:
 * The binding deadline is FIRST PUBLISH, not rf2-k97c. rf2-k97c is spike -> decision ->
   implement and is nowhere near done. Coupling the rename to it risks the window closing.
 * rf2-k97c makes the rename LARGER. If its Design B wins, rf2-k97c.3 re-authors ~51 Xray
   views in Hicasso — a pile of NEW hicasso-named code in tools/xray/ that a later sweep would
   have to rename too. Renaming first means rf2-k97c.3 writes `fresco` from day one.
 * The conflict argument does NOT point the other way. rf2-k97c.1 is a SPIKE on throwaway
   branches that deliberately opens no PR against main, so it cannot conflict with the sweep
   at all. rf2-k97c.5 (evidence-integrity pin) touches tools/xray only.
 * Where they genuinely overlap is trivial and self-resolving: rf2-k97c.4 deletes Xray's
   denylist, which contains `:rf.adapter/hicasso` — one of the 42 keyword sites. Whichever
   lands second simply has less to do.
NO DEPENDENCY IS RECORDED between the two epics, deliberately: a hard edge could deadlock this
if child .1 returns NO-GO. Both epics carry a cross-reference note instead. A worker on
rf2-k97c.3 writes whichever spelling is live in the tree it checks out.

== POSTURE ==
Pre-alpha, aiming at a masterpiece: elegance, power, correctness. No back-compat shims, no
deprecation aliases, no dual-name transition period — nothing has been published, so there is
nobody to be compatible with. Trust the programmer. Do not gold-plate this into a
"renaming framework". It is one sweep and one ratchet.

== SUCCESS CRITERIA ==
1. `hicasso` (all four case forms) reads 0 across tracked files excluding .beads/, with a
   positive control proving the instrument works.
2. The full local gate sweep is green: scripts/test-fast-pr.sh, test-jvm-implementation.sh,
   test-jvm-tools.sh, and `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list`
   enumerating the renamed build ids.
3. CI green on the PR, including the api-manifest job (all three files moved together) and
   check_provenance_pins.py against the renamed docs/design/fresco/ tree.
4. The naming rationale reads as though Fresco were always the name — no orphaned Picasso or
   Cubism prose (child .3).
5. `hicasso` cannot come back: the retired-spelling gate refuses it (child .4).

== CHILDREN ==
.1 verify the name is free and apply the pre-committed go/no-go rule (READY NOW; gates all)
.2 the sweep — one worker, one PR
.3 the meaning pass — rationale, HD-001 supersession, prose a sed cannot fix
.4 the ratchet — retired-spelling gate so `hicasso` cannot return

--- MAYOR NOTE 2026-09-09 ~19:1x AUSEST: THIS EPIC HAD NO EDGE TO THE RELEASE CHAIN. Fence recorded; sequencing stated. ---

MEASURED, WITH CONTROLS: this epic and all four children were probed for any mention of `rf2-fo4ng`, `rf2-kmqx3`, `rf2-uelji`, "first tag" or "first publish" as a link to the release programme. Every count read 0. Live positive controls on the same field ("Fresco": 3 on the epic, 7/1/3 on .1/.2/.3) confirm the instrument bites, so those zeros are informative — except on .4, whose control also read 0 and whose zeros therefore say nothing. `.dependencies` on this epic is `[]`.

So the rename programme and the release programme were running at each other with nothing between them, and each would have looked healthy right up to the collision.

THE FENCE IS NOW RECORDED ON rf2-kmqx3 (the first-tag operator gate) as a BLOCKING row, because that is the bead this epic FENCES and therefore the one whose reader must meet it. Do not rely on this note to carry it — a fence written only on the fencing item is one its own reader never sees.

TWO COLLISIONS, restated here so a worker on this epic knows why it is sequenced:
1. WINDOW. This epic's whole premise is "before first publish". rf2-kmqx3 IS first publish — 14 artefacts, one irreversible run, no yank on Clojars. If that tag fires first, this epic is dead or becomes an adopter migration.
2. COORDINATE SURFACE. rf2-fo4ng renames 19 `day8/*` coordinates to `io.github.day8/*` in ONE PR. Child .2 is a second whole-tree sweep over the same coordinate strings plus 741 name-carrying paths in four case forms. THE TWO SWEEPS CANNOT RUN IN PARALLEL — they collide in `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`, `spec/API.md` and its two `api-manifest*.edn` sidecars (one holding, graded on a single surface by `lint.yml`'s `api-manifest` job), and most of the rest of CLAUDE.md's hot-zone list. Sequence them; whichever runs second rebases and RE-DERIVES ITS COUNTS rather than trusting the numbers in its own description.

UPSTREAM OF BOTH: rf2-uelji, a 10-minute Mike-only Clojars group verification, gates the coordinate work.

NOT RULED HERE, and deliberately left to Mike: WHICH of rf2-fo4ng and child .2 runs first. Both orders work. Doing .2 first means rf2-fo4ng then renames an already-Fresco coordinate, which is the tidier story; doing rf2-fo4ng first is defensible because it is smaller and already fully specified, but then .2 rebases onto it and the coordinate it is renaming changes underneath. The mayor's recommendation, recorded on rf2-kmqx3, is .2 first.

NOTHING IN THIS EPIC'S RULINGS IS DISTURBED. Fresco, `re-frame.fresco`, `io.github.day8/re-frame2-fresco`, alias stays `h`, `:rf.adapter/hicasso` NOT reserved, HD-001 superseded not deleted — all stand exactly as ruled.

title: [tools/story/runtime] Realize authored network fixtures in normal variant and inline runs
description:
Snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; relevant runtime/frames/plan/spec source unchanged at mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d.

Story accepts and explains a first-class :network fixture, but the normal runtime never installs its route replies. This breaks the advertised canned-network execution: a registered variant may execute the real managed HTTP effect instead, while an inline plan redirects to a stub id without registering its fixture handler.

Minimal supported sequence (proposed public integration reproduction; NOT executed in this review):
```clojure
(rf/reg-event :review/load
  (fn [_ _] {:fx [[:rf.http/managed
                   {:request {:method :get :url "/api/cart"}
                    :on-success [:review/loaded]}]]}))
(rf/reg-event :review/loaded
  (fn [_ [_ reply]] {:db {:cart (:value reply)}}))
(story/reg-variant :story.review/cart
  {:network {[:get "/api/cart"] {:reply {:ok {:items [1]}}}}
   :setup [[:dispatch [:review/load]]]})
(story/run :story.review/cart)
```
With normal runtime dependencies, the authored fixture should deliver {:items [1]} with zero live requests. Instrument the real managed HTTP handler with a capture-only sentinel when turning this into a test; do not issue an actual request to prove the omission. The equivalent inline map target must receive the same canned reply.

Exact causal evidence:
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:1579 run routes keyword/map targets into the lifecycle runtime. lifecycle.cljc:58 delegates registered runs to runtime/run-variant.
- plan.cljc:887 lower-network is pure: produces network route data plus {:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-test-stub}. compile-body stores these at :1704-1705 in [:world :network] and [:world :frame :fx-overrides]. The plan does not install handlers (correctly).
- runtime.cljc:767 prepares that plan. Registered phase 0 (:867-870) passes only decorator stack and classification to frames/allocate!. frames.cljc:761-821 creates frame fx-overrides only from decorators; the compiled managed override is not transferred, and no network installer runs. Therefore setup at runtime.cljc:264-266 reaches the real :rf.http/managed registration when present.
- Inline phase 0 (:1622-1625) DOES transfer the derived frame override to allocate-inline!, but neither this path nor run-inline-plan (:1718-1738) installs the network route map. With no prior stub installation, the override target is unregistered; with a preexisting external stub it is not this plan's route map.
- A full source search for install-managed-request-stubs! in tools/story/src finds the only executable call at artifact.cljc:275, inside with-network-stubs! used for artifact replay. None is reachable from normal run/prepare paths. This existing replay helper demonstrates the missing realization step.
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc:492-498 creates the stub registration over the provided route map; merely naming its id cannot do that.

Contract: tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md:2647-2667 says the runner installs the route map when creating the frame. :773 Network stubs requires matched canned replies and unmatched 'no stub matched' failure. :network is accepted by public registration and inspected by the controls provenance surface, not a rejected/unavailable API. plan_network_test.cljc:47 proves the emitted override map only; its mixed success/failure example never exercises a live run. Login testbed uses the older force-fx-stub decorator, which does get installed and therefore does not detect this omission.

Smallest repair: enact the compiled network fixture before any loader/setup/script effect, transfer its derived frame override on registered runs too, and keep the fixture owned for that run/frame lifetime with cleanup on reset/destroy/inline completion. Reuse managed HTTP's existing canned-reply machinery; do not add a second network simulator. The current installer has global stack semantics, so do not let two simultaneously mounted Story variants silently overwrite one another's route replies.

Acceptance: registered and inline variants each execute a managed request against authored :network and observe the declared success/failure, with a live-HTTP sentinel proving zero fallback. An unmatched URL follows the helper's canned no-match failure. Two concurrently mounted variants with different replies to the same URL remain isolated; reset/destroy removes only that fixture's ownership. Exercise the existing public run/prepare lifecycle, not just compile-body.

Dedupe: active+closed searches network, fx-overrides, Story runtime, fixture and narrow network-stubs/managed-request-stubs memories found no matching issue. The two fx-overrides title matches concern Hicasso documentation and MCP dry-run API, not Story execution. No compilation, suite, CLJS/browser or live HTTP executed; this finding is an exact source call/data-flow trace. Review intentionally records no separate duplicate bead for the dropped generic override map at the same registered-frame handoff.
notes:
--- 2026-09-07, worker/story-a — NOT FIXED, premise CONFIRMED at tip ---

Bundled with rf2-fjax / rf2-i6v4 / rf2-7aqo (all three fixed, PR #9366). This
one was left DELIBERATELY: it is larger than the other three combined and lands
in the runtime hot path. Nothing about it is blocked — it wants its own dispatch.
Bead left OPEN and untouched in code; no partial change was pushed.

PREMISE RE-VERIFIED AT TIP (base 763462d4db), construct by construct. The
reviewed snapshot 7ffdacf24d was two mayor HEADs behind; NOTHING had drifted.

  1. `plan/lower-network` is pure — it emits
     `{:network <routes> :fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-test-stub}}`
     and installs nothing. Correct, as the bead says.
  2. `plan/compile-body` stores the routes at `[:world :network]` and the derived
     override at `[:world :frame :fx-overrides]`.
  3. `runtime/run-phase-0!` calls
     `(frames/allocate! variant-id decorator-stack (select-keys (:world plan) [:sensitive :large]))`
     — the plan's `[:world :frame :fx-overrides]` is NOT passed. CONFIRMED.
  4. `frames/allocate!` derives `fx-overrides` from
     `(decorators/fx-overrides-map (:fx-override decorator-stack))` ALONE, so
     there is nowhere for the compiled override to arrive even if it were passed.
     CONFIRMED.
  5. `frames/allocate-inline!` DOES take `plan-fx-overrides` and merges it
     (`(merge decor-fx plan-fx-overrides)`), and `run-inline-phase-0!` passes it —
     so the inline path transfers the override but still installs no route map,
     leaving the redirect pointing at an unregistered fx. CONFIRMED, exactly the
     asymmetry the bead describes.
  6. The ONLY executable `install-managed-request-stubs!` call anywhere in
     `tools/story/src` is `artifact.cljc`'s `(install network)` inside
     `with-network-stubs!`, reachable from artifact REPLAY only. Searched with a
     control (the same search finds that one call), so the zero elsewhere is a
     real zero and not an instrument artefact.
  7. `http/test_support/install-managed-request-stubs!` is what REGISTERS the
     stub fx over a route map; naming the id registers nothing.
  8. And the surface really is advertised, which is what makes this a bug rather
     than an unimplemented idea: `:network` is a first-class optional key on the
     variant AND story body schemas in `story/schemas.cljc` (NetworkSpec), and
     `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md` §"Reuse, not reinvention" states
     that the helper "registers a per-call stub fx … an unmatched managed request
     synthesises the helper's existing 'no stub matched' transport failure",
     with the dep deliberately in Story's MAIN `:deps` (not `:test`) precisely
     because "the stub install is a runtime concern for running a `:network`
     variant". `tools/story/deps.edn`'s comment on `day8/re-frame2-http` says the
     same. So the runtime dependency exists for a step that never runs.

SHAPE OF THE REPAIR (for whoever picks it up), and one finding the bead does not
have. The bead's constraint "the current installer has global stack semantics, so
do not let two simultaneously mounted Story variants silently overwrite one
another's route replies" looks like it forces either a second simulator (which the
bead and spec/017 both forbid) or a change to `implementation/http`. It forces
neither. Two facts make per-frame isolation reachable from inside Story:

  - `http/test_support/stub-handler` reads the route map with a plain
    `(get stubs [method url])`. `stubs` therefore only has to satisfy ILookup —
    it does not have to be a literal map.
  - `re-frame.router` binds `rf.frame/*current-frame*` to the envelope's frame for
    the WHOLE event cascade, fx execution included.

  So ONE install of a Story-owned frame-scoped ILookup — resolving
  `[method url]` against a `{frame-id → routes}` registry keyed on
  `*current-frame*` at lookup time — gives exact per-variant isolation while
  reusing the existing canned-reply machinery untouched, with no second simulator
  and no edit to `implementation/http`. Two caveats to check BEFORE building on
  this, both of which I noted but did not resolve:
    (a) `*current-frame*` holds a frame ID on the router path but a frame OBJECT
        at `frame.cljc`'s own binding site, so the registry key needs normalising;
    (b) `stub-fx-handler-stack` is LIFO while Story's mount/destroy order is not,
        which is why the shape is install-once / release-when-the-registry-empties
        rather than install-per-variant.

  The rest is mechanical but wide: `runtime/run-phase-0!` must install before any
  loader/setup/script effect AND thread `[:world :frame :fx-overrides]` through;
  `frames/allocate!` needs the `plan-fx-overrides` parameter `allocate-inline!`
  already has, merged the same way; `run-inline-phase-0!` needs the install;
  and `frames/destroy!` / `destroy-inline!` / `runtime/reset-variant` / the inline
  teardown all need the release.

WHY IT WAS LEFT. Five acceptance properties (registered path, inline path,
live-HTTP sentinel proving zero fallback, unmatched-URL canned failure, two
concurrently-mounted variants isolated, cleanup on reset/destroy) exercised
through the public run/prepare lifecycle rather than `compile-body`. That is a

title: [implementation/ssr] Resolve explicitly targeted queries through that frame's generation
description:
At snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd, unchanged in the relevant sources at mayor HEAD a7b6793a0d6a0614a1cc64d5988afa93d1e4c490, the explicit frame on the SSR head query selects that frame's data but not its registrations.

Supported minimal caller (after ordinary SSR/adapter boot):
(rf/make-frame
  {:id ::page-frame
   :images [(rf/image
              {:id ::page-image
               :registrations
               {:reg-head [[::page-head {} (fn [_ _] {:title "Image title"})]]}})]})
(head/render-head ::page-head {:frame ::page-frame})
Call outside a with-frame binding, as the explicit-target API and ssr_head_test.clj callers do. The frame image contains the head declaration and a frame-resolved registrar lookup finds it. Expected {:title "Image title"}; actual public query looks in the process registrar and throws :rf.error/no-such-head. If the process/current ambient generation has the same id, it instead silently executes THAT body against the requested frame's app-db. A head preview inside frame A targeting B has the same wrong-generation behavior.

Exact causal trace:
- implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/registry.cljc:90-126 requires the explicit :frame, reads its route and app-db, but invokes rf.registrar/lookup :head at 111 with no target-resolution extent.
- Its active-head branch:179-207 also resolves route metadata via route-head-id:159-177, which calls ambient lookup :route at 176 before selecting the head. Both lookups must target the same frame.
- head.cljc:40-41 only re-exports these fns; the core facade hook is also a pass-through, so there is no caller-side target binding that repairs the public door.
- registrar.cljc:828-862 explicitly consults the bound generation, otherwise the process registrar. live_frame.cljc:330 provides the target-generation extent used elsewhere.
- :reg-head is supported inline image grammar (image.cljc:296,401), and :head/:route are generation resolver kinds. ssr_head_test.clj:110-151 establishes unbound explicit-target calls as normal usage.

Impact: valid image-local head declarations fail to render, or a multi-image application returns another image's title/meta/link model for the selected page. Ring normally wraps its request frame and can mask the defect; the explicit public head query/custom host or preview path is affected.

Smallest repair: establish target-frame registration resolution across route-head selection and head lookup/invocation, using the existing core seam. Do not change global registrar behavior or require callers to supply a redundant with-frame.

Dedupe/current work: active+closed searches head/render-head/generation and relevant memories; rf2-kuky.89's complete current description/notes concerns renaming/consolidating these reads as ssr/head-model and contains no generation-resolution repair. Preserve that accepted API direction and coordinate the small fix with its owner. rf2-kuky.44's single-door ruling is not challenged. Root confirmed no registry reviewer owns this query-execution gap; rf2-zimh concerns live subscription-cache metadata, not head rendering.

Acceptance: under no ambient frame, an image-only head renders from its explicit target; with A in scope and B explicitly targeted, both direct named-head and active route-head lookup use B's generation and data. Include different same-id head bodies and image-only route metadata; ordinary process/default-image calls remain unchanged. Carry the same checks onto ssr/head-model if rf2-kuky.89 lands first.

ONE PREMISE OF THIS BEAD DOES NOT HOLD — the stated minimal caller cannot be run as written. It registers the head through an inline image section:
  (rf/image {:id ::page-image :registrations {:reg-head [[::page-head {} (fn [_ _] ...)]]}})
`:reg-head` is NOT supported inline grammar. The two sites the bead cites as evidence that it is (image.cljc:296 and :401) are exactly the REJECTION list: EP-0026 standardises inline grammar for :reg-event / :reg-sub / :reg-fx / :reg-cofx ONLY, and every other kind — :reg-head and :reg-error-projector named explicitly in both — fails loud. Executed: the call above throws :rf.error/invalid-image, "unsupported inline registrations section :reg-head".
Consequently the bead's predicted :rf.error/no-such-head outcome is UNREACHABLE by any door: `register!` writes the registrar ATOM and the provenance source store, so the atom is always a SUPERSET of any generation's :head view, and a process-registrar lookup can never miss a head some frame's image carries.

THE DEFECT ITSELF IS REAL and is the bead's SECOND predicted failure — the more serious one. Reproduced through the supported door (namespace-authored `reg-head` + `:select-ns`), because `source-store/descriptors-for` retains EVERY provenance-distinct descriptor for a [kind id] while the registrar atom keeps only the last writer. Executed against the unmodified sources, with ALPHA and BETA registering the same head id from two namespaces and two frames selecting one each:
  source-store descriptors-for [:head shared] -> (alpha beta)   [both retained]
  registrar atom               -> BETA's body
  rf/handler-meta {:frame alpha-frame ...}     -> ALPHA's body   [the correct answer, already available]
  render-head shared {:frame alpha-frame}      -> {:title "beta:A"}   [BETA's body, ALPHA's app-db]
  project-error alpha-frame (frame :ssr {:public-error-id ALPHA}) -> {:status 451 :code :beta ...}  [BETA's, not ALPHA's 418]
  render-head <a head the frame's image does NOT select> {:frame alpha-frame} -> rendered anyway
So: a plausible head model for the wrong page, and — via the addendum's project-error — the wrong STATUS and public body leaving the server.

  * project-error — one extent over the :error-projector lookup AND the projector call.
A target with no sealed generation binds nothing and takes the registrar-atom path exactly as before, so ordinary single-image / default-image applications are unchanged. WHY C, AGAINST "PURELY COSMETIC / GOLD-PLATING". The harm is cosmetic and both reviewers say so. That argument decides D (a rewrite of a sha-addressed repository across 11 live worktrees to remove two lines from three commits — the dossier's section D) and it decides against Codex's separate metadata workflow (below). It does not decide against C, for three reasons anchored in the posture. FIRST, "trust the programmer" is about the programmer, and this breach is not a programmer's judgement: it is a machine injecting text into every session that flatly contradicts the checked-in file, and the tie was broken by coin flip inside ONE wave (flowsettle-a declined citing CLAUDE.md; two siblings complied — the same session URL on all three commits). SECOND, the rule already exists and carries Mike's stated reason (e4529560df: "so commit messages and PR descriptions read as the maintainer's own work"); the honest alternatives are enforce or delete (E), and nobody proposed deleting it. A rule written down and not enforced is the misleading kind — it failed silently seven times, and this repository's own principles (spec/Principles.md, no silent swallow) are about failures that report themselves. THIRD, the marginal cost is now near zero: the hook, detector, installer registration, .gitattributes pin, README row, test layer 10 (10a–10n) AND the test.yml step are already written in #9317 — nine files plus the workflow — and the step is a STEP in the existing beads-pr-boundary job (test.yml:1243, inserted after the `check-beads-pr-boundary.sh "origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}"` line at 1282, under its fetch-depth: 0), so the check rollup and the clause-5 band do not move. What remains is a repair, a settings key and two `gh pr edit`s. Low friction holds in the sense that matters: a clean commit pays nothing; only a commit carrying the trailer is refused, and the refusal says why and how to quote one on purpose.

WHERE THE LINE IS. Codex's acceptance item 4 — a separate cheap metadata workflow on `pull_request: edited` that reports into the required checks so a body-only edit re-grades — is DECLINED. That is a new workflow file (hot-zone), a new required check (the band moves) and a new trigger, to catch a residual that is not the observed failure mode: the harness writes the body at `gh pr create`, which the `opened` event grades, and the settings key removes that source anyway. A post-push hand edit that ADDS a marker is a deliberate act, not the harness's, and stays a mayor read at merge time.
