title: api(testing): fold the four sequester-/reinstate-app-* vars into a make-reset-runtime-fixture :app-ns option
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from registration-and-testing.md (ref testing.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`re-frame.test-support` grew four public `v1`-status vars (`8b969af7c4`, 2026-07-12, rf2-h1vqa4 slice 2) that spell ONE idea twice, with a different selector shape AND a different state model each time (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc`):

| var | selector | captured rows live | lowers to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequester-app-registration!` `[kind id provenance-ns]` (:168) | one row | returned to the caller, who `def`s it and hands it back | ownership-guarded `swap! registrar dissoc` (:203-212) + `source-store/forget-descriptor!` (:214) |
| `reinstate-app-registration!` `[descriptor]` (:221) | that value | — | `registrar/register!` (registrar + source store in lockstep) |
| `sequester-app-namespaces!` `[ns-prefix]` (:237) | every row whose provenance ns starts with the prefix | a module-level memo atom `sequestered-namespace-rows` (:231), captured ONCE per prefix | the same two legs in a `doseq` (:262-274) |
| `reinstate-app-namespaces!` `[ns-prefix]` (:280) | the memo | — | `registrar/register!` over the memo |

They exist for one condition: the consolidated CLJS node bundle loads every example app before any test runs; two apps register the same per-app id (`:rf.route/not-found`; the RealWorld twins share `:settings/load`, `:auth/initialise`, …); the source store keeps both provenance rows; any suite whose fixture BASELINE is captured after the second app loads fails `make-frame {}` loud with `:rf.error/image-duplicate-id`. That is a baseline concern, and `make-reset-runtime-fixture` (:580) already OWNS the baseline: it captures `ns-load-baseline` and `source-store-baseline*` at build time (:818-819) and restores both around every test (`reinstate-and-snapshot!` :513, `finish-runtime-reset!` :565). The four verbs re-implement the fixture's own capture/restore cycle beside it — once as a value, once as a global.

Measured costs of the memo model: it captures ONCE, so a call before the sibling app finishes loading pins an incomplete set for every later suite (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_realworld_resources_boot_seed_cljs_test.cljs:84-88`: `:home/show-global-feed` left unsequestered, a sibling suite's frame creation failed); and because it is global rather than per-fixture, `realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:200` has to re-sequester the sibling on EVERY test from its `init!`. Behaviour determined by load order, not visible inputs (`spec/Principles.md` low-hidden-context).

Neither `spec/008-Testing.md` nor `spec/API.md` rows them (`grep -c sequester` → 0 in both), yet `spec/api-manifest.edn:564-568` tiers them `:testing` / `:owner "008"` / `v1`. The consumer pitch is `docs/api/re-frame.test-support.md:89-181` ("Bundle co-load hygiene"), and the pilots README says the opposite: "None of that applies to a workspace with one app in it, and none of it travels" (`docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/baseline/README.md:14`). Four permanent obligations on every conforming port for a harness-internal condition.

## Evidence

```sh
git grep -n -E 'sequester-app-|reinstate-app-|sequestered-namespace-rows' -- ':!implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc' ':!ai/' ':!.beads/'
```
Consumers by class: impl-test 6 files (5 reagent example suites + the own unit test); Story 0; Xray 0; examples 0; skills 0; pilots 0.

## Target API

Zero new verbs. One option on the fixture that already owns the baseline:

```clojure
(use-fixtures :each
  (ts/make-reset-runtime-fixture
    {:adapter reagent-adapter/adapter
     :app-ns  "realworld-http."      ;; rows whose provenance ns starts here are THIS suite's app
     :init-fn init!}))
```

- `:app-ns` — a string prefix, or a set of prefixes, matched against each source-store descriptor's provenance ns (`:rf.provenance/ns`, exactly as `sequester-app-namespaces!` matches at :248-252). The rule for callers: name your OWN app's root namespace; never a sibling's.
- **Build time** (this ns's load, after its `:require` chain — i.e. inside `make-reset-runtime-fixture`, BEFORE `ns-load-baseline` / `source-store-baseline*` are taken at :818-819): capture every matching row and remove it from the live registrar and the source store. The remover is the existing ownership-guarded two-leg form (registrar slot dropped ONLY when its current writer is under the prefix, :265-273; `forget-descriptor!` per provenance row) kept as a `defn-` inside test-support. **Not `registrar/unregister!`**: it forgets EVERY provenance slot for `(kind, id)` (`registrar.cljc:713-724`) and would clobber a sibling's row for a shared id.
- **Captured rows go into a fixture-internal registry keyed by prefix that UNIONS across fixture builds** — never first-capture-wins. This is what answers codex's objection ("CLJS loads a required namespace once; if suite A captures and removes an app's rows, suite B's later `:require` of that already-loaded app does not register them again") and the boot-seed memo trap: a second suite for the same app finds the rows already gone, captures whatever NEW rows its own requires registered, and reinstates the union; a late-loading part of the app is captured by whichever fixture builds after it. Repeated suites for one app are a LIVE case: `realworld_cljs_test`, `example_realworld_boot_seed_cljs_test`, `example_realworld_password_classification_cljs_test`, `example_frame_scoping_cljs_test` all load parts of `realworld-http.*`; `realworld_resources_cljs_test` and `example_realworld_resources_boot_seed_cljs_test` both load `realworld-resources.*`. The registry is internal; its whole contract is one docstring line — "rows under `:app-ns` are this suite's app: absent from every baseline, live during this suite's tests".
- **Per test**: after `reset-runtime!` (adapter installed, `:rf/default` ensured, :538) and BEFORE `:init-fn` runs, reinstate the union through `rf.registrar/register!` (registrar + source store in lockstep, as `reinstate-app-registration!` :221-229 does today). Setup ordering codex asked to preserve is preserved: the RealWorld resources `init!` still registers plans and stubs before it makes its URL-bound frame, because `:init-fn` runs after reinstatement exactly where it runs now.
- **Teardown**: `finish-runtime-reset!` (:565) already resets the source store to the suite's baseline (which excludes the app rows). Verify after each test that no `:app-ns` row remains in the SOURCE STORE (image assembly reads the store; the merge-form registrar restore may leave resolver slots — today's behaviour, and harmless for the same reason). The per-test re-scrub at `realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:200` becomes unnecessary because a sibling's rows never enter any baseline.

Before / after per use case:

| use case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| hide my own `:rf.route/not-found` row; reinstate per test (5 suites) | `(def ^:private row (ts/sequester-app-registration! :route :rf.route/not-found "x.core"))` + `(ts/reinstate-app-registration! row)` in `init!` | `:app-ns "x."` |
| hide a sibling's whole tree; sibling reinstates per test (2 suites) | `sequester-app-namespaces! "realworld-http."` at load AND per test in one suite; `reinstate-app-namespaces!` in the other | `:app-ns "realworld-http."` in one, `:app-ns "realworld-resources."` in the other; neither names the other |
| in-body rival-"/" removal for one deftest (`linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs:296-330`) | `sequester-app-registration!` per rival, `reinstate-app-registration!` in `finally` | a LOCAL `defn-` in that test doing both legs (ownership-guarded registrar dissoc + `source-store/forget-descriptor!`) and `registrar/register!` in `finally`. Codex: an L1/L2 `snapshot-registrar` / `restore-registrar!` bracket touches only the resolver atom and would leave the source store mutated — both stores, always. It stays because its rivals can come from suites that do not self-hide. |
| own unit test (`sequester_app_registration_cljs_test.cljc`, 168 lines) | three rf2-22vzb guard cases on the pair | the same three cases as `:app-ns` cases in the fixture's own test |

## Corroboration

One-reviewer. Fable: "the cleanest proposal in the wave — ship it". Codex: "the four public bundle-hygiene verbs expose a real harness concern, and the memoized-prefix mechanism has a concrete weakness … the proposed `:app-ns` fixture option is not yet a complete or low-risk replacement" — with four gaps this bead answers explicitly: (1) repeated suites for one app → the prefix-keyed union above; (2) prefix ≠ one `[kind id provenance]` row → the single-row case is the prefix case with a narrower prefix, and the ownership guard means a sibling's live slot for a shared id is never touched; (3) the in-body fallback must restore both stores → the Linearlite rewrite names both legs; (4) the option ships only if a concrete implementation handles repeated suites, shared prefixes, late registration and coordinated restoration "without a new hidden global protocol" → the union registry is internal and prefix-keyed, and the regression matrix below is codex's own. Codex's preferred alternative — a repo-local, non-shipped helper holding an explicit captured app-descriptor value shared among an app's suites — is the fallback named under Risks.

## Deletion list

- `test_support.cljc`: `sequester-app-registration!` (:168), `reinstate-app-registration!` (:221), `sequestered-namespace-rows` (:231), `sequester-app-namespaces!` (:237), `reinstate-app-namespaces!` (:280). The ownership-guarded remover survives as a `defn-` for the fixture.
- `spec/api-manifest.edn:564,565,567,568` and `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1544-1547` (4 rows each) — regenerated, not hand-edited.
- `docs/api/re-frame.test-support.md:89-181` ("Bundle co-load hygiene") → one `:app-ns` row in the `make-reset-runtime-fixture` opts table (:66-75).
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/sequester_app_registration_cljs_test.cljc` → folded into the fixture's test.

## The problem

The only growth since July is one idea spelled twice, with a different selector shape *and* a different state model each time (all `test_support.cljc`, landed together in `8b969af7c4` 2026-07-12, rf2-h1vqa4 slice 2):

| Spelling | Selector | Where the captured rows live | Lowers to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequester-app-registration!` `[kind id provenance-ns]` (`:168`) | one row | **returned to the caller**, who must `def` it and hand it back | `swap! registrar dissoc` (ownership-guarded) + `source-store/forget-descriptor!` |
| `reinstate-app-registration!` `[descriptor]` (`:221`) | that value | — | `registrar/register!` |
| `sequester-app-namespaces!` `[ns-prefix]` (`:237`) | every row whose provenance starts with the prefix | **a private module-level memo atom** `sequestered-namespace-rows` (`:231`), captured once per prefix | same two legs, in a `doseq` |
| `reinstate-app-namespaces!` `[ns-prefix]` (`:280`) | the memo | — | `registrar/register!` over the memo |

Both pairs solve one problem: the consolidated CLJS node bundle loads every example app before any test runs, two apps register the same per-app id (`:rf.route/not-found`; the RealWorld twins share `:settings/load` …), the source store keeps both provenance rows, and any suite whose fixture *baseline* is captured after the second app loads fails `make-frame {}` loud with `:rf.error/image-duplicate-id`. The cure is "hide my rows from sibling baselines at ns-load, put them back per test". That is a *baseline* concern — and `make-reset-runtime-fixture` already owns the baseline: it captures `ns-load-baseline` and `source-store-baseline*` at build time (`:818-819`) and restores both around every test (`finish-runtime-reset!`, `:565`). The four verbs re-implement the fixture's own capture/restore cycle beside it, once as a value and once as a global.

Two measured costs of the second state model: the memo captures **once**, so a call before the sibling app finishes loading pins an incomplete set for every later suite (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_realworld_resources_boot_seed_cljs_test.cljs:84-88` — measured, `:home/show-global-feed` left unsequestered, a sibling suite's frame creation failed); and because the memo is global rather than per-fixture, `realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:200` has to **re-sequester the sibling on every test** from its `init!`, a second call whose only job is to undo what the fixture's merge-form restore folded back.

Neither `spec/008-Testing.md` nor `spec/API.md` §Testing (`:778`) rows them (`grep -c sequester` → 0 in both), yet the manifest tiers them `:testing` / `:owner "008"` / `v1`. The prose home is `docs/api/re-frame.test-support.md:89-181` ("Bundle co-load hygiene"), which pitches them to consumers — and the pilots README says the opposite: "None of that applies to a workspace with one app in it, and none of it travels" (`docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/baseline/README.md:14`).

## Simpler elegant target

**Zero new verbs. One option on the fixture that already owns the baseline.**

```clojure
(use-fixtures :each
  (ts/make-reset-runtime-fixture
    {:adapter reagent-adapter/adapter
     :app-ns  "realworld-http."      ;; rows whose provenance ns starts here are MINE
     :init-fn init!}))
```

Semantics, in the fixture's existing lifecycle: at **build time** (= this ns's load, after its `:require` chain) capture the `:app-ns` rows into the fixture's closure and remove them from the live registrar + source store *before* `ns-load-baseline` is taken, so no later-loading suite's baseline can ever hold them; at **each test** reinstate them through `registrar/register!` after `reset-runtime!` and before `:init-fn`; the existing `finish-runtime-reset!` already restores registrar and store to the app-less baseline on the way out. Self-hiding is the invariant: when every app suite hides *itself*, no suite needs to know its sibling's name, the per-test re-scrub (`realworld_resources:200`) disappears, and the memo trap cannot occur because the capture is per-fixture and after this ns's own requires by construction.

| 2 (2 suites) | sibling-naming `sequester-app-namespaces!` at load **and** per test; `reinstate-app-namespaces!` in the other suite | `:app-ns "realworld-http."` in one suite, `:app-ns "realworld-resources."` in the other; neither names the other |

## Why this is better (ethos)

**The demand bar, read honestly (`spec/Principles.md:124`).** "A public surface ships only for a *named consumer*." The named consumer here is the repo's own consolidated test bundle; a consumer app with one app in its bundle never meets the collision, and the pilots README says so. Four `v1` names for a harness-internal condition are four permanent obligations on every conforming port for a problem the port's users will not have. An option on a fixture the port already ships is the pre-settled promotion shape the principle asks for: cheap to carry, invisible until needed.

**Low hidden context (`:87`).** `sequester-app-namespaces!` behaves differently on its first and second call, and differently depending on *which namespace called it first* — that is behaviour determined by load order, not by visible inputs, and the boot-seed test measured exactly that. A closure captured by the fixture at build time has one input: this ns's own requires.

**Regularity over cleverness.** Two selector shapes and two state models for one operation is the *one-fact-many-names* hazard the demand bar names in its own text. A single key with one semantics ("rows under this prefix are mine") is the regular form; the single-row case is the prefix case with a narrower prefix, so nothing is lost.

**Clojure.** Configuration as data on the thing that already owns the lifecycle beats a pair of stateful verbs the caller must sequence correctly across two files. The fixture *is* the bracket; giving it one more key keeps the composition the corpus already voted for (fixture ∘ walkers ∘ poll — 615 files) instead of teaching a second, order-sensitive ceremony beside it.

**Honest cost.** Five suites edit their `use-fixtures` form and drop a `def`; one Linearlite test rewrites a nine-line bracket onto primitives it already imports; per-test reinstate of a whole app tree is a `doseq` of `register!` over tens of rows rather than one — unmeasurable against the adapter dispose/install the fixture already does each test.

## Grok Thoughts

**Bother handling?** Yes. The July sweep landed. The only growth is four public verbs for a fixture option, and one of the two state models is a measured trap: `sequester-app-namespaces!` captures once into a module-level memo, so a call before the sibling app finishes loading pins an incomplete set (`:home/show-global-feed` left live; a later suite's `make-frame {}` failed with `:rf.error/image-duplicate-id`). **Diagnosis.** Correct. Two selector shapes and two state models for one operation, neither rowed in spec/008 or API.md, pitched to consumers in `docs/api/re-frame.test-support.md`. The fixture already owns `ns-load-baseline` / `source-store-baseline*` and restores both around every test. The four verbs re-implement that cycle beside it.

**Options.** Keep a private row-remover for the fixture vs keep one public pair. No public verbs. The Linearlite in-body rival-removal test is a different job (L2 snapshot/restore), not a reason to keep the public pair.

**Recommendation.** One `:app-ns` key on `make-reset-runtime-fixture`. This is the cleanest proposal in the wave — ship it.

Leave the testid/attr split, `poll-until`, adapter `flush-views!`, the three Story testbed hand-rolls (written reason), and the L2 snapshot primitives. Note, do not bead: Hicasso's private `wait-until!` (boolean-on-timeout) and reagent-slim's second `flush-views!` (Promise return, zero external callers). Flag the 008:1013 `subscribe-once` teaching vs the RETAIN ruling as a doc fix for the state-reads owner.

## Codex Thoughts

**Verdict: the four public bundle-hygiene verbs expose a real harness concern, and the memoized-prefix mechanism has a concrete weakness. The proposed `:app-ns` fixture option is not yet a complete or low-risk replacement.**

The diagnosis of hidden first-capture state is confirmed by [`sequester-app-namespaces!`](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc) and the [boot-seed regression commentary](../../../../implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_realworld_resources_boot_seed_cljs_test.cljs): capture before an application's full namespace tree has loaded can permanently omit later registrations.

But moving capture into each fixture closure does not itself remove load-order coupling. ClojureScript loads a required namespace once. If suite A captures and removes an application's rows, suite B's later `:require` of that already-loaded app does not register them again. Suite B can capture an empty or incomplete set even though its own requires have finished. A per-fixture owner is therefore insufficient when multiple suites exercise the same app.

There are two further gaps:

- A prefix selector is not equivalent to selecting one `[kind id provenance]` row. It removes unrelated registrations under the same namespace and can affect suites sharing those definitions.
- The proposed in-body fallback does not restore everything it changes. `snapshot-registrar` and `restore-registrar!` touch only the resolver atom; `forget-descriptor!` mutates the separate source store. Wrapping that operation in a registrar snapshot bracket leaves image-visible source rows removed. Preserve both stores coherently or reinstate the captured descriptors through `registrar/register!`.

Consider the actual alternatives before adding a shipped fixture option:

1. Keep a small, **repo-local bundle helper** with an explicit captured app-descriptor value. Capture once at an app-support boundary after its complete registration graph loads; share that immutable value among its suites.
2. Use explicit app image selection for tests that do not need to test default-image assembly. This avoids treating every co-loaded app as part of one application, although suites exercising boot's default selection still need faithful isolation.
3. Put conflicting app integration suites in separate bundles. This costs runner setup but removes the collision instead of making global baseline choreography more sophisticated.
4. Add the fixture option only if a concrete implementation handles repeated suites, shared prefixes, late registration, and coordinated source-store/registrar restoration without a new hidden global protocol.

For the present, I favor the first approach: consolidate ownership locally and remove public names once the existing suites migrate. Do not promote a repository-specific multiplexing problem into every port's testing contract just to reduce the visible function count.

Keep setup ordering explicit. [`reset-runtime!`](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc) installs an adapter and can establish a default frame; the [RealWorld resources setup](../../../../implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs) deliberately registers resource plans and stubs before creating its URL-bound frame. A new fixture path must preserve that ordering rather than merely reinstate rows somewhere before the test body.

A focused regression matrix is enough: two suites for one app, two conflicting apps, reversed suite order, an absent requested row, and exceptional teardown. Assert both registrar lookup and image assembly. This is useful harness repair, not a reason to invent a general namespace-ownership framework.

# Testing surface — twin polls, an unadopted harness, and hand-rolled fixtures

**Status:** medium-high (real duplication + dead surface inside a defensible split; wave 2, 2026-07-10 14:30 AUSEST, Fable-authored)
**Surfaces:** `re-frame.test-support` (10 vars) and `re-frame.test-helpers` (14 vars)

---

## The problem

The two-namespace **split is sound** — `test-support` asserts on runtime state (registrar, frames,
app-db, drain, trace), `test-helpers` on the view tree (hiccup walkers, testids, handlers); both are
JVM-runnable, and the axis is documented. The problems live *inside* it:

1. **Twin polls.** `test-support/poll-until` and `test-helpers/wait-until` are the same function —
   identical mechanism, opts, defaults (`:timeout-ms 2000 :interval-ms 5 :label`), identical
   JVM-sync/CLJS-promise split — differing only in error-id and one fixture-coupled extra arity. The
   docs even admit it: "the view-test counterpart to `poll-until`."
2. **An unadopted e2e harness.** The single-frame trio `with-app-fixture` + `expect-text` +
   `wait-until` (plus two dynamic vars) is consumed by **exactly its own unit test**. The corpus's 200+
   test files compose `make-reset-runtime-fixture` + hiccup walkers + `poll-until` instead.
3. **Hand-rolled fixture duplication.** 21 adapter/story DOM test files re-implement the reset that
   `make-reset-runtime-fixture` composes (raw `snapshot-registrar`/`restore-registrar!` +
   `(reset! frame/frames {})` + `dispose-adapter!` in manual `before!`/`after!`).
4. **A dead tail.** `dispatch-sequence` and `assert-db-equals` are used only by their own unit tests;
   `with-fresh-registrar` has one consumer; `merge-registrar-snapshots` is called only internally.

---

## Empirical use cases

| Use case | What the corpus actually reaches for | Scale |
|---|---|---|
| Per-test runtime reset | `make-reset-runtime-fixture` | **200+ files** (dominant) — plus 21 files hand-rolling the same |
| Async settle | `poll-until` | 24 files / 68 uses (HTTP, capture-frame) — `wait-until`: own test only |
| View-tree walking/asserting | `find-by-testid` & family, `text-content` | 293 uses of `find-by-testid` alone (Xray epoch panel: 255) |
| Trace-bracket assertion | `with-trace-recorder!` | 11 files / 70 uses (reagent DOM tests) |
| Snapshot/restore primitives | `snapshot-registrar` / `restore-registrar!` | 21 files — exactly the hand-rollers above |
| Single-frame e2e bracket | `with-app-fixture` trio | **own unit test only** |
| Event-sequence driver | `dispatch-sequence` | own unit test only |
| Whole/path db asserts | `assert-path-equals` (1 Story consumer + mirrors `:rf.assert/path-equals`) / `assert-db-equals` (own test only) | marginal |

The corpus has voted: **fixture + walkers + poll** is the testing API. Everything else is either a
primitive under it or speculation that never landed.

---

## Simpler elegant target

### Ship the discovered API; delete the speculated one

1. **One poll.** Delete `wait-until`; `poll-until` is the single bounded poll (wider adoption, the
   state-axis home, one error-id). Its fixture-coupled testid arity dies with the trio below.
2. **Delete the unadopted e2e trio** — `with-app-fixture`, `expect-text`, `wait-until`, both dynamic
   vars. Zero consumers, pre-alpha, tombstone-free. The corpus's own composition *is* the e2e story and
   the docs should teach exactly that composition.
3. **Delete `dispatch-sequence` and `assert-db-equals`.** Own-test-only; the first is a `doseq` over
   `dispatch-sync`, the second is `(is (= …))`. Keep `assert-path-equals` — it has a real consumer
   (Story invariants) and is the documented cross-channel mirror of the `:rf.assert/path-equals` play
   event (one fact, two runners, spec-acknowledged).
4. **Demote the internals.** `merge-registrar-snapshots` → private (internal to the fixture);
   `with-fresh-registrar` → delete (one consumer migrates to `make-reset-runtime-fixture`); raw
   `snapshot-registrar`/`restore-registrar!` stay public as the primitives the fixture composes.
5. **Sweep the 21 hand-rolled resets** onto `make-reset-runtime-fixture` — or, if the DOM tests
   genuinely need a different bracket, grow the fixture's opts once and say why. Either way the corpus
   stops teaching two spellings of its own dominant idiom.

Net result: `test-support` = fixture + primitives + `poll-until` + `with-trace-recorder!` +
`assert-path-equals`; `test-helpers` = the hiccup/testid toolkit. Two namespaces, two axes, zero twins,
zero dead vars, one composition taught everywhere.

---

## Why this is better (ethos)

**re-frame2:** the corpus's own thesis is that testing falls out of the architecture ("bend the edges,
never the middle") rather than being a library. The parts of this surface the corpus adopted are
exactly the architectural corollaries (reset the world-table, poll the async seam, walk the pure
hiccup); the parts it ignored are the parts that tried to be a framework. Trust the vote.

**The demand bar, retroactively:** `with-app-fixture` & co. shipped without a named consumer and found
none in 200+ test files' worth of opportunities. That is the strongest demand-bar evidence the repo has
ever produced — refusing to carry it further is the principle working, not churn.


**Clojure:** small orthogonal functions that compose (fixture ∘ walkers ∘ poll) beat a bundled harness;
the corpus independently converged on composition, which is the Clojure ethos validating itself.

**Masterpiece:** a testing API is where users learn whether the project means what it says — dead vars
and twin names teach distrust exactly where trust matters most.

---

## Non-goals

- Do not merge the two namespaces — the state-axis/view-axis split is real, documented, and both sides
  are heavily used; renaming 200+ consumers buys nothing.
- Do not build a replacement e2e harness — the composition is the harness.
- Do not touch the `:test` preset, canned-HTTP stubs, or dispatch-opt seams (they are the actual
  testing story and they are clean).
- Do not remove `snapshot-registrar`/`restore-registrar!` — they are the primitives power users
  legitimately compose (the fix for the 21 hand-rollers is adoption or fixture opts, not deletion).

## Grok Thoughts

**Bother handling?** Yes, and the work landed in full (`88b20f1d22`, `1ca51af64c`). Twin polls, the unadopted e2e trio, `dispatch-sequence` / `assert-db-equals`, and the 21 hand-rolled fixtures are gone. The corpus's vote — fixture ∘ walkers ∘ `poll-until` — is now the surface. The original diagnosis was right; the demand-bar evidence (200+ files ignoring `with-app-fixture`) was as strong as this repo gets.

**What grew afterwards.** Four `sequester-`/`reinstate-` verbs (see `test-isolation-surface.md`) — one idea, two selector shapes, two state models, a load-order memo trap. That is the only API-shaped regrowth. Treat it as the sequel to this doc, not a re-litigation. The three remaining Story testbed hand-rolls have a written reason (source-store baseline the per-ns fixture would get wrong); leave them.

**Leftover nits, not beads.** Hicasso's private `wait-until!` (boolean-on-timeout, four DOM suites). reagent-slim's second `flush-views!` (Promise return vs the spine's nil). 008:1013 still teaching `subscribe-once` as the canonical read-then-discard primitive beside `compute-sub` after wave 1 retained `subscribe-once` for a different reason. None of these reopen the July split.

**Do not** merge `test-support` and `test-helpers`. The state-axis / view-axis split is real and both sides are heavily used.

## Codex Thoughts

**Verdict: this was a useful simplification and is now substantially implemented. Preserve the resulting composition; do not turn the historical inventory into another cleanup campaign.**

Current [`test_helpers.cljc`](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_helpers.cljc) no longer contains the redundant `wait-until`, `with-app-fixture`, `expect-text`, or event-sequence/whole-db helpers. [`test_support.cljc`](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc) keeps `merge-registrar-snapshots` private and no longer exports `with-fresh-registrar`. The newer [test-isolation dossier](test-isolation-surface.md) is the relevant account of the remaining surface.

The central recommendation still reads well: reset the runtime with a fixture, inspect the view with small walkers, and wait through one bounded poll. Runtime-state support and view-tree inspection are different responsibilities; combining their namespaces would change names without simplifying the model. Likewise, `find-by-testid` earns its convenience role alongside generic attribute lookup. It serves the dominant readable form without concealing different behavior or lifecycle.

The original “sweep all hand-rolled fixtures” instruction needs its documented qualification. The remaining [Story counter fixture](../../../../tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/stories_cljs_test.cljs) restores a stable source-store baseline that contains the application registrations its selected images need. Its commentary records why replacing it with another namespace's incomplete baseline lost those registrations. Until the shared fixture can express that requirement straightforwardly, keeping this local bracket is better than either forcing the migration or growing a speculative fixture framework.

Raw registrar snapshots are also intentionally narrower than whole-runtime snapshots. They are appropriate for scoped resolver assertions, but must not be presented as undoing source-store changes. If a test mutates provenance descriptors or constructs images from them, its bracket needs the corresponding source-store restoration. That qualification belongs beside the primitive's teaching example, not in another public snapshot API unless a named consumer truly requires it.

For implementation today, the proportionate action is documentation status and recipe maintenance: identify this dossier's retired names as completed work, point remaining bundle-isolation work to its separate dossier, and retain one short example of the adopted fixture/walkers/poll composition. No new runtime change follows from this historical review alone.

If a future fixture consolidation is attempted, verify the test body actually executes on both hosts: the existing `:async?` option deliberately returns a CLJS map fixture but a JVM function fixture. Also check async teardown and exception cleanup rather than counting migrated files. These are the useful semantic boundaries; the precise count of helpers or local wrappers is not the quality target.

The Clojure lesson here is successful composition, not a universal ban on convenience functions. Stop once the supported pieces are understandable, orthogonal, and pleasant to use.

This is NOT a mechanical arity bump some other fix could dodge. The assertion's

## 2. The regression witness rf2-8icg's acceptance criteria 1 and 6 ask for

Not written, for the same fence. Deterministic held-transport CLJS coverage,
patterned on the same suite's held-request cross-slug tests (around lines
1900-2130):

[:profile/follow-rollback true {:kind :rf.http/http-4xx}]. Against the new

The brief offered keeping the identity-free dispatch as a NEGATIVE test. I did

WELL-FORMED settle for a profile the slice no longer targets, which no

So the existing assertion got its identity ("eve") and kept its job — the

The bead asked for the guard to be inverted. Instead the WHOLE production
change was reverted (profile.cljs + schema.cljs restored to the merge base,
973c26fdc7, which is byte-identical to origin/main on those paths) with the

  WITHOUT the fix: exit 1 — "Ran 11209 tests containing 56614 assertions.

                   1 in realworld-favorites-follow-feed (the repaired line),

Identical test and assertion totals both ways, so nothing dropped out of the

All NINE settle handlers the fix re-arity'd (:profile/loaded,
/load-failed, :profile.articles/loaded, /load-failed,
:profile.favorites/loaded, /load-failed, :profile/followed, /unfollowed,

There is no late-alice FAVORITES settle. :profile.favorites/loaded and

rather than filing a bead; reopen if you want the symmetry.

The harness reported "exit code 0" for FIVE background runs whose own .exit

title: skill(pair-retro): issue-draft ownership requires sources the self-contained package cannot reach
description:
## Problem

The pair-retro skill's issue-draft contract requires exact ownership evidence that a normally installed, self-contained copy cannot access, and it points agents at the wrong sibling document when a source checkout happens to be available.

At reviewed base `bf0b43dbcb68d57dfa493ebcf26ea8f67e7752d9`:

- `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md:86` requires every framework-shaped draft to name the relevant `spec/Tool-Pair.md` capability/restore row and shipped Pair tool, then says the tool catalogue is `re-frame2-pair`'s README.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair/README.md` contains no catalogue table; it is a short human-facing overview/examples page.
- The actual 30-tool catalogue is `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/mcp-transport.md:63-103`. `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py:1130-1137` treats that file—not the README—as the descriptor-backed tool reference.
- The retro's own `references/known-frictions.md:201` correctly distinguishes sources: ops for vocabulary, mcp-transport for per-tool behavior, and live `tools/list` as authoritative. This contradicts the operational instruction in SKILL.md.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/package.json:25-32` ships only this package's SKILL, README, LICENSE, agent metadata, references, and plugin metadata. It does not ship sibling Pair references or root `spec/Tool-Pair.md`.
- `SKILL.md:29`, `README.md:34`, and design L7 promise normal operation is self-contained, while `spec/inputs.md:48` explicitly says the skill does not consume the re-frame2 spec corpus.
- `SKILL.md:55` forbids live probing and requires unseen facts to remain unknown. A supported recap-only input therefore commonly contains neither `tools/list` nor a Tool-Pair excerpt.

These constraints cannot all be satisfied. On the normal standalone path, the agent must either invent a current capability row/tool from memory, violate the one-turn draft workflow to seek unavailable evidence, or omit/misclassify ownership despite the mandatory contract.

## Reproduction and impact

1. Install/use only the published `re-frame2-pair-retro` package.
2. Supply a recap saying that a Pair operation lacked enough information; include no `tools/list`, sibling documentation, or spec excerpt.
3. Ask for the prescribed framework issue draft.

The skill promises an exact authoritative row/tool citation but exposes no authoritative source. In a monorepo checkout it additionally directs the agent to a README that has no catalogue. A plausible but stale/nonexistent tool name or wrong capability row can send maintainers to the wrong layer, encode the wrong retrospective lesson, and leave the original SPA tooling defect unresolved.

## Bounded repair

- Correct the source map: the descriptor-backed catalogue is `re-frame2-pair/references/mcp-transport.md`, with live `tools/list` authoritative when already supplied as session evidence.
- Apply the existing “unknown over inferred” invariant to ownership: cite a tool and Tool-Pair row only when present in supplied evidence or a readable authoritative source; otherwise label ownership unverified and never invent a name.
- To retain exact, one-turn standalone drafts, optionally ship a small local ownership index containing only capability/restore-row labels and tool names, pinned by the existing descriptor/document drift machinery. If that small leaf is not worth maintaining, explicitly relax exact citation certainty for recap-only inputs instead.

## Non-goals

No live probe permission, network fetch, MCP grant, full sibling/spec vendoring, runtime/API change, generic evaluation framework, or additional filing ceremony.

## Duplicate research and history

Targeted searches of `.beads/issues.jsonl` and git history found no open issue for this runtime source-availability contradiction.

- Closed `rf2-d4h52` / commit `dff863728a` introduced the exact-citation rule and stale README pointer.
- Commit `d89385efd9` / closed `rf2-wz1qa` corrected the source pointer in `known-frictions.md` but left SKILL.md unchanged.
- Closed `rf2-lsqmp` fixed a related stale pointer only in the family README.
- Open `rf2-nvbz` concerns cross-package link spelling/gating; it cannot make an unshipped source available at runtime or define the honest fallback.
- Closed `rf2-t19ve` covers the self-contained redesign generally; this is a residual contradiction in the resulting contract.
- Closed `rf2-3cjhl` covers stale known-friction behaviors, not issue-draft source availability.

## Uncertainty

A host could choose to provide repository files or a captured `tools/list` in context, in which case exact ownership may be recoverable. The defect remains because recap-only input is explicitly supported and no such host capability is required or declared.
acceptance_criteria:
1. In an extracted/published-package replay whose recap contains no catalogue or spec excerpt, the skill produces an honest one-turn draft without inventing a shipped tool or Tool-Pair row; unavailable ownership is explicitly marked unverified.
2. With authoritative evidence supplied, a known-but-unused tool routes as tool-shaped, a used-tool/runtime gap cites the correct current Tool-Pair row, and an unknown name is not promoted to fact.
3. No shipped pair-retro instruction names `re-frame2-pair/README.md` as the tool catalogue; source guidance consistently identifies mcp-transport and the conditional authority of already-supplied live `tools/list`.
4. If a local ownership index is chosen, `npm pack --dry-run` proves it ships and a narrow drift test fails when a descriptor-backed tool name or indexed capability/restore-row label changes.
5. Existing pair-retro transcript/issue-draft checks remain green, with a new recap-only fixture covering the unavailable-evidence fallback.
close_reason:
Fixed by PR #9230 (branch worker/skretro-a).

PREMISE HELD IN FULL — every claim verified at source. npm pack --dry-run confirms the package is exactly seven files (SKILL.md, README.md, LICENSE, package.json, agents/openai.yaml, references/known-frictions.md, .claude-plugin/plugin.json): no sibling re-frame2-pair references, no spec corpus, and not even this skill's own spec/ or evals/. re-frame2-pair/README.md has zero pipe-table rows, so it carries no catalogue; check_skill_mcp_drift.py's DOC_COVERAGE_RULES pins re-frame2-pair/references/mcp-transport.md against descriptors_data.cljs, exactly as filed. SKILL.md:29 promises 'every instruction it runs on ships under its own directory', so SKILL.md:86 was a direct violation of design L7.

REPAIR: option 2, and NOT on taste. Design L7 reads 'no vendored peer copy', which locks out the local ownership index outright; independently, a vendored index would convert an honest 'unknown' into a confident STALE citation on every installed version — the precise failure the bead describes. The citation is now evidence-bound rather than mandatory: session evidence first (tools/list, error payload, pasted spec row — authoritative when present), then a repository checkout when the conversation genuinely has one (mcp-transport.md, never the README), otherwise marked unverified under the existing 'unknown over inferred' invariant and never reconstructed from memory. A third worked shape gives the unverified draft a template. Both authoring sources (spec/design.md L3, spec/authoring-prompt.md rule 6) moved in the same commit so a re-authoring pass cannot regenerate the unconditional rule. Three files, +8/-3; package membership unchanged.

AC1/AC2/AC3 met. AC4 does not apply (no index shipped).

AC5 NOT MET, AND DELIBERATELY SO — it conflicts with a lock it did not consider. spec/design.md L2 states tests/duplicate_search_test.clj 'is the skill's sole test and stays so: no session-evidence scorer is to be added', and evals/evals.json is a TRIGGER-ONLY corpus whose README says behavioural verification is manual by design and 'there is no automated scorer and none should be added'. A recap-only behavioural fixture is therefore forbidden by the skill's own locked design; a trigger-shaped one would duplicate existing positives and add nothing. The existing test stays green (5 tests, 16 assertions). Recording this plainly: the change is gated STRUCTURALLY and by prose contract only, with no behavioural execution — this repo has no eval executor, and this skill has no prompt-regression harness. If Mike wants the behavioural fixture, L2 needs unlocking first.

GATES (exit codes captured to file, run on the final rebased base): check_doc_slugs.py 0, check_skill_eval_packaging.py 0, check_skill_eval_docs.py 0, check_skill_description_budget.py 0, check_skill_mcp_drift.py 0, bb tests/duplicate_search_test.clj 0, api-manifest skills-check 0 (575 refs). check_doc_slugs.py exits 0 with an empty log, so it was proven live with a planted broken anchor: exit 1 naming SKILL.md:88, restored byte-identical per cmp, back to exit 0. mkdocs build --strict not nominated (docs_dir is docs; the hook stages only spec and migration, never skills/).

GATE FINDING, filed as rf2-7mcp: check_skill_eval_packaging.py could not have caught this. Despite the name its only subject is whether a skill's prose and its files array contradict each other about evals/ shipping. Nothing gates 'a shipped instruction may only require shipped sources'. Not fixed here — this bead's non-goals exclude a generic evaluation framework.

title: examples(routing): advertised route schema has no validator or observable effect
description:
## Finding

The canonical routing example presents its article-detail declaration as a working Malli route contract, but the app never loads the optional schemas artefact.

`examples/capabilities/routing/routing/core.cljs:49-51` declares `:params [:map [:id :string]]`; `README.md:24-28` explicitly calls out the Malli `:params` schema as a demonstrated feature. Yet the namespace requires only `re-frame.routing` and the Reagent adapter (`core.cljs:24-31`), and the `:examples/routing` build has no schema preload (`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1544-1548`). Having `schemas/src` on the compiler source path does not execute the namespace.

Routing deliberately does not require schemas: `implementation/routing/deps.edn:33-40` gives the production artefact only core, while `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:1190-1210` documents and implements `[false nil]` when no validator hook is registered. The hook is published only when `re-frame.schemas` loads (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc:93,122`). The public guide is explicit that the require itself wires the validator (`docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md:20,39-41`), and Spec 010 lines 7 and 766 say schema implies validation only after requiring that artefact; omitting it is the Malli-free posture.

This instance hides the defect especially well: path captures are already strings, and routing's schema-derived coercion treats `:string` as passthrough (`registry.cljc:635-680`), so the declaration has no observable effect and the app still works. Routing can inspect other Malli-shaped metadata for limited coercion without loading schemas; the finding is specifically that validation is absent, not that every route schema is universally inert.

## Impact

This is a canonical teaching surface for programmers and coding agents, so it demonstrates a silent half-configuration as the happy path. Copying it and changing `:string` to `:int`, an enum, constraints, or a closed map can appear to work for valid input because routing derives coercions, while malformed input remains unvalidated. The registry's schema-free tests pin the revealing behavior: `?flag=maybe` and `?n=abc` remain strings (`implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_registry_test.clj:1257-1269`); with no validator the declared boundary does not reject them. Programmatic `route-url` validation likewise no-ops (`registry.cljc:1909-1915`). That is precisely the kind of subtle API lesson an example should not teach.

## Bounded recommendation

Keep this example minimal and routing-focused: remove the unnecessary `:params [:map [:id :string]]` from article-detail and remove the README parenthetical claiming it demonstrates Malli. The path param remains a string and visible behavior is unchanged. A terse cross-link may mention that route validation requires `[re-frame.schemas]`, but do not add that artefact merely to preserve a declaration with no visible learning payoff: Spec 010's measured matched A/B cost is +39.9 KB gzip (`spec/010-Schemas.md:726-733`). If a future example intentionally teaches route validation, it should load schemas and visibly exercise valid and invalid input; that is outside this bead.

## Non-goals

No change to routing's schemas-optional packaging, late-bind soft-pass, coercion rules, validator APIs, route IDs/URLs/navigation, article data, other examples, or a new browser/test harness. Do not make routing depend on schemas or add generic schema machinery.

## History and duplicate search

The schema line dates to initial import `8c6e5a5060` (2026-05-06); routing became its own optional artefact in `c435165251` (2026-05-09); schema-implies-validation landed in `d0b95fdc54` (2026-06-01); README's Malli claim came later in `fdecf54a1fc` (2026-06-26). The declaration survived those contract shifts untouched.

Exact `rg` searches of `.beads/issues.jsonl` for this example plus schema/Malli/validation and the current `HEAD..origin/main` beads delta found no owner. Nearby but non-duplicate: `rf2-nvcp` (route-link boot failure), `rf2-ujdn0` (one-command README launcher), `rf2-g1gt` / `rf2-do50` (relative asset/deep-link hosting), and `rf2-6r9j.3` (unconsumed internal RouteAddress constant). The standalone-server history-fallback candidate was discarded because existing beads already discuss that mechanism.

## Uncertainty

No runtime was executed during this read-only review. The namespace load graph and explicit missing-hook branch are direct evidence; the recommended source/prose deletion preserves the currently observed string-param behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `routing.core` no longer presents a route schema while loading only routing (preferred: article-detail metadata retains only `:doc`), and `/articles/:id` still supplies the same string `:id` to the existing detail view.
2. The routing README no longer claims this app demonstrates or carries a Malli `:params` schema; its route-table description stays accurate.
3. If a schema note is retained, it states that loading `re-frame.schemas` is required for validation; this minimal example gains no schema dependency solely for the inert `:string` declaration.
4. `:examples/routing` compiles cleanly through the existing example compile gate. No bespoke runtime suite or scanner is introduced for this two-line teaching correction.
5. No runtime, package, coercion, or other-example behavior changes.
notes:
PR #9241 audit residual (2026-09-05): examples/capabilities/routing/routing/core.cljs:49-53 now says :params/:query schemas “only do anything” when re-frame.schemas loads. That is broader than the actual boundary. reg-route unconditionally compiles those schemas into :rf.route/params-coerce and :rf.route/query-coerce (registry.cljc:508, 526-536), and match-url applies coerce-path/coerce-query before the optional validator (968-1015, 1132-1160, 1314-1326). Existing routing tests pin :int, enum, and :boolean coercion. Only validation/enforcement is gated on the late-bound schemas hook (1190-1210). The README’s “validate only” wording is accurate. Bounded fix: change the source comment to say route schemas validate/enforce only when re-frame.schemas loads; preserve the schemas-free example and all runtime/dependency behavior. This reopens the exact owner rather than creating a duplicate.
Resolved on branch worker/exschema-a (PR #9261), commit 4ad4ac2f9e. Followed the 2026-09-05 audit note, not the description: PR #9241 had already removed the inert :params declaration and the README Malli claim, leaving only the overstated source comment.

Premise re-verified at source before editing. reg-route calls compile-schema-coercions on both :params and :query unconditionally and stores :rf.route/params-coerce / :rf.route/query-coerce; compile-schema-coercions contains no late-bind lookup. match-url applies coerce-path and coerce-query on every successful match, before validation. routing_registry_test.clj's path-param-coercion-against-params-schema pins :int and :uuid path coercion. Only validate-route-shape is gated, returning [false nil] when :schemas/validate-with-registered-fn is unregistered. So the audit note is exactly right and the comment was wrong on the coercion half.

Fix: the comment now separates the halves - coercion always happens, enforcement late-binds. Change is comment-only (proved mechanically: every added line begins with ';;'). Example stays schemas-free; no runtime, dependency, packaging or coercion behaviour changed. README left alone - its 'validate only' wording was already accurate, as the audit said.

Per acceptance criterion 4 no test was added. No automated gate covers a source comment in a .cljs file; the guide link target docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md was confirmed present by hand.
close_reason:
DONE IN THE TREE AND LEFT UNCLOSED. Found this tick by reading the RAW in_progress set against the worktree list: this bead read in_progress with no live worker and no worktree, which is the stranded shape reached from the tracker side rather than the fleet side.

Two merged PRs discharge it, both confirmed ancestors of origin/main: #9241 (merge 16b1407a06) landed the original fix, and #9261 (merge a44de668ce) landed the audit residual. The bead was never advanced past in_progress by either.

THE AUDIT RESIDUAL AND WHY IT MATTERED: after #9241, examples/capabilities/routing/routing/core.cljs said the :params/:query schemas 'only do anything' when re-frame.schemas loads. That was BROADER than the actual boundary and wrong on the coercion half. reg-route calls compile-schema-coercions on both :params and :query UNCONDITIONALLY and stores :rf.route/params-coerce / :rf.route/query-coerce; compile-schema-coercions contains no late-bind lookup; match-url applies coerce-path and coerce-query on every successful match, BEFORE validation. Only validate-route-shape is gated, returning [false nil] when :schemas/validate-with-registered-fn is unregistered. routing_registry_test.clj's path-param-coercion-against-params-schema pins :int and :uuid path coercion. So a reader was told the declared contract was wholly inert without the schemas artefact, when in fact half of it — the half that changes the value the page receives — always runs.

VERIFIED AT TIP BEFORE CLOSING rather than trusting the note: the comment now separates the halves in exactly those terms ('Coercion always happens... Enforcement is the half that late-binds'), names the concrete consequence (:id arrives as the string the URL held, because this example stays schemas-free), and links the schemas guide. Comment-only change, proved mechanically (every added line begins with ';;'); no runtime, dependency, packaging or coercion behaviour moved. The README's 'validate only' wording was already accurate and was correctly left alone.

No test was added, per the bead's own acceptance criterion 4: no automated gate covers a source comment in a .cljs file, and the guide link target docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md was confirmed present by hand. Notes carry no unmet obligation, no AUDIT-REOPEN marker and no outstanding follow-up — checked before closing, because re-closing a bead an audit reopened destroys a real finding.

title: examples(resources-ssr): client boot never acquires the route-free resource
description:
## Slice

`examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/**`, checked against the Resources/SSR implementation, Specs 011/016, the runnable Shadow build, example tests, tracker, and focused git history.

## Correctness finding

The route-free resource SSR example never causes its resource on the browser side. Its only `:rf.resource/ensure` is emitted by `:rf/server-init`, whose registration is server-only. Browser `run` creates the client frame, calls `rf.ssr/hydrate!`, and immediately renders `:app/root`; that view only dereferences the intentionally passive `[:rf/resource ...]` subscription. There is no client `ensure`/`refetch`, no live client owner, and no matching client release lifecycle.

Hydration cannot supply that missing liveness. The resource reconcile deliberately drops the baked `[:ssr request-id nav-token]` owner because it belongs to the completed server request. It computes/emits a hydration refetch plan, but does not issue those requests itself; the contract leaves issuance to a still-live route/consumer. This example explicitly has no route.

The result has three user-visible/semantic failures hidden behind one omission:

1. A client-only/no-payload load leaves the resource absent. `hydrate!` returns nil without seeding; the passive subscription projects the absent entry as `:idle`; `articles-page` falls through to an empty `<ul>`; nothing ever fetches.
2. The checked-in forever-fresh payload initially renders, but after hydration its SSR owner is removed and no client owner replaces it. The entry is not an active consumer: tag invalidation and focus/reconnect revalidation leave it stale instead of refetching, and the client ownership/GC lifecycle is never established.
3. A stale/no-data hydration disposition is only classified in `hydrate-refetch-plan`; this route-free boot never causes the load. The README nevertheless says stale/redacted/omitted entries refetch and that the client reconcile + refetch plan run end to end.

This is a teaching correctness bug, not a request for subscription-driven fetching. A programmer or AI copying the example learns that `hydrate!` plus a passive read is sufficient to acquire and keep a resource live, precisely opposite to the library's causal-command model.

## Evidence

- `examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/core.cljc:112-119` registers `:articles/list`.
- `core.cljc:136-148` is the only acquisition: server-only `:rf/server-init` dispatches `:rf.resource/ensure` under an SSR owner.
- `core.cljc:154-182` correctly says the view is passive; `core.cljc:395-413` hydrates and mounts without any client resource command while claiming an absent entry refetches.
- `README.md:99-110` claims fresh avoids a double-fetch and stale/redacted/omitted refetch; `README.md:122-125` says the refetch plan runs end to end.
- `index.html:69-90` bakes a `:loaded`, `:stale-at nil` entry with only an SSR owner. That deliberately easy fixture makes the documented run command look correct while avoiding every failing branch.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc:1-14` states subscriptions are pure passive reads; `:332-347` projects a missing entry as `:idle` with no loading/fetching signal.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc:154-163,323-327` skips hydration when no payload exists.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/ssr.cljc:1324-1431` drops SSR owners; `:1495-1503,1626-1633,2311-2319` computes the refetch plan and says a live route issues it.
- `spec/016-Resources.md:303-306` defines attach/hold/release/GC; `:1187,1197` says stale hydration refetches on mount and that the client ensure/fresh-skip re-establishes ownership; `:1597,1603-1607` conditions hydration refetch on a resource the route still needs.
- `docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:310,614,708-710` states passive reads never fetch and only active-owner entries refetch on focus/reconnect or invalidation.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1794-1804` runs this browser entrypoint against the static pre-baked page.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj:677-847` tests dynamic and checked-in fresh payload hydration. It asserts the fresh plan is empty, but never executes the browser startup with no payload/stale data, never asserts a client owner, and never proves an actual refetch after invalidation.

## History

The client acquisition omission dates to the initial example. Commit `48dd1b928e` fixed the baked payload's storage key and made it permanently fresh, then added a regression that only proves fresh hydration/no immediate refetch. Commit `cd6fd08587` moved the client mount onto the adapter handle while retaining the omission and the explicit “absent one refetches” claim. This is not a new runtime regression; the static fixture and coverage have continually selected the one branch that passes without acquisition.

## Recommended bounded repair

Keep the example route-free. After hydration and before the first client render, cause one explicit client acquisition of `:articles/list` with the same global scope/params and a named app/page owner. Give that app-minted owner a matching release path. For this example's real resource:

- a fresh hydrated entry must take `ensure`'s cache-hit/fresh-skip path, attach the client owner, and issue zero transport requests;
- an absent/no-payload or stale entry must issue exactly one request;
- later invalidation must refetch because the resource now has a live client owner.

Keep views passive. Correct the prose to distinguish “hydration reconciles/classifies” from “the live client acquisition causes work.” This resource declares no sensitive/large policy, so remove the claim that this particular route-free demo executes redacted/omitted refetch unless the implementation and test actually cause those cases; linking to the normative generic contract is enough.

## Non-goals

- Do not make subscriptions fetch.
- Do not add a route/router merely to obtain an owner; route-free is a useful minimal SSR shape.
- Do not add a general hydration orchestration API or redesign resource ownership.
- Do not add mutation, GraphQL, polling, or broad resource examples here.
- Do not turn this into a full failure-matrix exercise; cover the small startup/liveness invariant.

## Duplicate audit

All-status `rg` searches of `.beads/issues.jsonl` covered `resources_ssr`, `resources-ssr`, `client-only`, `no payload`, `passive`, `hydrate`, `owner`, `ensure`, `idle`, and `refetch`, including title combinations for hydrated owner/acquisition and SSR client fallback. No bead owns this outcome. Nearest hits are closed `rf2-6r9j.53` (projection metadata recording), closed `rf2-ujdn0` (copyable example run commands), and closed `rf2-ghxt` (a different RealWorld resources app-db schema boot defect).

## Uncertainty

This review was static by review-worker constraint: no runtime/browser/test execution. The documented runner always stages the forever-fresh payload, so the cold-load failure is masked in that command rather than visibly reproduced there. The causal absence is direct in source and contract, and the ownerless hydrated branch affects that documented fresh run after startup.

- With the actual checked-in fresh payload, startup issues zero managed-HTTP requests, preserves first-paint data/DOM adoption, removes the SSR owner, and attaches exactly the intended client owner via the fresh-skip/cache-hit path.

title: compile-node-test returns exit 0 when shadow-cljs is killed by a signal
description:
## Correctness finding

`implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs` turns a signal-killed `shadow-cljs` child into an exit-0 wrapper result. Node's ChildProcess `close` event supplies `(code, signal)` and sets `code` to `null` when a signal terminated the child. `runCapturing` currently accepts only `status` (lines 185-203), so it discards the signal. `main` correctly enters its nonzero/abnormal branch because `null !== 0`, but returns `result.status` unchanged (lines 263-268). The CLI then executes `process.exit(code)` (lines 313-315); `process.exit(null)` is success.

This contradicts the wrapper's central contract: an aborted compile must fail loudly, never hand an orchestrator a green status. The stderr and process status currently disagree: the human sees "did not complete (exit null)" while automation sees 0.

## Steps to Reproduce

A read-only process-boundary probe required the real module, replaced only `node:child_process.spawn` with an EventEmitter child that emitted `close(null, "SIGTERM")`, patched only `require.resolve` for the unused shadow runner path, and used an output path proven absent before and after. The real exported `main` and real CLI terminal operation produced:

```
compile-node-test: shadow-cljs compile signal-proof did not complete (exit null); out/codex-reviewpool-d-signal-proof-never-created.js was cleared before the attempt, not left stale.
RETURNED=null
OBSERVED_CLI_EXIT=0
```

Independent runtime controls produced `NODE_PROCESS_EXIT_NULL=0` and `NODE_PROCESS_EXIT_UNDEFINED=0`. The proof target remained absent and the worktree remained clean.

Source/history evidence:

- `runCapturing` was introduced in commit `91d7f6050b` when the wrapper moved from `spawnSync` to streaming `spawn`; that change retained the older `return result.status` branch from `01c54d87fd` but stopped carrying `spawnSync`'s `signal` field or the async close callback's second argument.
- `implementation/package.json` has five consumers of the wrapper (`test:cljs`, `test:cljs-isolation`, `test:security`, `test:testbed-support`, `test:cljs-perf-emit-nightly`). They normally chain a second command with `&&`, and because the wrapper deletes the output first, a signal before output emission will usually fail at that later command. That limits the current blast radius; it does not make this status truthful. A signal after emission can also leave a runnable output, and direct callers see the false success immediately.
- Repository census found direct compile-only usage documented in `docs/design/hicasso/defhost-ssr-provider-costing.md` and two certification records. No current CI workflow invokes the wrapper alone; current CI reaches it through the chained npm scripts.

## Impact

A developer, agent, or future gate that invokes this explicitly documented compile wrapper and checks its exit status can record a successful compile after OOM/administrative child termination, even though the wrapper itself says compilation did not complete. In chained npm lanes the missing-output defence often makes the overall command red one step later, but that gives worse feedback and is not guaranteed once an output was written. Gate status is an API to automation; contradictory red text plus exit 0 is particularly hazardous for AI/human orchestration.

## Bounded fix

Capture the `signal` argument from the ChildProcess close event and normalize every signal/`null`-status completion to a nonzero wrapper result (a stable 1 is sufficient), while naming the signal in the existing diagnostic. Preserve real numeric child exit codes. Keep output pre-deletion, warning-tally parsing, config-merge cache cleanup, streaming output, and the five package commands unchanged.

Do not build a general signal-forwarding/process-tree framework, redesign cancellation, alter shadow-cljs, or change the runner's compilation/warning policy. This is one outcome-normalization seam plus a focused regression test.

## Posture fit

The fix is a tiny honesty repair at a high-leverage tooling boundary: programmers and agents should be able to trust a command's exit code without learning Node's `null` signal convention. It improves low-friction feedback without adding API surface or speculative infrastructure.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status searches covered title/description/notes for `compile-node-test`, `exit null`, `process.exit(null)`, `terminated by signal`, `SIGTERM`, `return result.status`, `child signal`, `child-only`, `status null`, and `exit status null`; no bead owns this outcome. Closed `rf2-7r9w` is distinct: it corrected a pair-MCP consumer that treated shadow-cljs's successful compile status as an autorun TEST verdict. This finding is the wrapper converting an OS-signal/abnormal compile termination into success. Historical commit/bead citations `rf2-6t03c` and `rf2-4a6ei` created and hardened this wrapper for stale output and warning tallies; neither exists in the current tracker and neither handled the signal-null branch.

## Uncertainty

No real shadow/JVM process was killed in this review; the deterministic probe exercised the real wrapper logic with Node's documented/actual close-event shape. The canonical npm scripts normally become nonzero later when their deleted bundle is missing, and no current CI workflow was found calling the wrapper alone. The confirmed defect is the wrapper's own false exit status; how often a real child-only signal leaves the parent alive or leaves a runnable emitted bundle is environment-dependent.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add a focused process-boundary or equivalently faithful contract test in the existing compile-wrapper test surface: a child outcome `(code=null, signal=SIGTERM)` makes the CLI exit nonzero and the diagnostic names SIGTERM or clearly says signal termination. The test must fail against the current implementation by observing exit 0.
- Preserve ordinary outcome mapping: a numeric child exit 0 continues into output/tally validation, and representative nonzero numeric statuses remain nonzero rather than being collapsed to success.
- Preserve output pre-deletion, config-merge cache cleanup before and after the child, streamed stdout/stderr, missing-output rejection, and warning-tally rejection.
- The existing compile-node-test warning parser/self-tests and implementation JS harness tests pass.
- No general process supervisor, new public option, environment waiver, or package-script redesign is introduced.
close_reason:
MERGED as PR #9266 (mayor fast-forwarded to 0c87128ac0; five clauses met, 87/87, 0 non-terminal, 0 live runs, 0 job keys added since merge base).

PREMISE HELD EXACTLY, and the mechanism was measured rather than reasoned: child.on('close', (status) => ...) dropped the signal, and 'return result.status' handed NULL to process.exit(). Measured on this box: node -e 'process.exit(null)' exits 0, and a real child.kill('SIGTERM') really does yield close(null, 'SIGTERM'). So a signal-killed shadow-cljs build reported SUCCESS. That invalidates every green that runner produced under a kill.

THE FIX: numeric status passes through untouched, non-numeric normalises to a stable 1, and the diagnostic names the signal.

THE CONTROL IS THE DELIVERABLE HERE AND IT WAS BUILT PROPERLY. The new _compile-node-test-signal.test.cjs runs the real CLI as its own process and kills a REAL child with a REAL signal — only WHICH PROGRAM the child runs is substituted, via a --require preload. Four arms with their expected exit stated per arm, which is the discipline a refusing gate needs because non-zero is its NORMAL case: signal -> 1; the same stand-in with the kill DELETED -> 0; child exit 3 -> 3; clean exit with no bundle -> 1. Against the pre-fix file the suite captured exit 1 and ONLY the signal arm failed, the three control arms staying green — so the redness is the signal rather than the harness. That second arm is the mechanical hollow-gate test (delete the signal, keep the fault) and it passed. Restore verified by SHA-256.

title: Make reply work-id descriptor metadata fail closed
description:
## Finding

`every-work-id-is-a-comparable-edn-tuple` says every family descriptor supplies `:work-head` and that missing identity metadata fails explicitly, but its comprehension uses `:when (and builder work-head)`. A missing or accidentally renamed `:work-head` therefore removes every supported situation for that family from the work-id gate. The explicit `wid` presence, vector, expected-head, and EDN round-trip assertions never execute.

## Evidence

- `implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:489-505` contains the fail-closed claim and the `work-head` skip.
- All six current descriptors at lines 315-421 carry `:work-head`; it is not an optional field. The only legitimate filter is the situation builder, because `:error`/`:cancel` can be unsupported.
- `:work-head` has no other executable consumer in the repository. Removing it from a descriptor leaves the other vocabulary/status tests green; this work-id test silently omits that family's rows.
- History confirms the mismatch is accidental residue. Commit `55c28a5558` removed the old `wid` skip specifically to make the gate fail closed and stated every descriptor has a non-nil `:work-head`, but retained the older `work-head` guard. Later commit `5806d23efe` simplified the comment to “Missing ids fail explicitly” without changing the guard.
- The current JVM tier is healthy (`clojure -M:test`: 27 tests, 533 assertions), so this is a mutation false-green rather than an existing runtime failure.

## Impact

A future family-row edit can drop or misspell the expected work-id head and silently lose the tuple/head/EDN checks for that family. That defeats the cross-family conformance tier at exactly the metadata boundary it claims to lock.

## Recommendation

Filter only on `builder`. Assert that `work-head` is present before comparing it to `(first wid)`, or validate required descriptor metadata once for every family and then run the situation matrix. Add a mutation/non-vacuity control demonstrating that a descriptor without `:work-head` makes the gate red.

## Risks and contracts

Preserve optional situation builders: route and timer legitimately omit some error/cancel paths. Do not make `:error` or `:cancel` universal. This change is test-only and must not alter reply builders or the public reply vocabulary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every descriptor with a supported situation is exercised even when `:work-head` is nil or absent.
2. Missing `:work-head` produces an explicit, family-labelled failure rather than zero assertions.
3. Existing work-id presence, vector, head, and EDN-round-trip checks remain for all current supported family/situation rows.
4. A focused mutation/control proves deleting one descriptor's `:work-head` makes the suite fail.
5. Both JVM and consolidated CLJS reply-conformance lanes remain green after restoring the real matrix.
close_reason:
PR #9095 (head e99777468d). Premise HELD and was measured before the fix: deleting :work-head from the :http descriptor left the reply-conformance suite GREEN at exit 0 with 517 assertions instead of 533 — 16 assertions silently skipped by the ':when (and builder work-head)' filter, nothing on screen.

Fixed test-only, in implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc. The filter is now the situation builder ALONE (:error / :cancel stay legitimately optional for route and timer); a new family-level assertion requires :work-head to be a keyword; and work-id-head-matches? is a SHARED predicate the primary gate asserts TRUE and the new control work-id-gate-fails-closed-on-missing-descriptor-metadata asserts FALSE, so weakening it reddens one side or the other. work-id-rows makes the row set an explicit value, and the control pins that deleting :work-head does NOT reduce the visited row count — the silent-skip axis, which the value-only check would have missed.

Criterion 4 proved by mutation AFTER the fix: the same :work-head deletion now exits 1 with 556 assertions still running (five failures, family-labelled), where before it exited 0 with 16 fewer. Acceptance criteria 1-4 met; 5 (JVM lane) green at 30 tests / 556 assertions, up from 27 / 533. The CLJS lane was not run locally (no implementation/node_modules in the worker checkout) — the change is portable .cljc and CI owns that lane.

THE RULING. Option (b), in its narrow form. The React Fiber-walker is NOT the primary runtime view-hierarchy capture path and does not return; the 2026-05-19 lock is superseded. What a React-backed port owes is exactly what 006 section View tagging contract already requires and every shipped adapter already does: the dev-mode data-rf-view tag (and its sibling data-rf2-source-coord) on each registered view's rendered root, elision-gated, mutate-not-wrap. That tagging stays a MUST because it has live consumers today: forward index by id (Xray hover-highlight in panels/reactive_panel_view.cljs:245-262 and panels/epoch/view.cljs:1820-1840; Pair ui/read view-element at skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:2598-2606) and reverse index by nearest tagged ancestor (Pair nearest-view-root, runtime.cljs:2609-2619, the one live instance of the DOM-containment rule). HIERARCHY capture, a walk that produces a parent/children tree, becomes tool-owned and OPTIONAL: no port owes a walker, no React-version smoke is a MUST, no conformance surface grades it, and the reference ships no walker because no reference tool consumes one (the Views panel is a flow graph whose design never names a parent).
