title: conformance EDN gate accepts mismatched delimiter types because it tracks only aggregate depth
description:
DISCOVERED while fixing rf2-5mr6 (PR: spec/conformance/fixtures/routing-not-found.edn had one extra closing brace).

GAP. No gate in the tree checks that a conformance fixture is a well-formed EDN file containing exactly ONE top-level form. Both loaders use clojure.edn/read-string over the whole file, which returns the FIRST form and IGNORES everything after it. A fixture whose expectation block is closed early therefore loads, runs, and reports as PASSING while the assertions that fell outside the block are silently discarded. That is exactly what rf2-5mr6 was: bracket depth -1, two trace assertions never executed, green for however long it had been there (introducing commit not bisected).

WHY IT WAS NOT ADDED IN THAT PR. No script under scripts/ or .github/ iterates spec/conformance/fixtures/ at all — check_retired_spellings.py and report-changed-surfaces.sh only NAME the directory. So the check has no existing home; it is a new script plus its own CI wiring plus a fast-PR spine entry, which is a bigger call than the one-character fix it would have guarded.

TWO SHAPES, AND THE SECOND IS THE SHARPER ONE.

(a) A corpus scanner. Python, stdlib only, in the shape of the repo's other spec-coherence gates. The scanner used to measure rf2-5mr6 works and is the algorithm to lift: walk the text, blank ;; comments to end of line, treat a double-quoted string as opaque (honouring backslash escapes), treat a backslash as introducing a one-character char literal, then count ([{ against )]}. Report a defect when final depth is not 0, when min depth ever goes negative, or when the file holds other than exactly one top-level form. Measured 2026-09-03: 247 fixtures scanned, 0 defects after the fix; the pre-fix routing-not-found.edn reports final-depth=-1 top-level-forms=1 neg-at-line=60. Exercised in BOTH directions before either result was believed.

(b) Make the LOADERS refuse trailing text. This is the better fix because it cannot drift from what the runner actually parses, and it is a few lines in each of the two host-specific loaders: implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_fixtures.clj (load-fixture-from-file) and the JVM leaf's slurp + read-string in implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj. Read with a PushbackReader and assert EOF after the first form, or read (str "[" content "]") and assert exactly one element. A fixture with trailing text then fails LOUD at load, in the same run that would otherwise pass it, on every host that loads the corpus. The CLJS leaf inlines fixtures at compile time, so it needs the equivalent at its macro seam.

Prefer (b), or (b) plus (a) — (a) also catches a fixture that never reaches a loader because its capabilities are unclaimed, which (b) cannot see. A fixture whose capabilities are out of claim is SKIPPED by the runner, so a defect in one is invisible to (b) forever.

ACCEPTANCE. A fixture with a deliberately misplaced brace fails a gate that runs on every PR touching spec/conformance/. Prove it by planting one and showing the red, not by showing the green on a clean corpus — a search that returns zero is not a check that passed.
notes:
AUDIT OF PR #9038 (three-lens review).

CORRECTNESS. The scanner records only one aggregate depth for all three delimiter kinds, so mismatched pairs can cancel out. Measured at merge commit 46387ffee9: scan_edn("{:a [1 2)}") returns ok=True, final-depth=0, min-depth=0, top-level-forms=1, and _defect_reason returns None, even though this is not valid EDN. The unconditional gate therefore gives a false green against its stated invariant that every fixture is one well-formed EDN form.

COMPLETENESS. The self-test exercises extra, missing, and trailing delimiters, but no mismatched pair, so it cannot discriminate this failure mode. The package-reference half of the PR is complete against rf2-kgw8z: it scopes by resolved location and covers unshipped, shipped, marked, and genuinely external parent links.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / MINIMAL FIX. Keep the stdlib-only lexical design; replace aggregate-only closing with a tiny opener stack and require each closer to match the top opener. Add one compact regression such as {:a [1 2)}. No general EDN parser or broader semantic validation is needed.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9046 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9046). The audit's finding reproduced exactly at base 1b64fd6396: scan_edn('{:a [1 2)}') returned ok=True, final-depth=0 min-depth=0 top-level-forms=1, _defect_reason None. scan_edn now keeps an opener stack of (char, line) and requires each closer to match the delimiter it closes; still stdlib-only and lexical, no EDN parser. Self-test gained two regressions whose aggregate numbers are IDENTICAL to a clean file's (final-depth=0 min-depth=0 top-level-forms=1), so only an opener stack discriminates them, and both assert the REASON not just a defect count: 12/12 exit 0, and exit 1 with 4 named failures when the mismatch rule is disabled. Proved on live data rather than on a clean corpus: a cancelling mismatch planted in spec/conformance/fixtures/routing-not-found.edn gives the pre-fix scanner exit 0 (the false green) and this one exit 1 naming file, closer, opener and line. Plant restored, verified by git hash-object blob equality 7200be9e6536eb9a61dc79c34990ee08d1f28478. Corpus counts unchanged either side of the change: 247 fixtures, 0 defects, exit 0. Two notes: the gate is confirmed unconditional AND enforced (continue-on-error steps are aggregated by test.yml's 'Report every failing invariant check', which exits 1 on any outcome=='failure'), and this bead's recorded top-level-forms=1 for the pre-fix fixture measures as 2 with the committed scanner (final-depth=-1 and neg-at-line=60 match exactly; the verdict is driven by the negative depth, so nothing turns on it).

title: CLAUDE.md Build&Test states a false gate model: mkdocs --strict DOES cover spec/ (docs.yml stages it into docs/), and it catches link-resolution failures check_doc_slugs passes
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 by the specdrift-a worker (PR #9019) and confirmed by the mayor at source in mkdocs.yml.

WHAT CLAUDE.md SAYS, under Build & Test: that mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs is the authority on what the build cannot see from WITHIN docs_dir, and that 'docs_dir is docs, so anything outside it -- implementation/**, examples/**, tools/**, .github/**, repo-root markdown -- was never a candidate for exclusion and will never appear in that block.' A reader takes from this that spec/ is outside the strict build's reach.

WHAT IS TRUE AT TIP: the docs.yml CI step COPIES spec/ into docs/spec/, so the spec tree is STAGED INTO docs_dir and the strict build does see it. docs_dir: docs is true but not dispositive.

THE MEASUREMENT, on one tree, which is the part that makes this a defect rather than a wording quibble: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 ('no broken links') while mkdocs build --strict exit 1 on the SAME tree, naming spec/conformance/README.md's link to ../../docs/EP/EP-0012-....md as unresolvable. The link is CORRECT repo-relative -- which is what the slug gate validates and what GitHub browsing needs -- and wrong site-relative, because from staged docs/spec/conformance/ it resolves to docs/docs/EP/. mkdocs_hooks.py rewrites ../../spec/ -> ../spec/ for exactly this class but has NO ../../docs/ rule, so a page under spec/ cannot reach docs/ by a relative path at all.

THE TWO GATES ARE COMPLEMENTARY, NOT REDUNDANT, and CLAUDE.md should say so: check_doc_slugs.py validates ANCHORS (which strict grades at INFO and therefore never fails on) and repo-relative targets; mkdocs --strict validates LINK RESOLUTION INSIDE THE BUILT SITE, which the slug gate cannot see. Each is blind to the other's subject.

WHY IT MATTERS: the mayor nominated gates from this model in roughly a dozen briefs this session, telling workers editing spec/ that the strict build was not their gate. Nobody was harmed -- the doc gates ran in CI regardless -- but the nomination was wrong, and a worker acting on it would hand-verify what a gate already proved or trust a green that inspected nothing.

FIX SHAPE. Correct the Build & Test paragraph so it states: (1) docs.yml stages spec/ into docs/, so the strict build covers spec/ despite docs_dir being docs; (2) the two gates check different things -- anchors and repo-relative targets vs site-relative link resolution -- and neither substitutes for the other; (3) a page under spec/ cannot reach docs/ by a relative path, because mkdocs_hooks.py has no ../../docs/ rewrite rule. Keep the existing true parts: exclude_docs, the fence blindness both gates share, and the check_readme_links roster split.

DO NOT edit CLAUDE.md from the mayor checkout -- the commit guard refuses it. Dispatch to a worker in its own worktree.

PREMISES ARE CLAIMS: re-read mkdocs.yml, docs.yml and mkdocs_hooks.py at tip before writing, and reproduce the two-gate pairing rather than quoting this bead.
notes:
MAYOR ADDENDUM, 2026-09-03 00:5x AUSEST — A SECOND HALF OF THE GATE MODEL, MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY BY TWO WORKERS AFTER THIS BEAD WAS FILED, AND THE BEAD IS INCOMPLETE WITHOUT IT.

This bead currently says 'mkdocs --strict DOES cover spec/'. True of CI, and MISLEADING AS A LOCAL GATE INSTRUCTION — which is exactly how a worker will read it, because a gate nomination is a thing you run. A BARE LOCAL 'mkdocs build --strict' DOES NOT COVER spec/ AT ALL. The coverage comes entirely from docs.yml's staging step copying spec/ into docs/spec/ BEFORE the build; run the build without replicating that staging and it inspects none of your spec/ edits and exits 0, which is a green that proves nothing.

MEASURED TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY, BY WORKERS WHO DID NOT SHARE A CONTEXT. corpus-b (PR #9026) reported it in those words and replicated the staging so its strict run genuinely covered both edited paths. specdrift-b (PR #9025) reported 'mkdocs build --strict 0, AFTER staging spec/ -> docs/spec as docs.yml does — it built spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md'. Two workers, two trees, same finding, neither prompted for it.

SO THE CORRECTED PARAGRAPH NEEDS A FOURTH POINT alongside the three in FIX SHAPE: (4) the strict build reaches spec/ only through docs.yml's staging step, so CI covers it and a bare local run does not — a local run must replicate the staging (copy spec/ into docs/spec/, and migration/ into docs/migration/) or be cited as CI rather than as a local pass. Say it in the same breath as (1), because (1) alone is the sentence that misleads.

THIS ALSO CORRECTS MY OWN BRIEFS AGAIN, in the opposite direction from the first correction. I spent a dozen briefs telling workers the strict build was not their gate for spec/. Then I spent several telling them it was — without the staging caveat. The second error is smaller than the first but it is the same class: a gate nomination stated without the condition that makes it true.

title: Xray Trace drops every real FX argument by reading nonexistent singular tags
description:
## Scope

Repair the Dynamic Trace panel's FX target/detail projection in tools/xray. Scope is the raw-trace-to-row seam in day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.trace-helpers and its focused dual-target test. Reconcile the fixture with the framework's shipped FX vocabulary; do not redesign the panel.

## Findings

Correctness finding: target-detail reads :rf.fx/arg and :rf.fx/value, but the framework emits FX arguments under canonical :rf.fx/args. Every real :rf.fx/handled row therefore projects only its fx id, dropping the argument from the main target/detail column and hover title. The existing test is green because it fabricates the nonexistent singular :rf.fx/arg key.

## Evidence

- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers.cljc:575-579 reads :rf.fx/arg / :rf.fx/value.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:1234-1239 emits successful :rf.fx/handled rows with :rf.fx/id and :rf.fx/args. Exception, skipped-platform, and no-such-fx rows use the same plural key at lines 1455-1463, 1583-1601, 1617-1626, and 1651-1660.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/trace_collector.cljs:207-228 snapshots framework rings without renaming tag keys.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers.cljc:853-884 writes target-detail directly to :target; tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace.cljs:632-639 renders it in the target/detail column and hover title.
- tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:305-309 asserts the promised output using :rf.fx/arg, a shape no framework producer emits.
- tools/xray/spec/023-Trace-Panel.md:45-51 and line 264 promise fx-id -> arg in that column.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register :app/audit and return {:app/audit {:message "saved"}} from an event handler.
2. Dispatch the event and open Xray's Dynamic Trace panel on that event bundle.
3. Inspect the :rf.fx/handled row. The framework trace carries {:rf.fx/id :app/audit, :rf.fx/args {:message "saved"}}, but the target/detail cell and hover title show only :app/audit.

## Failure scenario / invariant

The payload distinguishing one effect invocation from another is absent from the primary diagnostic unless the operator expands raw EDN. When an FX trace row contains canonical :rf.fx/args, projected :target must include that exact value after pr-str-safe; when the key is absent, the row stays id-only. Key presence, not truthiness, is the distinction because false and nil are valid effect arguments.

## Recommended Action

Make the FX branch read canonical :rf.fx/args and distinguish an absent key from present false/nil with contains? or an equivalent sentinel. Replace the singular-key fixture with producer-shaped tags. Keep the id-only fallback for rows that genuinely omit arguments.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A focused test passes a producer-shaped :rf.fx/handled event with {:rf.fx/id :app/audit, :rf.fx/args {:message "saved"}} through target-detail or project-row and asserts :app/audit -> {:message "saved"}. The fixture explicitly contains neither singular key; this non-vacuity check fails on the current implementation.
2. The same table proves present false and present nil render as -> false and -> nil, while a control row with no :rf.fx/args renders only :app/audit. This pins key presence rather than a truthiness shortcut.
3. No production Xray code or focused test relies on the nonexistent singular FX argument tags.
4. From tools/xray, clojure -M:test -n day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.trace-helpers-cljs-test passes, and the CLJS node-test lane containing the same .cljc namespace passes.

## Non-goals

- No Trace layout, expansion, filtering, stage, or colour changes.
- No framework trace-schema change and no compatibility aliases for invented singular keys.
- No broad audit of other op families or historical fixture cleanup.
- No work on the separate Xray runtime retirement tracked by rf2-7htk7.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title searches for effect args, fx args, trace panel, target detail, target/detail, rf.fx, and effect detail found no owner. All-status description and notes searches for :rf.fx/args, :rf.fx/arg, target/detail, effect argument, fx argument, Trace panel, trace_helpers, and trace helpers also found no issue. Open rf2-tq26u concerns interceptor registration coordinates on exception traces, not FX argument projection. Open rf2-7htk7 retires the unused Xray agent runtime; it explicitly does not own the human Trace panel.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A producer-shaped :rf.fx/handled event carrying only :rf.fx/id and canonical :rf.fx/args projects the documented fx-id -> arg target; the assertion is red on the current singular-key reader.
2. Present false and nil arguments remain visible, while an absent :rf.fx/args control stays id-only.
3. Singular :rf.fx/arg / :rf.fx/value fixtures and production reads are absent from the focused Xray trace surface.
4. The focused JVM namespace and its CLJS node-test lane pass.

[2026-09-01 11:47:40 AUSEST] FIXED — PR #8852 (commit 8f2dd8ecca, rebased to trunk f902e800cc).

All four premises verified at tip before acting: trace_helpers.cljc read the singular :rf.fx/arg / :rf.fx/value; re-frame.fx emits the canonical plural :rf.fx/args on handled, exception, skipped-on-platform and no-such-fx rows alike (7 occurrences); the existing fixture fabricated the singular key; spec/023 promised fx-id -> arg.

FIX: the FX branch reads :rf.fx/args through the namespace's EXISTING tags-absent sentinel, so presence is decided by KEY PRESENCE, not truthiness — present false and present nil stay visible, and only a genuinely absent key falls back to the id-only form. implementation/** was read as evidence only, never edited; no compatibility alias for the invented singular keys.

NON-VACUITY (acceptance 1): the new producer-shaped fixture — containing NEITHER singular key — was driven RED FIRST against the unmodified reader: exit 1, 4 failures, each projecting the id alone (expected ':app/audit -> {:message "saved"}', actual ':app/audit'; likewise :app/toggle, :app/clear, :http-xhrio). Those four assertions account exactly for the suite's 6206 -> 6210 growth, and the red doubles as proof the gate read this worktree.

Acceptance 2: present false -> '-> false', present nil -> '-> nil', absent-key control -> id-only. Acceptance 3 (census): no production Xray code or focused test reads the singular tags; the same-shape control (:rf.fx/args) found 7 files, so the pattern machinery is sound. Acceptance 4: focused namespace exit 0 — 51 tests / 337 assertions / 0 failures; full Xray JVM suite exit 0 — 1312 / 6210 / 0. The CLJS node-test lane carrying the same .cljc namespace is CI's.

SPEC: spec/023 section 3 now names the canonical :rf.fx/args tag and the false/nil key-presence semantics — the promise it already made became true with the fix, but it was SILENT on which key backed it, which is the gap that let the singular read stand unchallenged. Non-goals honoured: no layout/expansion/filtering/stage/colour change, no framework trace-schema change, no broad fixture audit, no rf2-7htk7 drift.

Focused namespace 51/337/0 and full Xray JVM suite 1312/6210/0, both exit 0 on the final rebased base; spec/023 aligned.

title: surface-review(core): make destroy-frame! release generation-pool provenance
description:
## Scope

Correct the lifecycle ownership of generation provenance in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc` and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc`, with focused cross-host tests in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/**`. Update the nearby lifecycle/provenance commentary or `spec/002-Frames.md` only where needed to keep the teardown contract accurate. The public API stays `make-frame` + `destroy-frame!`.

## Correctness finding

Every successful public `rf/make-frame` writes an entry to the process-global `frame-generation-pool`, including ordinary one-arity frames whose value is `nil` (meaning the live source store). `destroy-frame!` removes the live frame and releases many other frame-keyed side tables, but never removes this entry. Destroying N never-reused frame ids therefore leaves N permanent keys; the two-arity constructor can additionally keep the caller's explicit descriptor pool reachable.

This violates the documented invariant that transient frame-scoped state is released at the single normative teardown boundary. The source comment classifies the residue as harmless "dev-process memory", but the write is unconditional in the public constructor and is exercised by server request lifecycles.

## Steps to Reproduce

From `implementation/core`, run:

```clojure
clojure -M -e "(require '[re-frame.core :as rf] '[re-frame.frame :as frame] '[re-frame.live-frame :as lf] '[re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as pa]) (rf/init! pa/adapter) (let [pool (var-get (ns-resolve 're-frame.live-frame 'frame-generation-pool)) baseline (count @pool) fs (vec (repeatedly 100 #(rf/make-frame {}))) after-create (count @pool)] (doseq [f fs] (rf/destroy-frame! f)) (println {:baseline baseline :after-create after-create :after-destroy (count @pool) :registered-frames (count (frame/frame-ids))}))"
```

Current-main exit 0 output is:

```clojure
{:baseline 0, :after-create 100, :after-destroy 100, :registered-frames 0}
```

The control proves the table acquired 100 rows; the terminal state proves all 100 frame records were destroyed while all 100 provenance rows remained.

## Evidence

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc:592-603` explicitly accepts a residual entry for every destroyed-and-never-reused id and calls it dev-process memory.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc:680-706` defines `frame-generation-pool` and records `runnable-id -> descriptors`; `nil` is a real recorded value for the normal live-store path.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc:989-998` performs that write for every successful `make-frame` before the frame engine commit, while preserving failure rollback.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc:1201-1219` reads the row during reprojection, establishing that the row is needed only while that frame is live.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:4267-4307` documents the destroy cleanup hooks; the corresponding calls at lines 4522-4619 precede `dissoc-frame!` at line 4668, but there is no live-frame provenance cleanup.
- `spec/002-Frames.md:603-608` says transient frame-scoped state is torn down on `destroy-frame!`; lines 705-711 make it the single teardown path and require every feature's frame-scoped state to hang cleanup there.
- `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:269-275,278-290,353-358` documents that teardown prevents a leak per request, creates a fresh gensym frame id, calls `rf/make-frame`, and destroys it in `finally`. `examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/core.cljc:245-250,271-276,352-353` has the same lifecycle.
- `rg -n "frame-generation-pool" implementation/core/src implementation/core/test` finds the production table only in `live_frame.cljc`; existing tests cover provenance selection, failure rollback, and construction contention, not successful destroy cleanup.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A long-lived JVM SSR service follows the documented per-request recipe: mint a unique id, construct a frame, render, and destroy in `finally`. The live frame registry returns to baseline after each request, but `frame-generation-pool` grows linearly with total requests served. The common path retains at least one unique keyword/map row per request; callers using distinct explicit descriptor snapshots can keep those larger object graphs reachable too. Tests, stories, and `with-new-frame` churn have the same process-lifetime accumulation.

Invariant: after a successful destruction, no frame-scoped generation-provenance row for that exact dead incarnation remains. An exact-value stale destroy must still be a no-op against a same-id successor and must not remove the successor's provenance.

## Recommended minimal fix

Keep provenance in its current private side table and add the missing symmetric teardown:

1. In `live_frame.cljc`, define a private idempotent cleanup function that `dissoc`s the destroyed frame id from `frame-generation-pool`, and publish it through `re-frame.late-bind` (for example `:live-frame/on-frame-destroyed!`).
2. In `frame/destroy-frame!`, invoke that hook through the existing `safe-call-hook!` cleanup path before `dissoc-frame!`.
3. Update the destroy recipe/comment and replace the accepted-residue claim with the lifecycle invariant.

No incarnation token is required at that point: destruction still holds the per-id reservation, and a same-id successor cannot be seated until the later registry dissoc. A stale exact-value destroy that does not own the live incarnation already exits before the cleanup walk.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused CLJC lifecycle test captures the private provenance table baseline, creates a uniquely named ordinary one-arity frame, proves its id is present while live (non-vacuity), destroys it through the public API, and proves both the frame record and provenance row are absent.
- A two-arity control uses distinct explicit descriptor-pool objects for same-id incarnations A and B: A's live row is its exact pool; destroying A removes it; constructing B installs B's pool; a later stale `destroy-frame! A` leaves B live and B's row intact; destroying B removes the row.
- A churn test creates at least 100 fresh anonymous/public frames before destroying them, proves the table grew by exactly that live set, destroys every returned frame value, and proves the table equals its captured baseline rather than merely checking a selected key.
- The focused tests execute on both the JVM and Node/CLJS lanes that exercise `live_frame.cljc` / frame teardown.
- Existing generation-provenance controls remain green: failed first construction leaves no row, failed re-construction restores the prior row, explicit-pool reprojection uses the original pool, and same-id construction contention cannot clobber a winner.
- The destroy recipe names the new cleanup and no source comment describes destroyed-frame provenance residue as harmless or dev-only.
- Negative control: disabling the new hook (or its registration/call site) makes the ordinary-row, explicit-pool, and churn assertions fail while their pre-destroy presence controls still pass.

## Non-goals

- No weak references, TTL/reaper, periodic sweep, global reset API, or SSR-specific cleanup call.
- No public provenance accessor and no new public lifecycle verb.
- No change to image selection, generation sealing, hot-reload/reprojection semantics, construction reservations, or failed-construction rollback.
- No redesign that moves provenance into the sealed generation/frame schema unless the minimal late-bound teardown proves impossible.
- No changes to per-request id policy, SSR payloads, Hicasso state, routing/resources/HTTP teardown, or unrelated process-global caches.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched the full bead corpus, including closed issues, with `bd search` for "generation pool", "generation", "descriptor pool", "make-frame", "destroy frame", "SSR leak", and "provenance"; and `bd list --all --desc-contains` / `--notes-contains` for "frame-generation-pool", "generation pool", "generation provenance", "residual entry", "no destroy-time cleanup", "explicit descriptor pool", "per-request frame", "destroy-frame!", and "live-frame". No issue owns this core table or invariant. The only related material issue is closed `rf2-uejlj`, which fixed the analogous Hicasso `!frame-ops` per-request retention by adding its own destroy hook; it neither mentions nor clears `frame-generation-pool`. The sole in-progress bead at filing time, `rf2-jui1c`, is an unrelated P3 prose sweep and remains locked.
notes:
VERDICT (rf2-cq0yi) — PR #8887, head 14e649a7ca8b23e9a8643aba28695f16d581e3f4, ready for review.

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE. The bead reproduction runs verbatim on trunk 24b33a618a at exit 0 and prints exactly the recorded output: {:baseline 0, :after-create 100, :after-destroy 100, :registered-frames 0}. Line deltas are negligible: the live_frame.cljc residue comment cited 592-603, actual 594-603; the defonce cited 680-706, actual starts 677 (record fn 698-706); write site 989-998 exact; reader 1201-1219 exact; frame.cljc 4267-4307 hook doc exact, 4522-4619 hook calls and dissoc-frame! 4668 all exact; spec/002-Frames.md 603-608 and 705-711 exact.

WHO READS THE POOL. One production reader: live-frame/reproject-live-frame!, which reads the row only inside (when-let [old-generation (frame/frame-generation frame-id)]) — a destroyed frame carries no generation, so the read never happens for one. Nothing consults the table for a destroyed frame. Repo-wide grep finds the production table only in live_frame.cljc; every other hit is a test. So no reader needs post-teardown access, and a plain keyed dissoc at teardown is the right shape rather than a compromise.

ARE THE NIL-VALUED ONE-ARITY ENTRIES A DISTINCT CASE. Informationally yes, mechanically no. To the only READER they are identical to absence: (get pool id) returns nil for a live ordinary frame and for a frame that never existed, so releasing them changes no reader answer — that is the safety argument for the release, and it applies to the explicit-pool rows too, since a destroyed frame is never reprojected either way. But they are NOT identical to record-frame-generation-pool!, which distinguishes had-row? from absent so restore-frame-generation-pool! can undo exactly (its docstring says so: nil is a legitimate recorded pool, so an absent row cannot be spelled by assoc-ing nil). The one place that distinction could have become observable post-release is a failed re-construction on a previously-destroyed id: pre-fix the rollback restored a present nil row, post-fix it dissocs. Both leave every reader seeing nil, so behaviour is unchanged. Conclusion: they did not warrant a narrower first cut — one unconditional release covers both cases with no asymmetry to explain.

THE REPAIR. live-frame/release-frame-generation-pool! (private, idempotent dissoc), published as :live-frame/on-frame-destroyed! from install-reprojection! — the same make-frame-rooted once-body that installs the other two :live-frame/* keys — and invoked from the destroy-frame! step-6 auxiliary-cleanup pass, after :hicasso/on-frame-destroyed!. Late-bind because live-frame requires frame (a back-require would invert the load order). Publishing from that once-body is what makes the timing airtight: make-frame calls ensure-reprojection-installed! at line 852 and writes its first row at 993, so the hook is bound before any row can exist, and a bundle that never constructs a frame roots neither (the elision DCE contract is preserved). Keyed and unconditional, no incarnation token: destroy still owns the id reservation at hook time and a same-id successor is seatable only after the step-9 dissoc, so every row standing there is the dying incarnation. A stale exact-value destroy fails claim-frame-destroy! before the cleanup walk. Plus a late_bind/directory.cljc entry, the accepted-residue comment replaced with the lifecycle invariant (its CORRECTNESS reasoning still holds and is kept; what it got wrong was retention), and the install-reprojection! arity prose brought in step.

SPEC/002-FRAMES.MD: TAKEN, and declared in the PR body. One clause in the normative Destroy step-6 ordered list, which carries "The ordering is pattern contract — a conformant port MUST mirror it", so adding a hook to that pass without listing it leaves the spec understating the recipe. Everything else fits in-tree and was written there instead. It serialises the fleet against that file while #8887 is open.

CONTROL, AND WHY IT IS NOT VACUOUS. New cross-host implementation/core/test/re_frame/frame_destroy_generation_provenance_cljs_test.cljc (.cljc ending -cljs-test, so it rides clojure -M:test via -test$ AND npm run test:cljs via cljs-test$). Every case asserts PRESENCE before absence: the ordinary case proves the row was written while the frame was live, the explicit-pool case proves A row is A exact pool by identical? and B row is B exact pool, and the churn case pins the table cardinality in BOTH directions (grew by exactly 100, returned to exactly the captured baseline) rather than probing a selected key. contains? is the presence probe throughout, never get — load-bearing, because an ordinary frame recorded pool IS nil, so get cannot separate a live ordinary row from no row at all. A fourth case pins that the hook is published at all, so a never-registered release cannot present as a broken one.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, RUN ON BOTH ARMS FROM THE SAME PLANT (call site commented out; match count checked as 1 before running; blob hash 296c1893 -> e1673701 on the JVM plant and -> a4ceb908 on the CLJS one, so neither plant no-opped). JVM captured exit 1: 4 tests, 18 assertions, 4 failures. CLJS captured exit 1: 4 failures, all in this file. The same four source lines on both arms — 135, 160, 174, 198 — with the other 14 assertions still green, so the reds are a missing release and not a make-frame that stopped recording. Test and assertion totals identical to the green runs, so no namespace was skipped. The CLJS red is also the positive evidence that the .cljc really executes on the node lane and that its white-box read of the private table compiles there. Restored and verified by git blob hash against the committed object each time, never by reading a diff.

FINDING NOT ASKED FOR, AND THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE. make_frame_generation_pool_window_jvm_test (rf2-rt4jz) used the leak as a SETUP STEP: it asserted as a control that a destroyed id row still names pool V1, and the fix made that false. The first repair restated that control to pin the release instead, arguing that an ABSENT row would redden the reproduction just as hard (nil reads as the live source store, which zero-matches that frame explicit include-ns composition). That argument is WRONG, and only a sabotage run found it: reverting the rf2-rt4jz ordering left the case at 0 failures, because the zero-match is swallowed by the RESILIENT flush, so the constructor generation survives and the pin goes silent exactly where it exists to shout. A restatement that reads perfectly had removed a regression pin teeth. The other candidate was measured and also fails to reproduce: a same-id RE-construction over a LIVE frame does leave a genuine previous-pool row, but :initial-events fires only on FIRST construction, so nothing resolves inside upsert-frame! and the window never opens (app-db stays empty). So the pairing the reproduction needs — a destroyed id, making the next construction a first one that runs the setup cascade, CARRYING a previous incarnation row — no longer arises on its own, and the row is now planted explicitly, in a namespace that is white-box by construction (it already reads the private provenance table and the private dirty flag directly) and says so. Verified in both directions with the same plant (a1f1c342 -> 0655bab5): 2 failures under the pre-rf2-rt4jz ordering, the constructor returning a frame running V1, which is the original defect; and 0 with the ordering as shipped. THE GENERAL LESSON: a test that consumes a leak as a precondition goes QUIET rather than red when the leak is fixed, and restating its control by reasoning about the new state is not enough — the restatement has to be re-sabotaged.

GATES, all re-run on the FINAL base 9f1f4713b5 after a rebase past 25 non-beads landings; pre-rebase greens are not quoted. Every exit code below was captured with the redirect and the echo on one command line and is quoted from that capture, never from a harness report. JVM clojure -M:test from implementation/core: captured exit 0, 2174 tests, 11127 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors. CLJS npm run test:cljs from implementation: captured exit 0, 11152 tests, 54863 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors (11150 / 54839 pre-rebase — the movement is itself the evidence the re-run read the new base rather than a stale artefact). Docs python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py from repo root: captured exit 0, and exercised first against a planted broken anchor (exit 1, naming spec/002-Frames.md:754) so its silence is a pass rather than a misconfiguration. mkdocs build --strict is NOT the gate here: docs_dir is docs, so spec/ was never a candidate for it. late_bind_drift_test rides the JVM lane and is green, so the new directory entry and the set-fn! site agree. Prose, tables and rendering are covered by no gate, so the one spec clause was read back by hand: a single ordered list item, no link, no anchor, and no table touched anywhere in the change.

AUDIT REOPEN 2026-09-01 — PR #8887

The fresh-process release is correct, but the new teardown publication was added inside an already-completed defonce once-body. In a live dev process upgraded from pre-#8887 code, reprojection-installed? is already true; reloading re-frame.live-frame therefore skips install-reprojection!, never publishes :live-frame/on-frame-destroyed!, and later make-frame/destroy-frame! calls keep leaking provenance rows until restart. This also contradicts re-frame.late-bind's stated hot-reload contract that a producing namespace re-registers its hook.

Measured against current production code in a disposable JVM: install once, remove only the new key to model the pre-upgrade registry, require re-frame.live-frame :reload, then create/destroy :audit/hmr. Output was {:hook-after-reload false, :row-before-destroy true} then {:row-after-destroy true}. The existing tests all start with the new four-effect once-body and cannot see this upgrade path.

Keep the repair narrow: make the newly introduced teardown publication re-arm when this namespace is hot-reloaded (without duplicating the registration hook, weakening the JVM install barrier, or rooting the reprojection graph for apps that never construct a frame). Add a focused preinstalled-flag/missing-new-key regression proving the hook becomes present and destroy returns the provenance table to baseline. No public API or lifecycle redesign.
VERDICT (rf2-cq0yi, AUDIT REOPEN) — PR #8926, draft-then-ready, base 5c66acd1de.

HISTORY WALK. 556 entries; all 555 adjacent pairs compared newest-first, bounded at the item's beginning rather than at any marker. Only FOUR pairs change any field. The description is byte-identical across the entire history — never edited — so the audit note is the newest text-bearing change (2026-09-01 20:30:58 +10:00 tracker time, notes 8968 -> 10402 chars, old text a strict prefix of new, status closed -> open in the same commit). The other three are the earlier VERDICT note plus close (17:00/17:01) and the original claim (15:37). No comments (bd comments --json returns []). No children (bd dep tree and bd list --parent both empty), so no ruling was recorded as a new child bead. The brief quoted the audit note faithfully; nothing in the item disagreed with it.

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE, NOT ASSUMED. The audit's measurement reproduces at tip in a disposable JVM using its own stated method — install once, remove ONLY :live-frame/on-frame-destroyed! from late-bind/hooks to model the pre-upgrade registry, (require 're-frame.live-frame :reload), create and destroy :audit/hmr. Captured exit 0, printing:

  {:hook-after-warm true, :installed-flag true}
  {:hook-after-reload false, :row-before-destroy true}
  {:row-after-destroy true, :frame-record-gone true}

The middle line is the audit's recorded pair exactly. The third line adds what the audit left implicit and is the leak stated plainly: the frame RECORD is gone while its provenance row is not. Post-repair the same harness prints :hook-after-reload true and :row-after-destroy false.

ROOT CAUSE. reprojection-installed? is a defonce atom, so it survives a namespace reload holding true and install-reprojection! is skipped on every reload after the first make-frame. A publication sited in that body is therefore published once per PROCESS, never once per LOAD. Invisible in a fresh process — where the first make-frame installs everything — and it bites only on the upgrade path, which is why every existing case passes over it. It also contradicts late-bind's own documented contract twice over: hooks' docstring says the map is "populated by the producing namespace at LOAD TIME", and set-fn!'s says its cache invalidation exists so "hot-reload of an artefact swaps the resolved fn on the very next dispatch".

THE REPAIR, AND HOW IT CLEARS EACH OF THE THREE FENCED NON-GOALS. The keyed publication moves to a top-level set-fn! at ns load, matching fx.cljc's :fx/on-frame-destroyed! precedent (bound once at ns-load, same destroy step-6 pass, same late-bind-because-load-order reasoning). That is the whole behavioural change; the rest of the diff is commentary the move would otherwise leave wrong.
  (1) NO DUPLICATE REGISTRATION HOOK. registrar/add-registration-hook! APPENDS, so re-running it per reload would accumulate duplicates and double-mark the projection dirty on every reg-*. It stays in the once-body. Only the idempotent KEYED set-fn! moved — re-running that overwrites one map entry.
  (2) NO WEAKENING OF THE JVM INSTALL BARRIER. The lock, the publish-last ordering and the flag are untouched over the effects they still own; the flag's promise narrows honestly to the registrar hook plus both reprojection keys. The moved key needs no promise from it, because ns load STRICTLY PRECEDES the first make-frame — the publication is now EARLIER than it was, never later, so the timing guarantee the once-body siting was chosen for is kept rather than traded away.
  (3) NO NEW ROOTING. release-frame-generation-pool! is one swap! against the provenance atom and references nothing in the reprojection / image-assembly graph. Load time roots that two-line fn and its atom and nothing else, so install-reprojection!, reproject-live-frame! and resolve-within-image stay unreachable from a bundle that never calls make-frame and the Spec 009 PROD_ABSENT_WHEN_UNUSED contract is untouched.

FINDING NOT ASKED FOR. reprojection_install_race_jvm_test's fixture already models the once-body as owning THREE effects — the registrar hook and the two reprojection keys — and its comment says so in as many words ("un-publish ONLY the two late-bind keys the once-body owns"). #8887's fourth effect was never added to that model, so the code and that test's stated model had been out of step since #8887 merged. This change restores the agreement rather than papering over it, which is corroboration from an independent direction that the once-body was the wrong home for the key.

THE REGRESSION. New implementation/core/test/re_frame/live_frame_teardown_hook_reload_jvm_test.clj constructs the state no existing case reaches — once-flag LATCHED and this one key MISSING — then proves the once-body cannot repair it (ensure-reprojection-installed! is a no-op behind the latched flag), performs a real (require :reload), and asserts the hook is present, that make-frame wrote a row while the frame was live (non-vacuity control), and that destroy returns the table to its captured baseline. The hook is restored surgically in a finally rather than by a whole-map reset!, mirroring the race test's discipline. JVM-ONLY DELIBERATELY: (require ... :reload) has no CLJS runtime analogue — a fact this test tree already states in cofx_cljs_test, conformance_corpus_cljs_test and test-support's own docstring — while the FIX is one top-level form in a .cljc file that shadow-cljs hot reload re-evaluates identically, so the mechanism is shared and only the harness is host-specific. The cross-host release coverage in frame_destroy_generation_provenance_cljs_test is unchanged and still runs on both lanes.

CONTROL, AND WHAT IT PROVED. Plant: the publication put back inside the once-body — the natural revert-the-fix plant. Both anchors checked to match exactly ONE line before running; git blob hash 45608c49 -> 78a3c1de, so the plant did not silently no-op; restored by checkout and re-verified by blob hash against the committed object (back to 45608c49) with zero residue, never by reading a diff. Control arm (clean tree, both namespaces): captured exit 0, 5 tests, 26 assertions, 0 failures. Sabotage arm (same two namespaces): captured exit 1, 5 tests, 26 assertions, 3 failures. Test and assertion totals IDENTICAL across arms, so no namespace was skipped and nothing crashed out. All three reds are in the new file — hook absent after reload, row surviving destroy, table not returning to baseline — and all four pre-existing provenance cases stayed GREEN. That is exactly the discrimination the audit said the existing tests could not make, demonstrated in both directions rather than asserted.

GATES, both re-run on the FINAL base 5c66acd1de after a rebase past 21 landings; the pre-rebase greens are not quoted. Every exit code was captured with the redirect and the echo on ONE command line and is quoted from that capture, never from a harness report. JVM core clojure -M:test from implementation/core: captured exit 0, 2175 tests, 11138 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors (2174/11127 was the pre-audit recorded figure; +1 test / +8 assertions is exactly the new file, and the further assertion movement across the rebase is itself the evidence the re-run read the new base rather than a stale artefact). CLJS npm run test:cljs from implementation: captured exit 0, 11148 tests, 55122 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors; that lane prints its config path and the line named this worker's own checkout, which is the cross-worktree check for the lane that affords one. late_bind_drift_test rides the JVM lane and is green.

NO NEW DIRECTORY ROW WAS NEEDED — the key already had one, since this change moves a publication rather than adding one. The row's description did carry a stale claim ("Published from re-frame.live-frame/install-reprojection!, the same make-frame-rooted once-body..."), which is now corrected to the ns-load account with the reasoning. That edit is ONE line in ONE file, isolated as the final commit, so a rebase conflict against a sibling adding rows stays a one-line conflict.

SPEC/002-FRAMES.MD NOT TOUCHED, and it did not need to be. Its Destroy step-6 ordered list names :live-frame/on-frame-destroyed! (lines 753-754) but nowhere states WHERE the hook is published, so the move leaves the normative recipe accurate. The hot-zone file is therefore not serialised against by this PR — the contrast with #8887, which did take a clause there.

DIFF REVIEWED AGAINST THE MERGE BASE (origin/main...HEAD) for reverts, not merely for conflicts: five files, all mine, purely additive; the directory row moved from line 1159 to 1163 under sibling rows added on trunk and my edit is confined to its own row's description, reverting nothing a sibling landed.
close_reason: PR #8926: the :live-frame/on-frame-destroyed! publication moves from the defonce-guarded reprojection once-body to a top-level set-fn! at ns load, so it re-arms on every hot reload of re-frame.live-frame. The audit's measurement reproduced verbatim at tip before any edit ({:hook-after-reload false, :row-before-destroy true} then {:row-after-destroy true}) and inverts after the repair. All three fenced non-goals cleared: the appending registrar hook stays in the once-body, the JVM install barrier is untouched over the effects it still owns (and the publication is now strictly EARLIER than it was, never later), and the two-line release roots no reprojection/image-assembly graph. New JVM-only live_frame_teardown_hook_reload_jvm_test builds the latched-flag/missing-key state the existing cases cannot reach; :reload has no CLJS analogue while the fix is one .cljc top-level form both hosts re-run. Negative control ran both arms from one verified plant (blob 45608c49->78a3c1de, restored and re-verified): 3 failures all in the new file, all four pre-existing provenance cases green, identical test/assertion totals. Gates on final base 5c66acd1de: JVM core captured exit 0 (2175 tests, 11138 assertions, 0F/0E), CLJS captured exit 0 (11148 tests, 55122 assertions, 0F/0E). No new late-bind directory row needed; that row's stale publication-site sentence corrected as an isolated one-line final commit. spec/002-Frames.md not touched and did not need to be.

title: surface-review(conformance-security): stop security-tier edits from arming production and browser gates
description:
## Scope

Correct PR changed-surface routing for the four source-less, cross-artefact test partitions under implementation/security, implementation/reply-conformance, implementation/derivation-conformance, and implementation/event-conformance. The implementation change should be confined to the classifier and its executable policy tests/comments unless a directly coupled testing-policy sentence must move with them.

## Findings

- All four partitions are test-only: each deps.edn has :paths [] and :deps {}, none has a src/ tree, and none publishes production code. Their responsibilities are substantial and distinct: reply vocabulary/egress across managed-async families; derivation algebra across five graph contributors; the event facade/runtime/isolation boundary; and adversarial security properties over schema, SSR, reply, profile, error-slot, and MCP egress.
- The suites deliberately complement artefact-local tests rather than replace them. Derivation composes family projections; event tests adversarial public seams after core-owned duplicates were removed; reply tests own cross-family vocabulary while family tests own lowering; security adds generated/sentinel/fail-closed coverage beyond fixed local pins. A broad semantic dedupe would trade away confidence for little benefit.
- CLJS already has the right shape: every namespace matches the consolidated :node-test build's cljs-test$ selector, and the focused test:security build is only a local-iteration subset. JVM CI likewise keeps four required clojure -M:test jobs. Current successful run 33307155376 reports security 92 tests/698 assertions, derivation 22/522, event 49/209, and reply 27/533.
- The changed-surface classifier treats the three *-conformance trees as source-less and sets only implementation_jvm=true plus cljs_node_test=true. The same probe on an actual security test currently also sets cljs_browser=true, examples_compile=true, cljs_prod=true, and bundle_isolation=true.
- Those four extra gates cannot observe a security-tier-only edit: :browser-test selects only *-dom-cljs-test namespaces; production and bundle-isolation builds do not require the test tree; and the all-examples compiler has no edge to it. implementation/security/deps.edn is also test-only.
- This is drift from recorded intent, not a new coverage trade. Commit 5bb3cd9cd1 says adding implementation/security/* was needed specifically to fire implementation_jvm and cljs_node_test, but placed it in a generic feature-artefact arm that sets five outputs. The later src-less conformance arm at report-changed-surfaces.sh:1202-1220 explicitly says security is the precedent for omitting browser/prod/bundle gates, while the earlier executable arm contradicts it.
- The examples-compile policy test reinforces the mistake with implementation/security/src/re_frame/security.cljc, a path that does not exist in this intentionally src-less partition, and asserts that this imaginary file can change an example closure.
- The toll is material. Security-only commit d1fa5ff493 changed deps/test commentary and its tests workflow run 29096118890 executed the relevant JVM/Node suites plus the all-examples job (10m24s), browser, two production browser builds, and bundle isolation. The all-examples job was the critical path; current direct classifier output still arms the same unrelated surfaces.
- Search across all tracker statuses and title/description/notes for conformance, security classifier/surface/tier, src-less, examples_compile, bundle_isolation, cljs_browser, and over-classification found no issue owning this exact mismatch.

## Recommended Action

Move implementation/security/* out of both the shipped-feature classifier arm and the examples_compile input arm, and classify it alongside reply-conformance, derivation-conformance, and event-conformance as a source-less cross-artefact tier: implementation_jvm=true and cljs_node_test=true only.

Update the classifier's executable mirror using real tracked security paths. Preserve the jvm-security required job, the local JVM roster entry, the consolidated Node inclusion, and the focused test:security command. Keep production artefact routing unchanged, so changes to core/schemas/machines/routing/flows/SSR still run their existing production/browser/bundle gates and continue to trigger the broad JVM and Node suites.

## Evidence

- implementation/security/deps.edn and the three *-conformance/deps.edn files: empty production paths/deps, test-only aliases.
- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:208-287 and 650-655: all four test roots feed the shared cljs-test$ Node build; security's focused selector is at 769-790.
- .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:574 includes security in examples compilation; 973-997 includes it in the full feature fan-out; 1202-1220 gives the three sibling tiers the intended narrow routing and states that security has the same posture.
- implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs:1983-2011 asserts examples compilation from the nonexistent implementation/security/src/re_frame/security.cljc; 3283-3311 already pins the narrow sibling-tier contract.
- .github/workflows/test.yml:2149-2198 and 2482-2610: required JVM jobs; 6026 and 6040-6042: aggregator membership.
- scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh:46-90: all four JVM lanes remain in the rigorous local roster.
- Commit 5bb3cd9cd1 and workflow runs 29096118890 / 33307155376 provide the intent, observed toll, and current suite tallies.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Classifying both implementation/security/deps.edn and at least one real tracked implementation/security/test/** file sets implementation_jvm=true and cljs_node_test=true, while examples_compile, cljs_browser, cljs_prod, and bundle_isolation are false.
2. Representative real files under reply-conformance, derivation-conformance, and event-conformance retain the same two-output routing.
3. The classifier policy test removes the imaginary implementation/security/src/** positive fixture, uses tracked paths for the security tier, and explicitly locks the four negative outputs so the broad arm cannot silently return.
4. jvm-security remains conditional on implementation_jvm, remains in all-required-passed, and still runs clojure -M:test from implementation/security. The local JVM roster entry, shadow :node-test root, and npm test:security focused command remain intact.
5. Production/source-bearing artefact probes retain their existing browser, production, examples, and bundle-isolation routing; this change narrows only the source-less security partition.
6. Classifier comments and TESTING.md, if touched, agree that all four source-less tiers use JVM + consolidated Node coverage and do not claim production-bundle reachability.
7. The changed-surface policy suite and gate-scheduling checks pass, with a direct classifier transcript for all four partitions included in the handoff.

## Non-goals

- Do not delete, merge, thin, or relocate semantic conformance/security tests.
- Do not combine the four JVM jobs or deps.edn files, redesign the broad implementation_jvm output, or add a new classifier output.
- Do not change security, reply, event, derivation, egress, redaction, or fail-open/fail-closed runtime behavior.
- Do not remove the focused test:security command merely because its namespaces also ride test:cljs.
- Do not narrow production artefact changes; only edits inside the source-less implementation/security partition are in scope.

## Related beads

- rf2-7rzg records the same general location-based over-classification shape for Hicasso prose, but is an independent operator decision with different observable gates; this task neither depends on nor settles it.
- Historical provenance cited by the repository: rf2-oni7gz/rf2-gj2ae established JVM security coverage; rf2-dxndhc established narrow routing for the three sibling source-less tiers; rf2-gzavkm established that examples_compile should follow actual compiled-closure inputs. These historical ids are not duplicate live owners in the current tracker.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-30 21:55:20 AUSEST (read-only agent at 556b8fabbc): premise REPRODUCED on tip — the classifier arms cljs_browser/examples_compile/cljs_prod/bundle_isolation for implementation/security/test/... and security/deps.edn while reply-conformance arms only implementation_jvm+cljs_node_test. Surfaces: the one-toucher pair .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh + implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs (this change alters OUTPUTS, so both halves in ONE commit), optionally TESTING.md. The test at _changed-surfaces.test.cjs:1983-2011 asserts from a phantom path implementation/security/src/re_frame/security.cljc — move security to the negative list including the examples_compile arm. Gates: node scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs; classifier transcript for all four tiers + one src-bearing control. Nobody live or queued is on the pair. DISPATCHABLE solo.
close_reason: PR #8903, commit b96903532b. NOT deferred -- it turned out to be exactly a classifier arm plus its mirror pin, so it stayed in the cluster. implementation/security/* removed from the examples_compile arm and from the production per-feature fan-out, and added to the src-less tier alongside reply/derivation/event-conformance. That closes a contradiction the file carried with ITSELF: the src-less arm already named security as the PRECEDENT for omitting the browser/production/bundle gates while two earlier executable arms armed all four, so prose lost to code silently. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, all met and measured. (1) security/deps.edn and real tracked security test files: implementation_jvm=true, cljs_node_test=true, with examples_compile, cljs_browser, cljs_prod, bundle_isolation all false. (2) The three sibling tiers retain the same two-output routing, unchanged. (3) The phantom implementation/security/src/re_frame/security.cljc removed from the examples_compile fixture list, replaced with four TRACKED security paths that lock the two positives and all four negatives. (4) jvm-security unchanged and untouched -- still gated on implementation_jvm, still in all-required-passed, still runs from implementation/security; the local JVM roster entry, shadow :node-test root and npm test:security are untouched, and new mirror tests now pin the first two. (5) Production/src-bearing probes retain full routing -- pinned for all seven per-feature artefacts. (6) TESTING.md needed no change: line 192 already describes implementation_jvm as covering the src-less conformance tiers plus jvm-security, and nothing there claims production-bundle reachability for security, so the hot-zone file stayed out of the diff. (7) Policy suite and gate-scheduling both pass; transcript for all four partitions plus a src-bearing control is in the PR body. NARROWING IS CONFINED: across 18 probes covering all four source-less tiers, all seven src-bearing per-feature artefacts, core, the Reagent adapter, examples and the two root build files, the full 28-output before/after diff is FOUR LINES, all on the two security paths. CONTROL: reverting the defect (putting security back in the examples_compile arm) made the mirror suite return exit 1 with 4 failures naming 'examples_compile cannot observe it', so the new pins genuinely lock the negatives and the broad arm cannot silently return; restore verified by git blob hash, re-run exit 0. Gates (all re-run on the final base after rebase): node --test _changed-surfaces.test.cjs 0 (314 passed), check_gate_scheduling 0, check_workflow_yaml 0, check_workflow_job_timeouts 0, check_jvm_lane_rosters 0, check_test_lane_bijection 0, bash -n and sh -n 0.

title: hicasso defhost: infer the callback contract by position, keep :callbacks as a 2-value override, delete :handler (executes ruling rf2-6c12m.2)
description:
Executes ruling rf2-6c12m.2 (RULED 2026-08-29 15:29:54 AUSEST, delegated review per Mike: Option B, 2 values). The FULL analysis - decisive facts, rejected options, before/after, id-by-id line pointers, doc/skill/test file lists, acceptance - is the RULING note on rf2-6c12m.2; brief from it. This description is the condensed DO.

THE RULE: a defhost or [:>] callback contract is inferred from the prop position exactly as native tags already do (intent.cljs:1200-1210 position-contract; intent.cljs:1212-1228 lower-prop): on*-spelled -> :event, any other walked prop -> :render, :ref -> React's, declared :slots -> markup. :callbacks survives ONLY as an optional override {<prop> :event|:render} written where inference is wrong (on*-named render props: Fluent onRenderItem/onRenderCell, Ant onRow/onCell/onFilter); a declared contract outranks the spelling. :handler is DELETED (a plain fn is the handler contract and already crosses untouched at every position - intent.cljs:1225,1228; codec.cljs:2865). A vector or map at a render position (inferred or overridden) crosses as data via host-prop-value, as at a native tag. An h/event at a declared :slots position stays refused.

title: merge criterion: measuring the band compares a git LOCAL time against gh's UTC mergedAt - naive comparison qualified 1 PR where 5 qualify, and the recovery from that reads a stale band
description:
FOUND 2026-09-17 by the §5 METHOD-REREAD LOOP on its named standing example. §5's first gotcha is
"a measured constant that has gone stale — the check-count band is the standing example", so this
tick re-measured the band. The band was FINE (88, unanimous). The measurement STEP was not.

## THE STEP THIS ATTACKS

loops.md §1 says: "The band moves; never trust a written number. **Measure it on changes merged
AFTER the last matrix change.**" CLAUDE.md repeats the discipline and adds the cheap confirmation:
"read the rollup TOTAL of a PR merged AFTER the suspect commit."

Both require comparing **a git commit time** to **PR merge times**. Two tools. Two conventions.
Neither labels itself at the point of comparison.

## SEAM ONE — TIMEZONE. git reports LOCAL, gh reports UTC.

Measured on the live case, the last workflow-matrix change `b9220b6dc2`:

    git log --date=iso   ->  2026-09-16 15:18:39 +1000     (local, AUSEST)
    gh mergedAt (#9914)  ->  2026-09-16T15:22:46Z          (UTC)

Compared naively, those are four minutes apart and only ONE of the five candidate PRs qualifies.
Converted properly the commit is **05:18 UTC** and all five qualify:

    PRs qualifying, NAIVE (local vs UTC, unconverted)  [9914]                        n=1
    PRs qualifying, CORRECT (both in UTC)              [9910,9911,9912,9913,9914]    n=5

## SEAM TWO — WHICH CLOCK. The same commit carries two, 42 minutes apart.

    git %ad (AUTHORED)   ->  2026-09-16 15:18:39 +1000  =  05:18 UTC
    git %cI (COMMITTED)  ->  2026-09-16T16:00:43+10:00  =  06:00 UTC

This is the two-clocks fact loops.md §3 already records for LIVENESS — "a rebase rewrites the
committed time and replays the authored one, so under rebase-merge they differ on essentially
every change" — arriving in a completely different loop, where §3's guidance does not reach
because §3 is answering "is this worker alive". For "did this land on trunk before that PR
merged", the COMMITTED time is the one that means entry into trunk history under rebase-merge.
**On this instance the band is 88 under either clock**, so the clock choice was not decisive here
and is recorded as a seam rather than as a demonstrated error.

## WHY IT MATTERS — THE IMMEDIATE EFFECT FAILS CLOSED, THE RECOVERY FAILS OPEN

Getting it wrong shrinks the qualifying set, which presents as "I do not have enough PRs to
measure the band". That is not itself dangerous. **The danger is the next move**, and it is the
obvious one: widen the window to get more samples — which reaches back PAST the matrix change and
measures the OLD band. A stale band then makes every subsequent PR read a fixed number of checks
away from a phantom, which CLAUDE.md already describes as indistinguishable from a change
genuinely missing coverage, after which the next move is to hunt for coverage that was never gone.

So it belongs with the merge-criterion traps by consequence, reached through a two-step path
rather than in one.

## IT HAS NO HOME — MEASURED

Over `CLAUDE.md`, with a live control:

    mergedAt          0        authored time     0
    utc               0        committed time    0
    --date=iso        0        CONTROL merge-base  4

`timezone` reads 1, and that one is the § Local working files timestamp-format bullet
("full datetime with timezone"), which is about how to WRITE a timestamp, not how to compare two.
A tracker search pairing a clock or timezone concern with the band returned 8 records, every one
a false positive from substring matches in unrelated prose; control, records mentioning
`timezone` at all: 6.

## THE FIX, AND WHY IT IS NOT IN loops.md

CLAUDE.md's merge-trap bullet, beside (a)/(b)/(c). It is a CLI CONCRETION — it names `gh`,
`mergedAt` and `--date=iso` — and loops.md is deliberately OS-neutral and tool-agnostic, which is
the same division of labour trap (b) has with clause 4's *Abbreviated revisions*, and (p), (q) and
(r) have with their method statements. **loops.md §1 is RIGHT as written and must NOT be edited
for this.**

The clause is short: when measuring the band, put both times in the same zone before comparing,
and prefer the committed time for "landed on trunk". One sentence, possibly two.

## NOT ESTABLISHED

  * **Whether this has ever actually produced a wrong band.** No history was taken. The band is
    88 today and was 88 before; this tick caught the seam in the act rather than after damage.
  * **Whether `gh` always reports `Z`.** One PR's raw `mergedAt` was read. The others were read
    through a formatter that had already trimmed the suffix, so strictly the UTC claim rests on
    one sample plus the documented API contract.
  * **Whether the committed-time choice is right in a case where the two clocks would change the
    verdict.** The argument is given above; no such case was constructed.
  * Whether other steps in these loops cross the same seam. Not swept. §5's own gotcha says a
    defect found here usually has siblings, and that sweep was not done.

## SCOPE

  * **Do NOT edit loops.md.** See above.
  * **Do NOT add a gate.** Nothing mechanical distinguishes a correct comparison from a naive one.
  * **Do NOT add a new lettered instrument item** unless whoever takes it judges the letters the
    right home — it is arguably a merge-criterion trap rather than an instrument misreport, since
    both tools report their own times correctly and honestly.

## FENCED AT FILING — THE SURFACE IS HELD

`CLAUDE.md` is held by a live worker on rf2-9h0f9 (dispatched 2026-09-17). Per the two-release-
conditions rule, that surface fence releases when **that worker's PR MERGES**, not when it
reports. Do not dispatch this onto CLAUDE.md before then.

That fence releases when THAT WORKER'S PR MERGES, not when it reports - a worker that has reported still has an open change editing the file, and a second worker branched off trunk would not carry it, so the two collide at merge.
