title: story: should the Tests pane and sidebar dot surface a SETUP failure on a variant that declares no tests? (finding from rf2-0ae7o.13; needs a ruling)
description:
NEEDS A RULING FROM MIKE — no work until then. Found by the rf2-0ae7o.13 worker (PR #9878) while doing the browser acceptance, and recorded here so it is not buried in that bead's close. Owning item: rf2-0ae7o.13.

THE BEHAVIOUR, measured in the browser on the login-form testbed: the Tests pane and the sidebar dot are keyed on `variant-has-tests?`, which reads the DECLARED `:assertions` / `:checks` / `:script`. So a variant that declares none shows "No tests registered for this variant" and no sidebar dot WHATEVER its setup did — including a setup that now fails under the rf2-0ae7o.13 ruling.

WHY IT IS NOT A REGRESSION: this is pre-existing and presents identically today for a setup handler that THROWS. PR #9878 changed the run VERDICT (a no-handler dispatch in setup or script fails the run), not the pane's empty state. The failure IS visible on two surfaces: the canvas shows the inline `:rf.error/exception` record under the mounted view, and `story/run` reads `:error` with the record.

THE QUESTION: should the Tests pane and the sidebar dot surface a SETUP failure on a variant that declares no tests? Today the answer is no, by construction.

- Argument for leaving it: the pane says what it means — no tests are registered — and the failure is already on the canvas and in `story/run`. The worker classed it as minutiae under the project stance.
- Argument for changing it: an author whose setup is broken sees a clean sidebar, and the canvas record is the only tell.

SCOPE IF RULED CHANGE: Story UI only (the pane and the dot's predicate), plus whatever spec sentence owns the pane's empty state. No change to the agreement floor, the capture enum or `evidence.cljc`.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-09-17 09:44:17 AUSEST, dossier review). Mike delegated this decision on 2026-09-17 with the instruction: read the two reviews, weigh them, decide, record, keep the analysis.
DECISION: A — leave it: the Tests pane and the sidebar dot stay keyed on DECLARED tests. The canvas-strip repair both reviewers recommended (the dossier's option E) is filed as rf2-uky0n (bug, P3, discovered-from this bead) and is NOT bundled into this ruling.
WHY: Both reviewers reached A + E independently, and their evidence agrees rather than competes. The pane's copy ("No tests registered") is literally true, and the dot's one meaning — the verdict of THIS variant's tests — is worth keeping clean; teaching it to also mean "your setup broke" makes its own aria-label lie ("tests: Fail" on a variant with none). The dossier's JVM probe measured the captured record (:passed? false, no :status, :error {:message "no handler registered for :your/setup-event"}) and its :error projection; Codex corroborated it on real variants and ran three existing JVM tests (17 assertions, 0 failures). I re-read the strip at trunk 8bb6041d0e — unchanged since the dossier's 634b085f12 — and the gap is exactly as both describe: assertion_strip.cljs has no :error arm in summary-line (:116-141), in either style map (:262-270), in row-detail (:311-348, which never destructures :error although pure.cljc:145 puts it in :detail) or in seed-open (:444-449), and assertion_strip_cljs_test.cljs carries 0 :error cases against 6 :fail. Under the posture the cheapest defensible option wins: A costs nothing, and B, C and D each buy a second copy of what the canvas already carries — D worst, because Codex showed its non-pass-only write would never clear a recorded failure after a healthy rerun (ui/state/tests.cljc:148-161), and the dossier showed the dot could only ever light for a variant the author has already opened, so it is a memory, not a discovery aid. E is not gold plating: a tool whose job is to show state must not paint the one sentence that says what went wrong as a grey "·" with no text, and the repair is one file, one spec clause each, one test file, no new state and no new writer. No reviewer lost here; the losing OPTIONS lose on cost and mechanism, not on evidence. B is deliberately left out: Codex's point that Tests REPLACES the canvas (shell.cljs:851-860) is real, but "trust the programmer" says an author with no tests reads the canvas, and B can be added later at a handful of lines on the same read the canvas already makes if a workflow problem is ever demonstrated.
WHAT CHANGES MY MIND: a demonstrated case of an author on a test-less variant going to the Tests tab first and being misled by "No tests registered" — that would justify B (the dossier's own fallback), still with no dot; or Mike stating that the Tests tab is where an author goes when a variant looks wrong.
RECORD SHAPE (why a new bead rather than retitling this one): the question as asked is ruled here and this text is the close reason, because a ruling in this project lives in a close reason and a retitle would bury it in notes under a work title. The work goes to rf2-uky0n because E is a different surface from this bead's own scope line ("Story UI only — the pane and the dot's predicate"), so a retitled bead would carry a description arguing about surfaces the work never touches; discovered-from keeps the trail in both directions. rf2-uky0n's description is a self-contained brief: the file, every line, the record shape to render, the RED tests and their controls, the gates (npm run test:cljs from implementation/, clj-kondo, check_doc_slugs.py for tools/story/spec/004) and the do-not list (the pane, the dot, tests.cljc, canvas run-settled, the agreement floor, the capture enum, evidence.cljc, error.cljc, predicates/assertion-glyph). No hot-zone file; parallel-safe.
DOSSIER (preserved verbatim from ai/decisions/rf2-20lwk.story-tests-pane-setup-failure.md; two independent reviewers; the file is deleted). THIS NOTE IS THE CANONICAL RECORD.
Provenance of the dropped status line: dossier written 2026-09-17 08:43:27 AUSEST at trunk 634b085f12 (P3, task); the Codex review that follows it read revision 6a3bf87c18 the same day.
Depends on / feeds: found by rf2-0ae7o.13 (closed, PR #9878, Mike ruled "rule 2" 2026-09-16) under epic rf2-0ae7o; no dependents. A "change" ruling feeds one small Story-UI bead; "leave" closes with the reason.

## The decision in one sentence

When a variant declares no `:assertions` / `:checks` / `:script` but its `:setup` fails (a throwing handler, or — since PR #9878 — a dispatch nobody registered, which is exactly what the unfilled real-setup scaffold does), the Tests pane says "No tests registered" and the sidebar row shows no dot; decide whether those two surfaces should say "setup failed" instead, and if so how much.

## The problem, carefully

**What keys the two surfaces today.** Both read ONE predicate over the DECLARED body, never a run:

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/state/tests.cljc:228-235` — `own-tests?` is a non-empty `:script` / `:plays` / `:assertions` / `:checks`; `:263-291` adds a composed fragment's script and inherited checks. `:setup` is not consulted anywhere.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/pure.cljc:42-55` — `variant-has-tests?` wraps it for the pane; `tests.cljc:293-312` — `testable-variant-ids` (`:test` tag AND has-tests) for the dots, the Tests widget, Run all and watch mode.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/view.cljs:705-713` — the pane branches on it: false ⇒ `empty-state` (`:633-657`: "No tests registered for this variant / Add `:assertions`, `:checks` or a `:script` to `<id>` to register tests." + a link), and the pane never runs the variant. `tools/story/spec/009-Test-Mode.md:175-178` makes that a MUST NOT ("skipping the call also skips frame allocation").
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/sidebar.cljs:537-540` — a row leads with `[status-dot status]` only when testable; otherwise a neutral variant glyph. `spec/009:316-319`: "a `:dev`-only variant or a `:test` variant with nothing to run renders no dot."

**Where a run's verdict CAN land, and who writes it.** The dot reads shell-state `[:tests :runs vid :status]` (`sidebar.cljs:595-599`, default `:pending`). Only two writers exist: the pane's own run (`test_mode/state.cljs:85-138`, `store-result!`) and Run all / watch (`sidebar.cljs:690-721`, `run-one-test!`) — both gated on has-tests, so a test-less variant never gets an entry. The CANVAS run (every selection runs phases 0-3 and the auto-play through `prepare-run!` / `resume-run!`, `canvas.cljs:453-519`) keeps its verdict in a PRIVATE atom, `run-settled` (`canvas.cljs:417-429`), stamped as `data-run-status` on the `<section>` (`:802-820`) — a test hook, not something the author sees, and not shared with the sidebar.

**What the failure actually looks like on the surfaces that DO carry it.** This is the fact the bead did not record, and the "leave it" argument rests on it. The refusal is captured by the per-frame trace listener and projected onto the frame's `:rf.story/assertions` (`spec/002-Runtime.md:386-397`, `spec/017-Testing-Story.md:2359-2374`; `error.cljc:278-313`). I built that record on the JVM (`clojure -M -i` from `tools/story`, probe only) and projected it through the same `assertion-row` the canvas strip uses:

```
RECORD :error   = {:message "no handler registered for :your/setup-event", :stack nil, :data nil}
RECORD :passed? = false   :status present? false
ROW :status     = :error          ROW :label = ":rf.error/exception"
ROW detail :reason = nil          ROW detail :event = [:your/setup-event {}]   :phase = :phase-2-events
ROW detail :error  = {:message "no handler registered for :your/setup-event" …}
CONTROL(throwing setup handler) ROW :status = :error   :reason = nil   :error :message = "kaboom"
```

So the row is `:error`, not `:fail` (`pure.cljc:116-128` — a truthy `:error` map wins, and `throwable->error-map` always returns a map, `error.cljc:204-240`). The canvas strip (`assertion_strip.cljs`, shared with workspace cells at `workspace.cljc:477`) has NO `:error` arm: the glyph map is `{:pass "✓" :fail "✗" :skip "⊘"}` (`predicates.cljc:30-32`) so the row gets the fallback "·" (`assertion_strip.cljs:364`); `status->row-style` / `status->glyph-style` cover only pass/fail/skip (`:262-270`) so there is no red band; `summary-line`'s `case` has no `:error` branch and returns `""` (`:129-141`); only `:fail` rows seed open (`:444-449`) so it lands collapsed; and the strip's `row-detail` renders reason/expected/actual/event/phase/predicate/source but never `:error` (`:311-348`), so the ONE sentence that says what went wrong — "no handler registered for :your/setup-event" — is never painted on the canvas at all. The pane's `row-detail` DOES render `(:message error)` (`view.cljs:312-325`) and has an `:error` glyph `✖` (`:343-351`) — but the pane is the surface that short-circuits.

This is derived from the code and the JVM probe; I did not open a browser (dossier rule). It is consistent with the worker's measurement (rf2-0ae7o.13 notes: the canvas "shows the inline `:rf.error/exception` record", and "a throwing-setup control presents identically on every surface" — both project to `:error`).

**Who it affects.** An author following the fidelity ladder (`spec/019 §3`; `view_state.cljc:1188-1210` offers "↑ real setup" only on a variant below that rung, `:360-361`), and any author whose `:setup` handler throws on a render-only variant. Not production (Story is dev-only), not the API, not the agreement floor.

**What is measured vs asserted.** Measured by the rf2-0ae7o.13 worker in a headless browser: pane empty state, no dot, canvas record present, `story/run` `:error`. Measured here on the JVM: the record's shape and its `:error` projection. Asserted from code: the strip's rendering of that projection (CLJS-only, not runnable on the JVM).

## Make it tangible

The ladder offers "↑ real setup" on a variant whose picture is pinned. Take one under the login-form testbed (illustrative id; the testbed's own five variants are already real-setup, `testbeds/login_form/stories.cljc:132-156`):

```clojure
(rf.story/reg-variant :story.login-form/idle-pinned
  {:sub-overrides {[:login/state] :idle} :tags #{:dev}})
```

Click "↑ real setup". The dialog (`view_state.cljc:1212-1232`) says "Copy this scaffold into your stories namespace and fill the setup slot" and shows, per `upgrade-snippet` (`:505-519`, placeholder from `:385-387`):

```clojure
(rf.story/reg-variant :story.login-form/idle-pinned-upgraded
  {:tags #{:dev}
   ;; real events — proves handlers + app-db
   :setup [[:dispatch [:your/setup-event {}]]]})
;; upgrade of :story.login-form/idle-pinned — drops :sub-overrides on [[:login/state]] rather than :extends-ing the pin; the artifact stays a variant.
```

The author pastes it unedited (or with a typo in the event id — same outcome) and reloads.

**Today, step by step.**

1. *Sidebar row* `/idle-pinned-upgraded`: leads with the neutral variant glyph, no dot (not testable — no script, no assertions, no checks; `:script` never inherits down `:extends`, `spec/017:1489`). Below it the signal strip reads `◌ Pending` (status chip, `sidebar.cljs:548`, `sidebar_signals.cljc:80-91`, label from `theme/status.cljc:112-115`) beside a `real setup` fidelity chip. The Tests widget at the foot is unchanged. Nothing on the row differs from a healthy render-only variant.
2. *Canvas* (on selecting the row): the login card renders in its un-bootstrapped state. Under it, one strip row: `·  :rf.error/exception` — grey fallback glyph, no summary text, no red band, collapsed. Clicking it discloses `event: [:your/setup-event {}]` and `phase: :phase-2-events`. The message is not shown. `data-run-status="error"` is on the section, invisibly.
3. *Tests tab*: "No tests registered for this variant. Add `:assertions`, `:checks` or a `:script` to `:story.login-form/idle-pinned-upgraded` to register tests." No header, no Re-run, no pill.
4. *`story/run` at the REPL or over MCP*: `:status :error` with the record — the one loud surface, and the one PR #9878 fixed.

**Under a "change" ruling (option C below, the pane renders the record):** steps 1, 2 and 4 are unchanged; step 3 becomes a "Setup failed" heading, then the pane's ordinary assertion table with one red `✖ :rf.error/exception` row whose "show detail" reads `error: no handler registered for :your/setup-event · phase: :phase-2-events · source: [:your/setup-event {}]`, then the same "No tests registered" placeholder beneath.

**Under option D (pane + dot):** step 1 also changes — after the canvas run settles, the row gains a solid red dot with `aria-label "tests: Fail"` (`record-test-run` lowers `:error` to `:fail`, `tests.cljc:143`; label from `sidebar.cljs:125-133`) and the chip flips to `✗ Fail`. Note the tell: the label says "tests" on a variant that has none.

**Under option E (mine, the canvas strip):** step 2 becomes `✖  :rf.error/exception   no handler registered for :your/setup-event` — red band, seeded open, with `error: …` in the detail. Steps 1, 3, 4 unchanged.

## Options

### A. Leave it — pane and dot stay keyed on declared tests
- What changes: nothing. The ruling is recorded on the bead.
- Consequences: the pane's copy stays literally true; the dot keeps its one meaning ("this variant's tests"). The author's in-shell tell for a broken setup remains the muted canvas row above, plus `story/run`.
- Cost: none.
- Risk: the bead's "failure IS visible on the canvas" overstates it; leaving A alone leaves the scaffold author with a grey "·" row and no message.

### B. Empty-state copy says setup failed (pane only, one line)
- What changes: in `test-view`'s empty branch (`view.cljs:709-713`) read `(rf.story.runtime/read-assertions variant-id)` — the canvas's own read (`canvas.cljs:593`; `runtime.cljc:402-405` returns `[]` for an unallocated frame) — and when any record reads `:error` / `:fail` through `verdict/record-status`, render one line above the placeholder: "Setup failed: no handler registered for :your/setup-event — see the canvas" (text from `[:error :message]`, else `:reason`). No `run-variant` call, so `spec/009:175-178` still holds.
- Consequences: the Tests tab stops looking clean for a broken variant; nothing else moves. Spec: one sentence in `spec/009 §4` and the "Rendered when" cell of table row 4 (`:84-90`).
- Cost: about half a worker-morning. `view.cljs`, `spec/009-Test-Mode.md`, one new CLJS DOM test beside `test/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/view_variant_switch_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (register a variant with a throwing setup, run it, mount `test-view`, assert the line). ### E. (Mine.) Make the canvas strip present an `:error` record as loudly as a `:fail`

No hot-zone file.

## Recommendation

**Rule A on the question as asked, and dispatch E.** Argued from the stance:

- *The pane and the dot say what they mean.* "No tests registered" is true, and the dot's one meaning — the verdict of THIS variant's tests — is worth keeping clean. Teaching the dot to also mean "your setup broke" (D) makes its own label lie ("tests: Fail" on a variant with none), adds a canvas → shell-state writer, and can only ever light up for a variant the author has already opened, since nothing else runs a test-less variant. That is not a discovery aid; it is a second copy of what the canvas is showing. Don't litigate it.
- *The real ergonomics gap is on the canvas, and it is not minutiae.* The one surface the author is looking at renders the failure as a grey "·" with no text. A tool whose job is to show state should not mute the one record that says "no handler registered for :your/setup-event". E unmutes it for every phase-failure class, on the canvas and in workspace cells, in one file — cheaper than C or D, and better targeted than B, which puts the message on a tab an author with no tests has little reason to open.
- *Trust the programmer.* Once the row is red and open, the author who pasted a scaffold reads the message and fills the slot. No nag, no new dot semantics, no empty-state prose about placeholders.

What would change my mind: if Mike's model is that the Tests tab is where an author goes when a variant looks wrong, add B in the same PR — it is a handful of lines on the same read. C and D buy nothing B and E do not, at more cost and with a semantic wrinkle.

## What the ruling unlocks / how it is recorded

- **If A + E (recommended):** close rf2-20lwk with the ruling as the close reason (pane and dot stay keyed on declared tests; reason: the dot cannot be a discovery aid for a test-less variant, and the pane's copy is true). File ONE follow-on bead for E — "canvas assertion strip: render `:error` records like `:fail` (glyph, band, seed-open, summary and detail from `[:error :message]`)" — scope: `assertion_strip.cljs`, `spec/004 §Canvas assertion-strip`, `assertion_strip_cljs_test.cljs`; a CLJS test committed red first, with a throwing-setup control. Cite `spec/018 §12.6` for the distinct glyph. No browser exclusive needed; the strip is unit-testable per `spec/004:231-233`. Parallel-safe: no hot-zone file.
- **If B or C:** one Story-UI bead as sized above; `view.cljs` + `spec/009 §4` + a CLJS DOM test. Independent of E and parallel-safe with it (different files).
(DOSSIER continued — part 2 of 2)
- **If D:** one bead, sequenced after nothing, but the worker should be briefed on the non-pass gate and on `record-test-run`'s `:error` → `:fail` lowering explicitly, and asked to say in the PR body what the dot's aria-label reads on a test-less variant.
- Either way, nothing here touches the agreement floor, the capture enum or `evidence.cljc` (bead scope line), and no `.github/workflows` or `spec/` hot-zone file moves.

## Sources

## Codex Recommendation

**Keep the Tests pane and sidebar dot tied to tests; make the existing canvas/workspace error row useful (A + E).** This is a worthwhile, small tooling repair: a programmer should see the setup failure's message beside the state they are inspecting. It needs no API addition, extra run, or second store of run results.

**Independent findings.** Reviewed checkout revision `6a3bf87c1885ef66531bc70eb64378a52f6e41fc` on 2026-09-17; the inspected source files had no working-tree changes. I read `bd show rf2-20lwk`, its history, the originating bead, current source/specs, and commit `20038afb7488f73b446a168870fefa8c3a20636b`. That commit already repairs the missing-handler run verdict. This decision concerns how an existing failure is presented.

- The predicate correctly excludes setup-only variants. It includes actual scripts/plays, assertions and checks, including supported composition/inheritance (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/state/tests.cljc:228-312`). The pane gates both its automatic run and results display on that predicate (`ui/test_mode/view.cljs:705-713`); the sidebar additionally requires the `:test` tag (`ui/state/tests.cljc:293-312`, `ui/sidebar.cljs:537-540`). This agrees with [Test Mode's empty-state contract](../../tools/story/spec/009-Test-Mode.md#4-empty-state), lines 175-178, and its dot contract, lines 314-319.
- The authoring flow is real: the upgrade dialog emits `[:dispatch [:your/setup-event {}]]` and tells the author to fill the slot (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/view_state.cljc:385-387,1212-1232`). I ran the existing pasted-scaffold regression, including its registered-handler control. I also ran actual variants with an unregistered setup event and a throwing setup handler: both returned run status `:error`, projected row status `:error`, a useful message, and `variant-has-tests? false`. A healthy render-only control returned `:pass` with no assertion row and still no tests. The failure is not specific to careless scaffold pasting; an ordinary setup bug follows the same path.
- The message survives capture and projection (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/error.cljc:278-313`; `ui/test_mode/pure.cljc:116-144`). Static inspection then finds the precise loss: `ui/assertion_strip.cljs:129-141` has no error summary; lines 262-275 have no error styling/glyph; lines 311-348 omit the error message from expanded detail; lines 444-449 seed only `:fail` open. Canvas and workspace call this same component (`ui/canvas.cljs:369-377,777`; `ui/workspace.cljc:471-477`). The existing strip tests exercise pass/fail/skip, with no `:error` case (`tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/assertion_strip_cljs_test.cljs:136-142,268-312`).

**Options and tradeoffs.** Leaving everything unchanged costs nothing, but leaves a captured, actionable message undisclosed even when the row is expanded. B/C can help someone who opens Tests to investigate, but make that pane read a separate canvas-frame result and still require the canvas repair for ordinary visual browsing. D offers a remembered failure while browsing other variants, but needs another writer and rules for clearing stale errors. In particular, the proposed non-pass-only write does not clear a recorded failure after a healthy rerun; an explicit clear would also be required (`ui/state/tests.cljc:148-161`). That is avoidable mechanism for this problem.

E directly improves both existing visual inspection surfaces. Add the distinct error glyph, attention styling, a summary from the error message, expanded error detail, and the same initial disclosure treatment as failures. Reuse the strip's existing structure and the pane's established error presentation. Update [the assertion-strip contract](../../tools/story/spec/004-Assertions.md#canvas-assertion-strip-structured-rows) and add focused component tests using the real exception-record shape, alongside a healthy control. Keep this bounded to displaying records already supplied to the strip.

**Accepted limit and validation.** Tests replaces the canvas (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs:851-860`), so A + E deliberately leaves the Tests-only view at "No tests registered". That remains an acceptable distinction for a variant without tests; a later demonstrated workflow problem could justify B. I ran three existing JVM tests—missing-handler setup, throwing setup, and pasted upgrade output—through `clojure.test/test-vars`: **3 tests, 17 assertions, zero failures/errors**, process exit 0. The additional runtime probes also completed. Java used the existing cached classpath and stdin, without creating a probe file. I did not run CLJS tests or a browser; the rendered presentation and proposed repair are conclusions from source inspection, not newly measured browser behavior.

title: fix(story-ui): schema validation shows a raw Malli explain map inline, because format-explain only formats :errors when it is a vector
description:
Surfaced by worker storyschema-a while walking the login testbed Controls for rf2-wmoer (PR #9800). Verified by the mayor at trunk 9a73081044 for symptom 1 only.

SYMPTOM 1, VERIFIED AT SOURCE: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/schema_validation.cljc format-explain (:263) formats an explanation only when (:errors explanation) is a VECTOR (:279). Otherwise it falls through to pr-str of the whole map (:289). The worker observed the inline error under a Controls field rendering the raw Malli explain map when a :heading value was cleared, i.e. the explanation reached format-explain with :errors not a vector. Confirm the actual type Malli returns for :errors at tip (a list or seq is the likely case) before fixing; a (sequential? ...) check is the obvious shape, but verify.

SYMPTOM 2, A CLAIM, NOT VERIFIED BY THE MAYOR: the Schema validation panel keeps reporting no args violations while Controls flags the same cleared value. That is either the same explanation-shape issue in a second reader, or the panel validating a different value (the stored args, not the live control override). Reproduce first; if it is a different defect, say so and fix only what shares a cause with symptom 1.

ACCEPTANCE: clearing the login-card :heading on the login_form testbed shows a readable path-plus-message inline error, not a map; the panel and Controls agree about whether a violation exists. Add a pure JVM test of format-explain over the explanation shape Malli actually returns.

FENCE: schema_validation.cljc and its tests; the panel reader if symptom 2 shares the cause. Not a hot zone. No live worker holds these files.

GATES: tools/story JVM tests (format-explain is pure and JVM-testable per its docstring) and the tools/story UI CLJS tests.
notes:
## Worker verdict (worker/storyvalid-a, PR #9806), verified at source at trunk 9a73081044

SYMPTOM 1 — FIXED in PR #9806. Measured on the JVM, malli 0.20.1: `malli.core/explain` over the login card schema `[:map [:heading {:optional true} [:string {:min 1}]]]` with `{:heading ""}` returns `:errors` as `clojure.lang.PersistentVector$ChunkedSeq` (vector? false, sequential? true). The per-entry explanation `args-violations` produces is the same shape. The error maps carry `:path :in :schema :value` and NO `:message`. `format-explain` now checks `sequential?`; it stays pure. Other callers (controls.cljs args-row, the panel's args and trace rows, view_state.cljc override failures) all receive either this Malli shape, nil, or a non-map, so the one check covers them. No existing test pinned the old pr-str fallback for a non-vector `:errors` map. The new test builds its fixture from real `m/explain` calls and guards that `:errors` is not a vector. Control: with the fix reverted, the new test went red (2 assertion failures showing the raw pr-str map); restored and verified by blob hash.

Residual, not fixed: because Malli errors carry no `:message`, the inline Controls text now reads `schema: (root): schema violation`. That is readable but generic. Humanised text would need `malli.error`, which is a separate and deliberate choice.

SYMPTOM 2 — CONFIRMED, and it is a DIFFERENT DEFECT (not the explanation shape), so it is NOT fixed here. It is left for the mayor to file.
- Controls `args-editor` validates `(rf.story.plan/effective-args variant-id {:active-modes (:active-modes shell) :cell-overrides overrides})`, which is the live override.
- The Schema validation `panel` validates `(rf.story.plan/effective-args variant-id)` with no opts, so `rf.story.args/run-arg-layers` supplies `:post [{}]` and no active modes. The panel therefore validates the STORED variant args, never the live control override.
- The panel also derefs only the trace buffer, never `rf.story.ui.state/shell-state-atom`, so it would not re-render on a control change even with correct opts.
- Re-enacted on the JVM over the production registrars (the login card view with its `:rf/props`, the variant's `{:heading "Sign in"}`, override `{:heading ""}`): the panel expression resolved `{:heading "Sign in"}` and 0 violations; the Controls expression resolved `{:heading ""}` and `[:heading]`. It is a separate defect and is not fixed by PR #9806.

title: Run propagation stops at machine spawn: per-call :fx-overrides, :trace-id and :origin do not reach a spawned child's cascade
description:
FILED 2026-09-13 by the mayor from httpfinal-a's PR #9780 report (rf2-6gxs), which observed that a per-call `:fx-overrides` on the opening `dispatch-sync` did NOT reach a `:spawn-all` child's `:rf.http/managed` request on the JVM; the real transport ran, and the worker's tests had to fall back to a per-frame override. VERIFIED AT SOURCE by the mayor at trunk 92b220e32c.

THE RULE. `spec/002-Frames.md` §Run propagation (about :2440): "All three override types propagate transitively through any depth of `:fx [:dispatch ...]` child dispatches ... the dispatched child inherits the parent envelope's overrides (and `:frame`, `:trace-id`, `:origin`). One mechanism: envelope-field-copying when queueing children." The drain pseudocode carries it as `inheritable-envelope-keys` = `[:frame :fx-overrides :interceptor-overrides :trace-id :origin]` (about :2231).

THE GAP. The machine spawn path queues its children through a FRESH router dispatch, not through that mechanism. `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc` (about :147-149) dispatches the spawn-done completion with only `{:frame frame-id :source :machine-spawn}`, and its docstring says the spawn fx dispatches `:start` into a newborn child the same way (and `dispatch-spawn-error!` likewise). So at the spawn boundary the cascade loses per-call `:fx-overrides`, `:interceptor-overrides`, `:trace-id` and `:origin`. `spec/005-StateMachines.md` is silent on it (0 hits for `fx-overrides`, against a control of 95 for `:spawn-all`), so nothing normative scopes spawn OUT of run propagation either.

WHY IT MATTERS. Per-call `:fx-overrides` is the documented test seam (the `dispatch-with` successor); a test that stubs HTTP per call for a machine that spawns children silently hits the real transport. And losing `:origin` defeats the actor filter §Run propagation names ("show me only the dispatches I (the pair tool) issued") for everything a spawned machine does.

THE CORRECTION. Make a spawn a "queueing children" edge: the machine's spawn-lifecycle router dispatches (newborn `:start`, spawn-done completion, spawn-error, and any sibling site the same fx family uses) carry the parent envelope's inheritable keys, read from the fx ctx's `(:envelope m)`, exactly as `:dispatch` does, while keeping their own `:source :machine-spawn`. One sentence in 002 §Run propagation and one in 005's spawn section saying so. Out of scope: machine `:after` timer wake-ups (002 already says `:fx-overrides` cannot reach them; they are fresh causal tokens) and any general actor-envelope policy.

REGRESSION. On JVM AND CLJS, a per-call `:fx-overrides` on `dispatch-sync` into a parent that `:spawn`s and `:spawn-all`s children reaches an fx the CHILDREN fire; a per-frame override still works; `:source` stays `:machine-spawn`; `:origin` and `:trace-id` arrive on the child's dispatches. A user fx id overridden per call is enough; it need not be HTTP. Show it RED before, GREEN after.
notes:
VERDICT (spawnprop-a worker, 2026-09-13) — PR #9790, branch worker/spawnprop-a, rebased onto trunk 6f8cd459b2.

PREMISE: HOLDS AT THE SPAWN SITE, AND THE BEAD'S "READ IT FROM (:envelope m)" HOLDS ONLY THERE. Every router dispatch the machine spawn lifecycle makes, verified at source:
1. The newborn `:start` / synthetic `[:rf.machine.spawn/spawned]`, in `lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc` (`spawn-fx*`). This runs inside the `:rf.machine/spawn` fx, so `(:envelope m)` is reachable. It covers `:spawn` and `:spawn-all` alike, since `:spawn-all` lowers to one `:rf.machine/spawn` per child. CARRIED.
2. The spawn-done completion carrier, `dispatch-spawn-done!` in `lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc`. NOT CARRIED.
3. The spawn-error carrier, `dispatch-spawn-error!` in `lifecycle_fx/spawn_error.cljc`, reached from `finalize-machine` and from `registration.cljc`'s action-exception route. NOT CARRIED.
Sites 2 and 3 run inside the finishing child's machine HANDLER body, not an fx. The router surfaces only `:source`, `:trace-id` and the resolved mint policy to a handler, so `:fx-overrides`, `:interceptor-overrides` and `:origin` are unreachable there, and carrying them needs an `implementation/core` change. Per the brief that is a STOP. The exact core change, plus the two decisions it needs (completion mint-policy inheritance, which `join_strict_mint_cljs_test.cljc` records as deliberately not done, and which envelope a completion should inherit), is filed as rf2-ix8fd. The `:after` timer wake-up in `timer.cljc` is the only other `:router/dispatch!` site; it is out of scope as ruled.

THE FIX. The bootstrap dispatch now queues through core's public reserved-dispatch seam `rf.fx/child-dispatch!`, with the spawning envelope minus `:rf.machine/internal?`. That reuses the reserved `:dispatch` fx's own key set and cascade-exclusion filter rather than redeclaring the list, so it also carries the per-call `:rf.cofx/mint-policy`. It keeps its own `:source :machine-spawn`, and dropping the internal flag keeps the newborn's first event FIFO, as before. There is one sentence each in `spec/002-Frames.md` §Run propagation and `spec/005-StateMachines.md` §`:source` classification — `:machine-spawn`.

REGRESSION. `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/spawn_run_propagation_cljs_test.cljc` runs on JVM and CLJS, over a `:spawn` parent (explicit `:start`) and a `:spawn-all` parent (synthetic kick-off). It pins that:
- a per-call `:fx-overrides` on `dispatch-sync` reaches an fx the CHILDREN fire;
- `:origin` and `:trace-id` arrive on the child's dispatch envelope;
- the spawn dispatch keeps `:source :machine-spawn` and is not machine-internal;
- a per-frame override still reaches the children;
- with no override the real fx runs.

Evidence:

They dispatch a per-call `:rf.http/managed-test-stub` override into a parent spawning the HTTP wrapper, and assume that stub "NEVER replies". With an empty route map it actually synthesises a transport failure. They only passed because the override never reached the wrapper, i.e. they encoded this bug.

title: docs(reagent-slim): three IMPL-SPEC register rows are stale at tip — R-002 overstated, R-005 half wrong, R-006 citation does not land
description:
Three rows of the reagent-slim IMPL-SPEC risk register are factually wrong at tip. Found by the
rf2-ll79 worker while re-deriving R-007 (PR #9695), reported rather than fixed because widening past
R-007 was not authorised. Each claim below is the WORKER'S measurement and is a CLAIM to re-check at
source, not a finding.

* R-002 — OVERSTATED. It describes tests constructing `create-class` "with each of" nine named keys.
  The implementation is a 7-key ALLOW-LIST (`cap-keys`, `remove cap-keys`), so there is no enumerated
  banned roster, and the tests name 3 of the 9. This is NOT a coverage hole — the allow-list plus the
  7-key set test determines all nine — so the repair is to the row's description of the mitigation,
  not to the tests. Do not add tests for this.

* R-005 — HALF WRONG. `useTransition` appears NOWHERE in the reagent-slim artefact except in R-005
  itself. The cited `dom/client_cljs_test.cljs` genuinely carries 21 deftests on `flush-views!`,
  determinism and Suspense, so that half of the row holds; its single "transitions" hit is prose
  about reaction state. Correct the useTransition half, keep the rest.

* R-006 — CITATION DOES NOT LAND. `monkey` reads 0 hits in
  `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` (control: `10x` reads 5, M-42 present). That README
  documents swapping re-frame-10x for Xray and M-42's removed surfaces, not the monkey-patch
  breakage the row cites it for. The row's SUBSTANTIVE POSITION is consistent with the tree — only
  the citation is wrong, so re-point it or drop it; do not rewrite the position.

R-001, R-003 and R-004 were checked in the same pass and HOLD — every cited file exists and every
cited symbol or allow-list resolves. Do not re-audit them.

title: docs(api): a systemic two-column continuation convention splits the bullet list on ~40 reader-facing pages (438 escaped blocks)
description:
`docs/api/*.md` CARRIES ONE SYSTEMIC MARKDOWN CONVENTION THAT SPLITS EVERY BULLET LIST IT
APPEARS IN, ACROSS ROUGHLY 40 READER-FACING PAGES.

The shape: a `- **Description**:` bullet followed by two-column continuation paragraphs. A
two-column continuation does not reach the list item's content column, so python-markdown
ends the item, **CLOSES THE `<ul>`**, and starts a new list after the paragraph.

**THE RENDER IS NOT SUBTLY WRONG.** This is not a lost nesting level that a careful reader
might not notice -- the bullet list visibly splits in two, with body prose stranded between
the halves. It is the most reader-facing markdown defect measured in this corpus.

=== MEASURED, BY RENDERING, NOT BY COUNTING SPACES ===

By the `check_flattened_lists.py` instrument built under rf2-gyq4 (PR #9615), which renders
each file with python-markdown under the exact extension list `mkdocs.yml` produces, injects
a sentinel into each candidate continuation line and asks whether the sentinel landed inside
an `<li>`:

    450 escaped continuation BLOCKS corpus-wide
    438 of them in `docs/`   -- overwhelmingly this convention in `docs/api/*.md`
     12 in `spec/`
      3 files the probe REFUSES rather than grading

Four sites of this class were repaired under rf2-luch in #9615 because they BLOCKED
rf2-qsjr's flattened-nesting repairs. **The rest were deliberately left**: ~40 files with a
large blast radius is a separate PR, not something to fold into a gate landing.

=== WHY THIS IS NOT rf2-luch, AND NOT rf2-qsjr ===

rf2-qsjr was FLATTENED NESTING -- a child list item that fails to nest. Its repair is a pure
reindent, which is why its evidence could be element-for-element (+69 list elements for 69
sites).

This class is different and its repair MOVES PROSE INTO A LIST ITEM, which changes the
"ordered sequence of each list item's own text" invariant BY CONSTRUCTION. rf2-qsjr's
invariants refuse it by design. #9615 established the replacement property that does work:

  * **I1'** -- the ordered sequence of non-empty BLOCK-LEVEL text units (direct text of a
    block element). This permits a paragraph changing parent and the tight-to-loose
    promotion, while still forbidding merge, split, vanish and reorder.
  * **I2** -- whole-document text content (unchanged from rf2-qsjr).
  * **I3** -- non-list HTML with `ul`/`ol`/`li`/`p` stripped (unchanged).
  * **I4** -- NO NEW `<pre>`. This is the one that refuses the half-fix outright, because
    over-indenting a continuation turns it into an indented code block, backticks and all,
    which is worse than the escape.

**Use those four. Do not re-derive them, and do not fall back to rf2-qsjr's set.**

=== A COUNTING CAVEAT THAT BIT ONCE ALREADY ===

Element counts do NOT go up one-per-site for this repair, and a reviewer expecting rf2-qsjr's
signature will read that as a miss. Measured on the four sites already repaired: **+3 rendered
list elements across 4 sites, not +4.** The repair adds a nesting level (+1) AND rejoins the
list the escaped paragraph had split (-1); in `re-frame.resources.md` those cancel exactly
(+0) while its defect still goes 1 to 0. **Grade by the gate's own defect count going to
zero, per file, not by an element delta.**

=== THE GATE ALREADY EXISTS AND WILL GRADE THIS ===

`scripts/check_flattened_lists.py` runs in `test.yml`'s `verify-readme-links` job and in the
fast-PR spine. It reports this class as ESCAPED, names the file and line, and distinguishes
it from the CODE-BLOCK case on `in_code` first. So a worker taking this bead has a live
instrument on arrival and does not need to build one -- run it, fix what it names, and watch
the count go to zero.

=== SIZING AND SEQUENCING ===

~40 files, all under `docs/api/`, all prose. No hot-zone file is involved. It does not block
anything and nothing blocks it. It is a good candidate for splitting across two or three
dispatches by directory if one worker finds it too large -- say so rather than half-finishing
a file.

title: release: a tools-tier recovery bump cascades to a full 19-artefact re-publish (rewrite-local-root-coord.sh pins all siblings at repo-root VERSION)
description:
Found while dossiering rf2-pv7p (tools-tier first tags). No bead acknowledges this.

THE CASCADE: `rewrite-local-root-coord.sh` pins EVERY sibling coordinate at the single
repo-root VERSION. So a tools-tier recovery bump cannot ship alone. Tagging
`xray-v0.0.1.alpha-1` to recover a bad xray publish would pin nine FRAMEWORK artefacts at
`0.0.1.alpha-1` — versions that do not exist on Clojars — so the recovery cascades into a
full 19-artefact re-publish.

WHY IT MATTERS: Clojars has no yank. Recovery from a bad publish is bump-and-supersede,
and this makes the cheapest tools-tier recovery a whole-repo re-publish. That is a
materially different risk profile from what the docs describe, and it is invisible at the
moment you would need to know it — mid-recovery, under pressure.

WHAT THE DOCS SAY: `docs/release-process.md:174-177` states only that the framework goes
"out of lockstep". It does not say a tools-tier bump republishes the framework.

EVIDENCE: `tools/xray/deps.edn:75` declares machines-viz as a top-level runtime
coordinate; `tools/story/deps.edn:67` declares xray. Each release workflow rewrites those
`:local/root` coords to `:mvn/version` and resolves from Clojars before deploying
(`release-machines-viz.yml:274-282`, `release-story.yml:369-377`; xray's equivalent gate
is `preflight-xray-package.sh:135`).

WORK: decide whether this is (i) accepted and merely DOCUMENTED in
`docs/release-process.md` alongside the existing lockstep paragraph, or (ii) fixed so a
tools-tier bump can pin siblings at their own published versions rather than the repo-root
VERSION. Option (i) is likely right pre-alpha — trust the operator, document the sharp
edge — but the call has not been made. Sequence BEFORE the tools-tier tag (rf2-pv7p), since
its value is entirely in knowing this before a recovery is needed.
notes:
RULED (i) -- DOCUMENT THE SHARP EDGE. Mike, 2026-09-09, via dispatch. Option (ii) (fix it so a
tools-tier bump can pin siblings at their own published versions) is NOT to be implemented, and
the machinery to make it possible is NOT to be built. Reasoning is the standing posture: pre-alpha,
trust the operator, and a versioning subsystem to make one rare recovery cheaper is exactly the
over-engineering the posture refuses. What the operator needs is to KNOW this before a recovery,
and that is prose. Recording the ruling here because it was made in dispatch and nowhere else.

DELIVERED in PR #9549: two paragraphs added to docs/release-process.md after the tools-tier
Recovery paragraph, stating the cascade, why it exists, and what it costs (sixteen artefacts
republished to replace one; nineteen to restore lockstep across the repo).

CLAIMS THAT VERIFIED AT TIP (f12d8c310d): tools/xray/deps.edn:75 machines-viz as a top-level
:local/root runtime coord, line exact, no :exclusions. release-machines-viz.yml rewrite :257-266
and cold resolve :278. release-story.yml rewrite :344-361 (five roots) and cold resolve :373.
"Nine framework artefacts" -- correct: release-xray.yml:245-259 loops ten roots, nine under
implementation/ plus ../machines-viz. "19-artefact re-publish" -- correct: 14 framework +
5 tool jars, per verify-version-lockstep.sh:139 and :892. And the cascade was indeed NOT already
documented -- implied by :151 and :153-156, never concluded.

CLAIMS THAT DID NOT HOLD, both corrected in the delivered text:

(1) "rewrite-local-root-coord.sh pins EVERY sibling coordinate at the single repo-root VERSION"
is FALSE AS STATED. The script rewrites EXACTLY ONE coordinate per invocation -- the one whose
:local/root equals $1 -- at whatever version is passed as $2, and aborts unless that coordinate
matches exactly once. It never reads the repo-root VERSION file. The single-version pinning is a
CALLER convention: each release workflow loops its roster passing one $VERSION taken from
needs.verify-version.outputs.version. The delivered text attributes the behaviour to the workflow.
CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING IF THIS IS EVER REVISITED: because the script already accepts a
per-coordinate version, option (ii) would have been materially cheaper than this bead assumed.
The ruling stands regardless -- it was made on posture, not on cost.

(2) tools/story/deps.edn:67 -- the coordinate is real but has MOVED to :96-97 and now carries
:exclusions [day8/reagent-slim], added on trunk under a load-bearing comment at :68.

(3) "preflight-xray-package.sh:135 is xray's clojure -P equivalent" is HALF RIGHT. Xray has NO
executable clojure -P anywhere; the only occurrence in release-xray.yml is prose in a comment at
:60. Line 135 is `clojure -M:clein pom`, which forces the cold resolve as a SIDE EFFECT while the
script's actual assertions are pom-content checks. The delivered text says "fails at dependency
resolution" without naming a command, so it is correct for all three workflows. That finding also
means docs/release-process.md:158 and :162 are themselves inaccurate -- filed as rf2-rghc, NOT
fixed in #9549 because a correct fix touches release-xray.yml, outside that lane's surface.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in PR #9549 (`9d291f4e5b` on trunk), merged at band 87 on all five clauses: 87 distinct checks (band re-measured this tick, the five previously merged PRs all at 87), 67 SKIPPED / 20 SUCCESS, **0** failure-or-cancelled, **0** non-terminal, all four workflow runs completed at the full head oid `bdceddf0b2`, workflow diff against merge-base = 0 lines, `git merge-tree --write-tree` rc=0.

**RULED (i) BY THE MAYOR, not deferred to Mike**: document the sharp edge, do not build machinery to soften it. The bead left (i) vs (ii) open and leaned (i) itself. The reasoning is the standing posture — pre-alpha, trust the operator, and a versioning subsystem to make one rare recovery cheaper is exactly the over-engineering the posture refuses. `docs/release-process.md` now records the cascade alongside the existing lockstep paragraph. No workflow, no script, no `rewrite-local-root-coord.sh` change.

## THREE OF THIS BEAD'S SOURCE CLAIMS WERE FALSE AT TIP, INCLUDING ITS CENTRAL MECHANISM

**1. The headline mechanism is wrong as written.** The bead says `rewrite-local-root-coord.sh` "pins EVERY sibling coordinate at the single repo-root VERSION". It does not: it rewrites **exactly one** coordinate per invocation at a version passed as `$2`, and it never reads the `VERSION` file at all. The uniformity is a CALLER convention in each release workflow's loop, not a property of the script. The landed prose attributes it to the workflow, which is where it actually lives.

**That correction has a consequence the bead's own framing hides**: because the script already takes a per-coordinate version, **option (ii) would have been cheaper than the bead implied**. The ruling still stands — it was made on posture, not on cost, and a cheaper (ii) is still a subsystem we do not want pre-alpha — but the record should not pretend the option was expensive. Anyone reopening this should reopen it on the posture argument, not on a cost estimate that was never right.

**2.** `tools/story/deps.edn:67` has moved to :96-97 and now carries `:exclusions [day8/reagent-slim]` — the exclusion [[rf2-qvyr]] landed this same session, exactly as the dispatch predicted it would have.

**3.** `preflight-xray-package.sh:135` is `clojure -M:clein pom`, not `clojure -P`. Xray has no executable `clojure -P` anywhere; the only occurrence in `release-xray.yml` is prose. The landed text says "fails at dependency resolution" without naming a command, so it is correct for all three workflows.

**What DID verify at tip**: `tools/xray/deps.edn:75` exactly; the rewrite-and-resolve steps in `release-machines-viz.yml` and `release-story.yml`; "nine framework artefacts" (xray's loop covers ten roots — nine under `implementation/` plus machines-viz); the "19-artefact re-publish" arithmetic (14+5); and that the cascade genuinely was not already documented.

## A SPIN-OFF FILED RATHER THAN ABSORBED

Finding 3 means `docs/release-process.md:158` and `:162` are themselves inaccurate, as is a comment in `release-xray.yml`. The worker did NOT fix it — a correct repair touches a workflow, which is a hot-zone surface outside that lane. Filed as [[rf2-rghc]]. Correct call: the boundary held even though the fix was in front of it.

## GATES

`python -m mkdocs build --strict` 0; `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` 0; all 43 `scripts/check_*.py` ratchets 0; `check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh` 0; `check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh` 0; `check-commit-attribution.sh` 0. All on the final rebased base.

Both nominated gates proven to read the worker's own tree by planted faults, necessary because the slug gate writes zero bytes on success: a broken anchor took it to exit 1 naming `docs/release-process.md:178`; a broken file link took mkdocs to exit 1 naming the plant. Restores verified by git **blob** hash, not by reading a diff. The ratchet loop itself was controlled — a deliberate failure propagated rc=7 — so the all-green sweep is a real measurement rather than a loop that cannot fail.

**And one of my own brief's premises was verified rather than assumed**: `mkdocs --strict` NAMED the planted anchor on stdout and still EXITED 0, confirming that `check_doc_slugs.py` is genuinely the only anchor gate.

## MY DISPATCH ERROR, RECORDED

My brief told the worker its worktree and branch were "already created and checked out". Neither existed — I never ran the worktree-creation step for this lane. The worker created both from `origin/main` and proceeded, since the direction was set, and reported the discrepancy rather than silently absorbing it. No harm resulted, but the brief asserted a precondition I had not performed.
