title: implementation/machines: three identical dedup-accumulator closures in cofx_attach.cljc — extract one, keep the volatile+transient
description:
SURFACE: implementation/machines (22,661 production lines, 0.5 mutations/kloc — one of the cleanest large surfaces). Found by the 2026-09-07 FP audit (rf2-5941).

THE MUTATION IS CORRECT AND MUST STAY. This is the lifecycle-diet walk over machine states, and it uses a volatile! around a transient for accumulation plus a volatile! set for dedup. That is the documented hot-zone exception: the walk runs during cofx attachment over every state in a machine spec, and the sibling namespace core/source_coords.cljc explains at length why the volatile!-around-transient shape is required rather than a bare transient (a transient array-map promotes to a transient hash-map on its 9th distinct key and RETURNS A NEW OBJECT, so assoc!'s return value cannot be discarded). The same reasoning applies here to conj!.

THE DEFECT IS THAT THE SAME add! CLOSURE IS WRITTEN THREE TIMES, in implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/cofx_attach.cljc:
  line 601-605
  line 779-783
  line 837-841

All three are the same shape:

    add! (fn [diet]
           (doseq [{:keys [id] :as e} diet]
             (when-not (contains? @seen-ids id)
               (vswap! seen-ids conj id)
               (vswap! acc conj e))))

Each is a dedup-on-:id accumulator over a "diet" sequence, closing over locally-bound seen-ids and acc volatiles. The three occurrences sit in different walk contexts (flat states, region walk, scope walk) but the closure body is the same dedup contract each time.

WHY IT MATTERS. The dedup key is :id and the ordering guarantee is first-wins. Neither is stated anywhere — it is implicit in three copies of the same four lines. If a future change needs dedup on a composite key, or needs last-wins, it has to be found in three places, and a partial edit produces a walk that dedups inconsistently between the flat and region paths. That is a silent correctness divergence, not a style issue.

ACTION: extract one helper taking the two volatiles and returning the closure:

    (defn- dedup-adder
      "Returns a fn that conj!es each entry of the diet onto acc unless its
       :id is already in seen-ids. First occurrence wins. Both args are
       volatiles around transients — see the promotion note in
       re-frame.source-coords."
      [seen-ids acc])

and call it at all three sites. State the :id key and the first-wins rule in that one docstring.

CHECK BEFORE EXTRACTING, and report if it is not true: that all three really do close over volatiles of the same shape, and that none of the three has an extra clause the audit's reading missed. The audit read the three closure bodies, not the surrounding let-bindings in full.

GATES: clojure -M:test from implementation/machines/, plus npm run test:cljs. Pure refactor, no behaviour change intended; if the machines suite goes red, the three sites were not identical and that is the finding.

RELATED: rf2-soie is the same class of defect (justified local mutation, triplicated) in tools/story. Two independent instances is why rf2-5941 calls it a pattern worth watching rather than two one-offs.
acceptance_criteria: One dedup-adder helper; three call sites; :id key and first-wins documented once; machines suite green.
notes:
DELIVERED 2026-09-07. PR #9360, merged as 9ae1b0029c.

WHAT LANDED. One private `dedup-adder` helper in
implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/cofx_attach.cljc, taking
[seen-ids acc] and returning the closure. Three call sites, exactly as the bead
specified.

THE TWO CHECKS THE BEAD ASKED FOR, BOTH RUN.

(1) "That all three really do close over volatiles of the same shape, and that
none of the three has an extra clause the audit's reading missed." CONFIRMED for
the closures: all three bodies are BYTE-IDENTICAL, verified by pairwise diff of
the extracted line ranges with leading whitespace stripped (the only difference
between site 1 and site 2 was the trailing `]` closing the enclosing let-binding
vector). No site carries an extra clause. The three contexts are the
flat/compound scope walk (ensure-set-in-scope), the parallel-region union
(ensure-set-for), and the initial-descent birth set (birth-ensure-set).

(2) PREMISE CORRECTION, and the bead asked to be told if the check failed. THE
ACCUMULATORS ARE NOT VOLATILES AROUND TRANSIENTS. The bead's description — "it
uses a volatile! around a transient for accumulation plus a volatile! set for
dedup" and "the same reasoning applies here to conj!" — is half right. At all
three sites:
    acc      (volatile! [])     ; volatile around a PERSISTENT VECTOR
    seen-ids (volatile! #{})    ; volatile around a PERSISTENT SET
Neither is transient. The transients that DO exist in this namespace are the
local `diet` transients built by `add-lifecycle!` and `add-scope!`, and those
are `persistent!`-ed before they are ever handed to `add!` — so they never meet
the closure the bead is about, and this change does not touch them.

The volatile is still load-bearing at these sites, but for the ordinary reason
rather than the source_coords one: `conj` on a persistent collection returns a
new object, so the return has to be captured somewhere, and `add!` is called
from several mutually-recursive helpers that take it as an argument, so there is
no single reduction to thread a value through. The source_coords array-map
promotion argument (a transient array-map promotes to a transient hash-map on
its 9th distinct key and RETURNS A NEW OBJECT, so assoc!'s return cannot be
discarded) is the STRICTER case and does not arise here. The new docstring says
that accurately and cites re-frame.source-coords as the exemplar for the
stricter case rather than claiming this is one — a wrong cross-reference would
be worse than none, and the next reader who follows it must not conclude that
these two volatiles wrap transients.

NOTHING WAS REMOVED. Both volatiles stay; the callers' local diet transients
stay; the walk shape is unchanged.

WHAT THE DOCSTRING NOW STATES, which is the bead's actual deliverable: the dedup
key is :id, and FIRST OCCURRENCE WINS — a later entry carrying an :id already
seen is dropped whole, not merged and not replacing the entry already
accumulated. Neither fact was written down anywhere before; both were implicit
in three copies of four lines. It also states why that matters: it is what makes
the ensure-set declaration-order-insensitive, which the walks' own docstrings
already promise to callers without saying what enforces it.

PROPORTIONALITY. One `defn-` in the same namespace, placed ahead of its three
consumers and of the two helpers (on-done-diet-for-event, after-diet-for-event)
that take `add!` as a parameter. No new namespace, no protocol, no macro. No
public name moves.

CONCURRENCY. The bead's file sits inside worker/machines-a's artefact. The
collision check was re-run three times against origin/worker/machines-a,
including after that branch force-pushed a rebased 11-commit history
(head 4f4a5c133471d05dec507d126bf92d871d62e993): cofx_attach.cljc appears in
none of its diffs against origin/main. Control on the same command read 11 files
touched under implementation/machines/src, so the search was live rather than
vacuously empty.

GATES (exit codes captured on the same command line as the redirect, never read
through a pipe):
  sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh                     exit 0   PASS fast PR spine
  clojure -M:test in implementation/machines     exit 0
  python scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py  exit 0
The spine's JVM tier picked up implementation/machines by construction — its
PASS line enumerates the artefact suites it SKIPPED and machines is not among
them.

ASSERTION COUNTS, implementation/machines, before and after the extraction —
taken by reverting the file to its merge-base content, running, restoring,
re-running, with the restore verified by git blob hash rather than by reading a
diff:
  BEFORE  1244 tests / 4528 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors
  AFTER   1244 tests / 4528 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors
Identical. The bead said "if the machines suite goes red, the three sites were
not identical and that is the finding" — it did not, and they were.

SABOTAGE CONTROL. Neutering dedup-adder's guard reddened the suite at exit 1
with 72 failures, at the same 1244/4528 totals (so the plant crashed no
namespace and truncated no lane). The plant existed only in the worker worktree,
so the red is positive evidence the gate read this tree rather than a sibling
checkout. Restored from HEAD, confirmed by blob hash.
close_reason: PR #9360 merged; verified HEAD == origin/main. The three identical dedup-accumulator closures in implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/cofx_attach.cljc are now one. The volatile!-around-transient shape was correctly KEPT: a transient array-map promotes to a hash-map on its 9th distinct key and returns a NEW object, so conj!/assoc! return values cannot be discarded — the same reasoning source_coords.cljc documents at length. FENCE NOTE: this file sits inside worker/machines-a's artefact, which was live throughout; the collision did not materialise, and machines-a's own PR #9353 is still open, so expect a rebase there rather than here.

title: FP audit 2026-09-07: /implementation /tools /examples reviewed for functional discipline — 391,400 lines, 46 surfaces, verdict PASS with two duplication defects
description:
FULL-TREE REVIEW of functional-programming discipline across every distinct surface under implementation/, tools/ and examples/, per Mike's 2026-09-07 request: is the code functional, and is imperative code confined to hot performance zones?

HEADLINE: THE CODEBASE IS STRONGLY FUNCTIONAL AND THE HOT-ZONE RULE IS BEING FOLLOWED. This audit did not find a systemic problem. It found two concrete duplication defects (filed separately) and one convention gap. Recording the clean result matters as much as the findings, so a later sweep does not re-derive it.

=== UNIVERSE, and how to reproduce it ===
819 tracked production source files, 391,400 lines, 46 surfaces. Definition: *.clj/.cljs/.cljc under implementation/, tools/, examples/, EXCLUDING test/, tests/, testbed(s)/, test_kit/, evals/, fixture(s)/ — production code only, since test code is allowed mutation freely.

INSTRUMENT NOTE, because two readings in this audit were wrong before they were right. (a) 'rg' in this shell is a FUNCTION wrapping the claude binary, so it is invisible to xargs — 'xargs ... rg' fails with 'No such file or directory' and a pipeline reports 0 matches with exit 0. Every census below was therefore taken with rg's own -g globs, and the universe was CONTROLLED against git ls-files: both read exactly 819 files with zero difference in either direction. (b) A per-file shell loop over 819 files exceeds the 120s tool timeout on this box; use one rg pass plus awk aggregation, or xargs with a real binary.

=== CENSUS (occurrences, production only) ===
swap!/reset! 1105 · transient/persistent! 454 · set! 416 · (atom 386 · defonce 357 · doseq 279 · loop 189 · volatile!/vswap! 138

Density leaders (mutations per kloc): adapters/test-react 32.1 (592 lines, local-test-only artefact, not shipped), flows 12.1, epoch 8.1, story 5.6, http 4.9, adapters/reagent-slim 4.8, core 4.1. Everything else under 4. Twenty-one of the 46 surfaces read 0.0.

=== VERDICT PER TREE ===
EXAMPLES — CLEAN, and this is the strongest result in the audit. Every single mutation site across all 20 example surfaces was read. All are justified: React root handles held in 'defonce ... (atom nil)' for HMR (uix counter/login/dashboard, hicasso login), or DELIBERATE MOCK BACKENDS simulating an external stateful system (realworld_http/http.cljs demo-state, realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs, patterns/websocket/messages.cljs sockets-by-actor + mock-server-state). Modelling a fake server as a mutable cell is the right shape, not a lapse. One nit, not worth its own bead: examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/core.cljs:171 keeps a module-level 'optimistic-id-seq' counter for temp ids, in teaching material where the value could be derived from app-db; harmless, mentioned so it is not re-found.

IMPLEMENTATION — CLEAN. Imperative code is confined to (i) the reactive substrate boundary, (ii) React/DOM interop, and (iii) documented hot paths. Sampled at source: core/substrate/spine.cljs (watchers, dispose hooks, active React roots, warn-once caches — all boundary state); machines' 79 doseq are all SIDE-EFFECTING registration and validation, which is exactly what doseq is for and not a finding; epoch/state.cljc holds 13 module-level defonce atoms and its namespace docstring justifies the split by ACCESS PATTERN and states that no operation needs a cross-store atomic update.

A SUSPECTED LEAK IN EPOCH WAS CHASED AND IS NOT ONE, recorded so nobody re-chases it: drop-frame-epoch-state! (state.cljc:1840) drops 5 frame-keyed stores and NOT the silence stores, which looks like unbounded growth across frame churn. It is not — open-silence-lineage! / close-silence-lineage! are balanced, the close dissocs outstanding-silence-lineages at zero and dissocs terminal-silence-marks with it (state.cljc:1332-1339, called 'the boundedness guarantee' in situ). And 'config' is a single global map, not frame-keyed, despite a docstring line that reads 'per-frame ring-buffer config'.

TOOLS — CLEAN on density (xray 1.7/kloc over 77,450 lines is the lowest of the large surfaces) with one duplication defect in story, filed separately.

=== THE ONE REAL PATTERN ===
Where this audit found defects, they are NOT 'imperative where functional would do'. They are JUSTIFIED local mutation, TRIPLICATED. Two instances, both filed:
  - tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc — three near-identical pending-atom + drain! collectors.
  - implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/cofx_attach.cljc — three identical dedup accumulators.
The atom is right in both; copying it three times is the defect. Worth watching for as a class.

=== FUNCTION-LOCAL SCRATCH ATOMS: 21 IN 391,400 LINES ===
The classic smell — '(let [x (atom ...)]' as a scratch accumulator where reduce/into would serve — occurs 21 times in the whole tree. Concentration is tools/story/frames.cljc (3, and those are the triplication above). This is the number that most supports the PASS verdict.

=== HOW THE HOT-ZONE RULE IS ACTUALLY HELD ===
169 production files use transient/volatile!/vswap!. 136 of them (80%) contain justification vocabulary in prose. THE REAL FIGURE IS HIGHER: two of the biggest apparent exceptions were instrument artefacts — core/derivation/egress.cljc's 12 'transient' hits are the DOMAIN TERM ':host-transient' (an in-flight HTTP handle) and contain no mutation at all, and core/trace/cascade.cljc documents its transients thoroughly using none of my search words. core/source_coords.cljc is the exemplar to point people at: it explains that the walker is deliberately mutation-heavy because it runs at MACRO-EXPANSION TIME on every reg-machine form, and documents why the accumulator must be a volatile! around the transient rather than a bare transient (array-map promotes to hash-map on the 9th key and returns a NEW object, so assoc!'s return cannot be discarded). That is the standard the rest of the tree is being measured against, and mostly meets.

The gap is that this discipline is a CONVENTION WITH NO SHARED VOCABULARY, which is what makes it un-auditable. Filed separately.

NO CODE WAS CHANGED BY THIS AUDIT.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded verdict; no action required on this bead itself. Its child findings are the actionable work.
notes:
2026-09-07 — BOTH DUPLICATION FINDINGS DELIVERED. PR #9360, merged as
9ae1b0029c. VERDICT ON THIS BEAD: COMPLETE AS A RECORD, NO OUTSTANDING
DELIVERABLE. Checked rather than assumed; the evidence is below. Not closed here
— that is the operator's call.

WHY IT IS COMPLETE. This bead's own acceptance criteria say it: "Recorded
verdict; no action required on this bead itself. Its child findings are the
actionable work." Its description ends "NO CODE WAS CHANGED BY THIS AUDIT". The
enumerated content resolves exhaustively:

  * "two concrete duplication defects (filed separately)" — rf2-soie and
    rf2-3oyn. Both delivered in PR #9360, both closed.
  * "one convention gap ... Filed separately" — rf2-cqs3 (deliberate-imperative
    code has no greppable marker). Open, independently tracked, P4, untouched by
    this work and not a dependency of it.
  * The two items the audit explicitly declined to file — the linearlite
    `optimistic-id-seq` module-level counter ("one nit, not worth its own bead
    ... mentioned so it is not re-found") and the chased-and-refuted epoch
    silence-store leak ("recorded so nobody re-chases it") — are cases where THE
    RECORD IS THE DELIVERABLE. Actioning either would be inventing work against
    the bead's own stated purpose.

So nothing in the description names an obligation that is still open. The 46-
surface census was deliberately NOT re-run: re-deriving it is exactly the cost
this bead exists to prevent.

THREE CORRECTIONS TO THIS RECORD'S OWN FIGURES, from reading the two defect
sites at source. Recorded here rather than left in a PR, because this bead is
the thing a later sweep will read.

(1) THE STORY TRIPLICATION WAS A NONUPLICATION. This record and rf2-soie both
say "three near-identical pending-atom + drain! collectors". The three named
`drain!` closures are real, but each of the three functions ALSO carried an
inlined "final drain" block after its listener unbinds — the same body a fourth,
fifth and sixth time — plus a `listener` closure identical modulo the frame id,
a seventh, eighth and ninth. The audit read the three `let`-bound closures and
not the trailing blocks. One factory replaced all nine.

(2) THE MACHINES ACCUMULATORS ARE NOT VOLATILES AROUND TRANSIENTS. rf2-3oyn
describes them as "a volatile! around a transient for accumulation plus a
volatile! set for dedup", and this record's own THE ONE REAL PATTERN section
inherits that framing. At all three sites the bindings are `(volatile! [])` and
`(volatile! #{})` — volatiles around PERSISTENT collections. The transients in
that namespace are the local `diet` transients built by `add-lifecycle!` /
`add-scope!`, which are `persistent!`-ed before they reach the closure. The
source_coords array-map-promotion argument is the STRICTER case and does not
apply to these three sites; source_coords remains the correct exemplar for that
case, just not an instance of it here. The distinction matters for the next
reader, because "the volatile is load-bearing" is true at both, for different
reasons: promotion returning a new object there, ordinary persistent `conj`
returning a new object here.

(3) THE SCRATCH-ATOM COUNT MOVED, and it is the figure this record leans on
hardest. "FUNCTION-LOCAL SCRATCH ATOMS: 21 IN 391,400 LINES ... Concentration is
tools/story/frames.cljc (3, and those are the triplication above). This is the
number that most supports the PASS verdict." Those three `(atom [])` are now
ONE — the factory's own — so that figure is 19, and frames.cljc's concentration
is 1. This is a delta applied to the recorded number, NOT a re-run of the
census.

WHAT THE TWO DELIVERIES SAY ABOUT "THE ONE REAL PATTERN". This record's central
claim — that where the audit found defects they are "JUSTIFIED LOCAL MUTATION,
TRIPLICATED" rather than "imperative where functional would do" — held up under
implementation. Neither fix removed a single `atom`, `volatile!` or `transient`;
both were pure deduplication. And the claim's practical stake was borne out at
one site: the story collector had ALREADY silently drifted. The final drain in
`apply-loaders-teardown!` omitted the `(pipeline-event-opts tev)` argument that
the other five copies passed, so a pipeline exception arriving after that one
walk's listener unbound lost its `:operation` / `:failing-id` attribution. Five
copies agreed, one did not, and no test pinned the difference. That is the harm
this record predicted as a class, found as an instance.
close_reason: COMPLETE AS A RECORD — closed on worker audit-a's explicit verdict, not on inference. Its own acceptance criteria say 'no action required on this bead itself'. Its two duplication findings were rf2-soie and rf2-3oyn, both delivered in PR #9360 (merged as 9ae1b0029c, blob hashes on origin/main byte-identical to commit 1881022c82) and both now closed. Its one convention gap is rf2-cqs3, which remains open and independently tracked, held for Mike on the ';; PERF:' marker question. Its two declined nits are cases where the record IS the deliverable. The worker did NOT re-run the 46-surface census — re-deriving it is precisely the cost this bead's description exists to prevent — and it did not close this bead itself, leaving that to the mayor. THE AUDIT'S HEADLINE STANDS: 819 tracked production source files, 391,400 lines, 46 surfaces, verdict PASS; the codebase is strongly functional and the hot-zone rule is being followed, with 169 files using transient/volatile!/vswap! and at least 80% carrying prose explaining why. Recording the clean result was the point.

title: beads backup remote has no retention policy — 130 .darc archives, 2.6 GB, two of them multi-GB and live
description:
Filed 2026-09-06 by the mayor while closing rf2-8az0, which reclaimed 2.4 GB but deliberately did not touch this.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (immediately after the rf2-8az0 reclaim): .beads/backup holds 130 .darc archives totalling 2.6 GB, of which two dominate — 5pqviklejsm175kig1a9gj3il21tj7qs at 1.5 GB and 7e8mhn7h6fv4ig9a0pdluahlt6h5rn21 at 1.1 GB. BOTH ARE LIVE: each returns a hit against .beads/backup/manifest, checked with a control that discriminates (the same grep returns 0 for a known-orphan name). So none of this is deletable today and nothing here suggests hand-deleting any of it.

THE POINT IS THE ABSENCE OF A POLICY, NOT THE CURRENT SIZE. The Dolt filesystem backup remote writes on a 15-minute interval and rewrites its manifest each time. rf2-8az0 established the accrual rate for .beads as a whole at roughly +100 MB/day. Nothing in that bead, in .beads/config.yaml or in any bd verb documented there establishes how long an archive stays referenced, when an old one falls out of the manifest, or whether anything ever prunes an unreferenced one. rf2-8az0's own survey found a 2.5 GB orphaned quarantine directory from 2026-08-03 that had sat unreferenced for a month with nothing to notice it — which is the shape of the risk here.

WHAT IS WANTED: establish what the backup remote's retention actually is (read bd's own configuration and the manifest's behaviour over a few rotations rather than inferring it), and decide whether it needs bounding. If archives do fall out of the manifest over time, the follow-on question is whether anything deletes them or whether unreferenced ones simply accumulate as the quarantine directory did.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: deleting any currently-referenced archive; changing the backup interval; anything touching .beads/embeddeddolt. This is a measure-and-decide bead, not a cleanup one.

NOT URGENT. Disk is not tight (348 GB free at filing) and the immediate 2.4 GB has already been recovered. P3.
notes:
NOT WORKER-DISPATCHABLE — established 2026-09-06 22:46:02 AUSEST by the mayor before dispatching it, not after. Recording so the next tick does not re-derive it.

I had this queued as a sixth dispatch (it is conflict-free against every live worker fence, which is what made it attractive) and checked its reachability first. THE SUBJECT OF THIS BEAD DOES NOT EXIST IN A WORKER WORKTREE. Measured:

  mayor checkout      .beads/backup   PRESENT
  worker worktree     .beads/backup   ABSENT
  worker worktree     .beads/embeddeddolt   ABSENT
  a worktree's .beads holds only: README.md, config.yaml, hooks, issues.jsonl, metadata.json

The cause is deliberate and is in .beads/.gitignore at tip: 'embeddeddolt/' (line 3) and 'backup/' (line 57). Only the tracked files propagate into a linked worktree; the Dolt database and the filesystem backup remote live in the primary checkout alone. So a worker dispatched here would find nothing to measure, and the two ways out are both wrong — reaching into the mayor checkout violates the worktree boundary every brief carries, and running bd from a worktree does not reach the backup remote either.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS rf2-ah6r AND rf2-8az0: infrastructure whose subject is the mayor checkout itself. It is mayor or operator work, done at fleet-zero in the primary checkout, and it should be surfaced that way rather than sitting in the ready list looking dispatchable. It is NOT urgent — 418 GB free after the rf2-ah6r gc, and the 2.4 GB this bead's parent recovered is already banked — so the natural moment is the next quiet window, alongside anything else that wants the primary checkout.

ONE SCOPE NOTE FOR WHOEVER DOES RUN IT, learned while closing rf2-8az0: the discriminating control is a grep against .beads/backup/manifest, which is a plain extension-less text file. An earlier attempt searched for *.json/*.yaml/*.manifest and found nothing either way — a zero that proved only that the glob never reached the file. Any retention finding here needs the same one-hit-one-miss control.
MAYOR 2026-09-07 04:1x AUSEST: THE OBSERVATION WINDOW THIS BEAD ASKED FOR HAS ELAPSED, AND THE MEASUREMENT DE-ESCALATES IT. All read-only; nothing was deleted, moved or configured.

This bead asked to "establish what the backup remote's retention actually is … over a few rotations rather than inferring". At a 15-minute interval, roughly 20 rotations have passed since filing. Measured now:

  archives         130 at filing  ->  155 now   (+25 in ~5 hours, consistent with a 15-min interval)
  total size       2.6 GB at filing -> 2624.6 MB now   (UNCHANGED to the tenth of a percent)

THE COUNT GREW AND THE SIZE DID NOT, and the distribution explains why:
  the two dominant archives   2550.1 MB   97.2% of the whole backup remote
  the other 153 archives         74.5 MB   averaging 0.49 MB each

SO THE 2.6 GB IN THIS BEAD'S TITLE IS 97% TWO FILES, AND BOTH ARE LIVE. I checked .beads/backup/manifest directly: both giants are referenced, once each. They are not retention candidates under any policy — they are the current backup. The thing an absent retention policy actually accumulates is the OTHER 153, and at 0.49 MB apiece the growth is about 2.4 MB/hour, or ~1.7 GB/month at today's unusually heavy cadence.

RETENTION CONFIG: THERE IS NONE, confirmed rather than inferred. .beads/config.yaml carries no retention key at all; its only backup-related content is a COMMENTED-OUT block describing a different mechanism ("JSONL backup (periodic export for off-machine recovery)", keys `enabled` and `git-repo`). So the bead's premise — that the absence of a policy is the finding rather than the current size — is exactly right, and now measured instead of asserted.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE DECISION. The bead was filed reading "2.6 GB and no policy", which invites deleting archives. The measurement says the recoverable amount today is 74.5 MB, not 2.6 GB, and the two files worth 2.55 GB must be kept. That is the same shape as rf2-gbuh's 427 — a headline number that turns out not to measure the job. Disk is not tight (348 GB free at filing), so on the project's stance this does not warrant machinery: no cleanup script, no cron, no retention implementation.

MY RECOMMENDATION: leave it. Re-measure if .beads/backup ever exceeds a threshold worth naming — 5 GB would be a reasonable trigger and is roughly two months away at today's rate, longer at a normal one. What would change the calculus is a NEW multi-GB archive appearing, since each of those is 1-1.5 GB; that is worth watching and is cheap to check (the two-giants line above). Recording this rather than closing, because the bead's own framing — policy absence, not size — remains true and a fresh mayor should not have to re-derive the distribution to see why it is not urgent.

NOTE ON MEASUREMENT METHOD, since it matters for anyone re-running this: the totals hide the shape completely. du on .beads/backup reports 2.6 GB whether the tail is 153 files or 1500; only the size distribution shows that 97% is two immovable files. Read the distribution, not the total.
close_reason:
MEASURE-AND-DECIDE BEAD, BOTH HALVES DELIVERED; the decision is LEAVE IT. Closed by the mayor 2026-09-07 21:22 AUSEST on the measurement already recorded in this bead's notes, not on a fresh assertion.

The bead asked two things: establish what the backup remote's retention actually is, and decide whether it needs bounding. (1) RETENTION IS NONE — confirmed rather than inferred: .beads/config.yaml carries no retention key, and its only backup-related content is a commented-out block describing a different mechanism. (2) IT DOES NOT NEED BOUNDING at current rates.

WHY THE ANSWER IS 'LEAVE IT' RATHER THAN 'BUILD A POLICY'. The bead's own follow-up measurement de-escalated it: of 2.6 GB, two archives hold 2550.1 MB (97.2%) and BOTH ARE LIVE, each referenced once in .beads/backup/manifest under a control that discriminates. The other 153 archives total 74.5 MB. So the recoverable amount today is 74.5 MB, not 2.6 GB — the same shape as rf2-gbuh's 427, a headline number that turns out not to measure the job. Over ~20 rotations the COUNT grew 130 -> 155 while the SIZE was unchanged to the tenth of a percent. Disk is not tight (348 GB free at filing, 418 GB after the rf2-ah6r gc). On the project stance — no over-engineering, no gold-plating — that does not warrant a cleanup script, a cron or a retention implementation.

WHAT CLOSING DOES NOT DISCARD. The prior mayor deliberately recorded rather than closed, reasoning that a fresh mayor should not have to re-derive the distribution. That concern is now answered durably instead: bd memory 'beads-backup-remote-watch-trigger' carries the distribution, the growth rate, the two measurement traps (du hides the shape — read the distribution, never the total; and the manifest is an EXTENSION-LESS file, so a *.json/*.yaml/*.manifest glob returns a zero that proves only the glob never reached it), and the re-open triggers: .beads/backup exceeding 5 GB (~2 months at the heavy rate), or a NEW multi-GB archive appearing.

ALSO RECORDED THERE, because it generalises beyond this bead: .beads/backup and .beads/embeddeddolt are gitignored and exist ONLY in the primary checkout, so this class of bead is never worker-dispatchable — it is mayor-or-operator work at fleet-zero, the same shape as rf2-ah6r and rf2-8az0.

NOTHING WAS DELETED, MOVED OR CONFIGURED by this bead or by its close. Re-open on either trigger above.

title: api(routing): DECISION — delete :rf.route/transitioned; the link door dispatches handle-url-change with cause :link
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from routing.md (ref routing.3); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

The URL-driven route commit is spelled as two event ids that are ONE function called with two constants. `:rf.route/transitioned` (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:312-314` → `routing/url_change.cljc:462-507 transitioned-handler`) and `:rf.route/handle-url-change` (`:315-317` → `:546-589 handle-url-change-handler`) both destructure the same cofx, call `require-frame-stamp!`, and hand the same map to `url-change-fx` — the ONLY differences are `:default-scroll :top` + `:cause :link` versus `:default-scroll :restore` + `:cause (url-change-cause frame opts)`. `handle-url-change` already discriminates its three doors by a data rider (`:rf.route/cause` ∈ `#{:popstate :initial :ssr}`, Spec 012:452, 531; `docs/routing/testing.md:108-127` "Say which door you meant"); the fourth door is spelled as a second event id where a fourth rider value would do, and the default scroll is a pure function of the cause. The app-facing porch is NOT in question and re-verified clean at HEAD: apps use exactly two navigation doors (`[:rf.route/navigate …]` 42 example dispatches, `[rf/route-link …]` 59 example renders; 0 example dispatches of `transitioned` / `handle-url-change` / `url-requested` / `:rf.nav/*`) and the granular `:rf.route/id|params|query` subs stay (22 app read sites, ten of them `:<-` chain inputs; the equality cut is the point). This is a framework-internal tier that tests, tools, docs and AI agents must learn.

## Evidence (all at HEAD 6445d0611ba0)

- No app dispatches either id (examples: 0 / 0); no app or tool re-registers either (`reg-event :rf.route/(transitioned|handle-url-change|url-requested)` outside routing src: 0).

## Options

**A — Collapse (recommended).** Delete `:rf.route/transitioned`. The link door dispatches `[:rf.route/handle-url-change app-url {:rf.route/cause :link :rf.route/decided? true}]`; the surviving handler derives `:default-scroll (if (= :link cause) :top :restore)`; the cause set THIS door honours is written as `#{:link :popstate :initial :ssr}` (a `:navigate` rider falls through to the rider-free resolution — `navigate` commits inline and never enters this door; `url-change-cause` gains that one exclusion or a docstring sentence, whichever is smaller). Everything else `url-change-fx` already owns — URL-before-state ordering for link activation, the `:rf.route/decided?` guard, fragment-only short-circuit, nav-token allocation, the SSR `:frame` threading — is unchanged because both handlers already pass the same map.

```clojure
;; decisions.cljc url-requested-handler, allowed branch — after
{:fx [(if replace? [:rf.nav/replace-url app-url] [:rf.nav/push-url app-url])
      [:dispatch [:rf.route/handle-url-change app-url
                  {:rf.route/cause :link :rf.route/decided? true}]]]}

;; url_change.cljc — one handler; transitioned-handler deleted
(defn handle-url-change-handler [cofx [_ url opts]]
  (let [cause (url-change-cause frame opts)]              ;; honoured set on this door: #{:link :popstate :initial :ssr}
    (url-change-fx {… :cause          cause
                      :default-scroll (if (= :link cause) :top :restore) …})))
```

Before/after for the tier that changes: a test writes `[:rf.route/handle-url-change "/x"]` and adds `{:rf.route/cause :link}` only when the cause matters (today it picks one of two ids by habit); the link door's child epoch reads `EVENT :rf.route/handle-url-change {:rf.route/cause :link}` instead of `EVENT :rf.route/transitioned`; Xray's cascade-root docstring (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/routing_helpers.cljc:452`) becomes "root ∈ {navigate, handle-url-change}" — its detection already reads the `nav-token/allocated` emit, not the event id, so no logic moves; popstate / initial / SSR unchanged.

**B — Keep both ids (status quo).** Codex: "Retaining separate well-named ingress events over the shared helper is also viable; a constant-specialised event can communicate intent without constituting another computation model." Cost: nothing moves; the written discriminator (012:37-38, 530-533, 1157-1158 "co-equal sibling handlers, not a delegate pair") stays as written; the trace row keeps reading `transitioned`.

**C — A plus rename the survivor to `:rf.route/url-changed`** (the only `:rf.route/*` event id carrying an imperative `handle-` prefix). Only defensible in the SAME PR as A: M-60 (`migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2433-2454`) shows this id was renamed once already (`:rf/url-changed` → `:rf.route/transitioned`), so a second move should be the last. Both the fable grok pass and codex lean against it ("avoid the optional extra event rename unless it clearly improves the resulting vocabulary; the implementation value comes from removing the redundant branch, not restyling every trace"). Roughly doubles the churn of A.

## Recommendation

A, without C. *Regularity over cleverness* (Principles:18): `:rf.route/planned` already carries `:cause ∈ {:navigate :link :popstate :initial :ssr}` (012:98) and three of the four URL-driven doors already ride one event with one rider; the fourth being an event id is the irregularity. *Data before magic* (Principles:46): `{:rf.route/cause :link}` is a map a test can build, assert on and diff; a second id is a name a reader must know is an alias. *One name per fact* (EP-0007, cited at 012:1146): "a link caused this URL change" is one fact with two spellings today — an id and a tag. Clojure's answer to two functions that differ by a constant is one function and the constant as an argument; `url-change-fx` already IS that function, and the two handlers are the wrapper the ethos says not to write.

## The problem

Apps have exactly two navigation doors and three route reads, and use nothing else — the July "verified clean" reading still holds at the porch. The overlap lives in the tier apps never touch but tests, tools, docs and AI agents must learn: the URL-driven commit is spelled twice.

| Spelling | Lowers to | Written discriminator |
|---|---|---|
| `[:rf.route/handle-url-change url opts]` | `url-change-fx {… :default-scroll :restore :cause (url-change-cause frame opts)}` (url_change.cljc:581-589); cause read off the `:rf.route/cause` rider ∈ `#{:popstate :initial :ssr}` | "popstate / initial / SSR; default scroll `:restore`" (spec 012:37, 531) |
| `[:rf.route/transitioned url opts]` | `url-change-fx {… :default-scroll :top :cause :link}` (url_change.cljc:499-505) — the SAME fn, two constants | "forward nav from a link click; default scroll `:top`; co-equal sibling, not a delegate" (spec 012:38, 530-533, 1157; API.md:281-282) |
| `[:rf.route/url-requested {:url :to :params :query :fragment & policy}]` | classify external → decide leave/enter → `[:rf.nav/push-url]` + `[:dispatch [:rf.route/transitioned url {:rf.route/decided? true}]]` (decisions.cljc:455-460) | the link door: a browser-side URL change modelled as an inbound event, URL-then-state (spec 012:1157-1161) |
| `[:rf.route/navigate {:url s}]` | inline commit, state-then-URL, same open-redirect classifier (spec 012:504-511, 1165) | the programmatic escape hatch (spec 012:509) |

Two things are wrong in that table, one Medium and one Low.

1. **`:rf.route/transitioned` is a name for a value.** `handle-url-change` already discriminates its three doors by a data rider (`:rf.route/cause`, spec 012:449-452), and the docs teach tests to "say which door you meant" by passing it (docs/routing/testing.md:108-127). The fourth door is spelled as a second event id instead of a fourth rider value, and the only other difference — the default scroll — is a pure function of the cause (`:link` → `:top`, everything else → `:restore`). The "co-equal, not a delegate" sentence records that neither *calls* the other; it does not record a reason for two ids. Empirically the discriminator is not load-bearing:
   - no app dispatches either (example code lines: 0 / 0);
   - no app or tool re-registers either (`reg-event :rf.route/(transitioned|handle-url-change|url-requested)` outside routing src: 0);
   - the test corpus treats them as two spellings of "go to this URL" — 26 direct `transitioned` dispatches vs 111 `handle-url-change` outside `implementation/routing`, 154 vs 66 inside it, and one file using both (`ssr/test/re_frame/framework_zero_ownership_diagnostics_test.clj:162-201`).
2. **The link door's payload violates the request grammar's own rule 2.** `url-requested-payload` (link.cljc:171-188) emits `{:url path-url :to …}` plus `:params` / `:query` / `:fragment`; the handler destructures `url replace? bypass-leave?` and `normalize-policy` selects only `:replace?` / `:scroll` (decisions.cljc:420, 160-165). Nothing in `implementation/routing/src` reads `:to` off that payload. The navigate door rejects exactly this shape — "`:url` excludes `:params`, `:query` … a raw URL IS the address" (spec 012:462) — so the two URL-string doors disagree about what an address is, and tests pin the disagreement (route_link_test.clj:185, route_link_seam_cljs_test.cljs:76, 120).

Everything else in this area is a designed dual with a written discriminator, or a single door; those are recorded under *Non-goals / verified clean*, with four low-severity trims listed in the target.

```clojure
;; decisions.cljc url-requested-handler, allowed branch — after
{:fx [(if replace? [:rf.nav/replace-url app-url] [:rf.nav/push-url app-url])
      [:dispatch [:rf.route/handle-url-change app-url
                  {:rf.route/cause :link :rf.route/decided? true}]]]}

;; url_change.cljc — one handler; the default scroll is derived from the cause
(defn handle-url-change-handler [cofx [_ url opts]]
  (let [cause (url-change-cause frame opts)]        ;; closed set becomes #{:link :popstate :initial :ssr}

```

## Why this is better (ethos)

*Regularity over cleverness* (Principles:18): every other door discriminates by a cause value — `:rf.route/planned` carries `:cause ∈ {:navigate :link :popstate :initial :ssr}` (spec 012:98) — and three of the four URL-driven doors already ride one event with one rider. The fourth being an event id is the irregularity; after the collapse "which door" is asked one way everywhere. *Data before magic* (Principles:46): `{:rf.route/cause :link}` is a map a test can build, assert on and diff; a second event id is a name a reader must know is an alias. *One name per fact* (EP-0007, cited at spec 012:1146): "a link caused this URL change" is one fact and currently has two spellings — an id and a tag. Clojure's own answer to "two functions that differ by a constant" is one function and the constant as an argument; `url-change-fx` already IS that function, and the two handlers are the wrapper the ethos says not to write.

The honest counter-weight, and why the sub family is left alone: in re-frame, cheap layer-2 subs are the idiom and their equality cut is the point. `:rf.route/id` is more than `(:route-id @(subscribe [:rf/route]))` — a `case` over it does not re-run when `:query-merge` pagination rewrites the slice, and ten of the twenty-two app read sites are `:<-` chain inputs, which need a vector to name (Conventions §Reserved sub-ids: "a sugar fn could never ride inside a `:<-` vector"). The whole-read-plus-projections shape is shared by machine, resource and mutation reads — one grammar across four features. The zero-consumer projections (`error`, `fragment`, `chain`) are the read half of shipped features and cost three lines each; the demand bar is noted, not enforced.

Costs of the collapse: ~180 mechanical test-line edits (the 154 inside `implementation/routing/test` are the bulk), three Xray spec pages and one helper, two migration-README rows, and a trace row that reads `handle-url-change {:cause :link}` where `transitioned` read prettier — the optional rename buys the aesthetics back at roughly double the churn.

## Codex Thoughts

The public routing API is largely already elegant. Keep navigation commands, link rendering, pending-navigation decisions, prefetch, and replan distinct. Their purposes differ, and the granular subscriptions provide useful reactive equality boundaries. This document correctly avoids replacing ordinary SPA authoring with a larger generic routing command.

Collapsing the two URL-commit events is defensible internal simplification, but its benefit is modest compared with changing an app-facing API: both handlers already delegate to one [implementation](../../../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/url_change.cljc). Do it alongside routing cleanup rather than commission a broad migration solely to reduce one event name. Retaining separate well-named ingress events over the shared helper is also viable; a constant-specialised event can communicate intent without constituting another computation model. The case for consolidation is that cause already travels as data throughout this pipeline.

One source correction matters: `url-change-cause` already accepts every member of [`resolve/causes`](../../../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/resolve.cljc), including both `:link` and `:navigate`. There is no current closed three-value implementation set to expand. The actual change is to make scroll defaults consistent with the selected URL-driven cause, update the link's emitted event, and decide/document which existing causes this ingress supports. Do not silently reinterpret an omitted rider as `:link`; direct client feeds currently default to `:initial`, server feeds to `:ssr`.

If consolidated, preserve URL-before-state ordering for link activation, the already-decided guard rider, fragment-only behavior, and navigation allocation. Programmatic `navigate` is not another spelling to delete: its state-before-URL ordering remains meaningful. Avoid the optional extra event rename unless it clearly improves the resulting vocabulary; the implementation value comes from removing the redundant branch, not restyling every trace.

The link payload's repeated address fields are removable if they are genuinely unused, but the diagnosis should distinguish command inputs from trace provenance. [The link builder](../../../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc) carries both authored destination and resolved URL; a successful `planned` trace is not necessarily a substitute for original intent on a malformed or unsuccessful route. Check actual trace consumers before removing those fields, then teach one authoritative address representation. Do not invent a second metadata envelope just to preserve speculative diagnostic demand.

The most concrete user-visible defect here is accepting `:prefetch :intent` without implementing it in [Hicasso route-link](../../../../implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/route_link.cljs). Prefer wiring the existing routing-owned intent behavior if the published option remains supported; otherwise reject it clearly. A silent no-op is poor ergonomics even for trusted programmers. Verify focus, pointer intent, existing user handlers, navigation cancellation, and frame capture; do not build another prefetch policy subsystem.

The small export removals are optional maintenance, not prerequisites. Keep pure URL algebra available to tooling, and don't substitute private runtime-state access merely to delete a helper. Prioritise honest link behavior and accurate cause semantics over polishing the last internal noun.

# rf2-7nk1 — Spell the Xray facade's `load-theme` as `load-theme!`, or write down why it is the one unbanged mutator

**Decision needed from Mike:** does `day8.re-frame2-xray.core/load-theme` — which installs a `<style>` block into `<head>` — take the `!` that Conventions §Naming bucket 3 gives every other process-level mutator, and if so, does the Lifecycle-verb roster need a `load-*` row first?
**Recommendation:** **A** — rename to `load-theme!` under §Naming alone; the roster does not govern the bang axis and needs no new row.
**Bead:** rf2-7nk1 (task, P3, open) · **Epic:** none — `discovered-from` rf2-ar67 (closed, PR #9210) · **Written:** 2026-09-06 16:28:23 AUSEST at tip 6d513ba07f

## The problem

The Xray facade has 16 public vars (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs:71-303`). Twelve mutate and carry `!`; three are reads and do not (`status`, `target-frame`, `valid-focus-panels`); one mutates and does not:

```clojure
;; core.cljs:259-271 — the facade today
(defn load-theme
  "... installs a dedicated <style> block appended LAST to <head> ... Idempotent:
   successive calls REPLACE the override in place; nil / blank clears it ..."
  [css-string]
  (global-styles/set-host-theme-css! css-string)   ; the OWNER is banged (global_styles.cljs:1656)
  nil)

;; what a host writes today                          ;; under option A
(xray/load-theme editor-palette-css)                 (xray/load-theme! editor-palette-css)
```

The mutation is real: `set-host-theme-css!` (`theme/global_styles.cljs:1656-1687`) does `createElement` / `appendChild` on `js/document.head`, or `set!`s an existing node's `textContent`, or `.remove`s it. That is §Naming bucket 3 — "process-level state mutation outside the registrar" — verbatim, and §Naming calls itself "principled, not stylistic".

**How it got this way.** The name predates the mutation. At `fae8d54d2e` (rf2-13bx9, Causa era) `load-theme` took `[_css-string]`, emitted `:rf.warning/causa-load-theme-not-yet-implemented` and returned nil — a stub whose only effect was a trace, so no bang was warranted. `e4d5cafb84` (rf2-ee38b.2) wired the DOM mutation, banged the new owner, and left the facade spelling untouched. The spelling itself comes from the UX finding (`tools/xray/spec/findings/xray-ux-design.md:407`: "Settings → Theme → Load CSS … `(rf.xray/load-theme css-string)`"). Nobody decided the bang off; it was never decided on.

**Who it hurts.** The reader who infers the rule from the other fifteen: on this facade "no bang" has meant "read" every time. An AI agent or host author writing boot code sees `(xray/load-theme css)` beside `(xray/set-editor! :cursor)` and reads the first as pure. That is hidden context in a facade whose whole job is to be legible without opening the owner.

**Why the sweep left it (the case for not renaming, stated fairly).** rf2-ar67 recorded `:keep` because `load-*` is on no row of §Lifecycle-verb law's closed roster, whose escape clause says "adding a verb is a Spec change to this table, not a per-author call". Two further pieces of counter-evidence Mike should weigh:

1. **The mayor already routed this jointly.** rf2-uimu's notes (2026-09-05, mayor verification): "rule kuky.4 first, then uimu+7nk1 together on whatever survives … one amendment to the Lifecycle-verb law answers both". rf2-uimu is HELD on that release condition, and rf2-kuky.4 (open, P3 RULING) is unruled. Coupling this bead to that chain means it waits.
2. **The bead's uniqueness claim is Xray-true, not repo-true.** `re-frame.core/init-platform` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2806`, "Set the host-wide active-platform marker", delegating to `interop/set-platform!`) has the identical shape — banged owner, unbanged facade — on the `:advanced` tier. It sits in rf2-kuky.4's prune table with 0 consumers, so its fate is decided there; but an "exception" written here would have to cover it or explain why not.

Against the roster argument, one measurement. The roster's nine rows (`spec/Conventions.md:1265-1275`) are:

    clear-*  unregister-*  destroy-*  reset-*  unsubscribe  watch-*  attach!/detach!  mount!/unmount!  open!/close!

plus `configure!` in its own subsection. Of the twelve banged mutators on this same facade, **eight** use verbs on no roster row either — `init!`, `toggle!`, `popout!`, `focus!`, `set-target-frame!`, `set-auto-open!`, `set-editor!`, `set-egress-profile!` — and nobody has proposed unbanging them. The roster has never been read as an exhaustive facade-verb list; it governs *which teardown/lifecycle verb* a surface takes.

*Whether* a surface takes `!` is §Naming's axis, and §Naming says its four buckets "are exhaustive for the surfaces in API.md". The precedent is on record at `spec/API.md:1017`: `register-trace-listener` (no bang) → `register-listener!`, "bang form matches the side-effecting nature of listener registration" — and no `register-*` roster row was added then either.

## The decision

**Which one:** **A** rename to `load-theme!` under §Naming, no roster change · **B** rename AND add a `load-*` row to the roster · **C** keep `load-theme` and record it as a documented exception · **D** fold it into `configure!` as a `:rf.xray/*` key.

### B. Keep both ids, make `transitioned` a documented alias

- **It is the shim the posture forbids.** "A redundant spelling is deleted, not deprecated." An alias exists to keep old dispatches working, and there are no old dispatches outside the framework's own tests and fixtures — zero apps, zero tools, zero overrides. The only consumers it would spare are the 193 + 33 literals A is going to rewrite anyway, and leaving them means the corpus keeps two spellings by habit forever.
- **It converts an accidental dual into a designed one with the weakest possible discriminator.** *Regularity over cleverness* (Principles:22) allows a documented alternative "with a stated use case"; the alias's use case would be "it saves typing a map". Spec 012:533 currently says "neither delegates to the other"; B makes it say the opposite, and the spec would then carry a delegate pair it has just finished explaining it does not have.

The test sweep is avoided, but the test sweep is the mechanical part.
- **Nobody advocated it.** Codex's "retaining separate well-named ingress events … is also viable" argues for two *distinct* events with communicated intent, not for one that is documented as the other.

### C. Keep as designed

What changes: nothing. Close the bead with the ruling as its reason.

Consequences: the two stale sentences stay unless a doc-drift bead is filed (012:533's "SSR `:frame` threading" difference; 012:38 / `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md:503`'s "programmatic push"); Xray 016/018 keep naming two of three event ids while 023 names a different one; `docs/routing/testing.md` keeps teaching the rider for three doors and an id for the fourth; the test corpus keeps two spellings chosen by habit; an AI agent learns a second event id that is a value of a rider it already knows. The design is coherent enough to live with — both handlers work, the cause is honoured, no consumer is confused in practice — which is why Codex calls this viable. The cost is a permanent small tax, not a bug.

## Recommendation

**A, without the rename rider.** Three principles decide it. *Regularity over cleverness* (Principles:18-22): "there is one obvious way to do a thing … when a feature admits two shapes for the same job, designate one as canonical and the other as the documented alternative with a stated use case" — three of the four URL-driven doors already share one event and a rider, `:rf.route/planned` already carries `:cause ∈ {:link :popstate :initial :ssr :navigate}` (012:98), and the fourth door's only stated use case is a constant. *Data before magic* (Principles:46): `{:rf.route/cause :link}` is a map a test can build, assert on and diff; a second id is a name a reader must know is an alias. *The demand bar* (Principles:124-128): "every shipped name is a permanent obligation on every conforming port … the demand bar is what … prevents one-fact-many-names hazards" — `:rf.route/transitioned` has no named consumer outside the framework's own link door, and "a link caused this URL change" is one fact with two spellings today, an id and a tag. Clojure's answer to two functions that differ by a constant is one function with the constant as an argument; `url-change-fx` already is that function, and the two wrappers are what the ethos says not to write. The counter is cost, and the cost is real — 264 test lines, 33 fixture lines, five hot-zone files, a migration row — but it is mechanical, framework-internal, and paid once; Codex's condition ("alongside routing cleanup, not a standalone migration") is met by sequencing bead 1 after rf2-kuky.36 and .37, which already open `routing.cljc`, `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md` and `spec/012-Routing.md`. **Fallback if Mike disagrees:** C, not B. Keeping a coherent two-id design is defensible; keeping two ids where one is documented as the other is not. On C, file one small doc-drift bead for 012:38 / :533 and `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md:503` plus the Xray 016/018 completeness fix, so the record of the kept design is at least true.

## Codex Recommendation

**Choose A: consolidate on `:rf.route/handle-url-change`, without an alias or another rename. Treat this as worthwhile, low-priority routing simplification, not an urgent correctness repair.** Refine A in two ways: preserve the old calls' cause semantics during migration, and retain the existing cause resolver rather than coupling this removal to a new four-member acceptance restriction.

Independently checked at `0ae438352476914f558c5ece11fad65597fbecf7`, **2026-09-06T16:31:07+10:00**. Both handlers and registrations remain present; `rf2-kuky.36`, `.37`, and `.38` are all open. This proposal has not landed.

### Why consolidation is justified — and what it does not prove

[The complete URL-change implementation](../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/url_change.cljc) confirms one substantial computation with two wrappers selecting cause and scroll defaults. Both already carry the same frame and allocation coeffects. [The link decision handler](../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/decisions.cljc) pushes/replaces the URL before dispatching the commit event, whereas [the history listener](../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/history.cljc) already expresses its initial/popstate distinction as data. Extending that existing representation to links is a useful regularity: callers describe the navigation's origin using the vocabulary the plan already carries.

The justification is **not** that two constant-specialised handlers violate Clojure. Such handlers can be an excellent way to name distinct intentions. The strongest alternative is therefore C in this dossier: keep the pair and correct its documentation. The implementation is already factored; ordinary SPA authors predominantly use `navigate` and `route-link`, not either commit event. Searches of examples, tools, and skills found no example dispatch of `transitioned`, while the Xray routes testbed and boot skill use the survivor. Consolidation improves the advanced/test vocabulary more than day-to-day app authoring. That modest benefit is sufficient during the planned routing cleanup, but not grounds for inventing a new routing abstraction.

Nor is this exclusively internal work. [The routing contract](../../spec/012-Routing.md#standard-runtime-events) expressly permits users to dispatch and override these events. The absence of in-repository overrides limits measured migration cost; it does not erase the contract. This is an intentional pre-alpha API change.

### Refinements that keep the change honest

**Preserve cause before simplifying tests.** The default migration for every old `transitioned` dispatch should associate `:rf.route/cause :link` into its existing opts, retaining other keys. It must override any conflicting old cause rider: `transitioned-handler` currently hardcodes `:link`. Do not automatically make apparently generic URL-setup tests rider-free. Apart from scroll, `decide` publishes cause in pending-navigation and entry-denial payloads. A fixture can stop exercising link behavior without an assertion failing. Deliberately converting a fixture to initial-load coverage is a separate, explained test change. Existing [scroll tests](../../implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_scroll_test.clj) demonstrate that the distinction is observable, not merely descriptive.

**Retain the existing five-member resolver in this consolidation.** Framework-produced URL feeds should be documented as link/popstate/initial/SSR, but [the shared cause vocabulary](../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/resolve.cljc) also includes `:navigate`, which `url-change-cause` already accepts. I found no explicit `:navigate` rider consumer; equally, no demonstrated problem requires a second accepted-cause subset. Silently converting that rider into `:initial` or `:ssr` is an independent behavior change, not a prerequisite for deleting an event. Preserve current unknown-value fallback and rider-free client/server defaults. If Mike specifically wants four accepted causes, make that a recorded additional ruling and executable resolver change; a docstring cannot implement the exclusion.


**Do not revive `:rf.route/url-changed`.** [M-60](../../migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md) records that exact keyword as the former *fragment trace operation*. Reusing it for the surviving event reintroduces a vocabulary collision in migration/history material, beyond the extra churn. Update the existing migration story instead. A custom `transitioned` override needs particular care: renaming its registration would now also intercept Back/Forward and SSR. Explain the widened scope and require intentional cause-aware adaptation, not a blind registration rename.

### Proportionate implementation and acceptance

Delete the wrapper/registration; resolve cause once in the survivor; derive default scroll as `:top` only for `:link`; retarget the link's dispatch while preserving `:rf.route/decided?`. Keep the dispatch hop, allocation metadata, frame attribution, and shared commit helper intact. Do not fold programmatic `navigate` into this event: its state-before-URL ordering remains a distinct operation.

Migrate tests and conformance data with cause preserved, then remove the redundant [algebra input](../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/tooling.cljc). Update contract, migration/skills, and Xray prose together with the coordinated change. [Xray's detector](../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/routing_helpers.cljc) already scans allocation operations, so no event-name detector rewrite is needed. Serialize overlapping routing/hot-zone ownership; do not ship a prolonged interval where the runtime removes the name but the migration guide still recommends it.

Focused acceptance should establish:

- Link commit: URL mutation precedes the child commit, guards run once, and cause/default scroll remain `:link`/`:top`.
- Initial, popstate, and server feeds retain their existing cause/defaults; route-level scroll overrides and suppression still work.
- Exact no-op and fragment-only navigation preserve token and `:on-match` behavior; rejection preserves pending/denial cause and URL restoration.
- The obsolete registration/algebra row is absent, migrated fixtures run on JVM and CLJS, and a recorded replay retains allocation/frame behavior.

This was a source-and-contract review, including the full bead description and notes, not an executed equivalence proof. No builds or runtime tests were run; repository searches cannot establish what external applications override. The recommendation adds no compatibility shim, new policy subsystem, or extra API door.

title: test(core-examples): pin both :error-shown exits in state-machine-walkthrough-runs-headless
description:
Follow-up to rf2-283u, which asked for this and could not do it: the implementing worker was fenced out of implementation/**, so the code fix landed (PR #9243) without the regression pin the item requested.

WHAT IS MISSING. rf2-283u fixed the walkthrough's stale-error lifecycle by adding `:exit :clear-error` to the `:error-shown` state node in examples/capabilities/machines/state_machine_walkthrough/core.cljc. The existing `state-machine-walkthrough-runs-headless` deftest in implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj still asserts only what it asserted before: its drain scenario dispatches Dismiss twice but checks nothing except the eventual :locked-out state, and never reads :walkthrough.login/error after a Dismiss or inspects a direct-retry snapshot. So nothing in CI would catch the `:exit` being dropped again.

WHAT TO ADD (both assertions were measured passing against the fixed table, and measured FAILING against the same table with :exit removed -- so they have teeth):

From the snapshot {:state :error-shown :data {:attempts 1 :error "bad creds"}}:
- Dismiss -> :idle, (get-in s [:data :error]) is nil, (get-in s [:data :attempts]) is 1.
- Submit -> :submitting, error nil, attempts 1, exactly one fx whose id is :rf.http/managed.

Both drive the pure fn, matching the namespace's existing style:
  (rf.machines/machine-transition login-flow snapshot [:walkthrough.login/dismiss])

NOTE ON MECHANISM, so the pin is written against what actually shipped: the clear is a state-level `:exit` hook, not a per-transition `:action` (see rf2-283u's close reason for why). Assert the OBSERVABLE snapshot, not the table shape -- a test that greps the table for :exit would pin the mechanism rather than the behaviour.

Non-goals: no new test namespace, no *.spec.cjs anywhere under examples/ (rf2-8cevm), no change to the example itself -- it is correct as merged.
notes:
WORKER OUTCOME (PR #9269, commit 03820027d1). Premise checked at source and CONFIRMED at tip: examples_test.clj had exactly ONE mention of :error-shown (a comment), no read of :error after a Dismiss, and no direct-retry case at all. Both assertions added as specified, driving the pure fn.

Two negative controls, the example restored byte-exact both times (sha256 378f401779406cf93fa0feefc5a9769e5432e1548a7f4fb990b72e982f0754ef before and after, git status clean on examples/):
  - remove :exit :clear-error entirely  -> BOTH new assertions red (:error still 'bad creds')
  - move the clear onto the Dismiss edge alone as an :action -> ONLY the Submit assertion red

The second control is the one that answers 'does the added assertion distinguish the two exits'. It does: neither edge's assertion passes for the other. Exact-vector equality rather than a membership check is what gives it that property.

Followed the bead's mechanism note — the pin is on the observable snapshot, never on the table shape, so the :action-per-edge table above is one the example stays entitled to adopt.

The example is UNCHANGED (fence: examples/ belongs to exschema-a's PR #9261 this wave, and the bead's non-goals say the same).

Gate (captured exit, final rebased base): implementation/core clojure -M:test exit 0, 2187 tests / 11320 assertions.
close_reason:
MERGED as PR #9269, commit 23924d9886 (five clauses met; see rf2-ni74's close reason).

Premise confirmed: the test had ONE mention of :error-shown — a comment — never read :error after a Dismiss, and never drove a direct retry. So one of the two exits was entirely unexercised and a change breaking it would have gone unnoticed.

Both assertions added, driving the pure fn. The example itself is UNCHANGED: it was fenced to another worker this wave and is also the bead's own stated non-goal, so the coverage was added where it belongs rather than by touching the subject.

THE CONTROLS DISCRIMINATE, which is the whole point of a coverage-completion bead: removing :exit :clear-error reds BOTH new assertions with :error still reading 'bad creds'; clearing on the Dismiss edge only reds ONLY the Submit assertion. So the two assertions distinguish the two exits rather than either passing for both — the exact failure a naive 'pin both exits' patch would have shipped. Restores hash-verified.
