title: surface-review(reagent-slim): the static-markup boolean roster has the same omissions rf2-r9kf fixed in SSR
description:
`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs` carries its OWN boolean-attribute roster, independent of the SSR artefact's:

    (def ^:private boolean-attributes
      #{"allowfullscreen" "async" "autofocus" "autoplay" "checked"
        "controls" "default" "defer" "disabled" "formnovalidate" "hidden"
        "loop" "multiple" "muted" "novalidate" "open" "playsinline"
        "readonly" "required" "reversed" "selected" "itemscope"})

Measured against the installed react-dom 19.2.0 it is missing the presence names `inert`, `noModule`, `scoped`, `seamless`, `disablePictureInPicture` and `disableRemotePlayback`, and it models NO stringifying class at all — so `contentEditable`, `draggable`, `spellCheck`, `autoReverse`, `externalResourcesRequired`, `focusable` and `preserveAlpha` do not get `="true"` / `="false"` treatment, and `download` / `capture` have no overloaded-boolean arm. That is the SAME defect class rf2-r9kf fixed in `re-frame.ssr.html-helpers`: a false value that carries meaning is dropped, and the markup asserts the opposite of what the author wrote.

WHY IT WAS NOT CAUGHT. `reagent2.dom.parity-cljs-test` already renders both ways and compares byte-for-byte against `react-dom/server.renderToStaticMarkup`, which is the right shape of check — but it is CORPUS-DRIVEN, so it only catches what its corpus happens to contain. None of the eleven names above appears to be in it. That is the same blind spot in a different disguise from the one the rf2-r9kf audit found: there, a parity test between two consumers of a shared roster could not see the roster's omissions; here, a genuine external parity test cannot see what its corpus omits.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, IF THIS IS DISPATCHED. PR #9207 landed `implementation/ssr/test/react_dom_probe/boolean_attr_classes.cjs`, which derives its candidate names from react-dom's own `possibleStandardNames` table and its boolean-ness from react-dom's own dev-build warning — so the roster under test cannot bound the probe. reagent-slim's parity test runs under `:node-test` with live `react-dom/server` available, so it could enumerate the same React-derived name set directly at test time rather than through a committed fixture, which is strictly better than what SSR could do. That is the cheap version: drive the existing parity harness over a React-derived name list instead of a hand-written corpus.

SCOPE NOTE. Separate artefact, separate roster, separate emitter — nothing is shared with `re-frame.ssr`, and rf2-r9kf deliberately did not touch it. Whether reagent-slim should model the stringifying and overloaded classes at all is a real question rather than an obvious yes: it is a static-markup emitter for a Reagent-compatible surface, and its IMPL-SPEC §8.7 already allow-lists known divergences from React. Decide that before widening the roster.
notes:
MAYOR SEQUENCING NOTE 2026-09-05. FENCED until slimadapter-a's PR merges. `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/**` is inside a live worker's fence right now — it is carrying rf2-cdoo (the P1 after-render/DOM-commit ordering bug) and rf2-vy0a (the vacuous sub-cache poison proof) together in one PR, because both live in that artefact. A third worker branching off main now would collide on the same files and, worse, could silently revert them on merge.

WHY THIS BEAD IS WORTH DOING RATHER THAN FOLDING INTO EITHER: it is the same CLASS of defect that rf2-r9kf's audit found in the SSR roster, arriving independently in a second artefact. reagent-slim's boolean roster omits inert, noModule, scoped, seamless, disablePictureInPicture and disableRemotePlayback, and carries NO stringifying or overloaded class at all.

AND THE SHARP PART, which generalises past this bead: reagent-slim's react-dom parity test is CORPUS-DRIVEN, so it only catches what the corpus happens to contain. That is the same structural blind spot the SSR audit named from the other side — there, two serialisers sharing one roster made their parity test agree on the same wrong answer. A parity test can only validate what something OUTSIDE the thing under test supplies. The SSR fix (PR #9207) shows the shape of the answer: its probe takes candidate names from react-dom's own `possibleStandardNames` and boolean-ness from React's own dev-build warning, so the roster under test cannot bound the probe. Reuse that technique here rather than extending the corpus.

ON DISPATCH: re-verify at tip. slimadapter-a may have touched neighbouring code, and PR #9207's probe (implementation/ssr/test/react_dom_probe/boolean_attr_classes.cjs) is the model to read first — it is committed and its .edn fixture is regenerated by hand, which is a limitation that worker recorded deliberately: a react-dom bump does not automatically red. Decide whether reagent-slim wants the same trade or an automatic regeneration.
close_reason:
FIXED. PR #9224 (worker/slimbool-a), gates green, opened not yet merged. Three files, all inside implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/.

THE PREMISE HELD, AND WAS WORSE THAN FILED. The bead described the roster as missing six presence names and modelling no stringifying class. Both true. But `emit-attribute` consulted the roster ONLY in its `(true? v)` arm, and `(false? v)` returned nil unconditionally — so a boolean value on ANY name outside the 22 was dropped in BOTH directions, not just on false. `{:aria-expanded true}` emitted nothing where react-dom emits `aria-expanded="true"`; `{:inert true}` emitted nothing; `{:download true}` emitted nothing. The bead named aria only implicitly (through the stringifying class); it is the loudest case, because boolean ARIA state is ordinary SPA authoring.

THE SIX NAMES ARE ALL REAL, re-measured against the installed react-dom 19.2.0 rather than transcribed, as the dispatch asked: `inert`, `noModule`, `scoped`, `seamless`, `disablePictureInPicture`, `disableRemotePlayback` are each a value of react-dom's `possibleStandardNames`, each accepted as a boolean with no dev warning, each rendering `name=""` on true and nothing on false. None is an `ismap` (rf2-u6zw's falsified 004B row was the cautionary case checked for).

WHERE THE ROSTER IS CONSULTED, since the dispatch asked whether React handles this before the roster is reached. It does not. `reagent2.dom.server` is a pure-CLJS serializer whose whole purpose is `render-to-static-markup` WITHOUT a runtime `react-dom/server` dependency (IMPL-SPEC §8, ~22-27 KB gzip of bundle). The roster IS the entire boolean implementation on that path; nothing upstream of it classifies. The CLIENT path is a different question and is React's — `template/as-element` hands React elements to `react-dom/client`, so React does its own attribute work there and the roster is not involved. So the finding is confined to static markup, and it is NOT dead weight there: `reagent2.dom.client/hydrate-root` exists and hydrates exactly this markup, which makes the divergence an attribute-only hydration mismatch, the class spec/011 records React as not guaranteeing to patch.

WHAT LANDED. Three classes, mirroring react-dom's, each measured: PRESENCE (bare name on true, omitted on false, bare name on other truthy values — react-dom collapses `{:disabled "yes"}` to `disabled=""` the same way) gaining the six names; STRINGIFYING (`="true"` / `="false"`), which the artefact modelled not at all, covering the `aria-*`/`data-*` prefix rule plus contentEditable, draggable, spellCheck, autoReverse, externalResourcesRequired, focusable, preserveAlpha and `value`; and OVERLOADED (`download`, `capture`) — bare on true, omitted on false, value kept otherwise. Overloaded could NOT simply join presence: the presence rule collapses every truthy value to the bare name, which would have thrown `{:download "report.pdf"}`'s filename away. A name in no class emits nothing for either boolean, matching react-dom for `children`, `is`, `defaultChecked` and every attribute it warns about.

THREE DECISIONS, each taken on measurement rather than by default. (1) Membership is keyed on the LOWERCASE name and presence names EMIT lowercase. react-dom preserves camelCase for most (`readOnly=""`, `noModule=""`) and lowercases others (`autoFocus` -> `autofocus`), so this diverges cosmetically — kept because HTML attribute names are ASCII case-insensitive, every presence member is an HTML rather than SVG attribute, hydration reads them case-insensitively, and the lowercase key is what makes `:read-only` / `:readOnly` / `:readonly` all classify (a React-cased roster would silently drop the third spelling). Recorded as an allow-listed §8.7 divergence beside the pre-existing short-form one, not hidden. (2) The STRINGIFYING class is NOT lowercased, because four members are case-sensitive SVG attributes; it emits `attribute-name`'s output, which already pins React's casing. (3) `value` is stringifying HERE where re-frame.ssr deliberately classified it ordinary — the reason is written into the roster: SSR's roster is shared with the 004B structural-tree serializer where `value` is a form-control special form, and this artefact has no such coupling and one contract only, byte-parity with `renderToStaticMarkup`. Following the measurement costs one string and removes a divergence rather than documenting one.

THE CORPUS BLIND SPOT IS CLOSED, NOT DECLINED, and by the technique the sequencing note named rather than by extending the corpus. `boolean_attr_react_parity_cljs_test.cljs` takes candidate NAMES from react-dom's own `possibleStandardNames` (scraped from the dev build) and BOOLEAN-NESS from react-dom's own dev warning, so the roster under test cannot bound the probe; the class is derived from React's markup bytes; and it checks BOTH directions over that whole candidate space — a name React classifies that the serializer does not, and a name the serializer treats as boolean-class that React puts no boolean into markup for. It reads the serializer's class from EMITTED MARKUP through the public entry point, never from the (private) rosters.

AND IT TOOK THE BETTER HALF OF THE TRADE THE DISPATCH ASKED ABOUT. The SSR probe's committed .edn is regenerated by hand because its consumer is a JVM suite that must not need node_modules, so a react-dom bump does not automatically red. This suite already runs under :node-test with react-dom resolvable, so it re-derives everything AT RUN TIME: a bump that moves a name into, out of, or between classes reds `npm run test:cljs` with nothing to regenerate and nothing to forget. It also closes ground (c) from rf2-r9kf's close note for this artefact — the overloaded class's distinct behaviour is pinned against LIVE react-dom with a third, non-boolean value, which that boolean-only fixture could not do.

NON-VACUITY WITNESS. Roster reverted to its pre-fix state with the new tests in place, same base: exit 1, 47 failures, the React-derived arm naming 20 attributes BY NAME (the six presence names, the seven stringifying names, aria-expanded/aria-hidden/data-open/data-collapsed, download, capture, value). Every pre-existing deftest in `parity_cljs_test.cljs` and `server_cljs_test.cljs` stayed GREEN through that run — the audit's point made mechanically. Source restored, `git diff --quiet` clean, blob hash equal to the committed one.

THE PROBE CAUGHT A BUG IN ITSELF FIRST, worth recording because it is the failure shape this whole bead is about. Its first run reddened on `autoFocus`: react-dom lowercases it to `autofocus=""`, and a case-sensitive read of REACT'S OWN BYTES called the attribute absent — a wrong class that still looks like a measurement. The SSR probe documents that exact trap in a comment I had read. Fixed by deriving React's class case-insensitively while keeping the serializer-side stringifying comparison byte-exact; the measurement is in the `react-class` docstring.

GATES (final base after rebase onto origin/main; each redirected to its own log, exit echoed on the same command line, number read back from the .exit file). `npm run test:cljs` exit 0, 11203 tests / 56532 assertions, 0 failures. `npm run test:reagent-slim:bundle-isolation` exit 0 — the `:advanced`/release compile, 93 files compiled with 0 warnings on both release builds, PASS 6 contracts / 25 sentinel checks. `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` exit 0 — the gate that covers IMPL-SPEC.md, nominated by path. `python scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py` exit 0, implementation/adapters at its floor of 337.

CONTROLS, because a zero is not a check that passed. readme-links: a planted broken target AND broken anchor in IMPL-SPEC.md gave exit 1 naming the file and line for both; restored and hash-verified. Alias ratchet: a planted `[re-frame.core :as core]` in the new test file gave exit 1 reading `338 violation(s), floor 337`; restored and re-verified. test:cljs: the witness above.

WRONG-GATE NOTES for the next carrier. `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` is NOT the gate for this artefact — its DEFAULT_ROOTS are docs/spec/skills/migration, so implementation/adapters/** is outside its surface and it exits 0 on a broken link there; `check_readme_links.py --ci` is the one. `test:adapter-smokes` is not a release compile and covers only Reagent and UIx; the slim release gate is `test:reagent-slim:bundle-isolation`, whose recipe runs `shadow-cljs release`.

GROUND A FOLLOW-ON STILL HAS, deliberately not taken here. (a) The presence branch's NON-boolean arm diverges from react-dom on JS-falsy-but-CLJS-truthy values: `{:disabled ""}` and `{:disabled 0}` emit the bare name where react-dom omits the attribute entirely. That is a truthiness-semantics gap rather than a roster gap, it is pre-existing and untouched, and this probe cannot see it because it supplies booleans only. (b) The reverse arm's candidate space is react-dom's, so a hypothetical roster entry that is not a `possibleStandardNames` value would escape it; every current entry is in that space, and the bound is stated in the test's docstring. (c) `parity_cljs_test.cljs` still carries its own 22-name `boolean-attr-set` for canonicalisation — a second copy of the presence roster, now short by six. It is inert for the corpus it drives (no new name appears there) and was left alone rather than silently widened, but it is a drift surface.

title: hic: RULING — a bead id in the design corpus is provenance, not a live pointer (rf2-wx96 census)
description:

THE CENSUS, across docs/design/. 86 distinct rf2-hic-NNN ids in 1,181 citations. FIVE resolve in the tracker: rf2-hic-051, -063, -064, -088, -090 (four closed, rf2-hic-063 open). Two of the 86 - rf2-hic-9001 and rf2-hic-9002 - are correction-ledger.md's deliberately fictional worked-example ids and were never beads.

THE MEASUREMENT rf2-wx96 DID NOT HAVE, AND IT CHANGES THE QUESTION. The ids were REAL and the citations were VALID when written. The tracker export at 63a3d44086 (2026-08-16) carries NINETY rf2-hic-NNN values as .id. The drop is between 1246e4e422 (2026-08-31, still 90) and dc88bc6aae (2026-09-02, 5).

AND IT IS NOT SPECIFIC TO THIS CORPUS. Comparing the whole id set at 1246e4e422 against tip: 1,145 ids then, 935 now, 848 gone - of which 85 are rf2-hic-* and 763 are not. So this is a general tracker compaction with a visible face in the hicasso corpus, not a hicasso bookkeeping defect, and EVERY closed bead id cited anywhere in the repository is subject to the same disappearance.

WHY THAT DECIDES (a) VERSUS (b) ON THE EVIDENCE. Option (b), "live owner references needing a mapping", cannot be sustained: it would require the design corpus to track a tracker that compacts, and the mapping would be 848 ids wide rather than 60. The surviving convention already reads the other way - the derivative beads that outlive a programme item carry hic-NNN in their TITLE and an ordinary rf2-<slug> id of their own (rf2-w01c is "hic-036 clock driver: ...", rf2-85og2 is "hic-071 remainder: ..."), and the five ids that DO resolve are all titled "hic-NNN - <name>", so id and title-prefix agree only where the bead survives.

RECOMMENDED RULING (a): a bead id in a design record is a PROVENANCE CITATION - the name of the bead under which a change was made - and not a resolvable pointer. Consequences if ruled: requirements-mine.md's "How to read a row" defines Owner as "the bead accountable for carrying the answer to done", which reads as resolvable and would need one sentence saying it need not be; the maintenance rules gain a rule for what a dead owner-id means; and the passes stop treating ids as look-ups, so a dead id is not a finding. What stays a finding is a row asserting a STATUS the tracker contradicts, which only binds ids the tracker still holds.

NOT DONE HERE, AND DELIBERATELY: no id was repointed. rf2-wx96 rules a mechanical repoint out as guesswork and that judgement stands - the compaction figures above make it worse, not better.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one ruling on (a) versus (b). If (a), the wording lands on requirements-mine.md's maintenance rules and its "How to read a row" table.

The boundary shell reads re-frame.adapter.context/frame-context — one defonce'd createContext — and collector/resolve-frame! refuses only when that context holds nil or the no-provider sentinel. h/mount!'s provider, rf/frame-provider and rf/frame-root all write that SAME object (views/provider.cljs aliases it rather than minting its own; frame_boundary.cljs goes through provider-element). So the requirement is any frame from any React-shaped adapter, not a Hicasso root.

Proof already in the tree: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/foreign_root_bridge_dom_cljs_test.cljs drives a :crossed/reagent-as-component route — a Reagent root, rf/frame-provider above, the as-component bridge inside, no Hicasso root — and asserts a write repaints through it.

This is the ONLY place in the package with that framing. native.cljc says 'outside every frame' twice; resolve-frame!'s own docstring says 'from the one context every React-shaped substrate in this repo writes'; the raise message says 'no frame in scope'. So the fix is a one-line docstring correction to match its siblings.

Left unfixed by PR #9149 because implementation/hicasso/** was read-only for that docs task.

Gate: docstring-only change, so the hicasso JVM/CLJS suites for the package. No guide page changes.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #9149 (2026-09-04): expand the one existing docstring repair rather than file a duplicate. When correcting implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:1795-1814, also name Reagent as a supported parent and qualify “values by identity”: that is only Hicasso's shallow decode, while a Reagent [:>] parent converts first (including named? keywords/symbols). rf2-d4n8 owns the corresponding public-guide/reference completeness.

Corrected as-component's docstring in implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs: 'outside every Hicasso root' -> outside every FRAME, naming the one re-frame.adapter.context/frame-context that h/mount!, rf/frame-provider and rf/frame-root all write, so the requirement is a frame from any React-shaped adapter. The audit note's two additions were applied to BOTH as-component docstrings - codec.cljs AND the public facade in hicasso.cljc, which was the sibling carrying the same defects: Reagent named as a supported parent, and 'values by identity' qualified as a fact about Hicasso's shallow decode rather than about what arrives, since a Reagent [:>] parent runs convert-prop-value first (names round-trip, values do not). title: spec: ResourceRoutePlanTags declares no :recovery key though every emitted route-plan record carries one
description:
REPORTED 2026-09-04 by worker/specdocs-a while landing rf2-ma8r (i). OUT OF ITS FENCE — spec/Spec-Schemas.md is HOT-ZONE and that worker did not hold it — so this is reported, not patched, and it is a CLAIM to check at source.

spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1729, the ResourceRoutePlanTags schema, declares NO :recovery key. Every emitted route-plan record carries one: the worker verified at source that :fix-registration is set at implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:116-124 and inherited via route.cljc:983.

SAME DRIFT CLASS as the defect rf2-ma8r (i) just repaired one file over — a normative record that is silent about a field the runtime actually emits — which is why it is worth fixing rather than filing and forgetting: the pair of them is a pattern, not a one-off.

WORTH KNOWING WHILE YOU FIX IT, and it is the detail that defeats a reader tracing the category: the recovery discriminator rides NESTED under :cause, not at the top level. And :fix-registration covers FOUR planner-reachable registry rejections, not only the unregistered-resource one — the worker measured that while widening spec/009's row, and it is the number to check before writing the schema.

SEQUENCING: spec/Spec-Schemas.md is hot-zone — sequential, never parallel. Confirm no live worker holds it before dispatching.

GATE: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py (spec/ is inside its roots — anchors and repo-relative targets) AND python -m mkdocs build --strict from the repo root, which DOES cover spec/ because mkdocs_hooks.py's on_pre_build stages it into docs_dir before MkDocs scans anything. The two are complementary and neither substitutes for the other. Neither looks inside a fenced code block, and Spec-Schemas.md is mostly fences — so if your edit is confined to a fenced schema, NEITHER GATE IS THE GATE: check it by hand and say so.
notes:
VERDICT: PREMISE REFUTED. ResourceRoutePlanTags is CORRECT as it stands; no edit made, no PR opened.

The literal observation is true — spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1729 declares no :recovery key (its keys are :category :route-id :resource-id :contributor :nav-token :plan-cause :replan-cause :cause :reason). But that silence is DELIBERATE and load-bearing, not drift.

WHY. A *Tags schema describes the :tags map, and :recovery is never in it. re-frame.trace/build-event DISSOCS :recovery from :tags (core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:693) and ASSOCS it on the envelope top level (trace.cljc:721, defaulting to :no-recovery on the error branch). The normative record declares it at that layer instead: TraceEvent (Spec-Schemas.md:799) and ErrorEvent (Spec-Schemas.md:869), both '[:recovery {:optional true} Recovery]' annotated as hoisted. Of 109 *Tags schemas in the file, ZERO declare :recovery — that uniformity is the post-rf2-v1sg5 invariant.

rf2-v1sg5 (commit 13f8e64aca, 'spec(schemas): type the :where slot and strike the dead :recovery declarations') struck :recovery from the six *Tags schemas that had it (MalformedSchemaTags, NoFrameContextTags, BadFrameProviderArgTags, EffectHandlerBadReturnTags, PrefetchBadAddressTags, NoAdapterSpecifiedTags) and narrowed envelope-only-tag-keys to #{:category}. Its own message: 'a schema re-declaring :recovery under :tags now reds instead of being absolved.' Adding the key would revert that commit's intent.

MEASURED, not reasoned. Gate: implementation/core, clojure -M:test -n re-frame.error-catalogue-channel-conformance-test.
  - clean tree: captured exit 0, 'Ran 30 tests containing 179 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.'
  - with :recovery planted into ResourceRoutePlanTags: captured exit 1, 2 failures in two arms (tags-column-keys-are-documented at test line 1492, and the mutation-proof arm at 2381), reporting exactly [[:rf.error/resource-route-plan "ResourceRoutePlanTags" (:recovery)]].
  Plant restored and verified by git blob hash (working == committed, 847bde4673c0221729de8c45028dc17fe74d8561).
  Note the two arms are a PINCER: tags-column-findings reds if the SCHEMA declares :recovery while the 009 row does not list it, and tags-column-recovery-listings reds any row whose :tags CELL lists :recovery. So :recovery may appear in neither side — there is no variant of this fix that greens.

THE FIELD IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED, in its own column. spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2047's Default :recovery column carries the full disposition: :fix-params, :fix-when, :fix-scope, :fix-after, :fix-parent, and :fix-registration for a registry rejection.

TWO BRIEF CLAIMS DID NOT HOLD.
(1) PATHS: the runtime is implementation/RESOURCES/, not implementation/routing/. The line numbers were right: resources/registry.cljc:124 (inside a private registration-error helper) and resources/route.cljc:983. re_frame/routing/route.cljc does not exist.
(2) 'the recovery discriminator rides NESTED under :cause, not at the top level' is INVERTED for :recovery itself. All three builders put :recovery at the TOP LEVEL of the emitted record: branch-plan-error (route.cljc:913, :fix-parent), collapse-cycle-error (route.cljc:935, :fix-after), plan-error (route.cljc:983, (get data :recovery :fix-params)). resources/test/re_frame/resources_route_plan_recovery_cljs_test.cljc:126-130 pins both readings in one form: (:recovery e) top level, (:rf.error/id (:cause e)) nested. What IS nested under :cause is the rejection's own :rf.error/id — which 009:2047 already states. Had the brief been followed literally the schema would have gained a NEW defect.

The record does carry :recovery at top level on the ROUTE SLICE (:error), which is where the test reads it; it is only the TRACE :tags that build-event strips. One record, two surfaces — and ResourceRoutePlanTags is the schema for the surface that does not carry it.

Follow-up filed: rf2-ni4l — 009:2047 says :fix-registration is 'the token all four registry rejections carry'; a FIFTH (:rf.error/resource-scope-not-registered) is planner-reachable via route.cljc:722 -> :507 -> :531 -> scope_registry.cljc:616 -> :629 -> :429, tagged at scope_registry.cljc:157. 009 is hot-zone, so it was reported rather than edited.
close_reason: PREMISE REFUTED — no edit warranted, no PR. ResourceRoutePlanTags (Spec-Schemas.md:1729) correctly declares no :recovery: a *Tags schema describes the :tags map, and re-frame.trace/build-event DISSOCS :recovery from :tags (trace.cljc:693) and hoists it to the envelope (trace.cljc:721), where TraceEvent (Spec-Schemas.md:799) and ErrorEvent (:869) already declare it. Zero of the file's 109 *Tags schemas declare it — the invariant rf2-v1sg5 (commit 13f8e64aca) established by striking it from six schemas and narrowing envelope-only-tag-keys to #{:category}, so that 'a schema re-declaring :recovery under :tags now reds'. MEASURED: the conformance gate is exit 0 clean (30 tests / 179 assertions) and exit 1 with :recovery planted, reporting [[:rf.error/resource-route-plan "ResourceRoutePlanTags" (:recovery)]] in two arms; plant restored, blob hash verified. The two arms are a pincer (schema side and cell side), so no variant of the proposed fix greens. The field is already documented in 009:2047's own Default :recovery column. Brief corrections: the runtime is implementation/RESOURCES/ not routing/ (line numbers right, paths wrong); and ':recovery rides nested under :cause' is inverted — all three builders (route.cljc:913/935/983) put it at TOP LEVEL, as resources_route_plan_recovery_cljs_test.cljc:126-130 pins; what is nested under :cause is the rejection's :rf.error/id. Follow-up rf2-ni4l filed: 009:2047 names four registry rejections, a fifth is planner-reachable.

title: hic tooling: the migration reporter's bare form silently writes its report into the tool's own directory inside the checkout
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 2 (LinearLite), a BLINDED
agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation, and it is evidence about the surface rather than a ratified design -
a pilot proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own
rule. The log is at ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-linearlite.friction-log.md
(local-only) and in the pilot workspace.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F03 · outcome 2 · `inferred` · `tooling`

**Trying to** Run the reporter without writing anything into the `re-frame2/`
checkout, which is a read-only build input for me.

**Expected** A report in my own workspace, or at worst on stdout.

**Instead** The chapter's first command is `cd re-frame2/migration/…/codemod`
followed by `clojure -M:run path/to/your/src/`, and the default run wrote
`reagent-to-hicasso-report.edn` **into that directory** — i.e. into the checkout
I had been told not to modify. `git status` in the checkout showed it. The run
also printed `WARNING: Use of :paths external to the project has been
deprecated, please remove: ../../../implementation/hicasso/src` — the tool's own
`deps.edn` has the escape that chapter 15 spends two paragraphs telling *me* to
avoid.

**Looked at** `20-migration-from-reagent.md` §1; `15-testing.md` §"Put the test
kit on the classpath" (for the `:paths` escape it warns about).

**Resolved by** Re-running with the documented `--report` flag pointing at an
absolute path outside the checkout, then `rm` of the stray file. Nothing warned
me the default was write-into-cwd; I inferred it from the `report:` line in the
output. A guess that cost nothing here but would have dirtied a shared clone.

**Bead** The chapter shows `clojure -M:run path/to/your/src/` before it shows
`--report out.edn`, and the first form silently writes into the tool's own
directory. Either default to the scanned tree's parent, or say in the fence that
the bare form writes `reagent-to-hicasso-report.edn` into the current directory.
close_reason: PR #9132 (head d98e796bb5). PREMISE HOLDS, reproduced: the default report path was the bare name reagent-to-hicasso-report.edn, which resolves against the process's WORKING DIRECTORY - and the chapter's first command is a cd into the tool's own directory, so the documented invocation wrote into the re-frame2 checkout the migrator had been told to treat as a read-only build input. Measured on the origin/main tool with a scratch corpus: the file landed in the tool's own directory, and the run's last line printed 'report: reagent-to-hicasso-report.edn' - the bare relative name, which names the file without naming the directory, which is the one thing a reader needed from it. FIXED by defaulting to BESIDE the first path scanned (point it at <repo>/src/ and the report lands at <repo>/, next to the tree it describes and inside the working copy the migrator is about to change anyway), and by printing 'wrote report: <ABSOLUTE path>'. Measured after: the report landed in the scanned tree's parent and the tool directory stayed clean. The usage text and the codemod README now state that every run writes one report and where it goes. THE :paths DEPRECATION WARNING IS NOT REPAIRED, deliberately, and the reason is recorded in deps.edn beside the entry: the sanctioned :local/root spelling would drag implementation/hicasso's own :deps (day8/re-frame2 and day8/re-frame2-ssr, by :local/root in turn) onto the classpath of a tool whose whole design premise is that it runs on a bare JVM and never loads re-frame2 - one pure .cljc file requiring clojure.string is the cheaper honesty. The bead's other limb - saying so in chapter 20's fence - was NOT taken: chapter 20 is held by another worker on worker/hicch20-a and is untouched here.

title: reagent-slim pr-atom: the *ratom-context* nil binding pops before pr-writer runs, so it guards nothing
description:
In reagent-slim's `ratom.cljs`, `pr-atom` reads:

  (pr-writer (binding [*ratom-context* nil] body) writer opts)

The `binding` scopes the nil `*ratom-context*` to evaluating `body` — which is an ALREADY-COMPUTED LOCAL — and pops the binding before `pr-writer` ever runs. So the guard covers no nested printing whatsoever.

The apparent intent is to stop printing from being captured as a reactive dependency: printing a ratom dereferences it, and doing that inside a live `*ratom-context*` would register a spurious dependency on whatever is currently tracking. If that is the intent, the binding must wrap the `pr-writer` call, not the argument.

ESTABLISH THE INTENT BEFORE MOVING IT. Two possibilities and they have different repairs:
- The guard is meant to cover the whole print, and its position is a bug. Repair: move the `binding` to wrap `pr-writer`. Prove it with a plant — construct a print inside a live `*ratom-context*` and show a dependency IS registered today and is NOT after the fix.
- The dereference genuinely all happens while computing `body`, and `pr-writer` cannot deref anything. Then the binding is correctly placed and merely looks wrong, and the deliverable is a comment saying so. A verified "this is correct as written" is a complete deliverable.

Do NOT move it on the strength of how it reads. This is a reactive-substrate seam; a wrong move here changes dependency capture.

CONTEXT: found while working rf2-6r9j.29 (PR #9127), which removed `pr-atom`'s unused receiver argument and ADDED the print pins that were previously absent — the suite had asserted nothing about either type's printed form, so "representation unchanged" had no instrument at all. Those new pins are your starting instrument. The line was explicitly outside .29's fence and is unchanged by its diff.

Surface: `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/ratom.cljs`.
close_reason: PR #9155. Intent ESTABLISHED, not assumed: the guard is real but mispositioned - the bead's first branch. binding wrapped 'body', an already-computed local, so it popped before pr-writer ran; but pr-writer recurses into the value and a NESTED ratom's own -pr-writer derefs it, and -deref calls notify-deref-watcher!. Demonstrated with a new test that prints a ratom-inside-a-ratom inside a live reactive context: BEFORE the fix both assertions failed - the nested ratom was in the reaction's .-watching set, and the printer re-ran (2 vs 1) when that nested ratom changed; AFTER moving the binding to wrap the pr-writer call both pass, suite totals unchanged at 11174 tests / 55752 assertions, 0 failures. Deliberately NOT changed: the receiver's own deref stays at the call site ({:val (-deref a)} in both -pr-writer methods), because a Reaction's -deref branches on *ratom-context* and a nil context additionally forces flush! plus an on-demand recompute - draining the reaction queue from inside pr-str is a behaviour change beyond suppressing capture, and is the wrong move at this seam the bead warns about. Rationale and residual recorded in the source comment. PR #9127 did not cause this; the shape dates from the file's first commit.

title: Clarify Hicasso collector queue and snapshot roles
description:
## Evidence
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs` implements two reaper queues and snapshot/notification loops with one-letter roles such as `q`, `x`, `id`, `r`, `n`, `c`, `ks`, and `k` across multi-stage mutation paths.
- The queue helpers carry distinct concepts (queue object, queued item, timer generation, target/due timestamps), while the snapshot loop distinguishes read keys from retained cells; the current names force readers to reconstruct those roles from property access.
- Whole-repo consumer and history review shows these are lexical/private implementation names only. Public vars, JS property strings, timing contracts, and documented `run-once` vocabulary need not move.

## Actionable insight
Rename only private arguments and locals to their semantic roles, e.g. `queue`, `item`, `arm-id`, `due-at-ms`, `now-ms`, `registration`, `notify`, `read-keys`, `read-key`, and `cell`. This makes timer supersession and snapshot fallback logic reviewable without altering executable structure.

## Ambiguity cost
The same one-letter name currently changes meaning between a queue, a registration, a callback, a read key, and a cell. That is especially expensive in the reaper and commit paths, where an incorrect role assumption can invert lifecycle or notification reasoning.

## Risks / migration
No public API migration. Preserve every public/private var name, JS object property (`items`, `due`, `target`, `seq`, etc.), serialized value, timeout ordering, and hot-path structure. Apply lexical renames only and verify exact old-name patterns plus runtime tests.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Collector queue, notification, entry-match, and snapshot locals state their roles rather than relying on one-letter names where the scope spans multiple operations.
2. No public var, JS property string, runtime operation, timing, or allocation structure changes.
3. Hicasso focused tests/lint pass and `git diff --check` is clean.
close_reason: Implemented and validated lexical role renames; focused Hicasso compile, kondo, invariants, node syntax, controlled browser, HMR, and diff gates pass.

title: Name SSR Ring non-streaming pipeline values by lifecycle stage
description:
## Finding

The facade and non-streaming response pipeline contain short or generic locals whose role changes by lifecycle stage. The middleware binds ssr; render-error-body uses status*/code*/msg*/hiccup; build-full-response* uses render, head-bag, rf-payload, html, post-render-resp, and post-error; project-render-throw->ring-response uses resp* and public-error*. These names make it unnecessarily difficult to distinguish resolved input, rendered HTML, hydration data, and post-render accumulator/error values in the longest correctness-critical flow.

## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:367-374: ssr is the constructed SSR request handler, not SSR state.
- implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:326-355: starred abbreviations and hiccup obscure the error document fields.
- pipeline.clj:583-658: the long response builder crosses render, head, payload, shell, and post-render flush stages, while generic locals do not encode those stage boundaries.
- pipeline.clj:693-707: resp*/public-error* mean the projected response and fallback-resolved public error.
- Spec 011 and docs/api/re-frame.ssr.ring.md establish public function/option/result names. These edits are internal locals only.
- Phase-1 bead rf2-6r9j.44 owns removal of build-full-response's obsolete resp argument; this naming work must not rename or otherwise churn that deletion target.

## Recommendation

Use stage-bearing local names such as ssr-request-handler, error-status/error-code/error-message/error-document, render-body, head-data, hydration-payload, response-html, post-render-response/post-render-public-error, projected-response, and resolved-public-error. Preserve all public function names and do not touch the obsolete resp parameter owned by rf2-6r9j.44.

## Risks / contracts

Do not alter evaluation order, frame scope, renderer input/result keys, payload keys, post-render flush timing, projected-error classification, or response bytes.

## Acceptance criteria

- Surviving locals clearly encode their lifecycle role and all consumers are updated.
- rf2-6r9j.44's slated-for-removal resp arguments are untouched.
- Public names, serialized keys, error ids, renderer map shape, and behavior are unchanged.
- Default SSR Ring tests and focused lint pass.
close_reason: Implemented scoped internal/private/local clarity renames; preserved public and wire contracts; clj-kondo, 231-test default lane, 9-test JVM-Node crossing lane, exact searches, and diff-check all pass.

title: Core namespaces: finish the canonical rf.* require-alias migration
description:
Partition: implementation/core namespace and require-alias vocabulary across source and tests.

Evidence:
- spec/Conventions.md, Require-alias dialect, requires re-frame.core to use rf and every framework subsystem re-frame.<leaf> to use the dotted rf.<leaf> alias; bare leaf aliases are reserved for application namespaces.
- A clj-kondo namespace-usage census over all 88 source and 272 test files found 1,616 distinct noncanonical framework require edges in 311 files after deduplicating CLJC host analysis: 328 edges in 68 source files and 1,288 in 243 test files. Examples include re-frame.late-bind :as late-bind, re-frame.frame :as frame, re-frame.trace :as trace, and re-frame.trace.tooling :as trace-tooling.
- Commit d848371f60 established the rule and explicitly deferred SCOPE 2, the repository-wide sweep. Current history shows narrow routing/machines documentation follow-ups but no core implementation sweep.
- All-status bead searches found only closed narrow machines/docs residues (rf2-qt7au, rf2-ur6kh, rf2-lzrza), not a core-wide migration.

Ambiguity cost:
Core currently teaches a different alias language from its own normative convention. Bare framework aliases collide conceptually with the application aliases the rule reserves, and readers cannot distinguish framework-owned dependencies at call sites without checking each ns form.

Recommendation:
Migrate core in coherent, reviewable families to the exact dotted namespace-tail aliases (for example re-frame.frame -> rf.frame, re-frame.late-bind -> rf.late-bind, re-frame.trace.tooling -> rf.trace.tooling), updating every qualified use. Keep re-frame.core -> rf as the explicit exemption. Add an automated ratchet based on parsed namespace usages so new bare framework aliases cannot enter while migration proceeds or after it reaches zero.

Risks/contracts:
Aliases are compile-time source vocabulary rather than runtime API, but this is a high-churn 311-file change spanning CLJ, CLJS, CLJC reader conditionals, macros, and test helpers. Mechanical replacement must avoid keyword roots, quoted data, late-bind keys, public symbols, prose, app namespaces, and external library aliases. Stage and gate it separately rather than folding it into unrelated semantic edits.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every tracked implementation/core source and test namespace aliases re-frame.core as rf and other re-frame subsystem namespaces with the canonical rf.<namespace-tail> spelling, unless an explicit convention exemption is documented.
- Every qualified symbol use is updated and exact parsed census reports zero non-exempt bare framework aliases.
- A syntax-aware CI ratchet rejects newly introduced violations and handles CLJC reader conditionals without double counting.
- Core JVM tests, relevant CLJS builds/tests, bundle-isolation checks, lint, and git diff --check pass.
- No keyword IDs, late-bind keys, serialized data, public vars, or application/external namespace aliases are changed.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #9103: reopened for one non-exempt core alias the migration census missed. implementation/core/test/re_frame/late_bind_drift_test.clj uses a real top-level (require ...) form at line 36, binding re-frame.late-bind.directory as bare directory, then calls directory/hooks, directory/hook-keys, and directory/entry. Spec Conventions reserves the bare leaf form for application namespaces; this must be rf.late-bind.directory with its qualified uses moved. A post-merge scan of every [re-frame.* :as *] form found 31 apparent exceptions: 16 documented host-conditional substrate bindings, 11 routing fixture strings, 3 user-facing/example forms, and this single executable core miss. Keep rf2-j5or as the existing owner of the shared future ratchet; no second ratchet is needed here.
close_reason:
PR #9128 (head fec380e7d83ce18dedb45196ba94c23d5c39ab39, branch worker/corealias-a). The residue behind PR #9103 was ONE edge in ONE file, and the merged-PR audit note on this bead named it exactly: implementation/core/test/re_frame/late_bind_drift_test.clj:36. Migrated to rf.late-bind.directory with its 8 qualified use sites. implementation/core now reads 0 non-exempt noncanonical require edges.

CENSUS, by balanced-bracket scan of every [re-frame...] libspec vector over 349 tracked core .clj/.cljs/.cljc files (1795 re-frame require edges total): pre-#9103 tree (1db71eac77^) 1617 non-exempt noncanonical edges across 311 files; post-#9103 origin/main 1 edge in 1 file; this branch 0. PR #9103 itself touched 312 core files, +11168/-11155.

WHY #9103 MISSED IT, and the account is exact rather than a guess. The edge is not an (ns ... (:require ...)) edge at all — it is a runtime top-level (require '[re-frame.late-bind.directory :as directory]), which clj-kondo's namespace-usage analysis does not report. That is why the bead's clj-kondo census read 1616 where a textual balanced-bracket scan of the SAME tree reads 1617: the one-edge delta IS this edge. Worth carrying to rf2-ydpr's ratchet design, which currently specifies scanning libspec vectors but does not say that runtime (require ...) forms must be in scope — they must, or the ratchet reproduces this exact miss.

LITERAL-KEYWORD MULTISET CONTROL: IDENTICAL before and after, 0 entries changed — 3652 distinct literal single-colon :ns/name keywords, 22833 occurrences, across all of implementation/core. Not a claim; the diff of the two multisets is empty.

HOST-CONDITIONAL EXEMPTIONS: ZERO in core, by the DERIVED predicate (an alias bound to 2+ distinct namespaces within one file), not a path list. This refines rf2-j5or's note, which said 'machines has one instance, routing had eight, core one'. Core has none: the predicate found no alias bound to two namespaces in any of the 349 files, including the 143 core .cljc files that carry BOTH reader conditionals and re-frame requires. Textual edge count equals deduplicated edge count (1795 = 1795), so no core file binds the same libspec twice across reader arms either — core's re-frame requires sit in the common part.

TRAP 1 CONFIRMED LIVE IN CORE: 39 libspec vectors in core SPAN LINES, e.g. [re-frame.trace :as rf.trace / #?@(:cljs [:include-macros true])]. A line-anchored regex would have missed every one. They are all already canonical, which is precisely why a line-oriented census would still have reported a clean run.

TRAP 5 DID NOT FIRE AND COULD NOT HAVE, both ways. This sweep produced no auto-resolved ::rf.* keyword at all (the file carries zero ::directory/, :directory/, #'directory/ and 'directory/ forms), and check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py's scan surface EXCLUDES test/ trees, where the whole change lives. So no false reservation arose and spec/Conventions.md needs NO row — the hot-zone one-toucher file was not touched and does not need to be.

GATES, captured exit codes read from files: core JVM clojure -M:test exit 0, 2177 tests / 11158 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors. Focused clojure -M:test -n re-frame.late-bind-drift-test exit 0, 8 tests / 695 assertions — the count matters because a file whose ns form the reader cannot read is INVISIBLE to cognitect.test-runner and the suite still exits 0 (the defect re-frame.test-quiet-discovery-integrity-test pins); counting the file's 8 deftests is what rules that out. check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py exit 0. clj-kondo --lint implementation/core: 640 warnings / 0 errors, IDENTICAL to the same tree with this file reverted, zero delta. git diff --check exit 0.

BOTH LIVE GATES PROVEN TO BITE AND TO BE READING THIS CHECKOUT. A planted rf.late-bind.directoryX/hooks returned exit 1 naming rf.late-bind.directoryX — a token existing only in this worktree, so a run that had wandered into a sibling would have come back green; restored and verified by blob hash 0c3b55026700f8569e0b998fc76a3d4a50c89ef7. A planted ::rf.zzzprobe/planted in late_bind.cljc returned the catalogue checker exit 1 naming :rf.zzzprobe/*; restored, blob a6afbfcf54067de601b2b438c770e0dfc5a8bac1. A FIRST plant attempt matched ZERO lines and its no-op was caught by reading the match count before spending a run — the sabotage would otherwise have returned a green that read as 'the control does not bite'.

npm run test:cljs NOT NOMINATED, by measurement rather than reasoning: the :node-test build selects on :ns-regexp "cljs-test$", which re-frame.late-bind-drift-test does not match (control: re-frame.foo-cljs-test does), the file is .clj rather than a CLJS source, and nothing :requires the namespace. It would have been a green over a subject the build cannot load.

CENSUS INSTRUMENT EXERCISED against inputs it should flag before its zero was believed: 339 noncanonical edges in implementation/adapters/, 112 in implementation/schemas/.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 3 REMAINS UNMET AND IS NOT ORPHANED: the syntax-aware CI ratchet is rf2-ydpr's, per rf2-j5or's disposition — scripts/ + .github/workflows/ are hot-zone and one repo-wide instrument is right, not one per artefact.

title: reagent-slim component lifecycle: name helpers and locals by role
description:
## Finding

The private Form-3 lifecycle plumbing in `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs` contains names that omit their decisive context (`validate-spec!`, `prev-argv-from`, `bind-and-call`, `install-lifecycle!`) and generic locals (`klass`, `proto`, lifecycle `f`, `cached-rea`). This makes a contract-heavy bridge harder to follow than its behavior warrants.

## Evidence and ambiguity cost

- `validate-spec!` at lines 135-155 validates specifically a `create-class` spec against the seven-key cap, not an arbitrary spec.
- `prev-argv-from` at lines 358-362 extracts `__rfArgv` specifically from React previous props; the omitted source is the important distinction fixed/documented by `rf2-08hx1`.
- `bind-and-call` at lines 364-371 is not a generic binding helper: it establishes `*current-component*` around one callback.
- `install-lifecycle!` at lines 382-495 installs several React prototype/static methods, not one lifecycle value. Nearby `klass`/`proto` and three unrelated `f` bindings force readers to reconstruct which class/prototype/callback each closure captures.
- `make-render-method` uses `cached-rea`/`new-rea` for the component render Reaction, even though `rea` is otherwise the namespace's scheduler abbreviation.
- Exact repository searches show the helpers are private and source-confined. Targeted history shows the lifecycle names originated in Stage 4-C; later correctness fixes changed behavior without establishing them as public compatibility seams.

## Recommendation

Rename to `validate-class-spec!`, `previous-argv-from-props`, `call-with-current-component`, and `install-lifecycle-methods!`; use `component-class`, `prototype`, lifecycle-specific callback names, and `render-reaction` locals where those values cross closure boundaries.

## Contracts and risk

Preserve all public `reagent2.core`/component Vars, `cap-keys`, lifecycle keywords, callback arities/order, React method names, emitted JS fields/metadata, dynamic `*current-component*`, and the seven-key cap. This is source-internal naming only; no alias/migration layer is appropriate. Do not alter the vacuous error-boundary tests owned by `rf2-6r9j.31` or dead test declarations owned by `rf2-6r9j.34`.

## Duplicate search

All-status beads were searched for every old helper and component/lifecycle naming concepts. `rf2-08hx1` is the closed behavioral/docs correction for previous argv semantics, not a private-helper naming task; no bead owns these renames.
acceptance_criteria:
- The proposed private helper names and role-specific lifecycle/render locals replace the ambiguous names throughout component source and directly referencing in-slice documentation.
- Exact old-name searches in `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim` are empty except immutable historical bead text outside the tracked slice.
- Callback arity/order, previous-props to previous-argv translation, current-component dynamic binding, StrictMode reattachment, error-boundary state, JS fields, and public component API remain unchanged.
- Focused component tests plus lint/compile checks pass, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- No code/test behavior owned by `rf2-6r9j.31` or `rf2-6r9j.34` is changed.
notes: Implemented private lifecycle helper renames and component-class/prototype/render-reaction locals. React lifecycle method names, cljsReagent fields, metadata, class cap, and public component surface are unchanged. Updated the in-slice spec/comment references. Final focused CLJS suite, JVM suite, lint, exact search, public-def audit, and diff-check pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in commit 218061b7b7: private/local naming clarified without public or serialized contract changes; focused JVM/CLJS/lint/bundle/search/diff gates pass.

title: Make the event-conformance explicit-live test discriminate the policy override
description:
## Finding

`reg-event-explicit-live-mint-policy-mints-the-declared-nondeterminism-escape` in `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_model_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` dispatches into the fixture's ordinary `:rf/default` frame, whose no-config mint policy is already `:live`. A missing generator-backed fact therefore mints whether `{:rf.cofx/mint-policy :explicit-live}` is honored, ignored, renamed, or removed. The test cannot detect the policy behavior named by its title; it only repeats the immediately preceding live-generation coverage.

Core's dual-runtime `explicit-live-overrides-strict-frame-generates` has the discriminating setup: a `:preset :test` frame defaults to `:strict`, the per-call `:explicit-live` value must override it, and the generator/run result prove the escape was used. Core also separately proves strict refuses the same class of missing fact.

## Recommendation

Remove the non-discriminating conformance row as a strict subset of the core owner, or reshape it around a strict frame with a paired control: without the per-call override, the generator stays at zero and dispatch fails missing-required; with `:explicit-live`, it runs exactly once and delivers the fact. Prefer one canonical dual-runtime owner rather than two copies.

## Risks and contracts

Preserve the public dispatch-options path and dual JVM/CLJS coverage for `:explicit-live`; do not replace it with a direct call to the internal policy resolver. The negative and positive legs must use equivalent frame/fact setup so the option is the only discriminator.

## Evidence

The conformance row creates no strict/test frame and supplies only `:rf.cofx/mint-policy :explicit-live`; the documented/default runtime policy is `:live`. `implementation/core/test/re_frame/cofx_cljs_test.cljc` already contains `router-default-is-live-generates`, `test-preset-default-is-strict-does-not-generate`, and `explicit-live-overrides-strict-frame-generates`, all through `rf/dispatch-sync` in a `.cljc` suite.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The event-conformance row is removed or changed so ignoring/removing the `:explicit-live` option makes it fail.
2. If retained, the test establishes a strict baseline/control and then proves the per-call option alone enables one mint and handler delivery.
3. Dual-runtime public-dispatch coverage remains in at least one canonical suite.
4. Event-conformance JVM tests and the consolidated CLJS Node suite pass.
close_reason: Premise held, proven by plant. Planting cofx/resolve-mint-policy to DROP its per-call argument -- the option honoured nowhere -- left the old row reg-event-explicit-live-mint-policy-mints-the-declared-nondeterminism-escape GREEN at exit 0 while core's explicit-live-overrides-strict-frame-generates went exit 1. Chose the bead's RESHAPE option over removal (the title asks for a discriminating row, and the public dispatch-options path is worth keeping at the conformance tier): renamed to reg-event-explicit-live-mint-policy-overrides-a-strict-frame, built on a :preset :test frame whose mint policy defaults to :strict, with a paired CONTROL that dispatches WITHOUT the opt (asserts :rf.error/missing-required-cofx, zero generator calls, handler never ran) and then the same dispatch WITH :explicit-live (exactly one mint, flat delivery). The new row was re-planted in BOTH directions: per-call ignored -> exit 1, escape leg errors missing-required; frame :strict ignored -> exit 1, control leg 4 failures. AC1-4 met: ignoring the option now makes it fail, the strict baseline/control is established, core keeps the dual-runtime owner, gates green (event-conformance JVM 44/186 exit 0, node suite 11163/55721 exit 0). PR #9123.

title: Stop serializing ssr-node worker stacks that receivers discard
description:
## Evidence

- The worker serializes err.stack into both cross-thread error messages: boot-error at implementation/ssr-node/src/worker.cjs:80-86 and render error at :210-223.
- The boot receiver at src/isolate.cjs:91-95 reads only msg.code and msg.message, then creates detail containing modulePath. It never reads msg.stack.
- The render receiver at src/isolate.cjs:186-195 reads code, message, detail, and afterChunks. It never reads msg.stack.
- A whole-repository search finds no consumer of either posted stack field. The stack assertions in egress.test.cjs concern the parent-created Refusal stack, not these worker-message properties.
- The separate Worker error-event handler at isolate.cjs:98-101 reads err.stack directly; that live diagnostic does not depend on the message fields and must remain.
- Both discarded message properties date to b2b35bf6e9. No existing bead found by worker stack, boot-error stack, render-error stack, or ssr-node searches owns them.

## Impact

Every application boot/render exception needlessly serializes a potentially large, path-bearing stack across the worker boundary and then drops it. The presence of the field falsely suggests that this diagnostic survives into the service refusal, which makes debugging and egress review harder.

## Disposition

Remove stack from the worker's boot-error and render-error payloads. Preserve the live Worker error-event stack handling and the normal parent Refusal stack. Do not wire an application stack into HTTP/client egress as a way to make the field live; the existing boundary intentionally limits diagnostics.

## Risks

The worker error payloads are security-sensitive egress. Removing the dead field is safer than broadening the receiver, but tests should continue proving that refusal objects and HTTP bodies do not leak application stack contents. Avoid conflating an application-thrown render error with a worker_threads error event.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Neither boot-error nor render-error worker messages serialize err.stack.
2. No application stack is added to the parent detail or HTTP refusal body.
3. The live Worker error-event path still retains err.stack in its internal Refusal detail.
4. Boot failure, render failure, post-chunk failure, egress, and full ssr-node tests remain green.
close_reason: PR #9099. Discard proven at BOTH receivers before the sends were removed. Boot receiver: isolate.cjs handleBootMessage reads message.code and message.message only, then builds new Refusal(code, message, {modulePath: this.modulePath}) -- the detail is the parent's own field, message.stack never appears. Render receiver: _handleRenderMessage's message.t==='error' branch reads code, message, detail and afterChunks, spreading message.detail only. Those two handlers are the whole of worker.on('message') in the parent, so no third consumer exists. err.stack removed from both worker.cjs payloads (boot-error and render error). The live worker.on('error') handler, which holds the real Error, still keeps err.stack in its internal Refusal detail (criterion 3). No stack added to parent detail or HTTP refusal body. egress.test.cjs:292's stack assertion was always about the parent-created Refusal's own JS stack, not these message properties -- verified. Suite 9/9 green, 108 rows; eslint exit 0.

title: Finish the flows exact-owner migration by removing dead bare-id registry paths
description:
Evidence
- `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:175-187` defines no-doc `drain-abandoned-output-paths!`, but exact whole-repository search finds no call. Its docstring still says `run-flows-on-db` consumes it; the live drain calls `pass-drain-abandoned-paths!` on a captured owner cell (`flows.cljc:304-311`, registry lines 242-251).
- Five legacy arities likewise have no repository caller: the 2-arity of `reset-frame-last-inputs-to!` (registry:127-134), `restore-abandoned-output-paths!` (189-196), private `write-flow-output-marks!` (468-479), private `clear-flow-output-marks!` (481-503), and private `vacate-output-path!` (816-830). Current calls use the owner-token arities: the router invokes the two late-bound restore hooks with three arguments (`core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1311-1321`), and registry registration/clear paths call the three private helpers with pinned incarnation tokens (registry:672,687,868,879).
- `38c9671d97` introduced captured flow-pass cells and moved flow evaluation/rollback off the bare-id drain/restore path. `b5c4599df0` moved mark and vacation writes to exact-owner arities. Both migrations left their prior unguarded entry points in place.
- These vars are private or marked `^:no-doc`; they are absent from the public flows API docs and manifest. Test-only `get/set-frame-flow-last-inputs!`, snapshot accessors, `legacy-flow-pass-state`, and the documented three-argument `run-flows-on-db` compatibility path do have consumers and are explicitly out of scope.

Impact and disposition
The unused entry points retain bare-frame-id mutations that bypass the incarnation fence the live lifecycle now requires, and one stale doc describes a consumer that no longer exists. Remove the zero-consumer drain helper and the five unused legacy arities/fallback branches, leaving the exact-owner and captured-cell paths as the single mutation authority.

Risk
Do not remove the public/direct three-argument `run-flows-on-db` compatibility contract or test accessors with real consumers. Preserve rollback semantics, post-commit hook behavior, lifecycle serialization, hot-reload cache invalidation, and exact-incarnation fencing. If version-skew compatibility for no-doc hooks is intentionally supported, document and test that policy instead of retaining an unverified fallback silently.
acceptance_criteria:
- Remove `drain-abandoned-output-paths!` and its false `run-flows-on-db` consumer claim.
- Remove the unused two-argument forms of `reset-frame-last-inputs-to!`, `restore-abandoned-output-paths!`, `write-flow-output-marks!`, `clear-flow-output-marks!`, and `vacate-output-path!`; live calls remain owner-token/captured-cell based.
- Exact repository search shows no unguarded bare-id caller or fallback branch for those lifecycle mutations.
- Preserve `legacy-flow-pass-state`, the documented three-argument `run-flows-on-db` path, and consumed test/snapshot accessors.
- Flow rollback, output-path vacation, registration/clear, watch-triggered same-id reincarnation, default JVM/CLJS, and slow contention suites pass.
close_reason: All SIX dead bare-id paths removed, not just the one the title names (PR #9082). Every line number in the bead re-derived exact (127, 175, 189, 468, 481, 816). drain-abandoned-output-paths! removed outright — census found exactly ONE tree-wide hit, its own defn, while its docstring still claimed run-flows-on-db consumed it and the live drain calls pass-drain-abandoned-paths!. Five arities collapsed to owner-token-only: reset-frame-last-inputs-to!, restore-abandoned-output-paths!, write-flow-output-marks!, clear-flow-output-marks!, vacate-output-path!, each with its (if owner-token ...) fallback branch. Verified rather than assumed: the router's only invocations of the two late-bind restore hooks pass THREE arguments (router.cljc:1311-1321, as filed), and the four private call sites all pass a pinned incarnation token. The one real hazard was checked at source — clear-flow's pinned has no nil guard and frame-incarnation-token can return nil — and dropping the fallback is safe because swap-partition!'s exact path admits a write only under (identical? owner-token (:drain-lock frame-record)), so a nil token is a no-op that writes nothing; the removed branch was the one that would have written through a bare id AFTER the incarnation fence failed. reg-flow additionally throws :rf.error/flow-frame-not-live first. Preserved: legacy-flow-pass-state, the three-argument run-flows-on-db path, test/snapshot accessors, and both ensure-*-atom! helpers (each keeps live callers). The drain-race test that patches vacate-output-path! through its var is unaffected — its replacement is variadic.
