title: Remove dead imports and bindings from schemas tests
description:
## Finding

The schemas test slice contains a bounded set of imports, local bindings, and nested `let` wrappers with no reader or behavioral effect. They are test-maintenance residue from earlier fixture/reset and handler shapes, distinct from namespaces intentionally required only for load/build side effects.

## Evidence

A focused clj-kondo run over `implementation/schemas/src` and `implementation/schemas/test`, followed by manual symbol and history checks, proves:

- Seven dead namespace aliases/imports: `re-frame.schemas.digest` in `schemas_concurrency_stress_test.clj`; `re-frame.substrate.adapter` in both `schemas_conformance_test.clj` and `schemas_reg_side_effects_test.clj`; `re-frame.schemas.validator` in `schemas_fail_open_test.clj`; `re-frame.registrar` and `re-frame.trace` in `schemas_test.clj`; and `re-frame.trace` in `schemas_validator_unavailable_warning_test.clj`. Repository searches find no qualified use of any alias in its file.
- Fifteen unused locals: three `db` destructurings in `schemas_cljs_test.cljs` (currently lines 62, 85, 342); two in `schemas_fail_open_test.clj` (169, 246); five in `schemas_sensitive_test.clj` (1561, 1597, 1632, 1728, 1753); four in `schemas_test.clj` (97, 124, 165, 297); plus the never-read `secret` binding in `schemas_sensitive_test.clj` (1161). The affected init handlers return fixed maps, so replacing their unused cofx destructure with `_` is behavior-neutral; the secret test dispatches integer `12345`, not that binding.
- Four single-body nested `let` forms in `schemas_fail_open_test.clj` (currently 178, 233, 255, 273) merely wrap an immediately enclosing `let` and are reported as redundant. Merging binding vectors preserves evaluation and assertion order.
- History ties several imports to superseded local reset fixtures. For example `c6017e7f32` moved registrar/frame/adapter cleanup to `schemas.test-fixture/reset-runtime` but left some caller imports behind.
- All-status bead searches for schemas test imports, schemas unused bindings, lint, and the named test paths found no owning issue.

## Deliberate exclusions

Do not remove `re-frame.core` from `schemas_bundle_control.cljs` or `schemas_bundle_probe.cljs`: both files explain that the unused alias is an intentional matched-build require and removing it invalidates the A/B. Do not blindly remove effect-only `re-frame.schemas` loads, unresolved macro/API references, or the app-db source's nested `let` around stale-incarnation checkpoints. Redundant direct Malli adapter test requires and their stale posture are owned separately by `rf2-6r9j.51`.

## Impact

Dead imports make test dependency boundaries look broader than they are; unused handler bindings and wrapper lets add noise to already large security/error-path suites and keep focused lint output noisy enough to hide new regressions. There is no intended runtime, public API, diagnostic, or fixture-isolation contract behind these items.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the seven proven-unused imports, replace only the fifteen unused locals with appropriately ignored parameters or delete the inert binding, and flatten the four test-only nested lets without changing their assertions or setup/cleanup order.

## Risks

Clojure namespace loads can be side-effectful and the bundle fixtures deliberately exploit that. Keep the change to the enumerated items, verify each require's absence does not alter hook/adapter initialization, and preserve `try/finally`, trace recorder, and stale-incarnation ordering.
acceptance_criteria:
- Focused clj-kondo no longer reports the seven enumerated unused namespaces, fifteen enumerated unused bindings, or four enumerated redundant lets.
- The intentional unused `re-frame.core` requires in both matched schemas bundle fixtures remain, with their explanatory contract intact.
- Effect-only facade/adapter wiring required for schema validation remains covered by `schemas_implies_validation_test` and `rf2-6r9j.51`; no load-order regression is introduced.
- Schemas JVM and CLJS suites pass, including conformance, fail-open, sensitive redaction, concurrency stress, validator-unavailable warning, and production boundary targets.
- Test names, assertion counts/semantics, `try/finally` restoration, and trace capture order are unchanged except for removal of inert syntax.
close_reason: PR #9111. All three enumerated groups landed; focused clj-kondo over implementation/schemas/{src,test} went 33 -> 7 warnings with errors 0, and the 26 cleared are exactly the enumerated set. Seven unused requires removed (schemas.digest in concurrency-stress; substrate.adapter in conformance and reg-side-effects; schemas.validator in fail-open; registrar and trace in schemas_test; trace in validator-unavailable-warning), each proven by TWO instruments -- a boundary-anchored git grep for the alias in its own file plus clj-kondo's alias resolution -- with a control alias in the SAME file returning a stable non-zero count every time. Worth recording: a naive substring grep for 'digest/' and 'trace/' returns FALSE HITS inside the qualified keywords :utdxg.digest/seed and :rf.trace/phase; the anchored form reads 0. Fifteen locals: fourteen cofx destructures on fixed-map init handlers replaced with _, plus the never-read secret binding at the container-level sensitive test (which dispatches the integer 12345, not the binding) -- adjacent sibling handlers that DO read db were left alone. Four single-body nested lets in fail-open merged into their enclosing let; the inner init depends on the outer binding so evaluation and assertion order are preserved. Kept per the bead's exclusions: both matched-build re-frame.core requires in the schemas bundle fixtures, the effect-only re-frame.schemas loads in conformance and reg-side-effects, and validate.cljc's nested let. Gates: schemas JVM 372 tests / 19221 assertions and npm run test:cljs 11168 / 55740, both exit 0, 0 failures 0 errors. Gate proven live by planting (is (neg? (count mal))) inside a FLATTENED let -- exit 1 naming schemas_fail_open_test.clj:178, the flattened block's own body line -- then restoring, hash-object identical. Test names, assertion counts and try/finally ordering unchanged.

title: Remove the response argument superseded by the post-render flush
description:
## Finding

The non-streaming response builder still accepts and forwards a pre-render `resp` argument that no longer participates in response materialisation. Both the private implementation and its internal public wrapper preserve an obsolete arity from before the pipeline began re-reading the live accumulator after rendering.

## Evidence

- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:569-658` defines private `build-full-response*` as `[frame-id resp opts]`; its body never reads `resp`. `clj-kondo` reports `pipeline.clj:576:13: warning: unused binding resp`.
- The wrapper at lines 709-765 also accepts `resp`, but only forwards it to the private helper. Its catch arm derives the current response from `ssr/peek-response` through `project-render-throw->ring-response`; it does not need the argument.
- The sole production call at `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:325` passes the response obtained before rendering. Three focused tests call the private helper with a dummy `{:status 200}` (`resource_payload_projection_test.clj:178,230,306`); no other code call exists.
- History identifies the superseding change. Before commit `2a97334c07` (2026-06-05), `build-full-response*` materialised from `resp`. That fail-closed fix replaced the read with `post-render-resp = (ssr/flush-response! frame-id)` so render-time response effects and projected failures cannot be lost, but left both parameter vectors and every call argument intact. Commit `555038b12f` later strengthened that re-read to `flush-response-result!`; the old input remained irrelevant.
- `re-frame.ssr.ring.pipeline` is explicitly internal in the API-manifest generator. The façade API is `ssr-handler`; no API page or spec promises this helper's arity.

Duplicate searches for `ssr-ring unused resp build-full-response`, `build-full-response obsolete response argument`, and `post-render-resp unused parameter` found no owning bead.

## Impact

The argument falsely suggests the wire result may be based on a pre-render response snapshot, obscuring the load-bearing invariant that response status/headers/cookies and post-render error projection are re-read after the render walk. Test calls reinforce the obsolete model with meaningless dummy maps, and the binding leaves a permanent lint warning.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `resp` from `build-full-response*`, `build-full-response`, the façade call, and the three direct private-helper tests. Preserve the pre-render `response` binding in `ssr-handler`, because redirect and projected-5xx branches still consume it before the happy-path builder.

## Risks

Do not replace the post-render flush with the caller snapshot or move it earlier. Render-time `:rf.server/*` effects, recovered-to-nil sub failures, projected 5xx diversion, and render-throw response materialisation must continue to use the live per-frame accumulator.
acceptance_criteria:
- `build-full-response*` and `build-full-response` accept only `frame-id` and `opts`; their production and test callers pass no dummy response map.
- The `ssr-handler` drain result still feeds redirect and projected-5xx branches, while the happy path calls the updated builder arity.
- `build-full-response*` still calls `flush-response-result!` after body/head/payload/shell work and materialises from `post-render-resp`; no behavior is changed to use a stale pre-render snapshot.
- Focused clj-kondo no longer reports the unused `resp` binding.
- ssr-ring tests pass, especially render-time sub fail-closed, drain-time projection, response headers/cookies accumulated during render, resource payload projection, and renderer-seam coverage.
notes: 2026-09-03 (httpvest-b worker, PR #9115 session) — NOT STARTED, premise mismatch in the dispatch, not in the bead. This bead was dispatched to me in a bundle briefed as 'all in implementation/http', with a fence that explicitly excluded implementation/ssr-ring because another worker holds it. Every file this bead names is in ssr-ring: implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj (build-full-response* at 578, build-full-response at 724, the forwarding call at 771), implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:325 (the sole production call), and implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/resource_payload_projection_test.clj:178,230,306 (the three dummy {:status 200} calls). Verified by git grep -F 'build-full-response' over tracked files: zero hits under implementation/http. NOTHING was done on this bead and no ssr-ring file was touched by PR #9115. The bead's own evidence and disposition still look sound on inspection — the dataflow claim was NOT disproved, merely not tested, because proving it requires reading and running ssr-ring, which was out of fence. Re-dispatch to whoever holds implementation/ssr-ring. Note for that worker: the .46 sibling in this bundle also names a JVM/CLJS gate pair, but the gate for this one is the ssr-ring suite, and the acceptance criteria call out render-time sub fail-closed, drain-time projection, response headers/cookies accumulated during render, resource payload projection and renderer-seam coverage specifically.
close_reason: PR #9162: build-full-response*/build-full-response drop the pre-render resp argument superseded by the post-render flush (2a97334c07, strengthened by 555038b12f). Body never read it; wrapper only forwarded it. ssr-handler keeps its pre-render response binding, still consumed by the redirect and projected-5xx branches. Three focused tests stop passing a dummy {:status 200}. ssr-ring suite exit 0 (231 tests/1163 assertions); reinstating the 3-arity call reds it with ArityException. Bead line numbers had drifted (588 not 569) because the :renderer seam landed in between; the dataflow claim held exactly.

title: reagent-slim IMPL-SPEC still specifies retired defview/util architecture
description:
## Finding

`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md` mixes a shipped disposition with earlier sections that still present retired or never-created Stage-4 architecture as the current implementation.

## Evidence

- The current source tree has no `reagent2.impl.util` namespace, yet the canonical layout lists `impl/util.cljs` at line 51 and §2.10 lines 354-361 specifies that file plus `fun-name`, `*non-reactive*`, and `dont-camel-case-pattern`. Exact repository searches find none of those slim symbols/files.
- The layout and current API inventory at lines 53, 318, 324, 337-338, 503, 522-548, 1090, and 1185 say `reagent2.impl.component/defview` ships. The same document's final disposition at line 1189 says it is not shipped; current `component.clj:10-12` and `component.cljs:31-33` agree with the disposition.
- §2.4 line 288 specifies an internal `apply-hiccup` used by render/hydrate; no such def exists. Both production entry points directly call `reagent2.impl.template/as-element`.
- §2.8 lines 326-334 lists nonexistent current component helpers (`do-render`, `wrap-funs`, `cancel-cleanup`, `queue-cleanup`) while omitting the actual lifecycle helper structure.
- §2.9 and the scheduler narrative describe separate atom-backed `dirty-set`, `scheduled?`, and `after-render-queue`; current batching uses one `RenderQueue` instance with fields and arrays.
- History shows §14 was amended to record the no-defview decision (`rf2-prkgge` referenced in the heading), but the earlier prescriptive sections were not reconciled.

## Impact

The document calls itself the implementation contract and is linked as such from README. Readers and coding agents can infer nonexistent public APIs, files, helpers, and state models, or spend work restoring deliberately rejected features. Contradictory current-tense claims also make it impossible to use the spec as a reachability inventory.

## Proposed disposition

Reconcile every current architecture/API inventory with the shipped tree. Remove or explicitly mark superseded Stage sketches as historical; make the no-defview disposition authoritative throughout; delete the nonexistent util/apply-hiccup/helper inventories; and describe the actual RenderQueue/component seams at contract-level detail. Preserve useful decision history and rejected-surface rationale without presenting it as shipped code.

## Risks

This is not permission to rewrite historical decisions or expand the slim API. Keep explicitly historical Stage rationale, public compatibility commitments, and rejected-surface explanations; change only statements presented as current/shipped architecture.

## Duplicate search

Searched all 575 bead records in every state for `IMPL-SPEC`, `defview`, `util.cljs`, `apply-hiccup`, and reagent-slim. `rf2-b9l8o` fixed the reaction macro and `rf2-08hx1` fixes lifecycle argv; Hicasso defview matches are a different namespace. No active or closed bead owns this reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria:
- A systematic inventory of every file/symbol named as current in §§2, 4, 5, 12, and 14 resolves to tracked shipped source or is explicitly labeled historical/rejected.
- No current-tense section says reagent-slim ships `defview`, `reagent2.impl.util`, `apply-hiccup`, `do-render`, `wrap-funs`, `cancel-cleanup`, or `queue-cleanup`.
- The scheduler description matches the `RenderQueue` representation and preserves the observable queue/flush contract without over-specifying dead internals.
- The canonical layout matches `rg --files implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src` exactly at namespace/file granularity.
- README, component namespace docs, and IMPL-SPEC agree that compile-time classification is folded into `reg-view` and no separate `defview` surface ships.
- Relevant docs-link/slug checks pass, and manual review confirms headings/tables remain coherent; no source/API behavior changes are included.
close_reason:
FIXED by PR #9119, https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9119, head 62983abf92. Every premise verified at source before editing; all of them held.

VERIFIED ABSENT from the shipped tree (git grep -F over tracked src+test, no -i, .beads excluded): reagent2.impl.util / impl/util.cljs, fun-name, *non-reactive*, dont-camel-case-pattern, apply-hiccup, do-render, wrap-funs, cancel-cleanup, queue-cleanup — zero files each. defview appears only in the two source docstrings that say it is NOT shipped, one test that asserts the same, and this document.

CORRECTED AS FALSE CURRENT-TENSE ARCHITECTURE (the doc calls itself the implementation contract and README links it as such, so each of these was buildable-against): §1.1 canonical layout (listed impl/util.cljs, duplicated the impl/ node, labelled component.clj "defview macro", omitted impl/diag.cljs, and used a _test.cljs test-file convention the tree does not use) — now mirrors git ls-files .../src file-for-file, which is the acceptance criterion. §2.4 internal apply-hiccup (render and hydrate-root each call template/as-element directly) and its omission of flush-render!, which ships. §2.7 "the defview macro lives in component.clj". §2.8 four nonexistent lifecycle helpers, replaced with the actual private structure at contract level (validate-class-spec!, install-lifecycle-methods!, make-render-method, argv-should-update?, sync-error-state!, ->react-element, and the argv/form-tag feeders) plus the correction that disposal is INLINE in an always-installed componentWillUnmount, not a deferred cleanup queue. §2.9 + §4.1 + §4.5 atom-backed dirty-set/scheduled? and set-membership dedup — the shipped scheduler is ONE RenderQueue deftype with three mutable fields and lazily allocated JS arrays, and dedup is a cljsIsDirty flag on the component instance (stock Reagent field name, kept so introspection hooks keep working). §2.10 entire nonexistent reagent2.impl.util namespace, replaced by reagent2.impl.diag, which DOES ship and which §2 documented nowhere. §4.2 flush-views! pseudocode and its "Stage 4 finalises the invocation; the import is react :refer [act]" forward-looking note. §5 defview framing; §5.1 wrap-render sketch (wrong arity, wrong cached-field name, no mention of the compile-time fold); §5.2, now describing the fold that actually ships — classify-form-body / tag-form-meta, called from the reg-view expansion — which is what the component.clj ns docstring already cites "§5.2 + §14.1" as. §12.1 and §12.5 test filenames.

PRESERVED AS DELIBERATE HISTORY — the retirement-category call the brief asked for. Every §14 "Disposition (as shipped)" record stays verbatim; §14.3-§14.6 rationale stays; every "not shipped" / DECISION-n row stays. §14.1 was the one needing judgement: its opening TWO PARAGRAPHS were written in the present tense ("Stage 4 ships reagent2.impl.component/defview...") directly ABOVE a disposition saying it was never shipped. Deleting them would have destroyed the question the rf2-yfbx decision answers, so they are marked as the question AS IT STOOD BEFORE STAGE 4 and left otherwise word-for-word. Only the tense was lying. Likewise R-003 in the risk register: reframed as retired-with-reason (no defview surface ships, so the risk cannot occur) rather than deleted, since the row records a real Stage-2 concern.

ONE IN-FENCE SOURCE DOCSTRING corrected alongside, same defect class: the component.cljs ns doc named a "reagent2.impl.component/-form-tag meta" that does not exist. The real meta key is :reagent2/form, built by tag-form-meta on the CLJ side.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: layout matches src exactly at file granularity; no current-tense section says slim ships defview, reagent2.impl.util, apply-hiccup, do-render, wrap-funs, cancel-cleanup or queue-cleanup; the scheduler description matches the RenderQueue representation and keeps the observable queue/flush contract (next-turn cascade holding and per-callback throw isolation are called out as contract, not incidental); README, the component ns docs and IMPL-SPEC now agree that compile-time classification is folded into reg-view and no separate defview surface ships. No source or API behaviour changed.

GATES: scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0 — this is the gate for markdown beside source, since check_doc_slugs.py roots do not reach implementation/ and nominating it here would have been the wrong gate — proved live by a planted broken link returning exit 1 with file, line and missing target. check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. clj-kondo exit 0 on the changed source. npm run test:cljs exit 0, 11169 tests / 55731 assertions. mkdocs build --strict NOT nominated: docs_dir is docs, and the hook stages only spec/ and migration/, neither of which this path is under. Headings and table column counts checked by hand — no gate validates markdown prose, tables or rendering.

title: Remove duplicate unused views.provider/*current-frame*
description:
Evidence
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs:247` defines `^:dynamic *current-frame*`, but a repository-wide exact qualified/reference search finds no binding or read of `re-frame.views.provider/*current-frame*`; definition-level analysis reports zero usages.
- The adjacent `current-frame` resolver reads the canonical `re-frame.frame/*current-frame*` at `provider.cljs:289`, then falls through to React context. Binding the provider-local Var therefore has no effect.
- Split commit `603e03b448` (2026-05-12) explicitly says it “drops the dead local def of ^:dynamic *current-frame* in views.cljs,” but the newly created `views/provider.cljs` in that same commit copied the dead definition into the split namespace.
- The Var is neither re-exported by `re-frame.views` nor listed in the API manifest/spec.

Why this is vestigial
This is a duplicate dynamic Var with the same semantic-looking name as the canonical frame scope Var, but it participates in no resolution path. Its presence invites internal or exploratory callers to bind the wrong Var and observe no effect.

Proposed disposition
Delete only `re-frame.views.provider/*current-frame*`. Keep `re-frame.frame/*current-frame*` as the sole dynamic frame carrier and preserve the React-context fallback.

Risks / constraints
The provider namespace is internal and the Var was never effective, but an unsupported caller might nevertheless bind it. Do not change the public resolution order, no-frame behavior, context coercion, or adapter hook while removing it.
acceptance_criteria:
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs` no longer defines `*current-frame*`; the canonical `re-frame.frame/*current-frame*` remains intact.
- Repository search finds no reference to `re-frame.views.provider/*current-frame*` or `provider/*current-frame*`.
- `current-frame` still resolves dynamic frame scope first and React context second, with existing no-frame behavior unchanged.
- Core view/current-component tests and React adapter frame-provider/context suites pass on supported hosts.
close_reason: Done in PR #9083. Premise re-verified at tip and HELD, and the two Vars were distinguished BY NAMESPACE rather than by name, which is the check an unqualified search would have got wrong. THE OTHER *current-frame* IS re-frame.frame/*current-frame* at core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:518. Exactly two ^:dynamic *current-frame* definitions exist repository-wide: that one and the duplicate at views/provider.cljs:247 (line re-derived, held). A BARE search conflates them at 338 hits and is useless here. HOW THEY WERE DISTINGUISHED - clj-kondo :analysis keyed on namespace: of 182 ':name *current-frame*' entries, 3 are :var-definitions (re-frame.frame 2, the .cljc clj+cljs branch; re-frame.views.provider 1, the .cljs single branch) and 179 are :var-usages, of which 179 resolve :to re-frame.frame and ZERO to re-frame.views.provider. That is the control and the target read off one instrument in one pass. Corroborated at the text level: 're-frame.views.provider/*current-frame*' returns 0 in all three normalisations and 'provider/*current-frame*' returns 0, while the sole alias route is real - exactly ONE ns requires re-frame.views.provider (views.cljs:60, :as provider) and the 'provider/' alias fires there on frame-provider, frame-root, build-frame-provider, current-frame, mint-instance-token! and frame-context. No :refer route exists anywhere. views.cljs does NOT re-export it, though it DOES re-export the dynamic *render-key*, so dynamic-var re-export is a live pattern there that this Var did not participate in. The bead's binding-form point was checked as its own census: every binding in the repository targets the canonical Var (126 via frame/, 2 fully qualified, 2 bare - one of those a ;; comment, the other inside re-frame.frame itself where bare IS canonical). Inside provider.cljs the Var was not even read by its own namespace: the only other occurrence, at what is now :287, is explicitly frame/-qualified. Deleted only the provider-local def. re-frame.frame/*current-frame* intact; current-frame still resolves dynamic scope first and React context second, with the no-provider sentinel handling, keyword/string coercion and no-frame behaviour unchanged. Core JVM :test exit 0, 2176 tests / 11149 assertions, 0 failures; test:cljs exit 0, 11209 tests / 55849 assertions, 0 failures - the lane that matters here, since provider.cljs is CLJS-only and the JVM suite never compiles it. The node-test compile was clean at 1894 files, 0 warnings.

title: vestigial(story): retire the standalone duplicate extends resolver
description:
Finding

`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/extends.cljc` is a 155-line standalone `:extends` resolver that is no longer on Story's runtime path. It is a duplicate, now-divergent implementation whose only actual consumer is a pair of focused tests of the duplicate itself.

Evidence

- Repo-wide search for `re-frame.story.extends`, `extends/resolve-extends`, and `extends/*max-extends-depth*` finds only: the namespace itself; the require at `tools/story/test/re_frame/story_test.clj:26`; calls in `extends-cycle-detection` and `extends-depth-cap` at lines 312/333; and a docstring cross-reference in `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc:163`. No production namespace, example, testbed, build alias, Story-MCP code, public facade, API page, or skill requires/calls it.
- The registration test immediately above those self-tests states that registered bodies keep raw `:extends` and that `re-frame.story.plan` is the single merge authority. Runtime compilation calls `plan/resolve-source-chain` (`plan.cljc:161-212`) and plan-owned merge logic; it never calls this namespace.
- The two implementations no longer express the same operation. `extends/resolve-extends` performs a straight parent-first map merge plus optional exclusive key groups. The compiled-plan authority applies field-specific semantics (for example setup append, local script/assertion ownership, deep/context merges). A passing standalone test therefore cannot prove the shipped runtime.
- `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/plan_test.cljc:229` already tests cycle failure through the actual plan compiler. Runtime inheritance/decorator behavior is also exercised in `story_test.clj`, `story_authoring_surface_test.clj`, and `story_decorator_chain_test.clj`; only the depth-cap witness still targets the duplicate rather than `plan/*max-extends-depth*`.
- History shows the standalone implementation arrived in `660fead138` (2026-05-11). The compiled-plan authority arrived later; by `82cd4bd1c8` (2026-07-10) the namespace doc explicitly acknowledged `re-frame.story.plan` as runtime authority and described this copy only as a helper for tooling/focused tests. No tooling consumer exists. The August vocabulary edit was mechanical (`:play-script` -> `:script`) and did not add a consumer.
- `tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md:303` still cites `story_test.clj`'s standalone bare-merge test as coverage even though runtime merge authority and semantics have moved to the plan compiler.
- Bead searches for `re-frame.story.extends`, `resolve-extends`, `extends resolver`, `Story extends`, `max-extends-depth`, and `standalone pure helper` returned no existing issue.

Impact

The duplicate ships code and a second public dynamic depth knob without a runtime/tooling consumer, lets tests go green against behavior the product does not execute, and invites error-id/depth/merge semantics to drift from the plan compiler. The coverage matrix overstates runtime coverage by naming the stale test.

Proposed disposition

Remove `re-frame.story.extends`. Move the still-useful depth-cap witness (and any missing unknown/cycle witness) to `re-frame.story.plan` through `variant-plan`/`resolve-source-chain`; delete redundant self-tests; remove the stale plan docstring cross-reference and update the spec/015 coverage row to name runtime-authority tests. Do not introduce a third facade shim. If a previously unknown downstream direct-require is discovered, consolidate both callers on one shared resolver rather than retaining divergent implementations.

Risks

Although the namespace is not facade-exported or documented as public API, a downstream project could direct-require it. Check published artifact/API policy and call out the removal in migration notes if required. Preserve the runtime error ids and the configurable depth-cap behavior at the plan authority.
acceptance_criteria:
- Repo-wide search finds no `re-frame.story.extends` namespace/file, `extends/resolve-extends`, or `extends/*max-extends-depth*` reference.
- The actual plan/runtime path has tests for unknown parent, cycle detection, the bound at `plan/*max-extends-depth*`, and representative field-specific inheritance (including setup/script/decorator behavior).
- `tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md` names tests that execute the plan/runtime authority and no longer claims the standalone bare merge proves runtime behavior.
- Story JVM and CLJS suites, source lint, API/spec drift checks, and affected feature-load/static build gates pass.
close_reason:
Done in PR #9075. title: skill(re-frame-migration): breaking-changes.md and inventory-and-plan.md teach the post-unwrap handler as (fn [_ {:keys [a b]}] ...) — the v1 reshaped shape; a v2 reg-event handler takes the event VECTOR
description:
CLAIM

Two leaves teach the post-`unwrap` handler as a **one-arg-map** destructure, which is the
v1 unwrap-reshaped shape, not a v2 handler:

- `skills/re-frame-migration/references/breaking-changes.md` (the preserved-surfaces

- `skills/re-frame-migration/references/inventory-and-plan.md` (the `unwrap` add-on-scan
  bullet): "the simplest fix is plain handler destructuring (`(fn [_ {:keys [...]}] ...)`,
  no interceptor)".

TRUTH AT TIP

A v2 `reg-event` handler takes the **coeffects map** and the **event vector**. Corpus M-59's
own worked example writes the destination as:

    (rf/reg-event :api/payload
      (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ {:keys [order-id total]}]] ...))

The payload map is the second element of the event vector, not the second argument. What
the two leaves show is what `unwrap` USED to hand the handler in v1 — which is precisely
the shape the migration is removing. An agent applying it writes a handler whose second
parameter is destructured as a map against a vector.

The class the migration-skill review keeps finding: a leaf teaching a form that does not
work. Milder than the retired-symbol cases in that `{:keys [...]}` against a vector binds
nils rather than throwing, which makes it a SILENT wrong-shape rather than a loud one.

fixes landed: the phrase appears identically in both leaves, so correcting one alone would
introduce a divergence between them.

title: docs: sweep the surviving wrong :rf/default claims and the dangling Spec 006 §706 citations — one small prose dispatch, not three beads
description:
THREE SMALL PROSE DEFECTS, ONE BEAD, BECAUSE THEY ARE ONE DISPATCH AND NONE OF THEM IS WORTH A
WORKER ON ITS OWN. Found by two workers in passing on 2026-09-11, neither of which widened to chase
them -- the right call both times.

=== PART A: THE WRONG `:rf/default` CLAIM, WHEREVER IT SURVIVES ===

The claim is that a plain `defn` invoked as a fn-call routes its ambient subscribes to `:rf/default`.
IT IS WRONG. Under EP-0002 there is no `:rf/default` floor:
`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1996` says the read "resolves to nil and RAISES
`:rf.error/no-frame-context` -- the operation fails fast rather than silently routing to a
conventional default. There is no silent fall-through to `:rf/default`." Confirmed at
`implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs`, where `current-frame` bottoms out at nil and
its docstring says the runtime never synthesises `:rf/default`.

KNOWN SURVIVING SITE: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs:1020`.

Two other instances are ALREADY FIXED and are named here only so nobody re-files them:
`panels.cljs`'s `render-panel!` docstring and three comments inside PR #9654, both corrected in that
PR.

DO NOT ASSUME THE LIST IS COMPLETE -- it is two workers' incidental sightings, not a census. Run one,
and take a control both ways: the phrase is short enough to sit inside one line, but if you search
for a longer form remember that hard-wrapped prose breaks a probe across lines and a commented
continuation survives a plain flatten.

WHAT THE CORRECTED TEXT SHOULD SAY, so three workers do not each invent a wording: keep any warning
that is about the MOUNT SEAM (building a provider-wrapped view inside a plain function really does
evaluate outside any React render, and really does raise), and drop the `:rf/default` destination in
favour of the raise. Do NOT generalise the warning to helpers -- for a helper inside an
already-provided tree the direction is REVERSED: heading is the footgun and inlining is the ruled
repair (HD-016). That reversal is recorded in full on rf2-k97c.3.

=== PART B: A DANGLING SPEC CITATION ===

`Spec 006 §706` is cited in prose but THAT ANCHOR EXISTS NOWHERE in
`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md`. It was found while correcting Part A, because the wrong claim and
the dead citation travel together -- they were copied as a pair.

KNOWN SURVIVING SITES: `tools/xray/spec/Conventions.md:115`, and one adapter DOM test.
Re-point them at the section that actually carries the material -- `Plain-fn footgun` -- or at
whatever heading holds it when you look. PR #9654 already re-pointed its own.

NOTE WHY NO GATE CAUGHT THIS, because it bounds what a fix can promise: `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`
validates markdown link targets and heading anchors, and a bare prose citation of the form
"Spec 006 §706" is NEITHER -- it is ordinary text. So this class is invisible to the link gates by
construction, and a fix here buys two corrected lines, not a guard. DO NOT BUILD A GATE FOR IT: a
prose-citation checker would have to parse section numbering conventions that are not stable, and
the failure it prevents is a reader losing a minute.

=== SCOPE, AND THE REASON THIS BEAD IS DELIBERATELY SMALL ===

This is a prose sweep. No behaviour changes, no test changes, no migration. If it grows past about a
dozen sites, stop and report rather than widening -- a larger population would mean the claim was
propagated systematically and that is a different bead with a different shape.

GATE: whichever lane covers the files actually touched. If the diff is confined to comments and
docstrings in `.cljs` files, the node lane compiling clean is the whole of what is needed and a
browser lane has nothing to say -- say so rather than running one for form. If it touches
`tools/xray/spec/*.md`, `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` covers that tree (`tools/*/spec` is inside its
roots) and runs unguarded in `test.yml`'s `verify-readme-links` job; note that it validates link
targets and anchors ONLY and does not look inside fenced code blocks at all, so check anything inside
a fence by hand and say so.

SEQUENCING: `shell.cljs` is in PR #9653's diff. Wait for that to merge before touching it.
notes: Merged-PR audit #9654 independently confirms the already-recorded residual at landing 9c16c6deeb5b: shell.cljs:1087 still says an ambient read would route to :rf/default, and the namespace prose around 115 repeats the fallback claim. Conventions.md:115 still cites Spec 006 §706. panels.cljs now uses the no-frame-context refusal and the real Plain-fn footgun section. Reused this literal-open exact prose-correction owner; retain its bounded prose-only scope and remeasure locations before editing. No status, criteria or closure change.
close_reason: LANDED IN PR #9657, merged at trunk 491c0ac2d0. VERIFIED AT SOURCE rather than from the PR body. PART A: SIX sites, not the one this bead named -- all in tools/xray. The five :rf/default mentions surviving in shell.cljs at tip all now DENY the floor or name the HOST's own default, which is a different and correct meaning: :105 'the host's :rf/default is untouched', :116 'under EP-0002 there is no :rf/default', :133 'a LOUD REFUSAL rather than a silent fall-through to :rf/default, which is the whole point', :197 'the sibling of the host's :rf/default', :1092 'EP-0002 removed the :rf/default floor the warning cited is retired'. PART B: zero Spec 006 §706 citations survive in any tracked source or doc file; the only tracked hit is .beads/issues.jsonl quoting this bead's own prose. THE LINE NUMBERS I GAVE WERE WRONG AND THE WORKER'S CENSUS WAS RIGHT: I briefed shell.cljs:1020; the real site was :1087, and a SECOND site sat at :115. The audit of #9654 independently confirmed both. WHY :115 IS EASY TO MISS, and this is the reusable half: THE CLAIM BREAKS ACROSS A LINE, so the line-oriented pass read ZERO there and only the flattened pass found it. That is the three-pass rule earning its place on a real target rather than in principle -- line-oriented, whitespace-collapsed, and comment-markers-stripped-before-collapsing, union of all three. A LARGER CLASS WAS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT SWEPT, exactly as this bead instructed: the DEFERRED-HANDLER form of the same wrong claim -- that a bare rf/dispatch from an :on-click 'leaks to :rf/default' -- across roughly ten files in tools/xray/src alone and not confined to Xray. Filed as rf2-mhpo and dispatched separately. This bead said to stop and report past about a dozen sites; the worker did. NO GATE WAS BUILT for the dangling-citation class and none should be: a bare prose citation is neither a markdown link nor a heading anchor, so check_doc_slugs.py cannot see it by construction, and a prose-citation checker would parse section numbering that is not stable to prevent a reader losing a minute.

title: CLAUDE.md: two new instrument-misreport entries (git ls-files pathspec union; Python/MSYS /tmp split)
description:
TWO NEW INSTRUMENT-MISREPORT HAZARDS, BOTH MEASURED ON THIS BOX ON 2026-09-10, both belonging in CLAUDE.md's
"Ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport on this machine" catalogue. That catalogue's own opening warns that its
letters are labels rather than a census and that it grows; this is it growing.

HAZARD 1 — `git ls-files A B -- C` UNIONS ITS PATHSPECS RATHER THAN INTERSECTING THEM.
  Measured by rf2-50fe's worker while counting bench files: the form returned 3013 paths where the correct
  answer was 156. It fails in the DANGEROUS direction for a scoping question — a census meant to be narrow
  comes back wide, and 3013 is a plausible-looking number that no error message contradicts. Exit 0
  throughout.
  GUARD: run one pathspec per invocation and intersect the results yourself, or filter the output. Take the
  control by counting a set you already know the size of.

HAZARD 2 — PYTHON-ON-WINDOWS AND MSYS DISAGREE ABOUT `/tmp`, SO A PYTHON HEREDOC WRITING THERE AND A SHELL
READING THERE TOUCH DIFFERENT FILES, SILENTLY.
  Git Bash maps `/tmp` onto the MSYS root; native Windows Python takes `/tmp` LITERALLY. So a script that
  writes with Python and reads back with shell tools gets STALE CONTENT — or an older run's file — with no
  error from either side, because both operations succeed against the file each believes in.
  IT FIRED TWICE INDEPENDENTLY THAT DAY: rf2-50fe's worker met it, and the mayor met it separately when a
  Python step could not read a file a shell step had just written to `/tmp`.
  This is the same FAMILY as catalogue item (d) — MSYS rewriting a path behind the caller's back — but the
  failure register is the opposite and worse: (d) exits 128 with a message naming the mangled argument, while
  this one is SILENT and hands back content that looks right.
  GUARD: never use `/tmp` as a handoff between a Python step and a shell step. Use the session scratchpad
  directory by its full Windows path, and have both sides name the SAME absolute path. If you must cross that
  seam, verify by reading back a sentinel the writer put in, not by checking that the write succeeded.

A THIRD ITEM IS NOT NEW BUT IS WORTH A SENTENCE UNDER (b)/(k), because it caught the mayor's own verification
this same day: A FIXED-STRING PROBE LONGER THAN ONE LINE CANNOT MATCH TEXT THAT WRAPS. Verifying a close
reason had landed, `grep -cF 'FOUR PR-time readers'` read 0 while the paragraph was demonstrably present —
the phrase spanned a newline in the source file. A sibling probe on the same paragraph read 1. This is the
word-wrap half of item (k) arriving through a plain file rather than through `bd show`'s renderer, so the
existing guidance — prefer a short INTERIOR phrase, and control both ways — is right but is currently
attached only to the tool.

AND ITEM (a) REPRODUCED LIVE THAT DAY, twice, which is worth recording as evidence the entry is still
accurate rather than historical: `grep -icF` aborted at exit 134 printing nothing, once in a worker's sweep
and once in the mayor's own close-reason verification, where the `||` fallback then answered
case-sensitively and returned a reassuring 0.

SCOPE: this bead is a CLAUDE.md edit to the catalogue and nothing else. Do not build a wrapper, a lint rule,
or a check script for any of these — the catalogue is the artefact, and every previous entry earned its place
by being written down rather than automated. Keep each entry in the established shape: what the instrument
did, the measurement in both directions, which direction it fails in, and the guard.

ONE EDITING TRAP THAT APPLIES TO THIS VERY FILE, from the catalogue itself: writing a catalogue entry that
mentions carriage returns has previously inserted REAL ones, reclassifying CLAUDE.md from `w/crlf` to
`w/-text` and staging 156 changed lines for a one-clause edit. After editing, check that the total CR count
equals the CRLF count.
close_reason:
CLOSED ON PR #9584, merged as 42d21fe4ba. One file, one insertion and one deletion — correct, because the
catalogue is a single line.

FOUR EDITS RATHER THAN THE THREE THE BRIEF SPECIFIED, and the worker REPORTED the difference instead of
choosing silently. The bead additionally asked that item (a)'s live reproduction be recorded as evidence the
entry is still accurate rather than historical; the bead governs, so (a) was extended too. That clause
carries real new content — the `||` fallback trap — rather than a date.

WHAT LANDED: (m) `git ls-files A B -- C` unions its pathspecs instead of intersecting them, and the `--`
that reads as a scope limiter is inert. (n) Python-on-Windows and MSYS disagree about `/tmp`, so a Python
step and a shell step naming the same literal path touch different files and the shell reads stale content.
(k) extended. (a) extended. No renumbering, no count added.

THREE THINGS THE BEAD DID NOT CARRY, ALL MEASURED BY THE WORKER:

  1. THE UNION IS PROVABLE, NOT INFERRED. The union form's output is byte-identical to `sort -u` of the two
     halves run separately (2949 + 222 with an overlap of 156), and dropping the `--` entirely reads 3015
     again. Four independent instruments agreed on 156.

  2. THE WRAPPED-PROBE REMEDY IS DEFEATED A SECOND TIME HERE, and the bead's guard implied flattening alone.
     Flatten-alone still reads 0 on this box, because the field came through `jq -r` and the surviving
     carriage return sits INSIDE the joined phrase — existing item (e), arriving from underneath. Strip
     first, flatten second, reads 1.

  3. A REFINEMENT OF THE BEAD'S "a sibling probe read 1", and it is the dangerous half: the worker's FIRST
     sibling probe also read 0, because it straddled the same line break. Only a genuinely single-line
     sibling read 1. A STRADDLING SIBLING PRESENTS AS CORROBORATION OF THE FALSE ZERO — two probes agreeing
     on absence, one broken instrument. That caution is now in (k).

ONE NUANCE RECORDED WITHOUT REWRITING THE GUARD IT QUALIFIES: item (a)'s headline says READ STDERR, and
grep's OWN stderr is empty. The `Aborted` line comes from the shell's job reporter, so a per-command `2>`
capture wrote 0 bytes. The guard still holds in the ordinary case; the worker recorded the fact rather than
inverting the entry on it, which is the right call for a correction that would otherwise overshoot.

THE 156-LINE TRAP WAS AVOIDED BY CONSTRUCTION, not by luck. Insertions were written through quoted heredocs,
verified at 0 CR bytes and 0 backslash bytes each, and spliced in binary mode. Before: 83,732 bytes, CR 156,
CRLF 156. After: 89,741 bytes, CR 156, CRLF 156. The `w/crlf` classification held and the diff stayed at one
changed line.

GATE PROVENANCE PROVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A planted broken link took `check_readme_links.py --ci` to exit 1
naming `CLAUDE.md:119` — the line this PR edits, so it demonstrably read the worker's own tree — while
`check_doc_slugs.py` stayed green at exit 0 on the identical fault, confirming that repo-root markdown lies
outside its roots. The vocab-ratchet plants went on a FRESH line deliberately, because line 119 already
carries removed-context markers that legitimately suppress the needle: a green there would have been a false
all-clear. Restore verified by git blob hash, not by reading a diff.

MEASUREMENTS THAT MOVED SINCE FILING, which is the ordinary case and not a defect: the union form read 3015
against the bead's 3013 on a tree two commits newer; the correct intersection read 156 exactly, as filed.

check_retired_composition_vocab.py 0, check-commit-attribution.sh 0 on both surfaces,
check-beads-pr-boundary.sh 0, check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh 0, worktree guard 0. CI 87 checks, 20 success,

title: spec 009: nothing gates the :reason roster against what the code can raise
description:
Filed by the mayor 2026-09-05 from a coverage question the rf2-qk8k worker answered honestly rather than glossing.

WHAT IT MEASURED. `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`'s catalogue row for `:rf.error/navigate-bad-request` enumerates the `:reason` values the gate can raise. That roster had drifted by exactly one value — `:query-merge-not-map`, added to the code by PR #9220 and never added to the catalogue — and the drift was found only because the worker that wrote the code reported it rather than reaching into a fenced file.

THE GATES THAT EXIST AND WHAT THEY ACTUALLY COVER, measured:
  * `re-frame.error-catalogue-channel-conformance-test` PARSES this very table out of the markdown, so it is a genuine witness that a row still parses — but it asserts CHANNEL values, not `:reason` sub-discriminators.
  * `check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py` works at the `:rf.error/*` ID level, not inside a row.
So the roster-to-code correspondence rests entirely on someone reading the source. It will drift again.

BEFORE PROPOSING A GATE, RUN THE ENUMERATION AXIS. This is the exact shape of rf2-p0b0, which was REFUTED: a worker concluded nothing gated a testbed because a name-grep found nothing, when the covering script DERIVED its target list and simply named no build. **So first ask every candidate tool what it covers — `--list`, `--check`, a self-test — rather than grepping for "reason" or for the keyword.** A verified "something already covers this and here is how" is the best outcome and closes this bead.

IF NOTHING COVERS IT, THE QUESTION IS WHETHER IT SHOULD, and the stance bears on it. A generic "every catalogue row's reason list matches its raiser" check is real work: it needs a way to find the raiser for a row, which is not mechanical across all rows. A narrower check — that every `:reason` keyword literal appearing in `implementation/**` appears somewhere in `spec/009`, and vice versa — is cheap, and would have caught this exact drift. **That narrower shape is probably the right size for a pre-alpha project that refuses gold-plating, but establish the false-positive rate before proposing it**: reason keywords may legitimately appear in tests and fixtures, and a gate that fires on those is worse than none.

P4 BECAUSE NOTHING IS BROKEN. The roster is correct at tip (PR #9240 fixed it and its census found no other gaps in the neighbouring rows, verified three ways). This is about whether the correspondence stays true without a human noticing, which is the same question `rf2-z65e` asks about skill tests and `rf2-p0b0` asked about testbed compiles. Consider reading those two first — the answers went opposite ways, and knowing why is most of the work here.

SEQUENCING: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` is HOT ZONE. If the answer is "add a check", the check itself lives in `scripts/` and needs no 009 edit — but confirm before dispatching, and check no peer holds 009.
notes:
CENSUS + RULING 2026-09-05 13:32 AUSEST (worker, worktree spec009-a, base 1ea4c7c278). NO GATE BUILT - refused with evidence, per this bead's own instruction: "If the honest answer is 'the roster is currently accurate and a gate is not worth its cost', say so with the census as evidence and close it that way."

ENUMERATION AXIS FIRST, as instructed (the rf2-p0b0 shape). Asked each candidate tool what it covers rather than grepping for "reason":
- scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py --help / --verbose self-describes as "an emitted :rf.error/:rf.warning id with no Spec 009 catalogue row, or an emitted :rf.* namespace with no Conventions reserved-namespace row". Ran clean: "scanned 304 implementation source file(s); 440 active + 93 retired catalogue row(s); check A findings=0, check B findings=0, check C findings=0". The token "reason" appears NOWHERE in the script. Category-ID level only.
- every-emitted-category-is-catalogued (error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj:738, rf2-9fvp25) and its siblings allow-list-stays-honest and always-on-mechanism-emits-are-catalogued-always-on: all three compare :category SETS (parse-catalogue -> map :category) against emitted-categories. No :reason sub-discriminator anywhere.
So the bead's premise HOLDS: nothing gates the :reason roster.

CENSUS, BOTH DIRECTIONS, at base 1ea4c7c278 (re-run and stable across a mid-session rebase).

DIRECTION A (code -> 009). 336 files under implementation/*/src/**; 89 distinct ":reason <keyword-literal>" values over 176 occurrences. 58 appear in spec/009; 31 do not. GENUINE CATALOGUE DRIFT AMONG THOSE 31: ZERO. All 31 classified: resource-lifecycle traces (:aborted, :clear-resource, :clear-scope, :mutation-clear, :mutation-remove, :remove, :dangling, :dangling-on-restore, :stale-reply, :stale-nav-orphan, :ssr-blocking-timeout); machine-timer cancellation traces (:on-exit, :on-frame-destroy, :on-resolution, :on-supersede, :on-join-resolution, :work-bearing-path); hicasso test-kit DOM-diff reasons (:node-kind, :only-in-candidate, :only-in-reference, :property, :text, :selector-matched-nothing, :selector-matched-one-side); hicasso evidence envelopes (:cap, :uncorrelated); elision markers (:classification); fx disposition maps (:malformed, :unregistered); the :rf.route/not-found EVENT payload (:malformed-url, :validation - Spec 012 vocabulary, not 009's); epoch replay refusals (the four :rf.epoch/replay-* values); a trace slot (:frame-not-url-bound, on :rf.fx/skipped-on-platform); schemas (:effect); http (:too-many-keys, Spec 014's :rf.http/decode-failure); and ONE pure instrument artefact - ":parent-frame-destroyed." WITH A TRAILING FULL STOP, harvested out of a docstring sentence at frame.cljc:4282.

An earlier pass of this census reported 41 rather than 31. That difference was an INSTRUMENT BUG worth recording: extracting only single-backtick-wrapped keywords from 009 misses values 009 writes as ":reason :scheme-not-allowed" INSIDE ONE backtick pair. Ten values, :scheme-not-allowed among them, are documented and were being reported as drift. Token-level extraction fixed it. Any future attempt at this gate must not key on backtick wrapping.

DIRECTION B (009 -> code). 23 distinct explicit ":reason :kw" pairs written in spec/009: ZERO absent from implementation/*/src/**. The enumerated roster that motivated this bead - :rf.error/navigate-bad-request, 11 values - every one resolves to a live raise site (address.cljc for 9; navigate.cljc + replan.cljc for :bad-event-arity; address.cljc + navigate.cljc for :request-not-a-map). For scale: 191 catalogue rows list :reason in their tags cell, none of them retired.

SO: DRIFT TODAY IS ZERO IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.

WHY NO GATE - and the two tunings fail in OPPOSITE directions, which is the actual finding.
- WIDE tuning (the bead's proposed narrow shape: every :reason keyword literal in implementation/** appears somewhere in spec/009, and vice versa): the false-positive rate is 31 of 31 = 100%. Every direction-A finding on today's tree is a legitimate non-catalogue use of the :reason KEY. The bead asked to establish the false-positive rate before proposing; established, and it is total. A gate whose every finding today is noise is worse than none - the bead says so itself.
- NARROW tuning (scope to a :reason literal co-located with an :rf.error/* category, which is what would suppress those 31): IT WOULD HAVE MISSED THE EXACT DRIFT IT WAS PROPOSED TO CATCH. :query-merge-not-map is stamped at routing/address.cljc:275 as a plain returned map, "{:reason :query-merge-not-map :keys [:query-merge]}". address.cljc names :rf.error/navigate-bad-request NOWHERE - its only two :rf.error/ mentions are :rf.error/prefetch-bad-address and :rf.error/resource-route-plan, different categories - and the value reaches the emit a namespace away at navigate.cljc:246 via ":reason (:reason bad)". Literal and category are not co-located, so no co-location heuristic reaches it.

That gap is STRUCTURAL, not a tuning constant. Reason values are computed by pure shape-validator fns that return {:reason <kw>} and are threaded to an emitter elsewhere; a gate that actually held the roster would have to follow that dataflow - which is precisely the "real work / not mechanical across all rows" this bead already identified. Against the project stance (pre-alpha, elegance without gold-plating, trust the programmer) that is not worth its cost for a correspondence measured accurate in both directions today.

IF DRIFT EVER RECURS, the cheap durable alternative is a per-row assertion inside the EXISTING error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test - which already parses this very table - for the handful of rows whose reasons come from ONE named validator fn, navigate-bad-request being the worked case. That is one row's worth of work when a row proves it needs it, not a corpus gate. Not built now; nothing is drifting.

NO FILES CHANGED. No PR - the census is the deliverable.
close_reason: Census run in both directions at base 1ea4c7c278: ZERO drift. Direction A 89 distinct :reason literals in implementation/*/src/**, 31 absent from 009 and all 31 legitimate non-catalogue uses (0 genuine drift). Direction B 23 explicit ':reason :kw' pairs in 009, 0 absent from code; navigate-bad-request's 11 values all raisable. Gate REFUSED with evidence per this bead's own instruction: the wide tuning has a 100% false-positive rate (31/31), and the narrow tuning that suppresses those would have MISSED the motivating rf2-qk8k drift, because :query-merge-not-map is stamped in address.cljc which names no :rf.error/ category at all. Structural, not a tuning constant. Full census in notes.

title: xray: 15 of 22 panel-gallery fixtures are zero-consumer, not just long-handler-buffer
description:
FILED 2026-09-04 by the mayor from worker/vest-a's out-of-scope observation on PR #9162 (rf2-6r9j.249). RELAYED, NOT VERIFIED BY ME — treat the count as a claim and re-census it.

WHAT IT REPORTED: while removing four zero-consumer helpers from tools/xray, it censused tools/xray/.../panel_gallery/fixtures.cljs and found FIFTEEN of its TWENTY-TWO fixtures have no consumer by the same method it used for the four it removed — not merely long-handler-buffer, which was the one its bead named. It recorded the observation rather than acting on it, correctly, because widening a bead's scope mid-flight is how a bounded deletion becomes an unreviewable one.

WHY THIS IS P4 AND NOT HIGHER: a fixture with no consumer is dead weight, not a defect. Nothing is wrong at runtime. The value is that a gallery of fixtures nobody renders misleads the next person who reads it as a menu of what the gallery covers.

BEFORE ACTING, TWO THINGS THE SAME WORKER LEARNED THE HARD WAY ON THIS EXACT SURFACE:
1. ITS OWN FIRST CENSUS PATTERN WAS DEFECTIVE — it excluded '/' on the left, so it could not see h/epoch-has-issues? and read ZERO where ten hits existed. The control caught it. Any census here needs a control that shares the shape of a qualified call.
2. THE NAME-COLLISION TRAP FIRED on this surface too: three of str-of's four repo-wide hits were pr-str-of-form and pr-str-of-rejection — different tokens entirely. Check the namespace and the arity, not just the symbol.

AND THE GATE FOR THIS SURFACE FAILS OPEN ON EXIT CODE: the panel-gallery compile grades a reference to a removed var as a WARNING and still exits 0 (measured, same PR). The discriminating signal is the WARNING COUNT against a zero baseline — vest-a's was 0 across 710 files. Do not gate a deletion here on exit status alone. Recorded as memory cljs-compile-gate-exit-0-over-removed-var.

FENCE WHEN DISPATCHED: tools/xray/** only. A dispatch touching tools/xray/ updates tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR or states 'spec unchanged because X' — vest-a established that none of ITS four symbols is named or contracted in that spec, with two instruments reading zero against a control reading 4, so the same check is needed for whichever fixtures this bead removes.

title: skills/README.md claims every spec/authoring-prompt.md defers on leaf size; two restate the figures
description:
Found while executing rf2-wh25 (PR #9065), which was scoped to skills/README.md only, so this was reported rather than fixed.

skills/README.md:237-238 states: 'Single source of truth for the per-leaf size ceiling - per-skill spec/authoring-prompt.md files defer here instead of restating.'

Measured across all 8 spec/authoring-prompt.md files, two RESTATE the numbers rather than defer:

  skills/re-frame2-implementor/spec/authoring-prompt.md:16  'leaf-size discipline (each leaf <=250 lines AND <=16 KB)'
  skills/re-frame2-implementor/spec/authoring-prompt.md:39  'Every leaf <=250 lines and <=16 KB.'
  skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/authoring-prompt.md:49         '<=250 lines AND <=16 KB; catalogue-shaped leaves (ops.md, recipes.md) may run longer where a split would not reduce tokens-per-session'

The other six defer correctly by link or pointer (re-frame2-setup, re-frame2, re-frame-migration are the explicit ones).

NOTHING IS STALE TODAY. rf2-wh25 deliberately did not move the 250-line or 16 KB figures, so the restatements still agree with the README. The pair one additionally carries its own catalogue carve-out, which is consistent with the README's - and is arguably useful locally. So this is a single-source-of-truth accuracy nit, not a live defect: the exposure is that a FUTURE change to either figure now has three places to update, and the README says there is one.

Two defensible dispositions, a maintainer's call:
  (a) make the two prompts defer (delete the restated figures, point at skills/README.md#leaf-size-discipline), or
  (b) soften the README's line to say the figures MAY be restated locally but the README governs.

Low priority - the numbers are not expected to move, and rf2-wh25 ruled they stay.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 08:0x AUSEST. TAKE DISPOSITION (a): MAKE THE TWO PROMPTS DEFER. DO NOT SOFTEN THE README.

I CONSIDERED CLOSING THIS AS MINUTIAE AND DECIDED AGAINST IT, so the reasoning is recorded rather than the verdict alone. The stance says not to litigate every last fine detail, and this bead argues its own case honestly: nothing is stale today, the restatements still agree, and the pair's local carve-out is arguably useful. That is a real argument for closing.

WHAT DECIDES IT THE OTHER WAY IS THAT THE README'S SENTENCE IS FALSE, NOT MERELY UNTIDY. It says "per-skill spec/authoring-prompt.md files defer here instead of restating", and two of eight do not. That is the same class of defect this project has just chosen to fix twice in a week on beads of the same size: rf2-yk2d, a code comment making measurably false claims, and rf2-sy1l, a classification reason asserting something untrue. Closing this one while fixing those two would be inconsistent, and the inconsistency would be invisible later.

(a) OVER (b) FOR ONE REASON: (b) makes the README describe the mess, (a) removes it. Softening the line to "figures MAY be restated locally but the README governs" buys a sentence that is true and a rule that is worse — three places to update and a written licence to add a fourth. (a) makes the claim true and leaves ONE source of truth, which is what the section is for.

THE PAIR'S CATALOGUE CARVE-OUT IS THE ONE JUDGEMENT CALL INSIDE (a). skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/authoring-prompt.md:49 restates the figures AND adds its own catalogue carve-out naming ops.md and recipes.md. Delete the restated FIGURES; whether the local carve-out survives is the worker's call on reading both texts — it names specific local leaves, which the README cannot, so keeping it as prose that carries no numbers is legitimate. What must not survive is a second copy of "<=250 lines AND <=16 KB".

NOTE THE TIMING, because it changes what "agree" means. PR #9065 landed on main at 89c56b38cd and WIDENED the README's carve-out to name dense teaching leaves alongside catalogue-shaped ones. So the pair prompt's carve-out is now a partial copy of a rule that has moved, which is this bead's stated exposure arriving early rather than in some future edit. Read skills/README.md at tip, not as this bead quotes it.

SCOPE: skills/re-frame2-implementor/spec/authoring-prompt.md and skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/authoring-prompt.md. Re-measure the other six defer correctly rather than trusting the census in this description.

title: api-manifest: the internal classification of routing.test-support asserts it is not a supported surface, while the skill tells authors to require it directly
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 07:3x AUSEST, on a contradiction the roster-a worker surfaced rather than papered over. KEEP THE INTERNAL CLASSIFICATION. CHANGE ITS REASON.

THE CONTRADICTION, verified at source by me. PR #9063 classified re-frame.routing.test-support (and its resources sibling) as internal, with a reason that says it is not a supported surface. But skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/routing.md:180 tells app authors, in as many words: "this fixture event is test-only, so (:require [re-frame.routing.test-support]) to register it (it is NOT wired into the production re-frame.routing facade)." The skill is not vague and it is not accidental - it names the namespace, explains WHY it is off the facade, and instructs the require.

BOTH RECORDS ARE RIGHT ABOUT DIFFERENT THINGS, WHICH IS WHY NEITHER SHOULD SIMPLY WIN. The worker classification is correct about what it MEASURED: the require is for its LOAD EFFECT - registering a :rf.test/* fixture event - and the namespace exports nothing an author calls. The skill is correct that the namespace is SUPPORTED AND MUST BE REQUIRED BY NAME. A namespace you are TOLD to require is a surface whose NAME is part of the contract even when none of its vars are: rename it and you break documented guidance.

SO THE DEFECT IS THE REASON TEXT, NOT THE TIER. Do not row it in the manifest - it is test-only and rowing it would put a test namespace in the public API surface, which is its own kind of wrong. Do not add a new tier for one case; that is machinery for a population of two. Instead make the internal-namespaces comment say what is actually true: DELIBERATELY OFF THE PRODUCTION FACADE, REQUIRED DIRECTLY BY DOCUMENTED TEST GUIDANCE FOR ITS LOAD EFFECT, THEREFORE NOT A CALLABLE PUBLIC SURFACE BUT NOT FREE TO RENAME EITHER. Cite skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/routing.md so the next reader can find the guidance rather than rediscovering the contradiction.

CHECK THE SIBLING BEFORE WRITING: the resources .test-support namespace was classified the same way. Establish whether any skill or doc instructs requiring IT by name. If none does, its reason is genuinely "internal" and the two should NOT get identical comments - say so rather than symmetrising.

THE .tooling SIBLINGS NEED NOTHING. The worker asked about those too, and spec/Derivations.md already settles them: internal registration metadata shipping no public accessor, with the public name deferred to a graduation gate, and their algebra views already rowed :tooling via the JVM facade aliases. A record exists; follow it.

FENCED — DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL: PR #9063 merges.

STATUS OF #9063 AT THIS READ: rollup 85 total, 28 SUCCESS, 56 SKIPPED, 1 IN_PROGRESS (CLJS shadow-cljs :node-test). Not a merge candidate on clause 3 yet; nothing failing. So this fence is expected to clear within the hour rather than being a long hold.

THE RULING IS ALREADY MADE AND IS NOT WHAT THIS BEAD IS WAITING ON: keep routing.test-support classified internal, do not row a test namespace in the public manifest, do not invent a tier for a population of two, and correct the REASON TEXT so it stops asserting the namespace is not a supported surface when the skill tells authors to require it for its load effect. That is a one-site prose fix in the generator's classification comment.
FENCE STRUCK 2026-09-03 07:4x AUSEST — PR #9063 MERGED (landed on main at 36aff155653df23fc0c685d53a056a13756d773e, one file, implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj, +225/-9). The "DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL PR #9063 merges" fence above is DISCHARGED. This bead is now free.

NOT DISPATCHED THIS TICK ONLY BECAUSE THE FLEET IS AT SIX. It is the next thing out when a slot frees, and it is small: one prose fix to the classification reason text that #9063 just wrote.

THE RULING STANDS UNCHANGED, and it is recorded above: keep routing.test-support classified internal, do not row a test namespace in the public manifest, do not invent a tier for a population of two, and correct the REASON TEXT so it stops asserting the namespace is not a supported surface while skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/routing.md:180 tells authors to require it. Both records are right about different things — the require is for its LOAD EFFECT and exports nothing callable, but a namespace you are told to require has its name in the contract even when none of its vars do.

WRITE SURFACE when it goes out: implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj only. Verify the reason text at source first; #9063 may have worded it differently from what this bead quotes.

DISCRIMINATION. The drift-check prints no root, so a green alone proves nothing about which tree it read. title: skill(re-frame-migration): split §M-11 (38 KB of 61 KB) out of guided-handlers-state.md into its own leaf; breaking-changes.md passes the catalogue test as-is
description:
CLAIM (structure — the one structure bead for partition B). skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-handlers-state.md is 61,261 bytes / 489 lines, ~4x the leaf ceiling (skills/README.md §Leaf size discipline: ≤250 lines AND ≤16 KB; catalogue-shaped leaves may exceed it only if splitting would not reduce tokens loaded per session). breaking-changes.md is 63,795 bytes and is also over.

TRUTH AT TIP — applying the catalogue test honestly to both:

 - breaking-changes.md PASSES. Its Required table (lines 25-86) is a per-rule index an agent greps as one read; splitting it would multiply file handles without cutting tokens. Its remaining sections are short and each is the single owner of its topic within the skill (add-on compile failure, compile-only vs compile-silent façade classes, failure-visibility axis, §M-30 flow-map triage). Leave its shape alone; its correctness drift is a separate bead ("breaking-changes.md index drift").

 - guided-handlers-state.md FAILS the test because it is two leaves stapled together. §M-11 spans lines 77-331 — 38,296 bytes, 62% of the file — and is a single-topic execution recipe (defn→reg-view Form-1/2/3, the `reg-view*` capture-once contract, the `defmulti` shape, function-position call sites, the async listener/timer/error-handler class). The other ten sections (M-3, M-5, M-10, M-12, M-13, M-14, M-15, M-15b, M-34, M-42) total ~23 KB and are short decision-shape walkthroughs. Sessions load them for different reasons: the M-11 sweep is "typically the largest single conversion" (SKILL.md:91) and an agent doing it needs none of M-34/M-42; an agent resolving M-13/M-15 pays 38 KB for M-11 it will not read. Splitting reduces tokens-per-session for both. SKILL.md already routes to §M-11 by SECTION anchor (line 91) rather than to the leaf, which is the tell that it is its own leaf.

IMPACT. Token cost per migration session, and a 489-line leaf that is hard to keep correct (the M-5 and M-15b drifts filed alongside this are in the non-M-11 half).

FIX SHAPE (one PR; ~8 files retargeted, all mechanical). Move lines 77-331 verbatim into a new leaf `skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-views-m11.md` (title: "guided-views — M-11: subscribing plain fns under a frame"), leaving a one-line M-11 pointer in guided-handlers-state.md's Contents. Retarget every `guided-handlers-state.md#m-11...` / `#executing-the-conversion...` / `#the-async-listener-timer-and-error-handler-class` link: SKILL.md:91,96; breaking-changes.md:38; auto-cross-cutting.md:317,392; inventory-and-plan.md:92; runtime-smoke-test.md:25,118; sequencing.md:121; implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/FORM-3.md:405,430,587,695 (adopter pointers that name "guided-handlers-state.md §M-11" in prose — update the prose too). Then update the contract-drift gate, which hard-codes the owner: scripts/check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py `GUIDED_HANDLERS_MD` (line ~1681), `FORM3_RECIPE_POINTER_RE` (line 1479, matches `guided-handlers-state\.md`), and the message strings at lines 1433, 1618, 1641, 1656, 1674 — point them at the new leaf. The gate globs references/*.md for its scan (lines 241-242), so the new leaf is scanned automatically; only the canonical-owner constants move.

GATE. `python scripts/check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py --verbose` (must still report "Form-3 capture-once retarget invariance in both owners" against the NEW leaf); `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (every retargeted anchor under skills/); `python scripts/check_skill_migration_cites.py --verbose`; `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` for the FORM-3.md links (implementation/** is that gate's surface, not check_doc_slugs's).

ACCEPTANCE. guided-handlers-state.md ≤ ~24 KB with no M-11 body; new guided-views-m11.md carries lines 77-331 unchanged; zero references to `guided-handlers-state.md#m-11` / `#executing-the-conversion` / `#the-async-listener` remain (`rg -n 'guided-handlers-state\.md#(m-11|executing|the-async)' skills implementation/adapters scripts` empty); all four gates green.

Reviewed at tip 72df4dd915 (d12181c4c3 = tip + one beads checkpoint; `git diff --stat 72df4dd915..HEAD -- skills/ migration/` empty) on 2026-09-02 11:05:46 AUSEST.
acceptance_criteria: guided-handlers-state.md has no M-11 body (<= ~24 KB); new guided-views-m11.md carries lines 77-331 verbatim; no guided-handlers-state.md#m-11 / #executing-the-conversion / #the-async-listener links remain in skills/, implementation/adapters/, scripts/; contract-drift (owner constants retargeted), doc-slugs, cites, readme-links green
notes:
PR #9029 (2026-09-03, worker migskill-f). NOT ATTEMPTED — BLOCKED, and the block is PROVEN by measurement rather than asserted. Left OPEN; needs re-dispatch with a wider fence.

THE SPLIT CANNOT BE DONE FROM A skills/-ONLY FENCE, and the skills-only half would land a RED gate on main. Simulated it: deleted §M-11 (lines 81-336) from guided-handlers-state.md and ran the gate:

  DRIFT_SABOTAGE_EXIT=1
  FORM3-CAPTURE-ONCE-MISSING: guided-handlers-state.md no longer frames the outer-callable
  (rf/capture-frame) as capture-once / a locked handle - the retarget invariance has no
  subject to attach to (rf2-aalo4n).

The capture-once invariance the gate pins is at line 264, INSIDE §M-11. check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py hard-codes the owner (GUIDED_HANDLERS_MD line 1927; FORM3_RECIPE_POINTER_RE line 1479) and form3_capture_once_retarget_problems() slurps that file for the canonical recipe — so this bead's own FIX SHAPE is right that the gate constants must move with the section. That is scripts/, and the four FORM-3.md prose pointers (implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/FORM-3.md:405,430,587,695) are implementation/ — both outside the dispatch fence this worker was given (skills/re-frame-migration/** only, implementation/ explicitly barred).

THIS BEAD'S SIZING IS SOUND; ONLY THE FENCE IT WAS DISPATCHED UNDER IS WRONG. Re-measured at PR base: guided-handlers-state.md is 492 lines / 62,740 bytes (bead said 489 / 61,261 — it has grown since filing). §M-11 = lines 81-336, and the measured post-split remainder is 236 lines / 24,020 bytes, matching this bead's '<= ~24 KB' acceptance exactly.

WORK SPLIT for the re-dispatch: 7 in-fence anchor retargets — auto-cross-cutting.md:392, breaking-changes.md:38, inventory-and-plan.md:93, runtime-smoke-test.md:25 and :110, sequencing.md:122, SKILL.md:90 — plus 2 out-of-fence files (the drift-gate owner constants, and FORM-3.md's four prose pointers). Dispatch it to ONE worker holding all three trees, since the gate and the leaf must move in one commit or the tree is self-contradictory.

Also confirmed as this bead states: breaking-changes.md passes the catalogue test as-is and was left alone (not touched for shape; its M-8 rows were corrected under rf2-n3mya in the same PR).
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 02:0x AUSEST — THE FENCE IS WIDENED. ONE WORKER HOLDS THE SKILL, THE GATE SCRIPT AND FORM-3.md, AND ALL THREE MOVE IN ONE COMMIT.

migskill-f did not attempt this and was right not to. It PROVED the blocker rather than asserting it: deleting SS-M-11 makes scripts/check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py exit 1 with FORM3-CAPTURE-ONCE-MISSING, because the invariance that gate pins lives at line 264 INSIDE SS-M-11 and the gate HARD-CODES guided-handlers-state.md as the owner of it. So the leaf cannot move while the gate names the leaf. Its sizing is sound — the post-split remainder measures 24,020 bytes, matching the bead's ~24 KB acceptance — and only the fence was wrong, which is a premise correction worth more than the split would have been.

THE FIX IS THE ONE-TOUCHER RULE APPLYING ACROSS A TRIPLE. CLAUDE.md states it for the report-changed-surfaces pair: a change that alters what a classifier OUTPUTS or what a test PINS about those outputs lands a tree where the suite contradicts the script unless both halves move in ONE commit. This is the same shape with three files instead of two — the leaf, the gate that names it, and implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/FORM-3.md, which the gate reads. Splitting the leaf without repointing the gate reds the trunk; repointing the gate without splitting the leaf is a no-op. So the write surface is all three, and the commit is one.

WHAT THE GATE CHANGE MUST BE: repoint the FORM3-CAPTURE-ONCE pin at whichever leaf ends up owning line 264's invariance after the split, rather than deleting the pin or loosening it. THE PIN IS NOT THE PROBLEM — it is doing its job, which is why the split was caught before it landed. A gate weakened to let a refactor through is worse than the oversized leaf.

DO NOT let the widened fence become a licence to edit reagent-slim beyond what the pin requires. Read FORM-3.md; change it only if the pin's target text genuinely moved.
PR #9033 (2026-09-03, worker migskill-g). DONE per the mayor ruling: the widened fence was used, and the leaf, the gate and FORM-3.md moved in ONE commit.

guided-handlers-state.md 492 L / 62,782 B -> 236 L / 24,231 B, matching this bead's '<= ~24 KB' acceptance. New leaf references/guided-views-m11.md 261 L / 39,701 B carries the 253-line M-11 body VERIFIED BYTE-IDENTICAL against the merge base. The new leaf is over the 16 KB ceiling; that is the inherent size of the section this bead measured at 38,296 B and never asked to be reduced, so the figure is reported rather than trimmed.

BLOCKER REPRODUCED BEFORE REPAIR, as briefed. Deleting SS-M-11 (lines 81-336) gave DRIFT_SABOTAGE_EXIT=1 / FORM3-CAPTURE-ONCE-MISSING; plant proven applied by a git blob hash change 1c562d9d -> 6008efc0 and the restore verified back to 1c562d9d.

THE PIN WAS REPOINTED, NOT LOOSENED OR DELETED, and re-armed with four proofs: (1) SS-M-11 deleted with the gate unchanged -> FORM3-CAPTURE-ONCE-MISSING; (2) gate repointed before FORM-3.md -> FORM3-RECIPE-POINTER-MISSING; (3) a DELIBERATELY-WRONG repoint aiming the constant back at the old owner -> FORM3-CAPTURE-ONCE-MISSING naming guided-views-m11.md; (4) the A->B retarget sentence broken inside the new leaf -> FORM3-STALE-RELATION-MISSING. Probe (3) is what shows the green is real rather than vacuous. The gate's own --self-test also passes after its fixtures moved.

THE GATE SURFACE WAS WIDER THAN THIS BEAD'S FIX SHAPE SAID. Beyond GUIDED_HANDLERS_MD and FORM3_RECIPE_POINTER_RE, the same constant also backs Rules 5, 5b and 5c and three LIVE self-tests, all of which slurp it for M-11 content. So the constant was renamed GUIDED_VIEWS_M11_MD and all 16 uses plus the message and fixture strings followed. The references/*.md glob does pick the new leaf up automatically, as this bead said: the gate scanned 26 files at base and 28 after both splits.

FORM-3.md GENUINELY NEEDED THE CHANGE, and it was demonstrated rather than assumed: running the gate after repointing it but before touching FORM-3.md returned FORM3-RECIPE-POINTER-MISSING. Five occurrences across four lines (405 twice, 430, 587, 695). Note this bead and the previous worker both said four sites - grep -n counts LINES, and line 405 carries the name as both display text and link target. SS-M-11 stays valid in the prose because the heading is preserved verbatim. Nothing else in reagent-slim was touched.

7 in-fence anchor retargets, exactly the set the previous worker predicted. Found by line-oriented AND whitespace-flattened searches (FORM-3.md is hard-wrapped), which agreed, and both correctly left #m-13 / #m-15 / #m-15b / #m-42 alone.

STALE OUT-OF-FENCE PROSE, reported not touched, none of them markdown links so no gate reds: migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2815; skills/re-frame2/patterns/stateful-components.md:98; implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/form_3_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs:506 and m11_recipe_reactive_owner_cljs_test.cljs:6. Worth a small follow-up bead.
