The failures show schema-marked sensitive slots riding unredacted (e.g. bearer-secret at [:tags :value :token]), so some state a PRIOR namespace's load or fixture normally establishes is missing in the solo ordering — likely a registration (schemas artefact load? classification hook?) that make-reset-runtime-fixture does not itself establish. Not introduced by rf2-lddbk: reproduced byte-identically on the base file. Impact: low — CI runs the full suite — but it makes focused local iteration on that namespace read false-red and could mask real regressions behind expected noise. Fix shape: make the namespace self-sufficient (require/establish whatever the redaction path needs) or teach the fixture to establish it.
notes:
VERDICT (PR #8889, branch worker/http-robust-o9e15): FIXED. Premise reproduced exactly at trunk 24b33a618a before any edit - solo exit 1 (20 tests, 3 failures, 1 error), full suite exit 0 (508 tests, 3881 assertions) - and the guess recorded in the description turned out RIGHT, now verified at source rather than guessed.

ROOT CAUSE - the missing establishment is the re-frame.schemas NAMESPACE LOAD. privacy-body/decode-schema-marks reaches the per-slot classifier through the late-bind hooks :schemas/extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema and :schemas/extract-large-paths-from-schema, which re-frame.schemas publishes at the bottom of its facade ns (re_frame/schemas.cljc). privacy-body/extract-paths returns an EMPTY MAP when the hook is unbound, so an unloaded schemas artefact does not error - it silently classifies nothing, and every schema-marked secret rides verbatim. Probed directly under this namespace own require set: hook unbound, marks empty; after requiring re-frame.schemas the same schema yields the expected [:token] sensitive mark. In the full suite the alphabetically earlier re-frame.http-privacy-body-test - which ALREADY carries this require, commented load-bearing - binds the hooks first, which is the accidental establishment that made the full ordering green.

All four reported failures are that one cause. The ERROR on response-body-large-slot-elided-in-replied-trace is the same thing wearing a different face: contains? was called on the UNelided String and threw IllegalArgumentException.

REPAIR - declare the dependency in this namespace require, exactly as the sibling re-frame.http-privacy-body-test already does. NOT fixed in make-reset-runtime-fixture: that fixture lives in implementation/core, which must not load an optional artefact, since the whole point of the late-bind seam is that core does not depend on schemas. No assertion was weakened - these pin that secrets are redacted, and making them laxer would have converted a test-ordering defect into a silent privacy hole.

GATES on the final rebased base, captured exit codes: solo re-frame.http-privacy-integration-test exit 0 (20 tests, 49 assertions) - the red-to-green control; full suite exit 0 (508 tests, 3883 assertions) - unchanged green. The diagnostic probe was exercised in BOTH directions in one run (unbound hook yielding no marks, then bound hook yielding the expected mark), so its nothing-here answer was checked against an input it should flag.

WORTH KNOWING - CI only ever runs the full-suite ordering (jvm-http in test.yml runs a bare clojure -M:test), so no gate would have caught this, and none will catch the next namespace that acquires the same latent dependency. Related: rf2-o9e15 rode the same worker; the two turned out INDEPENDENT - shared shape, unrelated mechanisms.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8889 (commit 54cc3e9f3e, branch worker/http-robust-o9e15). The missing establishment was the re-frame.schemas namespace load, which publishes the :schemas/extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema and :schemas/extract-large-paths-from-schema late-bind hooks; privacy-body/extract-paths returns an empty map when they are unbound, so classification silently did nothing and schema-marked secrets rode verbatim. Repaired by declaring that require in the test namespace, matching the sibling re-frame.http-privacy-body-test. Control: solo run exit 1 (3 failures, 1 error) before, exit 0 (20 tests, 49 assertions) after, with the full suite exit 0 (508 tests, 3883 assertions) throughout. No assertion weakened. Full verdict in the notes.

title: CLAUDE.md item (o) is scoped too narrowly: the Bash tool halves backslash runs in a plain single-quoted ARGUMENT, not only in a quoted heredoc
description:
CLAUDE.md instrument item **(o)** scopes the backslash-halving defect to a **quoted heredoc**. Measured
2026-09-21, that scope is too narrow and fails OPEN for the commonest spelling: **the Bash tool halves
runs of backslashes inside a plain SINGLE-QUOTED ARGUMENT too.**

## The measurement

Found by the rf2-lz6dl decider (another session), where it produced a **false-zero probe** that
Python-built probes refuted. **Re-measured here at trunk `5741906ee2` rather than relayed**, one case
per row, all as single-quoted arguments through the Bash tool:

| written in the command | arrives as |
|---|---|
| `a\b` | `a\b` — a LONE backslash is untouched |
| `a\\b` | `a\b` |
| `a\\\b` | `a\\b` |
| `a\\\\b` | `a\\b` |

and `printf '%s\n' 'x\\y'` piped through `cat -A` prints `x\y$`.

**CONTROL, the decisive half:** the identical four literals written to a file by Python and read back
with `cat -A` carry **`a\b`, `a\\b`, `a\\\b`, `a\\\\b`** — all intact. So the file layer and `cat` are
faithful; what moves is the command text before any shell sees it.

## Why the existing entry does not cover it

Item (o)'s headline names `<<'EOF'` and its remedy is *"write anything carrying a backslash with the
Write tool rather than through a heredoc"*. The REMEDY still works. **The DIAGNOSIS does not**, and
that is the failure: a reader who has internalised item (o), avoids heredocs entirely, and then writes
an ordinary inline `grep 'a\\b'` or `python -c '... chr(92)*2 ...'` is bitten by a defect they believe
they have already guarded against — which is worse than not knowing, because the guard is felt to be
discharged.

The halving RULE itself is unchanged and item (o) states it correctly: every RUN is halved while a
lone backslash before an ordinary character is untouched, which is exactly the selectivity that hides
it — nearly every backslash in an ordinary command survives and only the doubled ones move, and those
are precisely the ones that mean *a literal backslash*.

## The edit wanted

Widen item (o)'s scope sentence from the heredoc construct to **the Bash tool's command text**, keeping
its existing measurements, its both-registers LOUD/SILENT account, and its Write-tool remedy. Add the
single-quoted-argument row and the Python-written control above. **Do not narrow anything else**, and
do not add a gate: there is nothing mechanically checkable that would not also flag every legitimate
backslash.

## Fence and lane

**`CLAUDE.md` is a hot-zone file and THREE items now queue on it** — this one, `rf2-z0pma` and
`rf2-lz6dl`. They are sequential, never parallel: second waits for the first's PR to merge.

Gate is `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` (repo-root markdown is its surface, NOT
`check_doc_slugs.py`, whose roots exclude repo-root files). **`CLAUDE.md` is `w/crlf`**, so: never
`sed -i`; take the three numbers with Python on the raw bytes — total CR, total CRLF, bare LF —
requiring CR == CRLF and **bare LF == 0**, because the two-number form passes vacuously as `0 == 0` on
a flattened file. And per item (e), editing this file is itself the place where stray carriage returns
get introduced.

**Writing this entry will require writing backslash runs into `CLAUDE.md`, which is the very defect it
documents.** Use the Write/Edit tooling for the replacement text, never a heredoc and never an inline
single-quoted argument, and verify by EFFECT — read a distinctive backslash-bearing line back out of
the file after writing it.

Verified at trunk after the merge, not relayed: the new headline `ANYWHERE IN ITS COMMAND TEXT`
occurs **1**, the old narrow `INSIDE A *QUOTED* HEREDOC` headline occurs **0**, the widened remedy
`rather than through the Bash tool's command text` occurs **1**, and file health reads

characters** — exactly the shape the worker predicted.

All five merge clauses: band **88** measured from four settled PRs by ANCESTRY, rollup 88 / 0

`completed/success`, not a draft, zero workflow files changed across merge-base `a4e90ebaee`.

### THE TWO EDITS BEYOND THE LITERAL SCOPE SENTENCE — BOTH ACCEPTED, CHECKED IN THE PATCH

The worker flagged both for veto rather than burying them, which is why they were cheap to rule on.
I read them in the diff rather than from the summary.

1. **The remedy widening was NECESSARY, not optional.** It previously read *"write anything carrying
   a backslash with the Write tool rather than through a heredoc"*. Left alone, that remedy would

Editing item (o) means writing backslash runs into a file in order to document a defect about

had predicted BEFORE writing. Seven backslash-bearing probes, all intact.

### THE BYTES-VERSUS-CHARACTERS ACCOUNT IS NOW RECONCILED RATHER THAN MERELY CONFIRMED

The mayor's pre-`z0pma` note attributed the 476-byte gap to "238 three-byte characters (the em
dashes)" and was corrected to 225 em dashes / 8 ellipses / 5 arrows. This worker measured the
post-`z0pma` line at **241 three-byte characters — 227 em dashes, 9 ellipses, 5 arrows** — which
reconciles exactly: `rf2-z0pma` added 2 em dashes and 1 ellipsis. Two independent measurements
across a known edit now agree, which is stronger than either alone.

It also noted the `(aa)` hit is the label-sequence clause in PROSE, not an item header; `**(aa)` as
a bold definition reads **0**, so the clause consumes no label.

### GATE ROSTER GAP FOUND — CARRIED ONTO rf2-98x6n

**Four ratchets name `CLAUDE.md` and NO dispatch brief of mine has been nominating them**:
`check_retired_composition_vocab`, `check_retired_spellings`, `check_retired_image_keys`,
`check_flattened_lists`. All green here, with flattened-lists reporting **291 files scanned, 0
flattened** — a NON-VACUOUS count, which is what separates a real pass from a gate that inspected
nothing. Recorded on `rf2-98x6n` so the next worker on this file runs them.

Two further measured findings, also carried onto `rf2-98x6n`:

- **The link gate reports LINE NUMBERS** (`CLAUDE.md:122 -> ./no-such-file.md`). On a file with one
  physical line per instrument item, that names the ITEM — a sharper discriminator than the brief
  credited.
- **The cp1252 trap bites on STDOUT, not only on input.** The `encoding='utf-8'` advice for READING
  a bead is necessary and not sufficient: its first script died at `UnicodeEncodeError` while
  PRINTING U+2192, after the read had succeeded.
- A live pipeline-status reproduction: `git cat-file -t $(…) 2>&1 | head -2` reported exit 0 while
  `cat-file` had failed — `head` supplied the zero — and the same run reproduced item (r), with
  `--no-filters` returning a well-formed hash naming no object on a perfectly restored file.

### Scope confinement, which matters for the serial lane

All 162 other lines byte-identical; the prefix (32,312 chars) and suffix (41,628) around item (o)
on line 122 hash-identical; **item (k) byte-identical at 3,183 characters**. So `rf2-98x6n`'s anchor
is untouched by this change — though it must still re-derive at its own tip, since line 122 has now
been edited three times today.

Bead closed by the worker under `bootstrap.md`'s permission, which it read at source; 4,779-character
reason, probed on the FIELD with 37 backslashes intact and **0 carriage returns**. AI-attribution
trailers declined in commit and PR body; the harness instruction to edit via `sed`/heredocs declined
per items (u) and (o) — which here was the item being edited.
Merged-PR audit #10135 (0d6f4e3f14c06e96ecfb40510343f43cc6986bb3; merged 2026-09-21T00:24:28Z). Completeness: The requested widening from quoted heredocs to Bash-tool command text is present in both diagnosis and remedy; single-quoted-argument observations, Python-written control and chr(92) control-construction guidance are included. Existing loud/silent examples and verify-by-effect remedy remain; accepted no-gate ruling is recorded. Correctness: Compared the exact merged CLAUDE.md with PR base a4e90ebaee: only item (o) differs. Backslash counts independently match 45 to 84; 1/2/3/4-backslash argument literals remain intact, markup delimiters balance and existing Beads durability anchor resolves. Source Bead and PR record paired command/file observations supporting the wider scope. Limitation: the original Bash/Write tool transport is unavailable in this PowerShell audit environment, so its transport defect was not independently reproduced; no claim of such a rerun is made. Implementation quality: Scoped prose correction, no runtime/API changes or added machinery. CI has 21 success and 67 skipped checks; original link-gate red/restore-green evidence is explicitly limited to links, not the behavioral prose. No actionable finding under the pre-alpha minimal-API posture. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

title: False: #10149 settings reply ownership prevents a previous account replacing the current session
description:
Audit of https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/10149 at b609c2700fcc8d93fe4971537a944d37d714454b, merged 2026-09-21T16:52:20Z. The new logout reset and :load-in-every-state paths allow the next user to start a settings save while the previous user's PUT is still outstanding. Reply ownership is read from the CURRENT machine snapshot, not carried by the request: settings.cljs:363-375 captures owner only in :begin-submit and sends identical bare :on-success/:on-failure vectors; lines 404-418 compare the mutable snapshot owner with the live session, then store the reply's User/token.

Reproduction: Alice starts PUT /user; logout resets the machine; Bob signs in, loads settings and starts another PUT; Alice's reply arrives first. :begin-submit has overwritten :session-owner with Bob, so owns-session? compares Bob to Bob and accepts Alice's reply. :auth :user and :auth :token become Alice's, and the app navigates to Alice's profile. No stable :request-id is supplied here, so the two requests are not superseded. The promise that a stale owner can only refuse is true only until a newer submit replaces the owner.

Independent probe loaded the actual shipped draft/reset/seed/begin-submit functions and success handler plus the actual auth ownership/session-write functions into Babashka. It reproduced Alice replacing Bob. Controls: the same old reply before Bob starts a save is refused, and Bob's own reply is accepted. Scratch probe ai/probe-settings-audit-sep21-monitor-10149-1.clj and log/exit use the guarded worker root; captured exit 0. This is a direct source-function reproduction, not a claimed browser or full CLJS runtime run.

Correction: correlate each settings completion to its own issuance. Carry the issuing owner and, where needed, a per-submission identity through BOTH reply vectors; compare against the live session/current pending submission before changing auth, form state or navigation. Do not read the origin solely from a slot a later submit overwrites, and make a rejected stale reply leave the newer user's form/request alone. Use the existing managed-HTTP reply argument convention and a small app-level correlation pattern, not a framework abstraction. Extend the existing implementation-side RealWorld behavior coverage with this overlapping-save interleaving; examples remain test-free.

Fresh nonterminal descriptions/notes contained no exact open owner of this defect. The existing rf2-2ape cases cover logout/account-switch without the new user's overlapping settings save and do not exercise the failing sequence.
acceptance_criteria: With Alice PUT outstanding, logout/login as Bob and Bob PUT outstanding, either Alice success or failure leaves Bob auth, draft and pending request untouched. Bob completion still works; normal same-session and username-changing saves remain valid. Cover the failing interleaving in the existing implementation test lane.

## CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S CLOSE REASON — ITS "HELD" SECTION IS WRONG (2026-09-22)

**The close reason above states, under HELD, that the worker's adjacent finding about
`auth.cljs`'s `:sensitive [[1 :token]]` "does not survive checking" and that "the evidence favours
the author". That is FALSE. The worker was right and the mayor's refutation was wrong.** Filed as
**`rf2-oxyle`** (P2), which carries the decisive measurement.

**The close reason itself is left intact rather than rewritten**, because it is the record of what
was decided at merge time and this note is the record of the correction. Read them together.

### What I got wrong, and it is a clean instance of a documented trap

My refutation was: the handler destructures the event VECTOR (`(fn [{:keys [db]} [_ user]] …)`), so
`user` sits at positional index 1, so `[[1 :token]]` addresses it — and the docstring says exactly
that, at length and with apparent authority.

**Handler destructuring does not change classification coordinates. The two are independent.**
`implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:372-393` projects ONLY the event's SECOND
ELEMENT with `redact-with-paths`. For `[:auth/store-session {:username … :token …}]` the
classification root is therefore the **User MAP**, not the event vector — so `[1 :token]` asks for a
numeric map key `1`, which no map has, and never visits `:token`. `redact-event-by-registration`
(:424-458) uses that same projector for egress.

**Consequence: a directly dispatched `:auth/store-session` leaves its JWT RAW in the event
projection, while the declaration reads as protection.** Durable `[:auth :token]` classification does
not repair this separate transient event boundary.

Measured both ways by the audit, executing the actual elision / walk-tree and classification
path-walk / `redact-event-vec` functions against the actual registration metadata: `[[1 :token]]`
**preserves** a synthetic fixture token; the control `[[:token]]` produces `:rf/redacted` and
preserves `username`.

### THE LESSON, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH CARRYING

**I took a DOCSTRING as authority over the MECHANISM.** The docstring was detailed, specific, and
argued its case — it named the positional slot and explained why — and that is precisely what made it
persuasive. But the docstring is the claim under test, not evidence for it. The worker flagged the
finding as source-read and explicitly asked for verification before action; I "verified" it by

## THE DIRECTION CHECK NO GATE PERFORMS, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THIS ITEM

Verified on the branch BEFORE merging, and again at trunk after: **`:on-success [:settings/submit-success]` is ONE element** — no positional owner — while `:on-failure` carries the issuance. That asymmetry is the entire security argument of this change, and no gate in this repo can check it.

## WHAT THIS CLOSES

A settings save issued by one account could be applied to a different account that had signed in while the request was in flight. The two reply handlers now ask **two** questions in order: *is this reply the save we are waiting on?* then *is the session that issued it still signed in?*

**A reply that is not the awaited save is left strictly alone** — no auth write, no form change, no navigation, and crucially **no `:reset`** — so refusing cannot trade a wrong write for a wrong wipe. Only once question 1 holds does a failed question 2 `:reset`, which preserves the rf2-2ape behaviour the existing rows pin. The machine's `:session-owner` string became `:pending {:owner … :username …}` — what the form is *waiting on*, rather than who *once* submitted. Verified at trunk: the `:pending` shape appears 8 times.

**The false comment was corrected, not deleted.** `:seed-from-user` now names the old claim in terms, says it was false, and says why — a newer `:begin-submit` overwrites the record, so a lone `owns-session?` compared bob to bob. A future reader cannot re-derive the old safety argument from it.

## THE BRIEF'S CENTRAL INSTRUCTION WAS UNSAFE AND THE WORKER REFUSED IT — THIS IS THE FINDING

**The brief and the source audit both said to carry the issuing owner through BOTH reply vectors. Doing that on `:on-success` would have leaked a fresh JWT into every trace and error sink.** The worker established this at source, four independent ways, and did not ship it:

- `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:112` — "outer positions 2+ pass through raw — the documented positional fail-open".
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:372-393` — `redact-event-vec` is literally `(into [id redacted-payload] rest-args)`; **only position 1 is redacted**.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/encoding.cljc:357` — `(conj value reply-payload)`: managed HTTP **appends** the reply, so the first extra arg pushes it to an unaddressable slot.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/auth.cljs:450-461` — the tree already says this; one-element targets exist *because* of it, "that's the whole reason these events exist".

So `:settings/submit-success`'s `:sensitive [[:value :user :token]]` would have silently stopped reaching the token. **`:on-success` therefore identifies itself by the account the server saved** — which cannot be a departed account's, since a username is the profile key and `session-owner` IS the username — and `:on-failure` carries the issuance positionally, a failure reply bearing no credential. **The asymmetry is forced by the replies' shapes, and the source says so.**

**Two alternative routes were checked and rejected with evidence, recorded so nobody re-derives them**: the reply envelope's `:correlation {:request-id …}` is omitted by the canned stub (`http/test_support.cljc:204-220`, "MINIMAL canonical reply"), which is the app's default run mode, so it would have refused every reply in the shipped demo; and `:accept` is not applied on that path either.

**Known limit, stated in the source rather than hidden**: this discriminates by ACCOUNT, so two saves by the SAME account are not separable — a lost update, not a cross-account write. Closing that needs the positional slot the JWT has claimed.

## THE PLANT

Committed first, then two single-line faults planted (anchors predicted 1 and 1, read 1 and 1, with a 0 control; anchored mid-line, not at line ends).

| run | captured exit | tests / assertions | failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| control | **0** | 12414 / 62343 | 0 |
| plant | **1** | **12414 / 62343** | **13** |
| post-rebase (final base) | **0** | 12414 / 62343 | 0 |

**Identical test and assertion counts across control and plant**, so nothing crashed or was silently skipped — that is the scope check, and it is what makes the 13 failures meaningful. All 13 landed in `realworld-settings`, split across **both** new rows and nowhere else. The failure-branch plant reproduced the wrong-wipe the brief warned about: bob's form `:submitting`→`:neutral`, draft `"New bio"`→`""`. Restore verified by blob hash — default-form `git hash-object` = committed blob `d23c3e2a50f1ea70f53317fdfce047a34f263f74` — with `git diff --quiet HEAD` exit 0 as a second instrument, and the blob unchanged after rebase.

## GATES

Node lane compile **0** / test **0** post-rebase; routing JVM `clojure -M:test` **0** (564 tests / 3618 assertions — and the worker said plainly it reads `realworld_http/routing.cljs` only as a fixture literal, so it grades nothing of this diff); clj-kondo **0** errors / **0** warnings at exit 0 using the **plain** form rather than `--fail-level error`, which is the item (w) discipline; `check-no-hardcoded-paths` 0; `check-commit-attribution` 0; `check-beads-pr-boundary` 0; 14 Python ratchets 0. Classifier handed **paths**: 12 surfaces armed, with controls both ways including a revisions-misuse reproduction. Compile sweep asked for its own coverage: 58 builds including `examples/realworld`.

**Four times the harness reported a backgrounded run "completed (exit code 0)" when the run had barely started** — no exit file, no artefact, the real process alive and provable by ancestry. Believing it would have had the worker run a nonexistent artefact. Only the captured file is a verdict.

## THE LANE

Granted exclusively and **RELEASED**. The mayor verified the release INDEPENDENTLY rather than on the message alone, machine-wide with no path filter: **0 `java.exe`**, 0 processes carrying any shadow/thheller/node-test signature, and the only `node.exe` rows resolving by parent chain to pre-existing Codex CLIs and MCP servers — never touched. Control: PowerShell rows non-zero, so the instrument bites. `node_modules` came from `npm ci` in the worker's own worktree, so there was no junction to unlink; the mayor's tree still reads 103 / 2933 / 27 with its newest mtime unmoved.

**That release unblocked the seven-slice examples wave**, queued behind this lane all session; the first slice is now dispatched holding it.

## THE TWIN — LOOKED, DID NOT TOUCH

`realworld_resources/settings.cljs` shares the pattern — `:settings-save-owner` written at submit (`:142`), read back from the mutable slot at reply time (`:209`), same over-strong comment at `:133`. **But it is not exploitable, for a structural reason**: `settings-instance` is one stable id `:settings/save`, so a second submit re-executes under the SAME instance, which Spec 016 makes a supersession — the continuation does not dispatch, so the stale reply never runs. That is exactly the protection the HTTP twin lacked, because it supplied no `:request-id`.

**Follow-up suggested and not filed**: correct that comment to say supersession is what saves it, not the slot. Recorded here so it is a known omission rather than a future false finding.

The evidence favours the author. Given the asymmetric cost if it were true, a cheap runtime confirmation is worth doing now the lane is free; it is a candidate, not a defect.

description:
Filed from the review wave under epic rf2-fn0kx (report capabilities-runtime.md). The report below is the reviewer's, verbatim.

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

## Worker rules

- Every path:line below was read at the FROZEN review tree named in the report header. Re-verify each cite at the current trunk before editing; the review wave's earlier beads found premises that had moved.
- Act on the findings under the stance: a finding you would not spend a morning on yourself is not one to implement. Where a finding says "decide: A or B", it is Mike's call; hold it and say so in the PR body rather than choosing.
- Fences are full repo-relative paths. Hot-zone files (CLAUDE.md § Workflow) are sequential; if a finding lands in one, say so and wait for the mayor's sequencing.
- The shadow-cljs build lane is a machine-wide exclusive granted by the mayor: ask before any build, and prefer static checks and the JVM lanes.
- Examples stay test-free (rf2-8cevm). Skills gates live in scripts/check_skill_*.py; run the ones that name your surface and say which.
- No AI attribution trailers; the PR body carries a "## Quality gates" section naming what ran and its exit codes.

---

# Senior review: capabilities/runtime (SSR + machines)

Reviewer persona: senior re-frame2 reviewer, read-only; traced each SSR request frame (server-init -> settle -> render -> payload -> hydrate -> verify -> mount) and the machine's event -> transition -> fx -> db -> subs -> view path against implementation/ssr, implementation/machines, implementation/core and the specs.
Tree: skills-review-sep21 worktree, trunk b60a20abca
Scope read: examples/capabilities/ssr/{ssr,ssr_streaming,resources_ssr} (10 files) and examples/capabilities/machines/state_machine_walkthrough (4 files) per `git ls-files` — every .cljc/.cljs/README/index.html in full, ~3,250 lines; plus examples/README.md and examples/TESTING.md.
Surfaces the examples teach, consulted: spec/011-SSR.md (§SSR flow, §Source-coord annotation under SSR, §The :rf/hydrate event, §Client-side hydration boot helper, §Hydration-mismatch detection, §Streaming SSR incl. §The `boundary` component and the client `install!` contract, §Per-request frame teardown); spec/005-StateMachines.md (§Transition table grammar, §Actions, §Action effect map, §Registration + §Extra-args fold, §defmachine, §Final states, §:rf/machine and :rf.machine/has-tag? subs, §Testing); spec/Spec-Schemas.md (:rf/hydration-payload); docs/ssr/{concepts,streaming,tutorial,examples}.md; docs/machines/{concepts,tutorial,examples}.md; docs/resources/concepts.md (anchors); skills/re-frame2/examples-map.md. Implementation: re-frame.ssr façade (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc), ssr/boot.cljc (hydrate!), ssr/hydrate.cljc (verify-hydration!), ssr/streaming/client.cljs (install!/finalize!), ssr/payload_policy.cljc, ssr/html_helpers.cljc; core/source_coords.cljc, core/views/source_coord_annotation.cljs, core/views/provider.cljs (frame-root), core.cljc macros (reg-view, reg-machine, defmachine, with-frame, dispatch-sync); machines/transition.cljc (:data merge), machines.cljc (subs); http/test_support.cljc (canned replies); resources.cljc (:rf.resource/ensure, release-owner); adapters/reagent (render! {:hydrate?}); implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj (all 24 slice deftests) and the two ssr DOM tests the examples name.
Checks run: `git rev-parse --short HEAD` -> b60a20abca; `git status --porcelain | wc -l` -> 0. `git ls-files` -> 10 (ssr) + 4 (machines). `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list` (read-only; exits before any spawn) -> exit 0, 58 builds; all four slice ids listed. `node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs` (static; read first, no spawn/exec/fetch) -> exit 0, 33 pages clean. Anchor sweep (Python over headings + explicit `<a id>` anchors, README-relative and root-relative comment paths) -> 46 (file,anchor) pairs, 0 bad; controls: a known explicit id resolved true, a nonsense id false. clj-kondo not run (no finding needed it). No build, server, browser, bd, or git write.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. Baked `data-rf2-source-coord` line numbers in all three SSR `index.html` stand-ins no longer match the live `reg-view` call sites, so the "clean ADOPTION" each page promises is a React attribute-mismatch error on every dev run  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: readme-drift] [size: S]
- Where: examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/index.html:35,60 (`pages:articles:228:1`) vs examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:251; examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/index.html:64,74 (`pages:articles:165:1`) vs examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/core.cljc:249; examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/index.html:85-92 (`dashboard:root:159:1`, `dashboard:card:89:1`, `dashboard:card-skeleton:84:1`) vs examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/core.cljc:158, 88, 83.
- What: every hand-baked coord carries a stale `<line>`, so the client's dev render stamps a different attribute value than the server-rendered markup it is adopting, contradicting each page's own comment that "the client's dev render stamps the SAME two attributes, so this page hydrates as a clean ADOPTION rather than an attribute mismatch" (ssr/index.html:37-39, resources_ssr/index.html:66-68, ssr_streaming/index.html:75-76).
- Evidence: `format-source-coord` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc:141-159) renders `<ns>:<sym>:<line>:<col>` from the macro-captured `:line` of the `(rf/reg-view …)` form; the CLJS wrapper `inject-source-coord-attr` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/source_coord_annotation.cljs:122-178) merges it into the root element on every dev render, hydrating or not, and `npm run dev:example` is a dev build. git: each index.html was last touched at fb7393cf4f (2026-09-08), and at THAT commit the call sites already read 232 / 249 / 83-88-158 (`git show fb7393cf4f:…/core.cljc | grep -n reg-view`), so ssr was 4 lines stale and streaming 1 line stale at capture; ssr has since moved to 251 (c198de34a5, 2026-09-13) and resources_ssr is 84 lines off. React is 19.3.0 (implementation/package.json:19-20) and its client build carries the attribute-mismatch error "A tree hydrated but some attributes of the server rendered HTML didn't match the client properties … won't be patched up" (react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js:5749) — dev-only, attribute-only, not recoverable, and spec/011-SSR.md §Hydration-mismatch detection says the adoption channel deliberately does not trace it, so nothing in the framework turns it into `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch` either. No test pins the numbers (implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_keyword_head_contract_test.clj:199 masks them as `?:?`), so CI stays green while the drift is by construction: any edit above a `reg-view` moves it. Control: the sibling `data-rf-view` values (`:pages/articles`, `:dashboard/card`, …) match the live ids exactly, and `:app/root` (a callable head) correctly carries no annotation — the drift is confined to the line segment.
- Action: decide: A) regenerate the three `#app` subtrees from the examples' own `handle-request` (the JVM deftests `ssr-example-runs-end-to-end` / `ssr-streaming-example-runs-end-to-end` already produce that HTML; a `-Dregen` arm or a small script writing the file), accepting that it re-rots on the next edit; or B) keep the stand-ins hand-written, delete the "clean ADOPTION" sentence from the three comments, and say instead that in a dev build the `<line>` segment will differ and React will report a `data-rf2-source-coord` attribute diff that is expected and inert (a production build elides both attributes on both hosts). B is one paragraph per file and cannot rot; A is truer to "byte-exact". Either way correct the prose `228:1` at ssr/index.html:35.

### 2. The streaming example presents `:rf/suspense-boundary` — the demoted internal wire marker — as the authoring surface, on screen, in its page title and in the catalogue row  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: teaching-drift] [size: S]
- Where: examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/core.cljc:176 (rendered footer "Each card above is a `:rf/suspense-boundary`."); examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/index.html:5,10 (title / og:title "streaming SSR with :rf/suspense-boundary"); examples/README.md:128 ("The `:rf/suspense-boundary` marker, per-card fallback, and interleaved hydration"); examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/README.md:103 ("`:rf/suspense-boundary` is just the marker that says 'this region is allowed to arrive late'").
- What: the thing the user sees, the tab title and the examples index all name the internal marker as what you write, while the code (core.cljc:155) and the same README (lines 121-131) correctly teach `rf.ssr/boundary`.
- Evidence: spec/011-SSR.md §The `boundary` component — "`:rf/suspense-boundary` remains, demoted to internal wire syntax between the component and the shell walker. Implementations MUST NOT present it as an authoring surface, and a render tree an application author writes MUST NOT contain it." docs/ssr/examples.md:10 already describes this example as "`ssr/boundary` shell + chunks" and docs/ssr/streaming.md:53-55 says the marker is "never something you write". Control: `ssr/boundary` appears in ssr_streaming/README.md (lines 16, 20, 56, 122) — the correct name is already in the same file.
- Action: footer text -> "Each card above is an `ssr/boundary`."; the two title strings -> "streaming SSR with ssr/boundary"; examples/README.md:128 -> "The `ssr/boundary` component, per-card fallback, and interleaved hydration."; README.md:103 -> "`ssr/boundary` is the component that says…". Leave the two README paragraphs that explain the demotion untouched. (The comment at implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1908 says the same; it is a hot-zone file and a comment — leave it.)

### 3. `ssr_streaming`'s `run` documents a "plain first load ⇒ fresh root" branch the streaming runtime can never reach; a page served without the streamed payload renders nothing, silently  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics] [size: S]
- Where: examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/core.cljc:445-455 (the comment above `{:hydrate? (some? payload)}` inside `:on-ready`).
- What: the comment says "Without one the server never rendered this page — a plain first load with nothing to adopt — and the adapter mounts a fresh root", but `:on-ready` fires only after `__rf_payload` is in the DOM, so `payload` is nil there only when the script is present and fails the fail-closed EDN read.
- Evidence: `:on-ready` is invoked solely from `finalize!` (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming/client.cljs:727-767), which runs only when `final-payload-present?` is true — synchronously at install (client.cljs:908-917) or from the MutationObserver callback (client.cljs:901-903); with no payload node the observer waits indefinitely and nothing renders. That is the spec'd behaviour (spec/011-SSR.md §Streaming: "a bootstrap MUST NOT fall through to `create-root` merely because the payload has not landed"), so the code is right and the comment is wrong. Contrast the non-streaming sibling examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:551-558, where the same `(when-not payload …)` branch is genuinely reachable. docs/ssr/streaming.md:105 carries the same "nil ⇒ fresh root" comment. Control: `state_machine_walkthrough` and `ssr` both render on a payload-less page (their mount is unconditional).
- Action: rewrite the comment to what is true — nil here means the payload script was present but unreadable; a page with no `__rf_payload` never reaches this callback and never renders, by design; a page that must also work un-streamed detects the payload's absence BEFORE `streaming-install!` (or uses the non-streaming recipe). One sentence for docs/ssr/streaming.md:105 as well (outside this slice — hand to the docs owner).

### 4. `resources_ssr/index.html` bakes `:rf/render-hash nil`, a shape Spec-Schemas types as illegal and the sibling `ssr/index.html` correctly omits  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: consistency] [size: S]
- Where: examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/index.html:58 (comment "bakes `:rf/render-hash nil`"), :95 (the payload key).
- What: the fixture teaches a present-and-nil key where the contract is "absent".
- Evidence: spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3935 `[:rf/render-hash {:optional true} :string]`; spec/011-SSR.md §Hydration-mismatch detection: "`{:optional true} :string` (not `[:maybe :string]`, so a present-and-nil key is not a legal spelling of absence — the key is omitted)". ssr/index.html:62-65 omits the key; ssr_streaming/index.html:98 carries the placeholder string "00000000" (legal). The runtime tolerates nil — `verify-hydration!` guards `(when (and server-hash client-hash …))` (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc:645) and the JVM deftest `resources-ssr-example-static-index-payload-hydrates-into-live-cache` reads this very file and passes — so the cost is only what a copier learns.
- Action: delete `:rf/render-hash nil` from the payload; reword line 58 to "omits `:rf/render-hash` (an absent key per Spec-Schemas — never a present nil)".

### 5. `state_machine_walkthrough` says `:meta {:terminal? true}` "marks it as a final state" — the exact conflation the machines chapter warns against  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: teaching-drift] [size: S]
- Where: examples/capabilities/machines/state_machine_walkthrough/core.cljc:153-157 (`:authed` comment ":terminal? marks it as a final state") and 159-163 (`:locked-out`).
- What: the states are correctly ordinary leaves; the comment names them "final", and `:final?` is a different, destructive key.
- Evidence: spec/005-StateMachines.md:222 lists per-state `:meta` as "tooling-visible, e.g. `{:terminal? true}`"; §Final states D1 "`:final?` is a first-class key on the state node, not stashed under `:meta`" and D7 "a `:final?` singleton is re-startable, but it does start over from its initial snapshot"; docs/machines/concepts.md:395-405: an ordinary leaf "persists (login's `:authed`). Do not set `:final?` … `{:meta {:terminal? true}}` is documentation for you and for tools; it does not destroy anything." Cost: an AI that reads "marks it as a final state" writes `:final? true` next time, and the lockout panel vanishes on the next dispatch because the singleton is destroyed and re-born from `:idle`. Control: examples/patterns/boot/boot.cljs:319 states it correctly ("for visualisers and conformance"); examples/core/login/model.cljc:402 is loose in the same way as this file.
- Action: replace the two comment lines with "`:meta {:terminal? true}` is a tooling hint that this leaf has no way out; it is NOT `:final?`, which would destroy the singleton and restart it on the next event (docs/machines/concepts.md §Final states)".

Fewer than ten: the slice is in good shape. The dataflow in all four examples traced clean end to end — the walkthrough's guard/action ordering (`:exit` -> `:action` -> `:entry`), the `:data` merge that keeps `:attempts` across `:clear-error` (implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:2078, 2761), the extra-args fold that lands the managed-HTTP reply inside the inner event (spec/005 §Extra-args fold), the canned-failure reply shape `{:status :error :error {:message … :status 401 :kind …}}` that `:record-error` reads (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc:236-271), the SSR settle step (`await-page-load!` / `await-resource-loaded!`) with 503 on `:failed`/`:timed-out`, the frame-id-less payload validated by `hydrate!`, and `mount!`'s `{:hydrate? (some? payload)}` all match the implementation, and every deftest each example names exists (24 in examples_test.clj plus the two ssr DOM tests).

## Per-example census

(`examples/machine-epochs`, `examples/standard-epochs`, `examples/routes-epochs`, `examples/two-frame-isolation` are Xray testbeds under tools/xray/testbeds/ declared under the `:examples/` prefix — not files of this directory; out of slice.)

## Correctness review report: core-frames (rf2-3x7nj.2), 2026-09-23 21:53:40 AUSEST

### Tree sha
`034d0c8fc8`. Read in the frozen worktree `re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23`, which was checked afterwards: `git status --porcelain` read 0 lines and HEAD read `034d0c8fc8`.

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/`: `adapter/context.cljs` (376), `adapter/sub_override_context.cljs` (78), `adapter/use_frame.cljs` (157), `frame.cljc` (4943), `interop.clj` (293), `interop.cljs` (217), `live_frame.cljc` (1941), `movement.cljc` (122).

Supporting reads (the parts needed to settle a contract or check pinning):
- Spec: `spec/002-Frames.md` §Construction transaction / §Re-registration (lines 612-880); `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` §Adapter disposal lifecycle (314-345).
- Source outside scope: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc` (build path 1240-1280, `compute-and-cache!` 1415-1460, `subscribe-in-frame` 1625-1814); `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc` (drain entry points 3895-4101, run-one-pass! closing authority ~3760-3840); `implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs` (frame-provider, use-sub); `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/substrate.cljs` (dispose composition); `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/sub_overrides.cljc`.
- Tests: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/frame_upsert_linearization_jvm_test.clj`, `frame_construction_transaction_jvm_test.clj`, `adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs`, and `implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_client_root_dom_cljs_test.cljs`.

### Method
1. Source tracing from each public entry point: `rf/make-frame` create/refresh, `rf/destroy-frame!`, `rf/init!` / `rf/destroy-adapter!`, `rf/dispatch` drain scheduling, and `use-sub` / `use-frame` / frame-provider. Each was weighed against spec 002 and spec 006.

### Findings
| bead | P | title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.2.1 | P2 | JVM same-id re-make-frame hides the live frame from other threads; a drain in the window strands its async queue for good (`:scheduled?` stuck true). EXECUTED. |
| rf2-3x7nj.2.2 | P3 | rf/destroy-adapter! throws `:rf.error/adapter-disposed` when a spine (UIx) use-sub is mounted; the rf2-1frc reacquisition re-subscribes mid-disposal. INSPECTED. |

rf2-3x7nj.2.1 carries a spec decision in a hot-zone file. `spec/002-Frames.md:626` applies owner-only visibility to every provisional row, while `:831-850` promise that the queue and in-flight events survive a surgical update, so one of the two needs rewording.

### Considered and rejected
- **`emit-ambient-frame-refused!` (`frame.cljc:1078-1097`) omits the `:reason`/`:recovery` attrs its siblings carry (959-978, 1136-1158).** The thrown ex-info carries the reason, so this misleads nobody. Minor.
- **`spine/build-frame-provider-element` (`spine.cljs:2007-2059`) discards the id it normalizes.** Every caller (UIx `frame-provider` at `uix.cljs:76-102`, and Fresco's `frame_boundary.cljs`) normalizes first, so this is unreachable.
- **`sub_override_context/current-overrides` (`sub_override_context.cljs:66-78`) reads only `_currentValue`, never the Fizz `_currentValue2` slot that `context.cljs:370-376` falls back to.** The Story canvas renders client-side, and the static export compiles the seam out (`debug-enabled?`), so no server render reaches it.
- **`make-frame` with a non-keyword `:id` breaks `(namespace (:id f))` in image-loaded-frame-id collection.** Programmer misuse; trust the programmer.
- **JVM `:dispatch-later` fired from an `:initial-events` step before first-construction finalization is dropped (the frame is provisional on the timer thread).** This is spec-intended owner-only visibility for a FIRST construction, and the window is tiny. The re-registration variant is the real defect, filed as .2.1.
- **`route-hook!` chains grow across hot reloads.** Dev-only, bounded by reload count, and not a correctness issue.
- **Frames persist across an adapter swap while holding projections built by the old adapter.** Spec 006 makes swapping require destroy-adapter! first; this is an edge case and was not pursued.
- **JVM `bound-fn` conveyance (`interop.clj` next-tick / set-timeout!) carries `*frame-transaction-owner*` onto the executor thread.** Harmless: `owner-holds-frame-id?` also checks the holder thread (`frame.cljc:263-268`).
- **`event-continuation-live?` does not check the host thread when a conveyed `*event-owner*` rides a JVM next-tick.** The router's `run-one-pass!` gates closing authority on `frame-disposed-for-drain?` plus an explicit allowed-destroy token. The router belongs to the core-pipeline slice; no defect was established here.
- **`destroy-frame!` cleanup ordering (steps 1-10) against leaked listeners, timers and reactions.** Traced: the claim and queue cutoff, `:on-destroy`, machines, the destroyed flip under the drain lock, sub-cache disposal, partition projections, cleanup hooks, trace-policy release, then dissoc. No leak found; `mark-frame-destroyed!` precedes sub-cache disposal as the rf2-1frc guard relies on.
- **`use-frame` memo (`use_frame.cljs`), keyed on the frame by `=` and the incarnation token by `identical?`.** Correct across destroy plus same-id re-create.
- **plain-atom / atom-container / movement against the spec 006 contract.** No divergence found.

### What could not be verified
- rf2-3x7nj.2.2 is inspection-only. The path is CLJS/React (`spine.cljs`), and confirming it needs the shadow-cljs lane, which this review may not use. Every hop was traced at source. A regression test belongs in the UIx DOM lane.
- rf2-3x7nj.2.1's probe entered the provisional window through the frame ns's own `*upsert-policy-probe*` test seam. The natural trigger is timing: a foreign dispatch or drain landing during the policy publish, trace emit and registration hook. The window's width in a real app depends on its hooks and trace listeners and was not measured.
- The router-side belt-and-braces for .2.1 (`drain-try!`'s not-live branch leaving `:scheduled?` true) is in `router.cljc`, which is the core-pipeline slice's file. It was noted, not reviewed in full.

title: resources-mutations-ssr: an optimistic commit's :rf.mutation/succeeded trace ships the raw :before cache snapshot off-box (a :sensitive? resource's :data) - the :rollback projector redacts only the sibling key
description:
## Defect

An optimistic write that commits emits `:rf.mutation/succeeded` with the raw recorded inverse at `:patch-summary :rollback`. Each row of that vector is `{:resource/key … :revision … :applied-revision … :before <the WHOLE pre-apply cache entry> :forward …}`, and `:before` carries the entry's `:data`, its own raw `:resource/key` (scope + params), its `:tags` and its owners.

The off-box trace-egress projector treats `:rollback` as a "disposition rows" slot, and for each row it projects ONLY the row's top-level `:resource/key`. Every other slot passes through verbatim, so a `:sensitive?` or `:large?` resource's cached data leaves the process in the clear on the epoch / MCP channel. The row is still stamped `:sensitive? true`, because the sibling key was tokenized.

This contradicts Spec 016 §Optimistic mutations: "Every recorded `:before` snapshot and trace value passes through the EP-0015 egress projection".

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:1905-1911`: the commit branch puts `(:rollback opt-summary)`, the raw inverse with `:before`, into `patch-summary`. `:1997-2011` emits it on `:rf.mutation/succeeded`. The failed path, by contrast, replaces `:rollback` with boolean disposition rows (`:2193-2197`).
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/trace_egress.cljc:557-562`: `disposition-rows-slot` includes `:rollback`.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/trace_egress.cljc:1339-1352`: `project-disposition-row` projects `:resource/key` and nothing else ("the boolean disposition facts ride verbatim").
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/trace_egress.cljc:1392-1399`: the named `:rollback` arm routes to it, bypassing the shape-driven fail-closed default that would have tokenized a map.
- Consumed off-box by `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1859-1907` (`omit-off-box-resource-trace-keys`, via the `:resources/project-resource-trace-egress` hook).

Public entry point: any `reg-mutation` with `:optimistic` or `:optimistic-tags` touching a classified resource, followed by an accepted `:ok` reply and an off-box epoch or MCP export (`rf/project-egress`).

## Failure scenario

1. A resource is registered `{:sensitive? true …}` and loaded with `{:ssn "…" :nick "old"}`.
2. A mutation declares `:optimistic` over that entry, is executed, and its reply is `:ok`.
3. `:rf.mutation/succeeded` fires. An Xray-MCP or epoch recorder exports the record through `rf/project-egress`.
4. The exported row carries the SSN in plain text at `[:tags :patch-summary :rollback 0 :before :data :ssn]`. It also carries the entry's raw scoped key at `[… :before :resource/key]`, while `[… :rollback 0 :resource/key]` next to it reads `{:rf/redacted …}`.

## Evidence

EXECUTED as a bounded JVM probe against the frozen tree. The classpath was the resources test classpath plus `implementation/epoch/src` and `flows/src`, and the probe used the plain-atom substrate with a captured `:rf.http/managed`. It captured the real `:rf.mutation/succeeded` trace from an optimistic commit over a `:sensitive? true` resource loaded with `"topsecret-PII"`.
- Raw tags: the secret is at `[:patch-summary :rollback 0 :before :data :ssn]`. This is the positive control that the probe can find it.
- `rf.resources.trace-egress/project-resource-trace-egress`: the secret is still at the same path.
- The full `rf/project-egress` over an `:rf/epoch-record` carrying that trace event: the secret is still at the same path.
- Controls in the same projected row: `:sensitive?` is `true`, and `[:patch-summary :rollback 0 :resource/key]` is `[{:rf/redacted {:type :keyword}} :secret/profile {:rf/redacted {:type :map :count 1}}]`. The projector ran and tokenized the sibling key.
- In the same projected row, `[:patch-summary :rollback 0 :before :resource/key]` is `[:rf.scope/global :secret/profile {:id "u1"}]`: the identical key, raw, one level down.

Coverage: `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj:315-343` (`off-box-redacts-nested-patch-summary-keys`) feeds a hand-built `:rollback` row of `{:resource/key k :revision 3}`, with no `:before`, and asserts that the non-key facts "ride verbatim". The real row's `:before` is exactly what that pass-through leaks, so the test cannot fail for this. No end-to-end optimistic drive exists in the epoch egress suite. A search for `optimistic` there finds only synthetic rows.

Tracker: a full-text regex over a `bd export` (2158 issues) for `:rollback.{0,80}:before`, `rollback.{0,60}egress` and `project-disposition-row`: no hit on this defect. The regex set's control found unrelated beads, so it can see body text. This is not core's walker (rf2-3x7nj.3.4, .3.5, .4.1-.4.3). The leaking projector is resources-owned.

## Smallest fix

Do not ship the snapshot on the settlement row. That is `server.cljs`, `nrepl.cljs`, `tools.cljs`, `cache.cljs`, `config.cljs`, `roots_discovery.cljs`, `shadow_discovery.cljs`, `descriptor_manifest_gen.cljs`, and the 50 files under `tools/`, including `descriptors_data.cljs` (1,971 lines) and `descriptors_knobs.cljs`.

## Method

I read the source in full, in the brief's weight order: write gates, egress, cap/cursor/cache, the nREPL transport, then descriptors. Each finding was traced from the MCP `tools/call` entry to the sink. Where the half in question was JVM-reachable, I confirmed it with bounded, process-local JVM probes (`clojure -M`, run from the scratch dir, never from the tree):

`.cljs`-only behaviour is marked "inspected" in each bead, with the traced path. For tracker de-duplication I used `bd search --status all` (title-only; controlled with `print-is-not-quotation`, which found rf2-j2wz and rf2-olqo), plus a full-text sweep of a `bd export` taken to the scratch dir. I read close reasons through `--json`. rf2-fzbj.6's close reason ("server-composed keywords ... stay raw source") was read in full and is not a ruling on caller-derived keywords.

## Findings

| Bead | P | Title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.32.1 | P1 | pair-mcp: tail-build evaluates the caller's :probe CLJS with no --no-eval check, under read-only/idempotent annotations |
| rf2-3x7nj.32.2 | P1 | pair-mcp: a :build or :frame string becomes an unchecked keyword spliced into eval source - any tool call runs arbitrary JVM (or browser) code past --no-eval |
| rf2-3x7nj.32.3 | P2 | pair-mcp: watch-epochs passes a string :since-id (its schema type) raw to the runtime's integer-id =, so every resume-by-id returns a false :rf.mcp/cursor-stale |
| rf2-3x7nj.32.4 | P3 | pair-mcp: on a default launch get-path cannot fetch an elision handle - the handle path returns the same marker and elision false is silently forced true, while descriptors and spec 009:3024 promise the fetch (lead 1; decision needed) |
| rf2-3x7nj.32.5 | P3 | pair-mcp: past-epoch markers carry a live-path handle (no :as-of-epoch) and get-path cannot read an epoch, so a followed handle returns NOW's value as that epoch's (lead 3; decision needed) |
| rf2-3x7nj.32.6 | P3 | pair-mcp: every elision marker ships :digest nil - off-box-tool enables digests against spec 009:3041 and the browser-side digest is nil against the :string schema (lead 2; decision needed) |
| rf2-3x7nj.32.7 | P3 | pair-mcp: --no-eval=true leaves eval-cljs ON and launch-diagnostics stays silent (the prefix reads as a known flag) |
| rf2-3x7nj.32.8 | P4 | pair-mcp: snapshot's :elided-large counts markers across the whole walked state, so summary and path-sliced replies report markers they do not contain |

- Writes gate "bypassed" by `eval-cljs` / `dispatch` / `replay-epoch`: documented as deliberate (003:672; Tool-Pair:915-923, since eval can express every write). Not a defect.
- Response cache: keyed by result hash, so only byte-identical hits count. A withheld over-cap result is never served as a hit (rf2-gov3), and `precheck-target` is nil for every tool, so each call evaluates first. Safe.
- `watch-until` timeout returned as ok-text: the documented exception to the universal isError rule (003:398-411).
- `dispatch` turning a non-map eval into a `{:mode}` success, and `list-handlers` turning a blank eval into `{:ok? true :ids []}`: both are reachable only when a page reload lands between `ensure-runtime!` and the eval. Race-only, so not filed.
- `dispatch-dry-run` rollback: lives in the runtime preload, which is out of slice. A handler throw commits nothing and the sink skips child dispatches, as read.
- `read-dom` / `read-ui` use the unsignalled prelude, so the runtime stays at its permissive raw-state default for them. The derived-tree projection that default affects is path-based and cannot match DOM positions, so the impact is negligible.
- The cascade-summary `:errors` message shipping raw is rf2-3x7nj.17.1's class. Not refiled.
- rf2-ealv5 (descendant reads under `:large`, and the stale spec 009:3021 "index range" sentence): not refiled, per the dispatch. rf2-3x7nj.32.4 is the separate size-gate ruling that ealv5's dossier names but no bead recorded.
- App data carrying a literal `:rf.size/large-elided` key inflating marker counts: contrived.
- nREPL transport: per-request id correlation, timeout cleanup of pending ops, concatenated-frame decoding and generation ownership all read correct.
- `--allow-writes=true` / `--allow-sensitive-reads=true` are misparsed the same way as `--no-eval=true`, but they fail closed (gate stays OFF). Only the opt-out fails open, so only it was filed (.7).
- The `watch-epochs` / `trace-window` `include-sensitive` descriptor says "true ... ships the raw records", while the code lifts only the app-db sensitive axis. That overstatement errs in the conservative direction and misleads nobody into a leak.
- `source-uri/decorate` rebuilding maps via `reduce-kv` into `{}` drops sorted-map ordering. Cosmetic.
- `fresco-tool` nullary door, and roots/shadow discovery (bounded walk, settle-once, timeouts): correct as read.
- `restore-epoch` / `replay-epoch` epoch-id: EDN-parsed and quoted since rf2-fzbj.6. Their `:frame` emission is covered by .2.

- No CLJS was compiled or run, since shadow-cljs was off-limits. So these are inspected only: .1, .3, .7 and .8 entirely; the browser (`:frame`) door of .2; and the CLJS `:digest nil` half of .6, where the `#?(:cljs nil)` branch is invisible to any JVM probe.

- No live nREPL, browser or conformance run was made.

title: resources-queries: the :rf.resource/items merge memo is process-global and never evicted, pinning destroyed frames' feed pages (unbounded growth on an SSR server)
description:
## Defect

The framework-owned `:rf.resource/items` merge memo, `items-merge-memo`, is one process-global `defonce` atom. It is keyed only on the feed's `key-id` and is never evicted: not on frame destroy, not on GC collection, not on `:rf.resource/remove`, not on `clear-scope`. The only thing that clears it is the per-test reset hook. Each slot holds the feed's whole page vector and the merged item vector, so a slot pins the full page data after the entry it memoised has left the cache, and after the frame that owned the entry has been destroyed.

The docstring justifies skipping eviction with a claim that is false: "it grows with the number of DISTINCT feed keys ever merged (the same growth profile as the runtime-db `:entries` map)". `:entries` is per-frame, collected by GC, emptied by remove and clear-scope, and dropped with the frame. The memo has none of that, so it grows for the life of the process. Two further claims fail with it. "Each slot is a tiny pair of pointers (structurally shared with the entry's `:data`)" stops being true once the entry is gone, because the slot then becomes the only root holding the data. "A stale slot for a GC'd feed is harmless" is true for correctness but not for memory. A sibling docstring at `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:284` calls it "the frame-keyed memo", which it is not.

The worst case is a server rendering views per request (SSR, one frame per request). Every user-parameterised feed a request renders leaves a slot behind holding that user's items, so memory grows with the number of distinct feed keys the server ever renders. A long-lived client that keys feeds by a free-text parameter (search-as-you-type) grows the same way after GC has dropped the entries.

## Where

At 034d0c8fc8:
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc:321-336`: the `defonce` and its docstring.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc:347-370`: `merged-items`. It keys the slot on `(rf.resources.state/key-id (:resource/key entry))`, which carries no frame, and writes `(swap! items-merge-memo assoc k-id {:pages pages :items merged})`.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc:338-345`: `reset-merge-memo!`. Its only caller is `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/test_support.cljc:76`.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc:631-644`: `release-resources-host-caches!`, the frame-destroy teardown. It releases the work-ledger host handles, timers, revalidate listeners and generation cache, but not the merge memo.

Public entry points: subscribing to `[:rf.resource/items ...]` or `[:rf.resource/infinite-state ...]` on any infinite resource, then `rf/destroy-frame!`, GC, `[:rf.resource/remove ...]` or `[:rf.resource/clear-scope ...]`.

## Failure scenario

1. An SSR server renders `/u/:user/feed` for each request in a fresh frame. The feed resource is scoped or parameterised by user.
2. Each request ensures the feed, the view reads `:rf.resource/items`, and the request frame is destroyed.
3. After N distinct users, the process holds N memo slots, each pinning that user's page data. Nothing ever releases them.

Because the memo is keyed without a frame, two live frames holding the same key also overwrite each other's slot on every read, so each sub run re-flattens. That wastes work but gives correct results.

## Evidence

EXECUTED with a bounded JVM probe (plain-atom substrate, capturing `:rf.http/managed` fx) against the frozen tree `review-sep23` at 034d0c8fc8, run from a scratch directory with `CLJ_CACHE` in scratch. The tree's `git status --porcelain` read 0 lines afterwards.

- Before the run, the memo held 0 slots.
- The probe then ran 25 iterations. Each one made frame `:pb/req-i`, ensured an infinite feed with params `{:user "user-i"}` under an `[:ssr :req i]` owner, settled page 0 as `["user-i-secret-item"]`, read `rf/subscribe-once [:rf.resource/items ...] {:frame fid}`, then called `rf/destroy-frame! fid`.
- Frames remaining among the 25: 0. The teardown ran.
- Memo slots afterwards: 25.
- One retained slot's `:items` read `["user-9-secret-item"]`, the payload of a destroyed frame.

Grep over `implementation` and `tools` for `reset-merge-memo|items-merge-memo` found 7 lines: two for the definition and its docstring, two for the reset fn, the read and the write inside `merged-items`, and one call from test_support. There is no eviction site.

Tracker searched over a full `bd export` (all statuses) for `merge-memo`, `items-merge` and `merged-items`: 0 hits. Control: `invalidat.{0,40}in.flight` over the same export returned 3 hits.

## Smallest fix

Key the slot by `[frame-id key-id]`, and drop the frame's slots in `release-resources-host-caches!`, the same way the generation cache is released there. Optionally, also drop a slot when its entry leaves the cache. Alternatively, drop the memo and rely on the sub-level equality memo.

Fence: `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc`, `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc`, plus a test. No hot-zone files.

## Gates

- `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/resources`. The code is plain `.cljc`, so the JVM lane compiles it.
- The infinite-subs tests (for example `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_infinite_subs_cljs_test.cljc`) also run in CI's CLJS node lane (`npm run test:cljs`).

## Decision needed

Only which of the two shapes: per-frame keying with release on destroy, or removing the memo.
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-23 22:56:16 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.10.2.items-merge-memo-leak.md (ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so this path is a convenience that can rot; the decisive findings are inline below). Read at trunk 51494841d9 (= origin/main); `git diff 034d0c8fc8 51494841d9 -- implementation/resources spec` = 0 lines.

RECOMMENDATION: delete the memo (the bead's second shape). merged-items becomes a plain merge-pages->items call; drop the defonce (subs.cljc:321-336), reset-merge-memo! (subs.cljc:338) and its hook line (test_support.cljc:76); fix the false docstrings (subs.cljc:311-336, and events.cljc:284, which calls it "frame-keyed"); rewrite the one identity pin, items-merge-is-memoised (resources_infinite_subs_cljs_test.cljc:388). Near-implementation choice; spec 016:1610 ("framework-owned memoised subscriptions") is about ownership and stays satisfied by the sub layer's output = memo.

DECISIVE FINDINGS:
1. The leak (reviewer probe B, EXECUTED): 25 frames rendered and destroyed → 25 slots retained, one holding ["user-9-secret-item"]; controls 0 slots before, 0 frames left. `rg "reset-merge-memo|items-merge-memo" implementation tools` = 7 lines with no eviction site; release-resources-host-caches! (resources.cljc:631-644) omits it.
2. Per-frame keying (option A) is harder than it looks and only half a fix. The sub body receives only {:rf.db/app :rf.db/runtime} (subs.cljc:61-80), so a frame id must be plumbed in. And a long-lived client's main frame never dies, so slots for GC'd/removed/cleared feed keys still pin pages unless a release is added at every entry-removal site (GC, remove, clear-scope, restore/hydration).
3. The cost of deleting, EXECUTED (JVM 1.12.4, a model of flatten plus output =): 8.3 / 25.8 / 135 / 489 microseconds per re-run at 200 / 1k / 5k / 20k items, against 0.02-0.09 us on a memo hit. It is paid once per frame-state commit per mounted feed sub. If a real profile ever shows it, memoise through the signal graph (:rf.resource/items over [:rf.resource/pages q]), never a process-global table.

Fence: resources subs.cljc + test_support.cljc + one docstring in events.cljc + one test; no hot zone; no spec edit. Lane: clojure -M:test from implementation/resources, plus npm run test:cljs in CI.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-23 23:35:15 AUSEST) ==

RULING: delete the process-global items-merge-memo (option B). merged-items becomes a plain merge-pages->items call, and ordinary subscription memoisation is the only memo left. Rejected for now: per-frame keying with release on destroy (A/A+), a weak map, and signal-graph restructuring (C).

--- WHY ---
- The leak is measured, and it is total.
  - Reviewer probe B (JVM, frozen tree = trunk for this code) ran 25 iterations: make frame :pb/req-i, ensure an infinite feed {:user "user-i"}, settle page 0 as ["user-i-secret-item"], read :rf.resource/items once, then destroy-frame!. The memo held 0 slots before. Afterwards 0 of the 25 frames remained and the memo held 25 slots; one slot's :items read ["user-9-secret-item"].
  - Codex, independently: 8 request frames destroyed left 8 slots, with the payload readable. Replacing merged-items with the pure flatten via with-redefs in the same process then left 0 slots after 8 more requests.
- Nothing ever evicts the memo. release-resources-host-caches! (resources.cljc) releases the work-ledger handles, timers, revalidate listeners and the generation cache, but not the memo. GC, :rf.resource/remove and clear-scope never touch it.
- Its docstring's justification is false. It claims "the same growth profile as the runtime-db :entries map", but :entries is per-frame, GC'd and dropped with the frame. Once an entry is gone, the slot is the ONLY root holding its pages. events.cljc:284 calls it "the frame-keyed memo"; it is keyed on key-id alone.
- A (key per frame, release on destroy) fixes only the SSR case.
  - A long-lived client's main frame never dies, so a free-text feed key (search-as-you-type) still pins its pages after GC.
  - The sub body is not handed its frame id: runtime-of/app-of in subs.cljc give only {:rf.db/app :rf.db/runtime}.
  - A+ adds releases at GC, remove, clear-scope and restore: four or more sites for a derivation cache.
- A weak map: the JVM's WeakHashMap keys by equality, so two resources with equal pages and different accessors would share a slot.
- C (subscribe :rf.resource/items over [:rf.resource/pages …]) is the idiomatic answer. But :infinite-state also flattens, so doing C properly restructures both subs, which is not warranted without a profile.

title: machines-lifecycle: an invalid inline :definition spawns a zombie actor; its validation error is swallowed and every event reports :rf.error/no-such-handler
description:
## Defect

An inline `:definition` spawn is never validated when it is spawned. `spawn-fx` builds and installs its snapshot without running `validate-machine!` (the parent's registration checks only the `:machine-id`/`:definition` XOR, not the inline spec itself). Validation first happens lazily, when the actor's first event makes the resolver build a handler: `resolve-actor-handler-meta` → `handler-meta-for` → `make-machine-handler` → `validate-machine!` throws. The router's resolver call sits in a catch-all that degrades any throw to nil (`router.cljc:531-535`), so the real registration error (`:rf.error/machine-unresolved-target`, `-unresolved-guard`, `-bad-shape` …) is discarded, and every event to the actor, starting with its own bootstrap `[:rf.machine.spawn/spawned]`, reports `:rf.error/no-such-handler` for an address whose snapshot is plainly installed. The actor is a zombie: live by Spec 005's liveness rule (snapshot present), `:rf/bootstrap-pending? true` forever, and unable to process anything. Under `:spawn-all` it can never reach `:final?`, so an `:all` join hangs silently. That is the hang the spec rejects fail-closed for the sibling unregistered-TYPE case (005:3211, 005:3984). The posture elsewhere is fail-loud at definition time; this path fails late, with the wrong diagnosis.

## Where

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:89-105` (`resolve-spawn-machine` returns a `:definition` verbatim) and `:1082-1283` (`spawn-fx*`): no call to `validate-machine!` / `make-machine-handler` on the accepted path.
- `lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:1409-1436` `handler-meta-for` and `:1438-1480` `resolve-actor-handler-meta`: validation runs here, per dispatch.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:531-535`: `(try (resolve! event frame) (catch … _ nil))` swallows it.
- Public entry: `[:rf.machine/spawn {:definition <spec>}]`, or a declarative `:spawn {:definition <spec>}` / `:spawn-all` child with an inline definition.

## Failure scenario

`{:fx [[:rf.machine/spawn {:definition {:initial :a :states {:a {:on {:x :nowhere}}}} :fixed-actor-id :pf/kid}]]}`, then `[:pf/kid [:x]]`. The snapshot is installed at `:a` with `:rf/bootstrap-pending? true`. Two `:rf.error/no-such-handler` errors fire (the bootstrap dispatch and `[:x]`). No `:rf.error/machine-unresolved-target` appears anywhere.

## Evidence

Executed with a bounded JVM probe (`probe_f.clj`, frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`):
- Invalid definition: `snapshot installed: true state: :a bootstrap-pending? true`; error ops `{:rf.error/no-such-handler 2}`; no machine event is ever received.
- CONTROL, the same spawn with a valid definition (`:x :b`): `state: :b`, no errors, `:rf.machine/started 1`, `:rf.machine/transition 2`.

`validate-machine!` has exactly one caller (`registration.cljc:904`). Tracker searched (`inline definition`, resolver swallow): no bead.

## Smallest fix

Validate an inline `:definition` once, at spawn time, and reject fail-closed like the unregistered-TYPE path: no install, and a loud error carrying the validator's `:rf.error/id`. For `:spawn-all`, fold it into the invoke-level preflight as a fourth admission condition, so the reject stays atomic. Running `make-machine-handler` there (inside `*in-registration-home?*`) also gives a place to cache the built handler, instead of re-validating on every dispatch. Fence: `lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc`, plus one test. No hot-zone file (005 §Errors may want one sentence; optional).

## Gates

`.cljc` shared code, no reader conditional: `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh` (`implementation/machines`) and `npm run test:cljs`.

## Decision needed

no
