title: pair-mcp: a :build or :frame string becomes an unchecked keyword spliced into eval source - any tool call runs arbitrary JVM (or browser) code past --no-eval
description:
## Defect

Caller-supplied id strings are turned into keywords with `re-frame.mcp-base.args/fresh-keyword`, which accepts any characters. Those keywords are then printed into generated source with `str` or `pr-str`. A keyword built from `"app (do ...) #_"` prints as `:app (do ...) #_`, which is live code rather than a literal. That gives two doors.

- **JVM.** Every tool's `:build` argument goes through `wire/arg-build`, then `fresh-keyword`, then `nrepl/cljs-eval`. There it is spliced with `str` into `(shadow.cljs.devtools.api/cljs-eval <build> "<code>" {})`, which is sent as an nREPL `eval` op. That form is evaluated as Clojure on the developer's shadow-cljs JVM. So any tool call, read-only ones included, runs arbitrary JVM code: filesystem, shell, network. No pair tool has that authority by design. `eval-cljs` reaches only the browser. The same splice is in `freshness/jvm-build-freshness`. `stick-build!` then makes the poisoned build the session's sticky default, so every later call without `:build` runs it again.
- **Browser.** Every `:frame` argument (`args/->frame-keyword` is `fresh-keyword`), and likewise view-ids, fx-override keys and slice keys, is emitted with `pr-str` by `ef/rt-call`. The first emission is `(re-frame2-pair.runtime/current-frame <frame>)` in `frame_resolve.cljs:72`. So a `:frame` string becomes arbitrary CLJS in the page.

Both doors work with `--no-eval` set, and both sit behind tools annotated read-only. The rf2-fzbj.6 repair quoted every EDN-parsed argument. It deliberately left "server-composed keywords" raw, and `handler_meta.cljs:283-286` states that premise ("`kind` and `frame` are server-coerced from closed sets"). But these keywords are not server-composed. They are minted from caller strings with no grammar check.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/args.cljc:188-208` (`normalise-keyword-string`: strips `:` and splits on the first `/`, nothing else) and `:263-294` (`fresh-keyword`: `(keyword ns name)` on any string).
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/wire.cljs:321`, `:334` and `:354` (`arg-build`, `requested-build`, `stick-build!`, each `(fresh-keyword (arg args :build))`).
- `nrepl.cljs:759-763`: `build-pr (if (keyword? build-id) (str build-id) ...)`, then `wrapped (str "(shadow.cljs.devtools.api/cljs-eval " build-pr " " code-pr " {})")`, then `jvm-eval`.
- `tools/freshness.cljs:112-116`: `bid (str build-id)` is spliced into `(... supervisor/get-worker sup " bid ")`.
- `tools/probe.cljs:552-612`: `match-running-build` / `canonicalize-build!` pass an unmatched or namespaced request through unchanged, so there is no allowlist in front of the sink.
- `tools/args.cljs:103-117` (`->frame-keyword`), `tools/frame_resolve.cljs:72`, and the other frame emitters (for example `record.cljs:265`, `watch_until.cljs:83`, `handler_meta.cljs:289`/`:445`, `operating_frame.cljs:126-130`).

Entry point: MCP `tools/call` of any tool carrying `:build`, for example `get-path`. For the browser door, any tool carrying `:frame`, for example `get-path` or `watch-epochs`.

## Failure scenario

1. The server is launched with `--no-eval`.
2. The agent calls `get-path {:path "[:x]" :build "app (do (clojure.java.shell/sh \"touch\" \"/tmp/pwned\") :app) #_"}`. The agent may be steered there by text it read out of the app, or it may be a malformed build id.
3. `canonicalize-build!` finds no running build of that name and passes it through. `ensure-runtime!` then calls `runtime-preloaded?`, which calls `cljs-eval-value`, which calls `cljs-eval`. That sends `(shadow.cljs.devtools.api/cljs-eval :app (do (clojure.java.shell/sh "touch" "/tmp/pwned") :app) #_ "(some? ...)" {})`.
4. The JVM evaluates the `do` form, which creates the file. `#_` discards the real code string, so the call stays well formed (three arguments) and nothing errors.
5. `stick-build!` has recorded the string as the sticky build, so the next plain `get-path` runs it again.

For the browser door, `get-path {:path "[:x]" :frame "rf/default (re-frame.core/dispatch-sync [:account/delete] {:frame :rf/default})"}` emits `(re-frame2-pair.runtime/current-frame :rf/default (re-frame.core/dispatch-sync ...))`, and the dispatch runs as the argument is evaluated.

## Evidence

**Executed**: a bounded, process-local JVM probe (`clojure -M`, run from the scratch dir, nothing written to the tree). It `load-file`s the frozen `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/args.cljc`, replicates `nrepl.cljs:759-763` verbatim, stubs shadow's 3-arity `cljs-eval`, and `load-string`s the wrapped form, as the JVM nREPL `eval` op would.

- Control, build arg `"app"`: wrapped `(shadow.cljs.devtools.api/cljs-eval :app "(some? ...)" {})`, `cljs-eval` saw `[:app "(some? ...)" {}]`, side-effect atom `:untouched`.
- Attack, build arg `"app (do (reset! probe/side-effect :RAN-ON-THE-JVM) :app) #_"`: `fresh-keyword` returned a real keyword (`keyword?` true) printing as `:app (do (reset! probe/side-effect :RAN-ON-THE-JVM) :app) #_`. `cljs-eval` saw `[:app :app {}]`, with no exception. The side-effect atom read `:RAN-ON-THE-JVM`.
- Frame door: `(pr-str (fresh-keyword "rf/default (swap! ...)"))` printed `:rf/default (swap! ...)`, and `read-string` of the emitted `(re-frame2-pair.runtime/current-frame ...)` reads back as a two-argument call containing the `swap!` form.

**Inspected**: the CLJS half. `ef/rt-call` emits a bare keyword argument with `pr-str`, per rf2-fzbj.6's own account ("Bare data goes through pr-str"). CLJS `Keyword` printing writes `:` plus its fqn unescaped, exactly as on the JVM. The route from `:build` to `jvm-eval` for a tool is `tools/invoke` (`tools.cljs:327`), then the canonicalize step (`tools.cljs:164-216`), then the tool's `wire/arg-build`, then `probe/ensure-runtime!`, then `runtime-preloaded?` (`probe.cljs:230-250`), then `nrepl/cljs-eval-value`.

Tracker: rf2-fzbj.6, rf2-j2wz and rf2-olqo (all closed) fixed EDN-parsed data arguments. rf2-fzbj.6's close reason explicitly left "server-composed keywords" raw, and the keywords here are not server-composed, so this is not a refile. There is no bead naming `fresh-keyword`, `arg-build` or `jvm-eval` injection. A search for `print-is-not-quotation` finds rf2-j2wz and rf2-olqo, so that search can find hits. The mcp-base review (rf2-3x7nj.35) was still in progress when this was filed and owns `fresh-keyword` itself. This bead is the pair-mcp sink.

## Smallest fix

Validate id shape before minting. Route `arg-build`/`requested-build`/`stick-build!` and `->frame-keyword` (and the other caller-string keyword coercions in `tools/args.cljs`) through the existing `re-frame.mcp-base.args/fresh-keyword-checked` (`args.cljc:305-341`), with a keyword-character grammar for each part (for example `[A-Za-z0-9*+!_?<>=.-]+`, where a namespace segment may also contain `.`). On failure, return the tool's normal structured `:invalid-arg` refusal. As a belt-and-braces measure at the one JVM sink, `nrepl/cljs-eval` could also refuse a build-id whose printed form does not read back as a single keyword. Fence: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/{wire,args}.cljs`, `nrepl.cljs`, `tools/freshness.cljs`, plus tests. No hot-zone file. Do not quote keywords with `rt-quote`: `(quote <pr-str kw>)` breaks out the same way.

## Gates

`npm test` in `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp` (CLJS only; no JVM lane compiles these files). If `fresh-keyword-checked`'s grammar helper lands in mcp-base, add that artefact's JVM tests (`clojure -M:test` in `tools/mcp-base`).

## Decision needed

No. The one judgement is the id grammar, and shadow build ids and frame ids are ordinary keywords, so the standard keyword character set fits.

title: machines-viz: the :spawn :on-error parent transition is drawn by no emitter - chart, Mermaid and SCXML show its target unreachable
description:
## Defect

A `:spawn` map's `:on-error` is a real parent transition. Spec 005 calls it "an `:on`-shaped **transition** spec ... The parent moves to the transition's `:target`", and the engine resolves it in `pick-spawn-error-transition`. None of the three machines-viz emitters draws it. The chart's parse, Mermaid's edge collector and the SCXML exporter each walk `:on`, `:after`, `:always` and `:on-done` only. So a machine that uses the documented "child failed, so leave the spawning state" pattern charts the spawning state as a dead end, and the `:on-error` target as an unreachable node. The tool reads the slot, though: the shared grammar gate already validates the `:spawn :on-error` target (grammar.cljc:781). The chart therefore disagrees with the machine the engine runs. SCXML also drops `:spawn`, `:entry` and `:exit` altogether, while its docs list only `:spawn-all` as omitted and say that entry/exit names "are preserved as XML comments", which the emitter never does.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/layout.cljc:336-419`: `collect-state-edges` collects only `:on` / `:after` / `:always` / `:on-done`. `project-definition` (:1342) reaches it, and `MachineChart` calls that.
- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/mermaid.cljc:499-523`: `collect-edges` walks the same four slots. Reached from `mermaid/emit` (:946) and Xray's Copy Mermaid.
- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/scxml.cljc:568-623`: `emit-state` destructures `on after always on-done` only. Reached from `scxml/spec->scxml` (:809).
- It is validated but never drawn: `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/grammar.cljc:781`.
- The contract: `spec/005-StateMachines.md:3001` (the spawn-spec `:on-error` row) and :3337-3339. The engine: `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:1346` (`pick-spawn-error-transition`).
- The docs claims that are false: `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:2378-2381` and `scxml.cljc:127-129` (entry/exit names "preserved as XML comments"). The "Not supported" lists at API.md:2352 and scxml.cljc:88 name only `:spawn-all`.

## Failure scenario

```clojure
{:initial :idle
 :states {:idle    {:on {:go :working}}
          :working {:spawn {:machine-id :child :on-error :failed}}
          :failed  {:final? true}}}
```
- `grammar/valid-definition?` returns true.
- `layout/project-definition` projects exactly one edge, `[:idle] -> [:working] :go`. `:failed` renders with no incoming edge.
- `mermaid/emit` produces `idle --> working : go` and `failed --> [*]`, with no `working --> failed`.
- `spec->scxml` emits `<state id="working"/>`, and `scxml->spec` of that returns `:working {}`. The spawn, and with it the only way out of `:working`, is gone.

The engine meanwhile moves `:working -> :failed` when the child fails. Because no edge exists, a host also cannot highlight that fired transition.

## Evidence

Executed with bounded process-local JVM probes against the frozen tree (a scratch `deps.edn` using `:local/root`, so nothing was written into the tree). The probe was `p2.clj`, which printed "chart edges: [:idle] -> [:working] :go" and the Mermaid body above. `p1.clj` gave the SCXML round trip `{:working {} ...}` (`equal? false`), and it also showed a `:spawn {:machine-id :child :on-done :done :on-error :failed}` plus `:entry :log-in` / `:exit :log-out` state exporting as a bare `<state id="working"/>`, with no comment. Control: the same probe's `:go` edge is projected, so the collector runs. Tracker: `bd search` and the export found no bead on drawing `:spawn :on-error`. API.md:976-987 does rule out a "spawn edge" to the spawned child, but that is the child-actor affordance, not this parent transition.

## Smallest fix

Treat `(get-in node [:spawn :on-error])` as one more trigger slot, resolved at the spawning state's own level like `:on-done`:
- chart: an `:on-error?` edge with event `:rf.machine.spawn/error`, drawn through `transition-edge` in `collect-state-edges`;
- Mermaid: a `working --> failed : ✗ error` edge in `collect-edges`;
- SCXML: either emit an `error.<id>`-style transition or list `:spawn` / `:on-error` / `:entry` / `:exit` as dropped.

Also correct the "names preserved as XML comments" sentence in API.md and scxml.cljc. Fence: `chart/layout.cljc`, `chart/projection.cljc` (event-variant chip), `mermaid.cljc`, `scxml.cljc`, `spec/API.md`, plus their tests. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`tools/machines-viz`: `clojure -M:test` (JVM, `.cljc` corpus: `chart/projection_cljs_test.cljc`, `mermaid_cljs_test.cljc`, `scxml_cljs_test.cljc`, `cross_emitter_agreement_cljs_test.cljc`). An event-node chip for the new variant lives in `chart/nodes/event_node.cljs`, which only the CLJS lane grades (the `:machines-viz-node-test` build / `npm run test:cljs`).

## Decision needed

No. The only choice is SCXML's spelling (a synthetic `error.<state>` event versus documenting the drop), and either is fine.
notes:
== WORKER VERDICT 2026-09-24 (worker/mviz-3x7nj, PR #10312) — FIXED; SCXML took the documented-drop spelling ==

Reproduced at trunk b3fb23a6c4 (no machines-viz commit since the review tree 034d0c8fc8): the bead's machine charted one edge, [:idle] -> [:working] :go, and Mermaid had no working --> failed.

Chart: collect-state-edges projects (get-in node [:spawn :on-error]) through transition-edge as {:event :rf.machine.spawn/error :on-error? true}, resolved with the spawning state's own resolve-target-path (keyword target = sibling), which matches the engine's pick-spawn-error-transition decl-path (the invoke-id = the spawning state's path). An action-only :on-error self-anchors :internal? like every other trigger. layout/event-segment labels it "✗ error". projection/event-variant returns :on-error (event-node :variant "on-error"), and fireable? excludes it, since :rf.machine.spawn/error is engine-raised. event_node.cljs needed no change: its variant-glyph falls through to :eventLabel for any variant other than :after / :always.

Reason: an emitted transition would have to be special-cased by the importer, or it imports as a bogus :on event, and it still could not rebuild the :spawn map (no :machine-id carried); the drop is smaller and leaves the 33.5 importer untouched. The export of the bead's machine still reads back through our importer as :working {}.

Note: :spawn :on-done is a data-update CALLBACK (Spec 005 spawn-spec keys), not a transition, so there is no edge to draw for it.

title: spec/009: the large-elision passage promises a get-path index-range read, a handle-passing fetch and digests-off for MCP servers - none matches the code or spec 015 (hot zone, wording only)
description:
Discovered from rf2-ealv5 (ruled 2026-09-24: a `:large` declaration governs its whole subtree; raw content only through the per-call size override `elision false`, which pair-MCP will honour on every launch). Three sentences in spec/009-Instrumentation.md's large-elision passage describe a get-path drill route that does not exist. HOT ZONE (`spec/009-Instrumentation.md`): sequence after rf2-fc84b's 009 edit merges, and after any other in-flight 009 edit.

## What is wrong (verified at trunk a61f903c5c)

1. :3021 (marker `:type`): "a `:vector` is paginatable via `get-path` with an index range". No index-range read exists: pair-MCP `get-path` is plain `get-in` in both its singular and batch forms (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/get_path.cljs), `parse-path-arg` has no range syntax, and a range-shaped path `[:rows [0 2]]` reads as a missing key (JVM-measured under rf2-ealv5). A repo-wide search for `index.range` finds only this line on the subject.
2. :3024 (marker `:handle`): "Passing the handle to the existing re-frame2-pair-mcp `get-path` tool fetches the literal elided value", plus an `[:rf.elision/at <path> :as-of-epoch <epoch-id>]` form. `get-path` parses no handle (`[:rf.elision/at ...]` would be read as a literal path; pair-MCP code carries `rf.elision/at` only inside descriptor strings and `as-of-epoch` 0 times), and passing the handle's inner PATH returns the same marker again unless the call passes `elision false`.
3. :3041: the re-frame2-pair-mcp / Xray-MCP / story-mcp servers "MUST default `:rf.egress/include-digests?` to `false`". Those servers use `:rf.egress/off-box-tool`, which resolves `include-digests? true` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc `profile->size-opts`), and spec/015-Data-Classification.md :264 says off-box-tool includes "structural indicators / digests so the tool can reason about shape without seeing content". 015 and the code agree; the MCP-server clause of :3041 is stale (the Sentry / Honeybadger forwarders use `:rf.egress/off-box-observability`, digests false, and are correct).

## Smallest fix

Rewrite :3021, e.g. "a `:vector`'s elements are addressable by index through `get-path` (the batch `paths` form reads several at once); at or below a `:large` declaration they elide too unless the call passes the size override `elision false`; a 5 MB `:string` cannot be subdivided." Rewrite the :3024 fetch sentence to name the real route (re-call `get-path` on the marker's `:path` with `elision false`) and either drop the `:as-of-epoch` handle form or mark it unimplemented. Narrow :3041's MUST to the observability forwarders and point the MCP servers at the 015 §10 off-box-tool row. No code change.

## Gates

Prose in a hot-zone spec page. `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `mkdocs build --strict` (which stages `spec/`) cover link targets and site resolution only; nothing checks the prose, so verify the three sentences by hand and say so in the PR body.

## Decision needed

No. rf2-ealv5's ruling fixes the behaviour these sentences must describe; item 3 follows spec 015 and the code, which already agree.

- Item 2 (spec 009:3024, the handle / `:as-of-epoch` form) depends on rf2-3x7nj.32.5. The dossier recommends option (b): stop promising epoch-resolvable handles. Under (b) this item should DROP the `:as-of-epoch` handle form, and also correct 009:3063 and Spec-Schemas.md:3659, which carry the same promise. The marker schema at Spec-Schemas.md:3647 accepts only a two-element handle.

title: xray-epoch-panel: a :halted-depth epoch record renders as a clean cascade — HANDLER 'returned no :db', panel outcome :ok — for an event that never ran
description:
## Defect

The Epoch panel never reads an epoch record's framework `:outcome` or `:halt-reason`, so a `:halted-depth` record (the drain hit its depth limit and the halting event NEVER RAN) is projected exactly like an ordinary event: a DISPATCH step, a RECORDABLE COEFFECTS step, and an EVENT HANDLER step whose body says "— no :db (handler returned no :db)", with the panel outcome `:ok` and no card anywhere. In a runaway dispatch loop — the moment a programmer most needs Xray — the head epoch (which head-fallback shows by default) tells them the looping event ran cleanly and wrote nothing. The same blindness applies to `:halted-destroy` partial records. The record carries everything needed to say otherwise: `:outcome :halted-depth` and `:halt-reason {:operation :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded :depth .. :queue-size ..}`.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc:4113-4422` — `project` reads only `:trace-events`, `:db-before`, `:event-id`; it always emits `handler-row` (`:4379`) and never consults `(:outcome epoch-record)` / `:halt-reason`. The existing skip machinery (`handler-skipped-by-upstream?` / `mark-skipped-handler`, `:3580-3612`) keys only on coeffect / `:before`-interceptor throws.
- `projection.cljc:3946-3966` — `epoch-outcome` scans only attached step errors/violations, so it answers `:ok`.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs:4254-4257` — the "— no :db (handler returned no :db)" placeholder the halted HANDLER step renders; `view.cljs:1744-1752` — `skipped-body`, whose wording ("an upstream step threw") would also be wrong for a halt.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch_panel.cljs:357` — `:outcome (proj/epoch-outcome steps)`, the panel's only outcome.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/shared/focus_resolver.cljc:157-164` — head-fallback: with focus unset the panel shows the newest record, which after a runaway IS the halted one.
- Producer: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:3325-3330` ("The halting event never ran ... its buffer is empty"), `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:400-431` (`commit-halt-record!`) and `:288-294` (pins `:event-id` / `:trigger-event` from the halting event).

Entry point: the Epoch L4 tab (`:rf.xray/epoch-pipeline` sub → `proj/project-numbered`).

## Failure scenario

`(rf/reg-event ::loop (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (update db :n (fnil inc 0)) :fx [[:dispatch [::loop]]]}))`, `(rf/dispatch-sync [::loop])`. The drain halts at depth 100 and commits a `:halted-depth` record for the 101st `[::loop]`, which never ran. Open Xray's Epoch tab (focus unset → head): DISPATCH `[:user/loop]`, EVENT HANDLER `reg-event` with "— no :db (handler returned no :db)", `data-rf-xray-outcome="ok"`. Nothing says the event was refused by the depth limit.

## Evidence

EXECUTED (bounded JVM probe from the scratch dir against the frozen tree's `tools/xray` as a `:local/root`, no writes into the tree; `probe1.clj` section P3):

```
history count 50
head :outcome :halted-depth  :event-id :user/loop  :trigger-event [:user/loop]
head :halt-reason operation :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded
head trace ops [:rf.event/dispatched]
projected steps [step status flavour db-write?]: [[:dispatch nil nil nil] [:recordable-cofx nil nil nil] [:handler nil :db-only false]]
step-status per step: [:ok :ok :ok]
epoch-outcome (the panel's outcome): :ok
```

So the HANDLER step is present, not `:skipped`, `:db-write? false` (→ the "returned no :db" placeholder, inspected at view.cljs:4254), and the panel outcome is `:ok`. Control: the prior record (a genuinely-run `::loop`) reads `:outcome :ok`, so the probe distinguishes the two. Census: `:halt-reason` / `(:outcome epoch-record)` / `halted` read 0 times across projection.cljc, view.cljs and epoch_panel.cljs (the one `halt` hit is a docstring at projection.cljc:3958); control `:trace-events epoch-record` reads 2 in projection.cljc. Spec: `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §9.1.10.5 deliberately does NOT surface the framework `:outcome` for the recovered-handler-exception case (the record says `:ok` there) — that ruling is about `:ok` records and does not cover a record whose framework outcome is non-`:ok`; searched closed beads (`halted-depth`, `epoch panel`, rf2-y8doi.6 / .19) — no ruling on halt display.

## Smallest fix

In `project`, when `(:outcome epoch-record)` is non-`:ok`, stamp the HANDLER (and any SIDE EFFECTS) step `:status :skipped` and attach one card built from `:halt-reason`'s `:operation` / `:depth` / `:queue-size` to the DISPATCH step (reuse the existing skipped + card machinery; do NOT render `:halt-reason :last-event` — its raw args are the privacy leak rf2-3x7nj.17.1 already tracks); have `epoch-outcome` (or the sub) read `:error` for it; give `skipped-body` a halt wording. Fence: `panels/epoch/projection.cljc`, `panels/epoch/view.cljs`, `panels/epoch_panel.cljs`, `test/.../panels/epoch/projection_cljs_test.cljc`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

Projection change: JVM lane from `tools/xray` (`clojure -M:test`, which runs `projection_cljs_test.cljc`) and the node lane. The view wording is CLJS-only: `npm run test:cljs` (the `view_cljs_test.cljs` node-lane namespace).

## Decision needed

No.

title: examples-real-apps: a settings save that succeeds after the reader has left /settings still navigates them to their profile (both twins) — the one navigating write left outside the apps' 'a navigation is the route's' law
description:
## Defect

In BOTH RealWorld twins, a successful settings save navigates to the saver's profile with NO check that the reader is still on `/settings`. Nothing blocks leaving `/settings` mid-save: the route has no `:can-leave`. So this sequence yanks the reader off the page they chose:

1. Click Update Settings.
2. Walk to an article, the home feed or the editor while the PUT is in flight.
3. The reply lands and the reader is dragged to `/profile/<me>`.

When step 2 is the editor with a draft, the yank also runs the editor's `:can-leave` confirm dialog on a navigation the reader never asked for.

The apps teach the opposite law, and fixed exactly this for the other writes:

- `realworld_http/comments.cljs:104-122` (TWO QUESTIONS): "a NAVIGATION is the ROUTE's". A settle whose outcome is a navigation must ask whether the committed route is still the page that issued it, "because leaving ... for a NON-ARTICLE page ... exposes it, and a slug-only gate took that reader home just as an ungated one did". `article-route-for-slug?` (`:159-172`) is that gate.
- `realworld_resources/article_editor.cljs:385-403` (WRITE OWNERSHIP): a save can "answer after the reader has moved on to a profile, or anywhere else". Its continuation "acts only while the navigation that issued it is still the current one" (nav-token gate, `:479`). rf2-gwye.39 bound the editor write replies to their page, and rf2-fzbj.21 did the same for stale article-write continuations.

Settings is the one navigating write left ungated. Its owner check (rf2-2ape, rf2-0aub0, rf2-ktkhn, rf2-bq1fy) answers "whose SESSION is this?" and never "whose ROUTE is this?". That is the exact pairing the TWO QUESTIONS passage says not to conflate.

## Where

- `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/settings.cljs:637-705`, `:settings/submit-success`. The `:else` branch at `:689-705` dispatches `[:rf.route/navigate {:to :realworld.profile/show ...}]` at `:705`, with no route predicate.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/settings.cljs:183-230`, `:settings/replied`. The `:ok` branch at `:215-225` navigates at `:225` once the session-owner check (`:209`) passes.
- Routes: `realworld_http/routing.cljs:75-79` and `realworld_resources/routing.cljs:143-149`. `:realworld.user/settings` has `:on-match`, `:can-enter` and `:requires-auth`, and no `:can-leave`.

## Failure scenario

INSPECTED ONLY. The views and handlers are `.cljs`, and this review may not run shadow-cljs or a browser. Trace, in live-API mode or any backend slower than a click:

1. Signed in as alice, open `/settings`, edit the bio and click Update. The PUT `/user` is in flight.
2. Click Home (a `route-link`). The settings route has no `:can-leave`, so `/` commits and home renders.
3. The reply arrives.
   - http: `claims-outstanding` is 1, `awaited` matches, and `owns-session?` is true, so the handler reaches `:else`.
   - resources: `owns-session?` is true and the status is `:ok`.
4. Both dispatch `:rf.route/navigate` to `/profile/alice`. The reader, now on Home, is moved to alice's profile unasked.

If step 2 went to `/editor` and the reader typed a draft, the navigate hits `:editor/can-leave?` and pops the "are you sure?" dialog for a navigation the reader did not start.

Control: the same sequence through the editor's Publish (`article_editor.cljs:473-479`) is refused by the nav-token gate. Through the article page's Delete (`comments.cljs:668-685`), `article-route-for-slug?` refuses it.

## Evidence

- Both handlers read in full, and neither body reads `:rf.runtime/routing`. Every guard in them concerns the save ledger or the session owner.
- The session store in the same branch is correct and should stay: the session is the account's, wherever the reader is.
- Tracker: a full-text search for `settings/(replied|submit-success)` combined with `navigat` finds only rf2-ktkhn, rf2-0aub0, rf2-bq1fy and rf2-2ape. All four are session or ledger ownership, and none is about the navigation after the reader leaves.

## Smallest fix

Keep the session store, persist, ledger retire and `:submit-succeeded`. Make ONLY the navigate conditional on the committed route still being `:realworld.user/settings`, read from the `:rf.db/runtime` coeffect the way `article-route-for-slug?` does.

Do NOT carry a nav-token as a positional `:reply-to` or `:on-success` argument, as the editor does. Both settings files explain why (`realworld_resources/settings.cljs:168-176`, `realworld_http/settings.cljs` SESSION OWNERSHIP): a positional arg moves the reply off `(second event)`, and `:sensitive [[:value :user :token]]` would stop reaching the fresh JWT.

If "left and came back" should also be refused, record the issuing nav-token in the slot the owner already lives in:
- resources: beside `:settings-save-owner`;
- http: the machine's `:data` at `:begin-submit`.

Two files, `realworld_http/settings.cljs` and `realworld_resources/settings.cljs`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

- `npm run test:cljs`. The node lane loads both apps' settings namespaces through `realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs` and `realworld_cljs_test.cljs` (adapters/reagent/test), and existing settings-ownership tests there must stay green.
- CI's `cljs-examples-compile` sweep.

Examples are test-free (rf2-8cevm). Any pin of the route gate belongs in those framework-tree files, not under `examples/`.

## Decision needed

No, if the TWO QUESTIONS law is taken as settled: it is written into both apps and was enforced for the editor under rf2-gwye.39. Yes only if the navigation after a settings save is meant to win over the reader's own later navigation. Then the fix is a sentence saying so, and the TWO QUESTIONS passage needs an exception.
notes:
## WORKER VERDICT: FIXED in PR #10316 (commit 3064bc4936 on worker/realworld-3x7nj), 2026-09-24 08:23 AUSEST

The TWO QUESTIONS law was taken as settled, as the brief directed, so no design choice was made. The premise was re-verified at trunk `51fe95a7fb`. Neither twin's success handler read the route.

### Fix (smallest)

Both `:settings/replied` (resources) and `:settings/submit-success` (http) keep the session store, persist, ledger retire and form settle unchanged. ONLY the navigate is conditional, on `settings-route-current?`: the committed route read from the `:rf.db/runtime` coeffect is `:realworld.user/settings`. That is the same read `article-route-for-slug?` makes.

No nav-token is threaded. A positional arg would move the reply off `(second event)`, which is the files' own warning. The existing detour test pins that "left and came back" still navigates.

### Framework tests (fence widening granted by the coordinator)

Tests that asserted the profile navigation had never entered /settings; they dispatched `:settings/load` directly. They now open it by the real route (`[:rf.route/navigate {:to :realworld.user/settings}]`, whose `:on-match` is `[:settings/load]`):
- resources: `update-settings-mutation-folds-user-into-auth-and-navigates`, and the detour test's come-back step.
- http: `park-a-settings-save!` and `park-a-settings-rename!`.

Two further http edits follow from that:
- `logout-scrubbing-the-settings-snapshot!` now also takes the logout action's navigation home. Without it, the next account's Settings visit is a same-route re-entry, `:on-match` does not re-fire, and the draft is not seeded from that account.
- two `(nil? route-id)` assertions in `settings-occupied-name-rename-stale-success-test` now read `:realworld.user/settings`. Its no-navigation assertion is therefore discriminating again: the route gate would allow the navigate, so the ownership refusal is what stops it.

All of these are CLJS, and CI grades them.

### Control

A JVM probe (bb), deleted afterwards. It lifted each twin's SHIPPED handler, plus the route predicate where defined, out of the source. The session and ledger helpers were stubbed to say "your save, your session". It then read whether `:fx` navigates with the committed route at /settings, at Home, and at /editor.
- Before the fix: both twins navigated from all three routes.
- After the fix: both navigate from /settings only. The session store and the persist are kept (3 fx on /settings).
- Sabotage: `(settings-route-current? rt)` was planted to `true` (match count 1 per file). Both twins navigated from Home and /editor again. The restores were verified by the default-form blob hashes equal to the committed blobs: resources `577f899f71`, http `3de44ec68d`.
Merged-PR audit #10316 (423809164fa372d16aa3144a59baf41ba58f615b; merged 2026-09-23T23:33:22Z). Completeness: The four scoped example fixes land: correct token path, pagination nesting, route-gated settings navigation in both twins and resources draft reset. The acknowledged HTTP-twin principal crossing has an exact in_progress Bead, which cannot be reused under the open-only instruction; a separate open audit finding points to that existing work. Correctness: Read all five changed example files and framework test adjustments. Accepted shipped-form probes/negative controls, CI node 12668/63846 and 58 example builds. Route-id rather than nav-token gating and same-slug draft retention match the chosen scope. Implementation quality: Small changes follow the existing twin patterns and keep examples free of test infrastructure. The HTTP follow-up needs only session-boundary cleanup, not a new draft storage abstraction. Actionable findings: rf2-qtbeb. Existing finding updates: none.

title: story-authoring-data: canonicalize keeps :error-trace and the raw thrown exception, so every fx-error run reads :non-deterministic and golden-match? fails against its own artifact
description:
## Defect

The determinism strip in `re-frame.story.fingerprint` does not normalize two per-run values that every fx-error epoch carries:
- **`:error-trace`** on an `:effects` row. It is the trace-event `:id` of the `:rf.error/fx-handler-exception` (or `:rf.error/no-such-fx`) trace, drawn from the same PROCESS-GLOBAL trace counter the strip already removes as `:trace-id`.
- **The raw thrown exception object** the epoch record carries. It compares by identity, so it is never `=` across two replays.

The consequence is that two replays of the SAME program never canonicalize equal whenever an effect handler throws or an fx id is unregistered. That is precisely the run a fault sweep or a property falsification produces. Three things follow:
- `assert-deterministic` reports `:non-deterministic` for a perfectly reproducible failing artifact;
- `golden-match?` is `false` against the very artifact the golden was captured from;
- `diff-run-artifacts` shows a spurious divergence.

The strip's own docstring says it exists so "two semantically-equal runs canonicalize `=` and hash equal". It misses this pair.

## Where

All cites are at `034d0c8fc8`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/fingerprint.cljc:96-141` is `volatile-fields`, the recursive strip set: `#{:elapsed-ms :dispatch-id :source :source-coord :runner :variant/id :plan-hash :run-hash :epoch-id :trace-id :committed-at :schema-digest}`. There is no `:error-trace`. `strip-run-stamps` at `:374` and `canonicalize` at `:810` carry no throwable projection.
- Producer: `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/capture.cljc:647-660`, where the `:effects` rows for fx-handler-exception and no-such-fx carry `:error-trace (:id trace-event)`.
- Consumers:
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/determinism.cljc:151-205` (`compare-runs`) and `:217-284` (`assert-deterministic`; `:fail` runs are compared, not short-circuited);
  - `golden.cljc:335` (`golden-match?`);
  - `diff.cljc:655` (`diff-run-artifacts`).
- Public entry points:
  - `re-frame.story/assert-deterministic` (`story.cljc:1210`);
  - `golden-match?` (`:1336`);
  - `diff-run-artifacts` (`:1299`).
- Contract: `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md:3535` §Canonicalization MUST strip / normalize the per-run stamps, which lists "runtime object identities — `:epoch-id` / `:trace-id` … the trace event's `:id`".

## Failure scenario

`(rf/reg-fx :probe.fx/boom {:platforms #{:client :server}} (fn [_ _] (throw (ex-info "boom" {:k 1}))))` and `(rf/reg-event :probe/boom (fn [_ _] {:fx [[:probe.fx/boom {}]]}))`. Then:
- `(story/assert-deterministic {:event-program [[:dispatch [:probe/boom]]]})` returns `:non-deterministic`, with both replays `:fail`.
- `(story/golden-match? (story/capture-golden art) art)` on that artifact returns `false`.

The consequence is that a generated failure's artifact, the one thing `check-property!` exists to hand over, cannot pass the determinism gate or be pinned as a golden. The gate reads as "flaky" on a deterministic bug.

## Evidence

All of this was EXECUTED: one-shot JVM scripts through `clojure.main`, on the `tools/story` `:test` classpath, in the frozen tree (scratch `probe4`, `probe5` and `probe6`, `.clj` / `.out`).
- E0 control: `assert-deterministic` on a plain `:probe/inc` program gives `:deterministic`.
- E1: the throwing-fx program gives `:non-deterministic [:fail :fail]`. Per-key canonical comparison of the two results differs in exactly `:epoch-tape` and `:effects`:
  - the `:effects` difference is a lone integer, `98` vs `107`;
  - the `:epoch-tape` difference is that integer plus the `#error {:cause "boom" …}` object.
- F1: the replay `:effects` row is `{:fx-id :probe.fx/boom, :args {}, :outcome :error, :error-trace 76, :epoch-id 1}`. `:epoch-id` is stripped and `:error-trace` is not.
- G1 `golden-match?` on the same failing artifact gives `false`. The G2 control on a passing artifact gives `true`.

No tracker duplicate. `bd search` for `:error-trace` together with canonical, determinism and run-hash finds nothing.

Slice note: `fingerprint.cljc` is in the story-execution slice's file list. This is filed here because the failure is reached through this slice's determinism gate (`determinism.cljc`). The sibling rf2-3x7nj.30.4 is the OPPOSITE defect in the same set: `volatile-fields` strips app keys (`:source`, `:elapsed-ms`, `:runner`) at every depth. This bead is the under-strip. Both edit `volatile-fields` / `project`, so sequence them or land them in one change.

## Smallest fix

In `fingerprint.cljc`:
- add `:error-trace` to the per-run stamp strip. It is a trace-counter pointer like `:trace-id`, reserved and framework-specific;
- project a throwable in `canonical-form` to data (`ex-message` plus `ex-data`, and the class/`name` on the JVM or CLJS) instead of carrying the object.

Pin both in `determinism_test.cljc` with a throwing-fx program expected to read `:deterministic`, and in `golden_test.cljc` with a failing artifact matching its own golden.

Fence: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/fingerprint.cljc` plus those two tests. Moving canonical form changes `run-hash` and golden `:canonical` values, so check whether `canonical-version` wants a bump (the file's own §Snapshot-identity migration note governs; `content-hash` is untouched if the change sits on the strip path only). No hot-zone file is touched.

## Gates

- JVM: `clojure -M:test` in `tools/story`.
- The throwable projection needs a CLJS arm (`js/Error`), which lives in a `#?(:cljs …)` branch graded only by `npm run test:cljs`. A JVM green says nothing about it.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
== WORKER VERDICT (2026-09-24 10:00 AUSEST): FIXED in PR #10321 (branch worker/story-art-3x7nj), awaiting review/merge. Not closed.

Reproduced at trunk 423809164f: assert-deterministic on a program whose fx throws read :non-deterministic (both runs :fail); each effect row carried :error-trace <n> (a per-run trace id); the raw exception object sat in the epoch tape at [:epoch-tape 0 :trace-events 2 :tags :exception]; golden-match? of a failing artifact against its own replay was false.

Fix (fingerprint.cljc):
- strip-run-stamps drops :error-trace STRUCTURALLY from an effect row (:fx-id + :outcome) rather than recursively, so an app key named :error-trace stays semantic (consistent with rf2-3x7nj.30.4's principle; a test pins it).
- project turns a thrown value (JVM Throwable; CLJS ExceptionInfo or js/Error) into data: {:rf/throwable <"ex-info" | class/name> :message ... :data (ex-data, when present) :cause (recursive)}. A different message or ex-data still hashes differently.

canonical-version decision: NOT bumped; stays :rf/snapshot-canonical-v2. The change is on the strip path only (canonicalize / canonical-hash / run-hash / plan-hash); content-hash (snapshot identity) is untouched. Precedent: rf2-luzky's :rf.fx/elapsed-ms strip and the :rf.cofx strip both landed on v2. An existing golden can only mismatch where the stripped keys are involved, so no silent false match either way. 017 §Canonicalization now states that a strip revision does not bump the version.

Regressions: determinism_test gate-throwing-fx-program-is-deterministic; golden_test golden-of-a-failing-artifact-matches-its-own-replay; story_fingerprint_test fx-error-stamps-canonicalize-equal (message/data sensitivity; :error-trace in app-db not stripped); story_fingerprint_cljs_test fx-error-stamps-canonicalize-equal-on-cljs (ex-info and js/Error pairs) - that one is node-lane, graded by CI only (the shadow-cljs lane was not granted locally).

Control: effect-row strip -> identity and throwable branch -> false -> exit 1, 5 failures; each half alone also red (3 failures each). Restore verified by git hash-object == committed blob.
Merged-PR audit #10321 (982fb2ce41a7163eab03e24255f5ac7967aa6f6a; merged 2026-09-24T00:20:00Z). Completeness: Reviewed all four claims and ruling B. Replay now executes dispatchable assertions and refuses headless actions, but tape-evaluated schema/causal checkpoints still skip; separately tracked open. Normalized-plan determinism/golden refusal and explicit artifact coercion limits match the ruling. Correctness: Accepted author Story 2075 tests/7792 assertions, Story-MCP 306/1781, negative controls and CI. Source traced replay-result, exec-step!, assertion matchers and evidence projection to establish the residual; no redundant suite run. Throwable/error-trace normalization and semantic app keys checked. Implementation quality: Reuses existing runner and structural fingerprint carriers. Correction should reuse existing boundary matchers; no second executor or broader redesign required. Actionable findings: rf2-0viz4. Existing finding updates: none.

title: story-execution: canonicalize strips :source / :elapsed-ms / :runner at every depth, so golden, diff-runs, determinism, run-hash and plan-hash are blind to app-db and args under those keys (017 safety claim spec-stale)
description:
## Defect

`fingerprint/project` drops every key in `volatile-fields` at ANY depth. That set is `#{:elapsed-ms :dispatch-id :source :source-coord :runner :variant/id :plan-hash :run-hash :epoch-id :trace-id :committed-at :schema-digest}`, and `project` also rewrites `:variant-id` to `:variant/id`. The strip is applied to app data as well as Story's own metadata, so every consumer of `canonicalize` is blind to a change in a user's app-db, or in a variant's args, db-seed or network replies, under any of those keys. The consumers are golden slices, `diff-runs`, the determinism gate, `:run-hash` and `:plan-hash`. `:source` (a feed or data source, an image source) and `:elapsed-ms` (any timer or stopwatch app) are ordinary domain keys. A golden therefore reports MATCH, and a diff `:same? true`, on a real regression in that state.

The code's own reasoning already rules this out for `:id`, `:time` and `:frame`, which it strips only STRUCTURALLY because "stripping them globally would erase semantic app-db data" (`fingerprint.cljc:126-132`). The same argument applies to `:source`, `:elapsed-ms` and `:runner`. Spec 017 carries the other half of the error: it calls those three "reserved / framework-specific keys" that are safe to strip recursively (017:3576-3579), which is spec-stale.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/fingerprint.cljc`:
  - 139-141, `volatile-fields`;
  - 176-208, `project` (recursive strip plus the `:variant-id` reconcile);
  - 810-835, `canonicalize`;
  - 910-925 / 944-959, the `plan-hash` / `run-hash` input keys, which include `:world` / `:app-db`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/golden.cljc:116-126` (`slice-canonical`) and 318-333 (`matches?`).
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/diff.cljc:501-512` (`strip-noise`) and 567-635 (`diff-runs`).
- `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md:2651-2653` (the set) and 3576-3579 (the safety claim).
- Public entry points: `story/capture-golden` / `golden-match?` / `compare-golden`, `story/diff-runs`, `test/assert-deterministic`, and the `:run-hash` / `:plan-hash` on every run-result.

## Failure scenario

A stopwatch variant's golden is captured with `{:timer {:elapsed-ms 1000}}`. A regression makes the handler write 9999. `golden-match?` is true, `diff-runs` reports `{:same? true}`, and `run-hash` is unchanged. The same happens for `{:feed {:source "rss"}}` becoming `"atom"`, and for `{:race {:runner "alice"}}` becoming `"bob"`. Two variants that differ only in `:args {:source "a"}` versus `{:source "b"}`, or in a `:db-seed` value keyed `:source`, get the SAME `:plan-hash`.

## Evidence

EXECUTED. A process-local JVM probe (`:local/root` on the frozen tree) built run-results that differ only at one app-db path. For each pair it compared `run-hash`, `canonicalize`, `golden-match?` against `make-golden` of the base, and `(:same? (diff-runs …))`:

- CONTROL `[:app-db :src]` "rss" to "atom": run-hash equal false, canonical equal false, golden-match false, diff same false.
- CONTROL `[:app-db :feed :n]` 1 to 2: all four report a difference.
- `[:app-db :feed :source]` "rss" to "atom": run-hash equal true, canonical equal true, golden-match TRUE, diff same TRUE.
- `[:app-db :timer :elapsed-ms]` 1000 to 9999: the same, all blind.
- `[:app-db :race :runner]` "alice" to "bob": the same, all blind.
- `plan-hash` of inline plans:
  - `{:args {:src "a"}}` against `{:args {:src "b"}}` differ (control);
  - `{:args {:source "a"}}` against `{:args {:source "b"}}` are EQUAL;
  - `{:db-seed {[:feed] {:source "a"}}}` against the same with `"b"` are EQUAL.

Tracker: `volatile-fields` 0, `strip-run-stamps` 0, and volatile plus fingerprint/canonical returns only unrelated beads. Control: `canonicalize` matches 18.

## Smallest fix

Move `:source`, `:runner` and `:elapsed-ms` out of the recursive set and into `strip-run-stamps`' STRUCTURAL strip. They would then be stripped only on the carriers that actually stamp them:

- a run-result's own top level;
- the plan's `:source` coords;
- trace-event and epoch records;
- effect / assertion rows.

Do this exactly as `:id` / `:time` / `:frame` are already handled. Keep the genuinely reserved per-run ids (`:epoch-id`, `:trace-id`, `:committed-at`, `:schema-digest`, `:plan-hash`, `:run-hash`) recursive if preferred. Correct 017:3576-3579 to match. This changes canonical VALUES, so bump `canonical-version`, as the ns already requires for a form change.

Fence:
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/fingerprint.cljc`;
- `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md` (§Canonicalization table and §Determinism strip);
- the fingerprint / golden / diff / determinism JVM tests.

No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`cd tools/story && clojure -M:test`: the fingerprint, golden, diff and determinism tests, plus a regression in the probe's shape. `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` grades only the 017 edit's link targets and anchors, so verify the prose by hand.

## Decision needed

No. The code's own rationale for `:id` / `:time` / `:frame` settles it. The only choice is which carriers get the structural strip, and that is the implementer's.

The determinism gate and the golden family now REFUSE a normalized variant plan, and the sanctioned route to "is my variant deterministic / still the same?" is to run the VARIANT: `(story/run :variant-id)` twice, compared with `re-frame.story.determinism/compare-runs`, or `capture-golden` of one run-result checked with `golden-match?` against a second. title: examples-substrates: the Fresco login README's JVM-host REPL command 'clojure -A:test' runs ssr-ring's test suite (the alias's :main-opts) and exits - no REPL opens, so the documented host boot cannot be followed
description:
## Defect

The Fresco login README's JVM-host recipe says to start "a REPL with the host on the classpath" with `clojure -A:test` from `implementation/ssr-ring/`. The `:test` alias there carries `:main-opts ["-m" "re-frame.test-quiet.runner" "--dir" "test" "-e" ":slow" "-e" ":stress" "-e" ":crossing"]`, and the Clojure CLI still EXECUTES an alias's `:main-opts` under `-A` (it only prints a deprecation warning). So the command runs ssr-ring's whole default JVM test suite and exits; no REPL ever opens, and the `(require '[fresco.login.host …])` / `(host/init!)` / `run-jetty` block the README gives next has nowhere to be typed. The recipe was added by the rf2-fn0kx.8 fix (its finding 6 suggested "`-A:test` for a REPL"); no gate reads it.

## Where

Cited at `034d0c8fc8` (frozen tree):
- `examples/substrates/fresco/login/README.md:275-280` — `# From implementation/ssr-ring/ — a REPL with the host on the classpath.` then `clojure -A:test`; `:282-299` — the REPL forms that follow it.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/deps.edn` `:test` alias, its `:main-opts` (the test-quiet runner with `-e :slow -e :stress -e :crossing`); `:slow-test` and `:crossing-test` likewise carry runner `:main-opts`, so no alias there opens a REPL.
- `examples/substrates/fresco/login/host.clj:101-110` (the `client-dir` docstring) points readers at "a host booted the way the README describes".
- Public entry: the README's "Build it and run it" section, the only documented way to serve `host/app`.

## Failure scenario

From `implementation/ssr-ring/`, run exactly `LOGIN_FRESCO_SSR_NODE=… LOGIN_FRESCO_CLIENT_DIR=../out/examples/login-fresco clojure -A:test`. Expected (per the README): a REPL. Actual: `WARNING: Use of :main-opts with -A is deprecated. Use -M instead.`, then the ssr-ring default test suite runs to completion and the process exits. The reader never reaches `(host/init!)`, so the SSR route is never served.

## Evidence

EXECUTED on this machine's CLI (`clojure --version` → deps.clj 1.12.4.1618, which tracks the official CLI's version and behaviour), in a scratch directory with a throwaway `deps.edn` (`:x {:extra-paths ["extra"] :main-opts ["-e" "(println :MAIN-OPTS-RAN)"]}`), stdin carrying one REPL form: `clojure -A:x` printed the deprecation warning and `:MAIN-OPTS-RAN` and never evaluated the stdin form — i.e. `-A` ran the alias's main-opts, not a REPL. Control the other way: `clojure -Sdeps '{:aliases {:repl {:main-opts ["-r"]}}}' -M:x:repl` with the same stdin opened a REPL (`user=>` prompt, the form evaluated) and did NOT print `:MAIN-OPTS-RAN` — the last alias's `:main-opts` wins, while `:x`'s classpath still applies. I did not run the ssr-ring `:test` alias itself (that would be a test sweep); its `:main-opts` are read at source.
Census: `-A:test|-A:crossing|-A:slow` over the frozen tree (ripgrep, node_modules excluded) matches this README line only, beside three `.beads/issues.jsonl` records — so the search is live and there is no second copy. Tracker: no bead covers it (full-export search for `-A:test` returns rf2-fn0kx.8, where it was proposed, and unrelated story-mcp / xray beads).

## Smallest fix

Give the README a command that opens a REPL on that classpath. README-only: `clojure -Sdeps '{:aliases {:repl {:main-opts ["-r"]}}}' -M:test:repl` (measured shape above). Tidier: add a no-`:main-opts` alias to `implementation/ssr-ring/deps.edn` (for example `:login-host`, reusing `:test`'s extra paths and deps) and name it in the README. Fence: `examples/substrates/fresco/login/README.md`, optionally `implementation/ssr-ring/deps.edn` (not a hot-zone file; the top-level `implementation/deps.edn` is untouched).

## Gates

No gate reads a README command, so verification is by hand: run the new command from `implementation/ssr-ring/`, evaluate the README's `(require …)` and `(host/init!)` forms, and see them succeed. If a deps.edn alias is added, `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/ssr-ring/` must still pass (JVM lane). The link gates (`scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci`) grade only the README's links.

## Decision needed

No.

title: examples-scripts: examples/README.md catalogue row presents the demoted :rf/suspense-boundary wire marker as what the streaming example demonstrates (spec 011:1661 MUST NOT)
description:
## Defect

The examples catalogue row for the streaming-SSR example tells the reader that what the example demonstrates is "the `:rf/suspense-boundary` marker". Spec 011 demotes that keyword to internal wire syntax and forbids presenting it as something an author writes. The example itself, its own README and the SSR guide all teach the `ssr/boundary` component. This catalogue row is the last place that still names the marker as the thing to use. The 2026-09-21 wave fixed the other sites (rf2-fn0kx.6 finding 2, commit `c383969c5f`). Its worker recorded this row as "OUT OF FENCE -- NAMED AND NOT TOUCHED" because several beads were editing `examples/README.md` at once, and it never became a bead.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `examples/README.md:136`, the `examples/ssr-streaming` row, reads: "Streaming SSR: a dashboard whose shell renders immediately, then each slow card streams as its fetch resolves. The `:rf/suspense-boundary` marker, per-card fallback, and interleaved hydration."
- `spec/011-SSR.md:1661`: "`:rf/suspense-boundary` remains, demoted to **internal wire syntax** between the component and the shell walker. Implementations MUST NOT present it as an authoring surface, and a render tree an application author writes MUST NOT contain it."
- `spec/011-SSR.md:1659` gives the reason. A keyword head is an HTML element on every host, so "a `:rf/suspense-boundary` left in a client render tree paints a phantom `<suspense-boundary>` element — silently".
- Readers reach this row from the catalogue at the top of the examples tree, the entry page for anyone browsing the runnable apps.

## Failure scenario

A reader scans the catalogue for "how do I stream a slow region" and sees that the streaming example demonstrates "the `:rf/suspense-boundary` marker". They write `[:rf/suspense-boundary {:id :x :fallback [:p "…"]} [slow-card]]` in a view. On the client, that tree paints a `<suspense-boundary>` element with no error (spec 011:1659). Only the server's non-streaming emitter fails loudly. The correct form is `[ssr/boundary {...} ...]`, which the example's own code and README already use.

## Evidence

Inspected, no probe needed. This is prose against a normative spec sentence.

- The row text was read at the frozen tree, line 136 above.
- `ssr/boundary` is already the taught surface at `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/README.md` lines 16, 20, 56 and 103.
- `docs/ssr/streaming.md:54-57` says the marker is internal wire syntax.
- Tracker: `bd search "suspense-boundary" --status all` returns exactly one bead, rf2-fn0kx.6 (closed). The instrument does return hits, so this is a real absence, and no other bead covers this row. The rf2-fn0kx.6 notes name this line as out of fence and not touched. Its line number was `:128` at that tree; it is `:136` now.

## Smallest fix

Change the row's middle sentence to "The `ssr/boundary` component, per-card fallback, and interleaved hydration." This is the wording the rf2-fn0kx.6 report proposed. The `#streaming-ssr` link stays valid (`### Streaming SSR` at spec 011:1642).

Fence: `examples/README.md` only. Not a hot-zone file.

Adjacent, outside this fence: spec 011's own status note at `spec/011-SSR.md:1644` still opens "The `:rf/suspense-boundary` hiccup marker described below ships…", two paragraphs above its own MUST NOT. That is for the SSR spec owner; it is not part of this change.

## Gates

`python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` is the link gate for `examples/README.md`. It validates link targets only, and this edit keeps the same link, so it cannot fail on the change. Check the reworded row by hand (table column count unchanged) and say so in the PR body. `check_doc_slugs.py` does not cover `examples/`.

## Decision needed

No. Spec 011:1661 already rules it, and rf2-fn0kx.6 fixed every other site the same way.

title: adapters/ssr: static markup writes javascript: URLs unchanged in href/src/action/formAction/xlink:href where react-dom 19 neutralises them
description:
## Defect

react-dom 19 blocks `javascript:` URLs in the URL-bearing attributes `href`, `src`, `action`, `formAction` and `xlinkHref`: it replaces the value with a URL that throws. Two re-frame2 static emitters write such a value UNCHANGED:
- reagent-slim's `render-to-static-markup` (`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs`);
- re-frame.ssr's hiccup emitter (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/`, around `ui_tree.cljc` and the HTML emitter).

So a `javascript:` URL that react-dom would neutralise ships live in server HTML.

PR #10336 (rf2-u0xpc, merged at trunk ab8fc0052e) made `:xlink-href` render as the real `xlink:href` attribute. Before that, slim wrote a lowercase name no browser recognised. The fix was correct, but it gives `xlink:href` the same exposure `href` already had. The #10336 worker found this, measured nothing further, and filed nothing, because it was outside its fence.

## Why it matters beyond hygiene

- **Parity contract.** slim's static markup is pinned against react-dom by the parity tests (`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/dom/parity_cljs_test.cljs`), so this is a parity gap, not a new policy.
- **Hydration.** Where server HTML is hydrated by a React substrate, the client renders the neutralised URL and the server does not. The two sides disagree on that attribute.

## Correction

Measure first, at trunk:
1. What each emitter writes for `javascript:` values, including mixed-case and whitespace-padded forms, in each of the five attributes.
2. What react-dom 19.3.0 writes for the same values, read from the installed bundle's own sanitiser (the same source #10336's sweep test reads).
3. For re-frame.ssr: which client substrate hydrates each output path, and what that client renders for the same value.

Then:
- **reagent-slim:** match react-dom exactly. Reuse react-dom's own rule, as #10336's derivation test reuses its attribute list.
- **re-frame.ssr's hiccup emitter:** match what the hydrating client substrate renders for the same attribute, so server and client agree. If the emitter serves a non-React path whose client does NOT sanitise, stop and report that path rather than inventing a policy for it.

Add parity rows for each attribute, plus a control showing an ordinary `https:` URL is untouched.

## Decision needed

No for reagent-slim: this is parity with react-dom, the adapter's own contract.

For re-frame.ssr, it is conditional. If every hydrating client sanitises, match it. If a non-sanitising path exists, report it with the measurement, and the mayor rules.
notes:
WORKER (jsurl-3x7nj, 2026-09-24 13:20 AUSEST): IMPLEMENTED in PR #10345 (branch worker/jsurl-3x7nj, head 40e9b47227, rebased onto trunk e0121f9f5c). Two halves are fixed; three re-frame.ssr paths are STOPPED FOR A RULING.

MEASURED AT TRUNK ab8fc0052e.
(1) Both emitters wrote every javascript: spelling unchanged in all six URL attributes (href, src, action, formAction, xlink:href, and data on an <object>). The spellings covered were plain, mixed case, leading spaces, leading C0 controls, tab/LF/CR inside the scheme, and a trailing space. For reagent-slim this was read from the source (no scheme handling anywhere) and then seen in CI on the red run below. For re-frame.ssr it was measured on the JVM: render-to-string, the streaming shell walk, emit-ui-tree, the head emitter and attr-string all wrote the value verbatim.
(2) react-dom 19.3.0 (installed bundle) blocks through sanitizeURL. The regex is isJavaScriptProtocol, /^[\u0000-\u001F ]*j[\r\n\t]*a[\r\n\t]*v[\r\n\t]*a[\r\n\t]*s[\r\n\t]*c[\r\n\t]*r[\r\n\t]*i[\r\n\t]*p[\r\n\t]*t[\r\n\t]*:/i. The substituted URL is javascript:throw new Error('React has blocked a javascript: URL as a security precaution.'). It is applied in pushAttribute's href / src / action / formAction / xlinkHref cases on any element, and in data on an <object> only. It is NOT applied on a custom element (a hyphenated tag other than the eight SVG and MathML names react-dom exempts: annotation-xml, color-profile, font-face, font-face-src, font-face-uri, font-face-format, font-face-name, missing-glyph). The rule is keyed on the exact prop name, so the string prop "xlink:href" and HREF are not blocked. The regex and the substituted URL are byte-identical in the server and client production builds. Near-misses it leaves alone: a space before the colon, a leading no-break space, and an https URL containing javascript:.
(3) Hydrating clients. render-to-string and the streaming shell walk are hydrated by Reagent-tier clients (stock Reagent, reagent-slim) painting through react-dom, whose setProp blocks. Production hydration (prepareToHydrateHostInstance) never touches attributes, so the server's unblocked URL stayed live on the hydrated page. Development hydration's hydrateSanitizedAttribute reports it as a mismatch. UIx is not hiccup, and Fresco's server renders through react-dom/server itself, so neither uses this emitter.

FIX.
- reagent-slim (implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs): block-javascript-url, applied on the ordinary attribute-value path. The tag is threaded through emit-attributes / emit-attribute, and the prop token is keyed as react-dom keys it (prop-token, extracted from attribute-name). IMPL-SPEC §8.3 records the rule.
- re-frame.ssr (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc): block-javascript-url, applied in convert-dom-attrs. Both hiccup walkers already share that through dom-element-props, so streaming.cljc is untouched. The prop name is the React prop name the Reagent-tier adapter produces. Spec 011 gains one paragraph after "Form controls take react-dom's special forms".

CONTROL.
- reagent-slim, CI only (no local shadow-cljs run). The tests were pushed AHEAD of the fix. On head 6e0281393b (run 35947329168), the node lane was RED: 43 failures, 0 errors, 12753 tests / 65158 assertions. That is exactly 36 rows of parity_cljs_test's parity-javascript-urls-are-blocked-rf2-w1hd8 (6 attributes x 6 spellings), the 5 names of boolean_attr_react_parity_cljs_test's javascript-url-blocking-agrees-with-installed-react-dom sweep (href, src, action, formAction, xlinkHref), and 2 byte pins. No control failed: the near-misses, data on a <div>, and href on a custom element all passed. With the fix (head 40e9b47227), the node lane was green: 0 failures over 12753 / 65158. The count did not move because both runs graded the same merge-ref test set.
- re-frame.ssr, JVM. The new implementation/ssr/test/react_dom_probe/javascript_url.cjs renders 9 targets x 9 values through the installed react-dom into javascript_url.edn. It aborts unless the server and client builds carry one regex and one substituted URL. The new re_frame/ssr_javascript_url_react_parity_test compares both walkers against that fixture from every author spelling of each prop. It was RED before the fix (192 failures, 0 errors, 365 assertions, every failure a blocked row) and GREEN after. Re-sabotaged on the final base by disabling the match: red at 192 again, restored, and the restored blob hash equals the committed blob.

GATES on the final base: implementation/ssr clojure -M:test exit 0; scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh exit 0 (705 tests); the JVM implementation sweep, all 21 artefacts, exit 0. That sweep had one ssr-ring node-body-deadline timing flake on its first pass under machine load, green on 4 of 4 re-runs. It exercises no URL attribute. The fast-PR spine's 65 always-on checks and its 20-step docs tier (mkdocs --strict included) were run individually, each exit 0. Pinned clj-kondo exit 0. CI rollup: 88 checks, 65 success and 23 skipped, with all 4 runs completed.

STOPPED FOR A RULING, measured and NOT changed. These are paths with no sanitising client, so the brief's stop condition applies:
(a) The re-frame.ssr <head> emitter (<link href>, <script src>) and the Ring host shell's :html-attrs / :body-attrs bags. Spec 011 says no adapter re-renders them, and no client-side head manager exists in implementation/. They write javascript: values unchanged. (react-dom would block <link href>.)
(b) emit-ui-tree. It has no hydrating client in the tree, because its producers were retired under rf2-0yp7w and only the Fresco test kit builds 004B trees, for tests. It writes the value unchanged. Its conversion table is 004B's, outside the fence.

SEEN, NOT IN SCOPE, NOT FILED.
- reagent-slim's attribute escape covers & and " only, where react-dom escapes all of & < > " ' in attribute values. The bytes differ but parse to the same value, which is why the parity rows canonicalise '.
- re-frame.ssr's attribute-NAME conversion treats all eight react-dom-exempt hyphenated tags as custom elements. The new URL rule uses react-dom's exact test.
- react-dom drops an empty src and an empty <object data>, and re-frame.ssr keeps them (measured).
Merged-PR audit #10345 (8a14494757dc1ab45de0fcd0cb30f73f541b55a8; merged 2026-09-24T03:15:41Z). Completeness: The scoped URL-parity defect is corrected in reagent-slim and both hydratable SSR hiccup walks, including object data in addition to the original five props. Source and audit companion are already closed by their owners. Item 19 is verified on open uoeyl. The brief explicitly requested measurements/reporting for paths without a sanitising client; head/host bags and the unhydrated structural serializer are reported, with no unrequested policy added. Correctness: Read the scheme regex, prop-token conversion, custom-element exceptions, shared SSR attr seam, React fixture generator and parity consumers. Accepted reported CI tests-only 43 failures then node 12753/65158 green; JVM parity 192 failures then 365 assertions green; SSR 705 tests, all 21 JVM artefacts and CI 65 success/23 skipped. The author disclosed an unrelated timing flake and four green reruns. No tests rerun; no actionable residual within the parity claim. Implementation quality: Copies the installed React rule by intent and tests against React-derived evidence, with explicit near-miss/custom-element controls. Existing shared SSR conversion reaches both walkers. Attribute escaping equivalence and obsolete-tag name differences are not escalated as useful corrective work for this bounded change. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: rf2-uoeyl.

title: examples-patterns: boot demo promises to show :on-any-failed cancelling two siblings, but equal 60 ms reply delays mean both siblings always finish first
description:
## Defect

The boot demo's failure seam promises "you also watch `:on-any-failed` cancel its two siblings on the way to `:failed`" (core.cljs:57-59). That is the stated reason `/user.json` was chosen (`:99-102`). It never happens.

Every canned reply, success or failure, rides the same 60 ms `:dispatch-later`, and `:user` is the last of the three `:spawn-all` children. So the routes and flags replies always land first, both siblings complete and fold, and the user failure resolves the join with no survivor to cancel. A reader who opens Xray to watch the advertised cancellation sees two normal completions and may conclude that cancellation is broken.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `examples/patterns/boot/core.cljs`: the claim is at `:54-61`, the one shared delay at `:97` (`reply-delay-ms 60`), and the rationale at `:99-103`. The failure branch at `:148-155` passes the same `:after-ms reply-delay-ms` the success branch uses at `:162-165`.
- `examples/patterns/boot/boot.cljs:274-301` gives the children's order: routes, flags, user.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc:336-392`: both canned fxs defer through `:rf.http/deliver-canned-reply` and one `:dispatch-later {:ms after-ms}`, which is a FIFO setTimeout.
- Public entry: the demo's "Fail the next boot" plus "Re-run boot".

## Failure scenario

Tick "Fail the next boot", then click "Re-run boot". The routes and flags loaders reach `:done` and fold their payloads, then `/user.json` fails. `:on-any-failed` resolves the join with zero survivors, so no `:rf.machine.spawn/cancelled-on-join-resolution` ever fires. The README-level statement at `README.md:45-46`, that a failure cancels the rest, is true in general; the demo's promise to *show* it is not.

## Evidence

**Executed.** The bounded JVM probe loaded `boot.cljs` verbatim and eval'd `core.cljs`'s stub forms verbatim, without the schemas artefact, so the separate `:data`-schema hang filed alongside this does not mask the branch. Output is in the review scratch dir at `probe/boot.out`.
- **As shipped:** `state=:failed routes?=true flags?=true`. Both siblings folded their payloads, so both completed rather than being cancelled.
- **Control:** the same stub with only the armed failure's `:after-ms` changed from 60 to 10 gives `state=:failed routes?=false flags?=false`. Both siblings were cancelled before folding, so the observable discriminates.

**Tracker.** An all-status search found 0 hits for `fail-next-boot` and for "cancel its two siblings". rf2-fn0kx.5's report cites sibling cancellation only as a Spec 005 match for long_running_work.

## Smallest fix

In the armed branch pass a shorter delay, for example `:after-ms 10`, or 0, which lands in the same drain. Then the two siblings are still in flight when `/user.json` fails and the cancellation the comment promises is visible. Keep the 60 ms on the success path.

Alternatively, drop the "cancel its two siblings" clause. One file, `examples/patterns/boot/core.cljs`.

## Gates

None mechanical, because examples are test-free (rf2-8cevm). `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs` compiles it, but that script is shadow-cljs and needs the exclusive lane. `boot_cljs_test.cljs` does not exercise the seam. Verify by hand in Xray.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
== NOTE FROM rf2-3x7nj.41.1's RULING (mayor's ruling agent, 2026-09-24 13:20:56 AUSEST): verify this bead AFTER rf2-3x7nj.41.1 lands ==

The dev build (`npm run dev:example -- examples/boot`) loads the schemas artefact, and there the failure seam never reaches `:failed` today. The failed `/user.json` child's per-child `:on-done` folds the 503 map into `:data :user`. `BootData`'s `[:maybe User]` rejects it, and the schema rollback discards the whole carrier macrostep. So `:on-any-failed` never fires and NO sibling is ever cancelled, whatever the reply delays are. This bead's own evidence was taken without the schemas artefact, which is why it saw `:failed`.

rf2-3x7nj.41.1 is now ruled: a failed child's per-child `:on-done` no longer runs, so the join records the failure and `:on-any-failed` fires. That means the hand verification in Xray this bead prescribes can only show the cancellation once 41.1 has landed.

The one-file change here (`examples/patterns/boot/core.cljs`) does not overlap 41.1's fence (the machines lifecycle_fx sources, a machines test, boot_cljs_test.cljs, spec/005, spec/Spec-Schemas.md and spec/API.md). 41.1's boot witness asserts `:failed` without assuming which siblings finished first, so it holds under either delay.

No tracker dependency edge links the two beads; add one if the ordering should be enforced.
== IMPLEMENTED (worker spawnfail-3x7nj, 2026-09-24 14:20 AUSEST): PR #10351, draft until CI settles ==

The change is one file, examples/patterns/boot/core.cljs, but it is NOT the suggested shorter-delay fix, because of a measurement.

The suggested fix answers /user.json sooner, for example at :after-ms 10. It does cancel both siblings. But their canned 60 ms replies still land about 50 ms later at the destroyed loaders' addresses, and each is reported as :rf.error/no-such-handler, which the dev console prints via the unowned-error fallback. A real :rf.http/managed request is aborted when its loader is destroyed (Spec 014 Abort on actor destroy). The fake backend has nothing to abort.

So while the seam is armed, the stub now leaves /routes.json and /flags.json unanswered: "theirs a longer one", taken to its limit. The 60 ms delay stays on every reply that is answered, including the 503. The prose explains both the hold and why a shorter delay would not do. This is deterministic: all three children issue their GET before the queued disarm event is handled.

Measured with a JVM probe that loads the example's schema.cljs and boot.cljs verbatim and evals core.cljs's stub forms, on PR #10351's machines code:
- As shipped: the armed re-boot reaches :failed, the siblings complete, 0 are cancelled, and there are 0 no-such-handler.
- Failure at 10 ms: :failed, cancelled [:routes :flags], and 2 :rf.error/no-such-handler.
- This branch: :failed, cancelled [:routes :flags], 0 no-such-handler, and Retry reaches :ready.
On shipped machines code the armed re-boot hangs at :loading-deps whatever the delays are (rf2-3x7nj.41.1), so this bead depends on 41.1 landing. They ship in the same PR.

Examples are test-free. The rf2-3x7nj.41.1 boot witness in boot_cljs_test.cljs pins "both siblings cancelled and torn down" with its own stub, which never answers them, so it does not depend on this example's delays.
Merged-PR audit #10351 (089680d239613b45d3c4d05cfb1e8c3b96e5800d; merged 2026-09-24T04:17:21Z). Completeness: The ruled changes for rf2-3x7nj.41.1 and the measured boot seam for rf2-3x7nj.41.4 are present. Join folds are success-only; both single-spawn failure producers use the failure carrier regardless of :on-error; dead parent-spec resolution is removed; required spec/API/skill prose and 13-row routing tests plus the schema-bearing boot witness landed. One disclosed residual docstring remains: rf2-2573j is separately open because exact implementation rf2-2bk24 is in_progress. Correctness: Read the full PR production changes at merge 089680d239, checked the ruling and boot stub ordering, success/failure split, unchanged stale/liveness guards and join failure bookkeeping. The existing parent engine handles failure resolution; no redundant fold guard was added. Accept author-reported 16 failures before the fix, three mutation controls, machines JVM 1323/4954, all 21 JVM artifacts, machines-viz 668/2995 and schema-bearing boot/retry measurements. All 76 applicable CI checks succeeded (12 skipped); the owner records CLJS +14 tests/+44 assertions. No suites rerun. Implementation quality: Small changes at existing carrier boundaries remove obsolete lookup helpers and preserve the ergonomic API. The fake backend leaves the two cancellable sibling requests unanswered while armed, avoiding measured late replies to destroyed actors without adding transport machinery. Public declarations and manifest sidecars remain unchanged. Only the obsolete internal carrier docstring warrants follow-up; no further actionable finding. Actionable findings: rf2-2573j. Existing finding updates: none.

CI at that head: 88 checks, 0 pending, 0 failed, all four workflow runs complete; CLJS (shadow-cljs :node-test) is CI's run and moved +14 tests / +44 assertions over main at the merge base — exactly the new namespace plus the boot witness. title: xstate-parity: :rf.machine/transition :microsteps reads 0 when the macrostep's only :always step ran inside a raised event's nested handling (per-microstep stream emits the row; spec/005:722 counts every :always iteration)
description:
Routed by the mayor from dimension B's handoffs (rf2-2n6uv.4, findings doc `ai/findings/xstate-v6-parity/B-semantics.md` §Handoffs, "Instrumentation"). Trace correctness, not a semantic: the machine lands in the right state; the rollup tag Xray groups by is wrong.

## Gap

The outer `:rf.machine/transition` trace's `:microsteps` tag reads **0** when the macrostep's only `:always` microstep was taken INSIDE a raised event's nested handling, while the per-microstep stream emits the row for it. spec/005 defines the tag as the count of `:always` iterations the macrostep ran (spec/005:722 "it remains the count of `:always` iterations"; spec/005:2069 "`:tags { ... :microsteps <count>}`"; spec/009:223 "`:microsteps <count>`"), and a `:raise` dequeue is part of the same macrostep (rf2-nb8nj: its rows are NESTED as `:raised-transition` steps of the one `:cascade`). XState's `getMicrosteps` returns every microstep of the macrostep, raised-event hops included (dimension B row 1, `xs/B-1-*.out`), so a consumer counting microsteps sees 1 there and 0 here for the same chart.

## re-frame2 evidence (executed, trunk 2c349f0a60)

`jvm/B/B-1-macrostep.clj` case 1a, output `jvm/B/B-1-macrostep.out` lines 1-5. Machine:

    {:initial :start
     :actions {:raise-next (fn [{:keys [data]}] {:data data :fx [[:raise [:next]]]})}
     :states {:start {:on {:go :a}}
              :a {:entry :raise-next :on {:next :b}}
              :b {:always :c}
              :c {:entry :raise-next :on {:next :d}}
              :d {}}}

After `[:rf.machine/start]` then `[:go]`: `state: :d`; `transition traces: [{:microsteps 0}]`; `microstep traces: [{:from :b, :to :c, :microstep-index 0}]`; op-types show exactly one `:rf.machine/transition` and one `:rf.machine.microstep/transition`. Control, case 1g (same `:b {:always :c}` shape reached by the dispatched event directly, no raise): `transition traces: [{:microsteps 1}]`.

Where: the headline emit reads `(rf.machines.result/microsteps step-result)` at `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:878`, i.e. the OUTER step's own `::microsteps` rider (`result.cljc:154`); the raise loop's nested settles carry their own counts that are folded into `:cascade` as `:raised-transition` steps but never summed into the rollup. The comment at `registration.cljc:860-862` says the count "does not include raised dequeues" — correct about DEQUEUES (a dequeue is not an `:always` iteration), but the `:always` iterations INSIDE a dequeue's settle are `:always` iterations of this macrostep and the spec's count includes them.

## Why it matters

spec/005:1961 says Xray groups an eventless round directly off the outer count "without reconstructing simultaneity from trace order"; a 0 beside a non-empty per-microstep stream is the shape every consumer has to special-case. Small, but it is the rollup the spec tells tools to trust.

## Options

1. Sum the nested settles' `::microsteps` into the outer rider inside the raise loop (runtime only, `transition.cljc` raise-drain + `result.cljc`), so the tag equals the number of `:rf.machine.microstep/transition` rows the macrostep emitted (parallel: rounds, per spec/005:1961). Smallest; no spec change; one pinned case moves from 0 to 1.
2. Keep the count as "the dispatched event's own settle only" and say so in spec/005:722/2069 and spec/009:223 (spec/005 and spec/009 are hot-zone).

## Recommendation

Option 1. The per-microstep stream already counts them; the rollup should agree with it.

## Fence

`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` (raise drain), `result.cljc`, `lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:878`; one new pin beside the existing microstep-count tests (`rg "microsteps" implementation/machines/test`). Option 2 touches hot-zone spec/005 and spec/009 instead.

## Gates

`clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines` (the engine is `.cljc` shared code, no `#?(:cljs` branch involved); the conformance corpus if a fixture pins `:microsteps 0` on a raised-always shape (`rg ":microsteps" implementation/*conformance*`).

## Decision needed

No.
