title: FALSE: shared React test prose describes cold render acquisition as net-zero
description:
PR #10367 at 5ebbf78cb189f894d5430c1fbec9983d0742f21d. This is the separately trackable correction for the shared render/acquisition narrative in rf2-tv5ac.81 reports 1-4.

implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs still says render acquisition is always a net-zero subscribe/unsubscribe round trip (4871, 5158-5186, 5242, 5280), that a cold first mount necessarily disposes its render reaction and commits a different object (5419-5425), and that the pre-commit fallback cannot live-read an intervening write (no-retention section). These statements conflict with its escrow/adoption tests and the actual implementation.

spine.cljs:3237-3265 balances an already-committed warm read but retains a cold +1 in a reaped escrow token. get-snap at 3364-3384 reads the live unspent token before falling back to the frozen render value. The commit at 3535-3564 adopts the same reaction if that token is still held; if the reaper wins, it rebuilds. The public browser runner deliberately pins a different timing outcome: assert-use-sub-browser-runner-schedule-rebuilds (6174 onward) says and asserts two builds, but its testing label at 6216 says the commit adopts.

Required correction: align this suite's lifecycle narrative with those warm/cold and timing distinctions, including the contradictory testing label. Preserve the two-build runner assertions and the separate act-driven adoption witness. This is one bounded correction of the render/commit contract as described by the suite, not a change to escrow, timing, runtime behavior, or test identifiers.

title: machines-viz: project the transition-shaped :spawn :on-done (chart edge, Mermaid edge/note, static grammar mirror, SCXML omission note)
description:
## What

Discovered from the ruling on rf2-2n6uv.2.1 (2026-09-24 20:55 AUSEST). That ruling WIDENS `:spawn :on-done`:
- A fn stays the data fold.
- An `:on`-shaped value (keyword / vector-path / `{:target :guard :action}` / guarded candidate vector) becomes a TRANSITION, resolved at the spawning state's own level. This is the `:spawn :on-error` symmetry.

tools/machines-viz enumerates `[:spawn :on-error]` by hand at every projection site and knows nothing of a transition-shaped `[:spawn :on-done]`. So once rf2-2n6uv.2.1 lands, the chart draws a spawning state whose success exit is a FALSE DEAD END.

Measured by the rf2-2n6uv.2.1 Codex review at trunk f798840db7: the current chart projector returns ZERO edges for a transition-shaped spawn `:on-done`, against ONE edge for the matching `:on-error` control.

## Sites (all under tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/, line numbers at trunk 16523099d2)

- `chart/layout.cljc:420-434` — the `:spawn :on-error` edge block in `collect-state-edges`. Add the twin for a NON-fn `[:spawn :on-done]`: event `:rf.machine.spawn/done`, resolved with the same `resolve-tgt` (keyword target = sibling of the spawning state).
- `chart/projection.cljc:217-230` `event-variant` — decide the chip.
  - The compound `:on-done` already buckets as `:on-done` (the ✓ done chip).
  - Reusing that bucket for the spawn success transition is the smallest move. Add a distinct flag only if the renderer needs one.
- `mermaid.cljc:284-290` (internal action-only notes) and `:524-530` (edges): add twins of the `:spawn :on-error` blocks.
- `grammar.cljc:789` — the static defect mirror of the runtime target validation. Add `[:spawn :on-done]` (NON-fn only) beside `:spawn/on-error`.
  - Its `known-spawn-spec-keys` (:560) already carries `:on-done`, so it needs no change.
- `scxml.cljc:91-95` — the docstring records that `:spawn` is omitted from SCXML export "INCLUDING its `:on-error` parent transition". Say the same of a transition-shaped `:on-done`; the export itself does not change.

## Rule

- ONLY a non-fn `:spawn :on-done` is an edge. A fn `:on-done` is a data fold and must NOT draw anything.
- A `:spawn-all` child's `:on-done` is always a fold, and draws nothing.

## Tests

- Extend `tools/machines-viz/test/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/projection_cljs_test.cljc` and `cross_emitter_agreement_cljs_test.cljc`: the chart and Mermaid must agree on the new edge.
- RED today:
  - a spawn `:on-done {:target :x}` projects one edge;
  - an action-only `:on-done {:action :a}` projects an internal note.
- CONTROLS:
  - a fn `:on-done` projects nothing;
  - the `:on-error` edge is unchanged;
  - the compound `:on-done` edge is unchanged.
- Red-with-fix-removed: revert the layout twin and the edge test goes red.

## Gate

`npm run test:tools-machines-viz` (in implementation/package.json). It enters shadow-cljs through `clojure -M:cljs-test -m shadow.cljs.devtools.cli`, so it takes the MACHINE-WIDE EXCLUSIVE shadow-cljs lane under the grant protocol; otherwise cite CI.

## Sequencing

- Land AFTER rf2-2n6uv.2.1's PR merges. The spec grammar and runtime must exist first.
- It does not touch implementation/ at all.

   RULING: the spec may specify planned normative behaviour, so KEEP Layer 2 as specified-not-yet-built. Mark it plainly as not yet implemented, in the way the spec marks other planned stages; find that convention at tip. Rewrite its references to removed pieces (`render-static`, Layer 1, the old default prefix) so it stands on its own against what ships. If it cannot stand on its own without Layer 1, delete it and say why.
2. **004B §Projections and the `t` alias in its status line.** Fresco's `ht/attrs` and `ht/text` cover only some of the arms.
   RULING: describe the projections in terms of the helpers that ship (re-frame.fresco.test and its ht/* helpers). Drop any arm with no shipped producer. Drop or correct the `t` alias if nothing defines it.
3. **004B conversion-table rows still phrase refusals per compiled/interpreted mode**, which are the removed modes.
   RULING: rephrase each refusal without the removed modes, keeping the refusal itself when a shipped producer or consumer enforces it. Check each against code.
4. **Contradiction:** the Fresco test kit says `ht/attrs` values are unnormalised, while 004B says `:attrs` values are normalised.
   Settle it against the fresco code, and make whichever text is wrong agree. If the CODE looks wrong against a clear normative 004B rule, report it as a possible defect and do not change behaviour.

Each note names a blocking bead: `rf2-7pgiz` or `rf2-blw1q`.
   - Neither bead exists: `bd show` answers "no issues found", and neither id appears in the tracker export.
   - `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md` says both pieces ARE wired.
   - `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/save_variant_cljs_test.cljc` asserts that the notes name the blocking bead. The sweep put the ids back when that test went red.

   Settle from the code whether db-seed capture and route sub-override capture are wired now.
   - If they are, correct the notes to say what the capture does.
   - If they are not, say plainly what is not captured, with no bead id.

   Either way, drop the dangling ids and move the test's expectation in the same commit (epic rf2-tv5ac's R6).
2. **Recorder redaction of dispatched events.** Both `.cjs` browser specs (`tools/story/test/story_browser_scenarios.cjs` and `tools/story/test/story_feature_load.cjs`) say nothing marks the `:rf.event/dispatched` trace as `:sensitive?`, the flag the recorder redacts on. But the counter testbed documents recorder redaction, and core has a classification projection over trace tags.

   Reproduce: record a session that dispatches an event carrying a value declared sensitive, and see whether the recorded tape shows it raw.
   - If it redacts, correct the two specs' comments to say how.
   - If it does not, that is a privacy defect. Stop and report it with the reproduction; do not design a fix.
3. **elision_demo docstring.** Item 2 of the ns docstring in `tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/elision_demo.cljs` contradicts that file's own SCHEMAS block and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc`. Make the docstring match the code.
4. **spec/017's invariant dedup key.** About line 2967 it says an invariant result is de-duplicated on `[invariant-id epoch-id]`, while the code keys on `[invariant-id frame epoch-id]`. Make the spec match the code.
5. **AGENTS.md token.** The ns docstring of `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/registrar.cljc` points at an AGENTS.md rule that no longer exists. Replace it with the reason in the present tense, or drop it.

## Ruling (mayor, 2026-09-25, under the stance)

Make each comment, note or spec line tell the truth about the code as it is now, and add no mechanism. The one exception is item 2: if it turns out to be a real leak, report it rather than fixing it inside this bead.

The bundle gate measures four surfaces (motion, overlay, forms, server) and has NO substrate row, and it gives no reason for leaving it out. The header's claim is therefore false as written.

The source-side gate does cover substrate. What is missing is the bundle-side confirmation that Closure leaves nothing behind. The :fresco-release exemplar (entry re-frame.fresco.consumer-app) picks the UIx adapter, not Fresco's own substrate, so a substrate-absence row would be meaningful on that bundle.

## Ruling (mayor, 2026-09-25, stance: the gate's own words must be true; do not gold-plate)

1. If substrate has a LOAD-BEARING sentinel, add a substrate row beside the other four, following the header's own sentinel rule: a string the surface cannot function without, which Closure keeps under :advanced when substrate is reachable. Show the row RED on a bundle where substrate IS reachable (e.g. a scratch entry requiring it), then green on the real bundle.
2. If substrate has NO such sentinel, add a NOT-ROWED paragraph like the native one, saying why, and make the heading's roster sentence name both exceptions.

Say which case applied and why. Do not change substrate's code to manufacture a sentinel.

## Fence

- implementation/fresco/scripts/check_bundle_isolation.cjs, plus its test file under implementation/fresco/scripts/ if one pins the row roster.
- Nothing in src/.

title: FALSE: swept flow fixtures say registration effects wait for a later poke to evaluate
description:
Audit of merged PR #10449 at 2ef4c604408a7fa9eb7b78e0f12ecee4482e4732, correctness/completeness. The present-tense sweep leaves two fixtures teaching a one-event lag for their reserved-effect registration path. flow-hot-reload-preserves-output.edn:44-47 says reg-v1 first fires on the next drain and attributes v1/v2 evaluation to the later poke events; its :fixture/doc at :15 likewise says the next drain materialises a changed body. hot-reload-handler-replaced-trace.edn:94 and :100 similarly attribute evaluation to poke 1/2. Both use :rf.fx/reg-flow, not a direct registration outside an event drain.

Evidence: core/src/re_frame/conformance.cljc:273-289 lowers the fixture DSL map into the reserved effect's normal triple. core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:1014-1023 always requests a settle after that registration hook returns; :868-874 enqueues :rf/settle-flows, before queued continuations and before dispatch returns. The flow runner preserves this real reserved effect (flows_conformance_test.clj:344-363). Spec 013:431 and :449-455 state that same dispatch-settle contract. The two fixtures' final-value/subsequence assertions do not establish the delayed timing their prose claims, so their green suites do not resolve this discrepancy.

Required correction: describe initial evaluation and replacement evaluation at the registration dispatch's settling boundary; describe the later no-op pokes as subsequent drains, normally dirty-check skips for unchanged inputs. Clearly distinguish a direct out-of-drain reg-flow (next-drain behavior) if retained as context. This is a small prose truth fix, not a request to change runtime scheduling or add follow-up events. Use existing flow-settle coverage as evidence; no new scheduling mechanism is needed.

FIXED by PR #10454 (rf2-gher2 item 3), merged at trunk 1b8fd7af6d. This audit was filed against #10449 before #10454 landed, and #10454 made exactly this correction. Verified at trunk 1b8fd7af6d:

The step commentary (lines 48-53) reads "dispatch settles -> :doubled 14" for each registration, and "[:doubled/poke 1] — :n is unchanged, so the flow skips".
- The same fixture now PINS that timing with an ordered trace expectation (lines 69-77): each flow evaluation must land after its registering event starts and before the next poke starts, "so a runtime that left either evaluation to the next drain fails here". #10454 showed this red with the settle disabled in fx.cljc, while the old fixture stayed green.
- hot-reload-handler-replaced-trace.edn: lines 93-94 say "the flow evaluates against the v1 body before this dispatch settles", and lines 100-101 say it re-evaluates "against the v2 body before this dispatch settles". The pokes read "the flow skips".

title: Attribution guard: enforce on the commit AUTHOR/COMMITTER field (noreply@anthropic.com) — RULED (a) by Mike 2026-09-26
description:
HELD — OPERATOR DECISION (Mike). Nothing to dispatch until Mike rules.

Finding (mayor, 2026-09-26): 12 commits merged to trunk today carry the git AUTHOR "Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>":
- 87730ea7f9, 45cc1c9d9a, 1a7152445c, 71d3b54403 (docs/api);
- c688702c50, c1ba89644a (docs/core, #10470);
- 05b89bda35, 323f12a377, 2e5cb8da8d (#10475);
- c97706044d, 61da0c8c3c, 36f9ccf0d7 (#10480).

All came from other agent sessions' PRs, whose platform sets that identity. CLAUDE.md § Git Conventions says "No AI attribution in commits or PRs … Commit and PR text should read as the user's own work". But scripts/check-commit-attribution.sh and the commit-msg hook grade message TEXT and the PR BODY only. The author field is ungraded, so these passed CI.

Options:
(a) Extend check-commit-attribution.sh, the CI arm, to refuse a commit whose author or committer email is noreply@anthropic.com. Cost: such PRs go red until their session sets its git identity, or until the PR is rebuilt with the author reset (as the mayor did for #10483, rebuilt from #10481).
(b) Accept the author field as outside the rule, and say so in CLAUDE.md.
(c) Leave it; the mayor resets authors case by case before merge.

Trunk history is NOT rewritten either way (same disposition as rf2-2e8f).

Mayor's recommendation: (a). It is enforcement of an existing rule rather than a new one, and the fix at the source is a one-line git identity setting in those sessions.
notes:
== INTERIM PRACTICE (mayor, 2026-09-26), pending Mike's ruling
Until this is ruled, the mayor applies option (c) case by case. Where another session's green PR carries commits authored "Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>", it is replayed onto a superseding PR with the author reset: content blob-identical, the original closed with a pointer, and its branch never force-pushed. Instances: #10481 -> #10483 (via worker rf2-0jz1b); #10487 -> #10513 (mayor replay, both commits, all 11 changed files blob-identical to 894439b9fc). Trunk history is not rewritten.
CORRECTION (mayor, same day): the #10487 -> #10513 replay changed 12 files, not 11. All 12 are blob-identical to 894439b9fc.

== INTERIM PRACTICE, third instance (mayor, 2026-09-26)
#10515 -> #10516: 4 commits, all 10 changed files blob-identical to 5953f58466, authors reset. The PR body also carried "_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_…)_", which the PR-guards check PASSED. That gap is filed separately as a guard bead: the trailing "_" defeats the "link at the end" shape.

== MIKE'S RULING (2026-09-26): OPTION (a), ENFORCE THE CHECK
Mike, in chat: "Yes, enforce the check." This DISCHARGES the HELD — OPERATOR DECISION marker at the top of this description. The bead is now dispatchable work under a decision already made.

What to build:
1. CI arm. scripts/check-commit-attribution.sh already grades the commits a PR introduces (merge-base..HEAD) and the PR body. Extend it to refuse any commit in that range whose AUTHOR or COMMITTER email is noreply@anthropic.com (and whose name is "Claude" with that email). Keep the shared-detector design: the matching lives in scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-commit-attribution.sh, and the CI script only chooses which text to grade. The failure message names the offending commits and the one-line remedy: set the session's git identity (git config user.name / user.email), or rebuild the branch with the author reset (git rebase --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit --reset-author' <base>), as #10483, #10513 and #10516 were.
2. Local arm. Refuse at commit time too, if cleanly possible. The commit-msg hook (or pre-commit) reads the ident git is about to use (git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT / GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT) and refuses noreply@anthropic.com. Say which hook you chose and why.
3. Tests, both ways, in scripts/git-hooks/test-pre-commit.sh (the layer-10 area) or the CI script's own tests:
   - a commit authored "Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>" is refused;
   - an ordinary author passes;
   - a commit whose MESSAGE merely mentions noreply@anthropic.com in prose still passes. It is the author field that is graded here; the message rules are unchanged.
4. CLAUDE.md § Git Conventions: add one sentence saying the author and committer email are graded too (this ruling). Operator-authorised by this ruling. CLAUDE.md is w/crlf, so apply item (e).

Out of scope: trunk history is NOT rewritten. The existing commits with that author are accepted, the same disposition as rf2-2e8f; the merge-base range already puts them behind every PR. .github/workflows/* is a hot zone: do not touch the job wiring unless the check cannot run without it, and if so STOP and report.
Consequence, accepted: another session's PR whose platform sets that identity goes red until its session sets a git identity or the branch is rebuilt. The mayor's interim replay practice ends once this merges.
Cluster: dispatch together with rf2-w1kma, the italic-wrapped generated-by body line that the detector misses. Same detector, same tests.

Built to Mike's ruling (a).
- CI arm, scripts/check-commit-attribution.sh: every commit in merge-base..HEAD has its recorded author and committer (%ae/%ce, not mailmapped) graded. The refusal names the sha, the identity, and the fix: git config user.name/user.email, then git rebase --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit --reset-author' <base>, then force-push the branch. title: Machine sub teardown leaks a spawned actor secret through :rf.sub/prev-value
description:
PR #10511 closes the live machine-sub trace leak but misses destruction of a spawned actor. Still reproduced on current origin/main fc45d9978c2d23bad1bc69e3a109c8299dfc1f17 using an isolated export of the committed core/machines sources (JVM, plain-atom adapter).

Reproduction: register :probe/type with {:sensitive [[:data :token]] :initial :idle :data {:token "AUDIT_SECRET_SENTINEL"} :states {:idle {}}}; spawn it via :rf.machine/spawn with :fixed-actor-id :probe/actor; hold and dereference (rf/subscribe [:rf/machine :probe/actor]); destroy :probe/actor through :rf.machine/destroy; dereference the held subscription again while capturing :rf.sub/run. The live value is present, the first trace redacts it, and the final value is nil, but the second trace contains the original secret in :rf.sub/prev-value. Probe produced exactly two sub-run traces; LIVE_VALUE_PRESENT=true, INITIAL_TRACE_REDACTED=true, DESTROYED_VALUE_NIL=true, DESTROY_PREV_VALUE_LEAKS=true (process exit 0).

Cause: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:258-274 drops the actor classification before removing the snapshot. implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:730-738 computes classification from the CURRENT registry and applies it to both value and prev-value. A spawned instance has no event registration under its actor id to supply the fallback, so the retained previous snapshot is emitted raw after its claims disappear. This defeats declared machine-data privacy on an ordinary teardown path; the added regression tests refresh a live actor but never destroy it.

Preserve enough classification for the previous snapshot when it is traced, reusing the existing projection mechanism. Do not retain dead actor registry entries indefinitely or redact the in-process value. Check explicit teardown and final-state completion through their shared lifecycle behavior.

Evidence: ai/probe-10511-current/probe.clj and ai/probe-10511-audit-sep23-monitor-1.log in audit-sep23-monitor; the reproduction above is standalone apart from the existing machine reset fixture. Source rf2-rgm64 remains closed and unchanged except its required forward pointer.
acceptance_criteria: A held subscription to a classified spawned actor emits no secret in either value or prev-value when the actor is destroyed. Regression asserts the initial live trace is classified, the destroyed value is nil, and the final previous value remains classified; cover the applicable final-state teardown too. In-process live reads remain raw, unclassified sibling values remain visible, and dead-actor claims are still removed.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #10598 (branch worker/machleak-85rta, commit 66017ecf8c on base fc45d9978c).

CAUSE (confirmed at source): teardown drops the actor's lowered :source :machine claims. Explicit destroy does it in destroy/teardown-live-actor! step 3; final state does it in finalize/finalize-machine, a SEPARATE lifecycle path with its own drop-at-destroy! call. After that, re-frame.classification/project-sub-tags classified the held [:rf/machine <id>] sub's :rf.sub/prev-value from the registry as it stood after the drop.

PREMISE CORRECTION: singletons leak too. reg-machine nests the spec under :rf/machine in the :event meta, so classification-when :event <id> finds no :sensitive and there is no registration fallback for any actor kind.

DECISIVE MEASUREMENT (JVM, plain-atom adapter): four regression cases in implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_sub_classification_test.clj — spawned or singleton, each with explicit destroy or final state.
- At base: 8 failures. Every failure is [:rf.sub/prev-value :data :token] = the sentinel, or the sentinel present in the sub trace. The live read is raw, the torn-down read nil, the claims present-then-removed, the live run redacted, the unclassified :note visible.
- Fixed: 7 tests / 67 assertions, 0 failures. That includes "no secret on any trace the teardown emits".
- Control on the committed tree:
  - removing the prior-claims union from the prev-value walk gives exit 1, 12 failures;
  - removing the layer-1 wrapper's prior-input hand-off gives exit 1, 12 failures.
  - Each restore was verified by blob hash against HEAD (classification.cljc da4fe98a8a, memo.cljc 89b15f3d57).

FIX: a prior value is classified by the registry that governed it.
- The layer-1 memo wrapper already holds the runtime-db it last read. The dev-gated :rf.sub/run emit carries it under the private :re-frame.classification/prev-inputs tag; production passes unset and allocates nothing.
- project-sub-tags unions the actor's snapshot claims from that runtime-db's [:rf.runtime/elision] into the prev-value walk only, reusing frame-snapshot-classification's re-rooting, then strips the tag.
- No dead-actor registry entry is retained, and the in-process value stays raw.
- Files: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc, implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc, and the test above. No spec change: Spec 005 already requires the machine sub's :rf.sub/prev-value to carry the machine's declared classification.

GATES:
- JVM machines: 1319/6169 at base, 1323/6217 final, 0 failures.
- JVM core: 2266/12368 at both base and final, 0 failures.
- Core prod gate: 1991/9022, 0 failures.
- routing 574/3688 and epoch 575/7532, 0 failures.
- Pinned clj-kondo errors 0.
- 33/33 always-on static checks plus lockstep: exit 0.
- CI on the head: 88 checks, 75 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed, CLJS :node-test and :browser-test included.

SIBLINGS FOUND, NOT FIXED (outside the fence, for the mayor to file). Both leak identically at base.
(1) Route read subs across a route change. Held [:rf/route] and [:rf.route/params], navigating from a route declaring :sensitive [[:params :secret]] to one declaring nothing: both :rf.sub/prev-value slots carry the secret. Route activation replaces the :source :route claims and the routing-owned projector walks against the live registry. The leaves are layer-2, so this carrier does not reach them.
(2) Epoch off-box egress with :rf.egress/include-runtime-db? true. After a destroy, the destroy record's :frame-state-before leaks the secret, and a record that projected clean while the actor lived leaks when re-projected. project-frame-state-slot walks a historic runtime-db against the live frame registry. The default profile does not leak.
UNMEASURED LEAD: resource and mutation read subs (:rf.resource/*, :rf/mutation …) are outside project-sub-tags' machine/route exceptions, and resources has no sub-trace projector.

title: docs(routing): JVM testing recipe imports the browser-only tutorial app
description:
Found during the merged-PR audit of #10483 (e7528bae81dddc37de6c94040f3e1e06a60d91b6); still present on origin/main 611f759f9a38bd449065a6e83e576616df17cc48.

docs/routing/testing.md:8-20 promises a JVM test namespace and requires [app.core], explicitly referring readers to the tutorial's complete articles app. That app (docs/routing/tutorial.md:488 onward) requires re-frame.adapter.reagent and contains browser boot/DOM code. The adapter exists only as implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs. A JVM cannot load that namespace. Keeping app.core as .cljs makes the first require fail; merely renaming it .cljc does not make its adapter or js/document calls loadable.

Verified with a bounded local JVM probe: clojure.string loads successfully; requiring re-frame.adapter.reagent with its absolute src directory on the classpath produces FileNotFoundException naming the missing reagent__init.class, reagent.clj and reagent.cljc. title: Epoch off-box export redacts historic app-db slots against the CURRENT classification registry, so a cleared flow's :sensitive output leaks under the DEFAULT profile
description:
Found by rf2-03jei's worker (PR #10603) as the app-db sibling of that fix. It is a CLAIM; reproduce it first.

MEASURED at trunk 71506fa86b, JVM, epoch artefact:
- A flow reg-flow ::out {:inputs [[:src]] :output-path [:out] :sensitive [[:token]]} derives {:token s :note "visible"}.
- [::seed secret] writes :src, and the flow writes [:out].
- While the flow is registered, (rf/project-egress record) under the DEFAULT profile gives [:db-after :out] = {:token :rf/redacted :note "visible"}.
- After (rf/clear :flow ::out), the live sensitive declarations read nil, and the SAME historic record re-projected gives [:db-after :out] = {:token <secret> :note "visible"}: the secret leaks under the DEFAULT profile.
- Note for a reproduction: the seed arg at [:src] is unclassified and carries the secret too, so probe [:db-after :out :token] itself rather than the whole record.

CAUSE: the same as rf2-03jei, on the app-db slots. They are projected against the frame's elision registry as it stands now, and removing an owner drops its claims:
- clearing a flow;
- route and resource owners reconciling (replace-owner-claims);
- an event's declassifying effect.
Meanwhile the ring still holds values those claims governed.

rf2-03jei fixed only the runtime-db partition under :rf.egress/include-runtime-db?, in implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc. It added redact-by-recorded-registry, which redacts a recorded partition by the registry that partition itself carries (:rf.runtime/elision) before the live walk. Each frame-state carries its registry, so the app-db slots can take theirs from the same record:
- :db-before and :frame-state-before :rf.db/app from :frame-state-before's runtime partition;
- :db-after, :frame-state-after :rf.db/app and the t1/t2 :rf.event/db trace slots from :frame-state-after's.

Surface: implementation/epoch (the egress projection). The fix must:
- keep no dead registry entries;
- leave the in-process value unredacted;
- redact a historic value by the classification that applied when it was recorded.

Whether a deliberate DECLASSIFICATION (an event effect clearing a claim) should also stay redacted on older records follows from that principle: the value was recorded while classified. Say so if you find it is a real choice.

A regression goes red at base, with a control showing the live-flow projection redacted.
notes:
== MAYOR ROUTING AND RULING 2026-09-29 12:09 AUSEST ==

ROUTING: rf2-hakdt goes to the live epoch worker (worker/epoch-03jei, draft PR #10603), as an addition to its dispatch. The reasons:
- It is the same file (`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc`) and has the same cause.
- It builds directly on the `redact-by-recorded-registry` helper that PR adds.
- A second worker would collide with it in that file.

RULING on the declassification question the description leaves open: a value recorded while classified STAYS REDACTED on that record, even after a later event effect deliberately declassifies it. A record projects under the classification that applied when it was recorded. That is the principle behind rf2-03jei and behind rf2-85rta's `:rf.sub/prev-value` fix (PR #10598), and declassification is not an exception to it. A declassifying effect changes how LATER values classify, never how earlier records egress. No choice remains here, so this needs no stop.

title: Xray cannot show a hydration mismatch: :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch carries :frame but no dispatch id, so neither the per-frame ring nor Xray's frameless ring retains it
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #10604 (commit "fix(xray): keep a hydration mismatch in Xray's buffer").

Reproduced at tip, the framework half by a JVM probe. A real :rf/hydrate with server hash "deadbeef" on frame :app was followed by verify-hydration! outside any dispatch:
- the emitted :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch carried [:tags :frame] = :app and no :rf.trace/dispatch-id;
- (rf/trace-buffer :app {:flat true}) held 7 events and 0 mismatches;
- a trace listener received 1.

The Xray half, read at source: trace_collector's frameless-event? pushed an event to the secondary ring only when it carried NEITHER a frame NOR a dispatch id. push-to-ring! keeps an event only when it carries BOTH. A frame-carrying, dispatch-less event therefore fell between them.

OWNER: Xray's intake, not core's retention.
- Spec 009's B3 rule is that events outside a run never enter the per-frame rings, and those rings are keyed by run. Keeping the event in core would change a hot-zone contract, and the event would still group under :ungrouped.
- Xray's own spec 013 already listed :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch among the events its secondary ring must hold. The defect was the predicate diverging from the ring condition it exists to complement.
- So no change to spec/009 or spec/011 was needed.

FIX:
- trace_collector.cljs: the predicate is now outside-frame-rings?, (not (and dispatch-id frame)), the exact complement of push-to-ring!'s condition. The old name has 0 references left in the tree; the control, the new name, finds 2.
- tools/xray/spec/013 and the namespace docs say the same.
- The mismatch now lands in the :ungrouped bundle, and l2-timeline/event-bundle-has-issue? reads it as an issue. With "Show :ungrouped pseudo-event-bundle events in L2" on (Settings → General), it appears as a pink-washed <no event> row.
- docs/xray/07-hydration.md now says how to find it.

REGRESSION: a-hydration-mismatch-reaches-xrays-buffer (preload_cljs_test, node lane). It calls the real rf.ssr/verify-hydration! and asserts:
- the per-frame ring skips the mismatch (precondition);
- Xray's buffer keeps exactly 1;
- it names :rf/default and has no dispatch id;
- it groups under :ungrouped as an issue.
With the fix reverted (base blob a75e794ae7): red, 4 failures ("Xray's buffer keeps it" read 0), and the precondition held. Restored (blob 0b59e018b9 == HEAD): green. Whole-lane totals: 12533 tests / 66235 assertions at exit 1 with 21 failures (all this PR's four new tests), then exit 0 with 0 failures.

REMAINING DESIGN QUESTION, not decided here: the row shows THAT a mismatch happened but not its hashes. Focusing :ungrouped settles no epoch, so Epoch and Trace show "The selected event settled no epoch.", and the details stay on listeners and :observability :errors sinks. Whether a panel should render the :ungrouped bucket's events is a design call.

Docs gates: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, mkdocs build --strict exit 0. Both were shown red on a broken link planted in 07-hydration.md, and the restore was verified by blob hash.

title: Route URL strings on navigation traces carry a declared-sensitive PATH param raw, while :rf.route/planned's :url redacts the sensitive QUERY in the same string
description:
Found by rf2-kuyza's worker (PR #10602, merged at trunk 194eb336f7) while searching for siblings of the prev-value leak. It has a different cause, so it was listed rather than fixed. It is a CLAIM; reproduce it first.

REPORTED: navigate to a route declaring `:sensitive [[:params :secret] [:query :token]]`, with a secret path param and a secret query value.
- The `:rf.route/planned` trace's `:url` redacts the query value but carries the path segment holding `:secret` RAW.
- The `[:rf.route/handle-url-change url]` event traces carry the whole URL string raw, path secret included.
- The routing code documents URL strings as deliberately visible on those traces.

THE QUESTION THIS BEAD ASKS: which half is right? A single `:url` field currently treats two declarations from ONE `:sensitive` vector differently. The query half is redacted and the path half is not. That inconsistency is the defect, whatever the documented intent.

title: Spec 016's canonical infinite-feed example declares an envelope path its items never reach
description:
Found while fixing rf2-cudar (PR #10624). Spec 016's canonical infinite-feed registration example (§Infinite resources and load-more feeds, §Registration — `:infinite`) pairs `:page->items :items` and enveloped pages (`:next-page-param` reads `[:page-info :next-cursor]`, so a page is `{:items [...] :page-info {...}}`) with `:sensitive [[:data :author-email]]`. Its comment says the index-free walk matches `[:data <page-idx> :author-email]`, so the field redacts on every page. But `:author-email` is an ITEM field, and the declaration names a page-envelope key no page carries. Index-free walking skips sequence positions, not map keys, so the declaration never reaches an item, on the durable pages or on any carrier derived from them.

Measured on the JVM at trunk 1c338d310c with re-frame.classification/redact-with-paths in index-free mode (the reading the sub projector and the continuation reply use) over `[{:items [{:author-email SECRET :text "hi"}] :page-info {:next-cursor "c1"}}]`:
- declaration path `[:author-email]` (the example's, `:data` head stripped): value UNCHANGED, secret raw;
- control `[:items :author-email]`: `:author-email :rf/redacted`.

A reader copying the canonical example gets a declaration that protects nothing. The fix is probably `[[:data :items :author-email]]` in the example and its comment, plus a check of any sentence restating it (the same page's per-page classification bullet and SSR bullet say `[:data :field]` matches `[:data <page-idx> :field]`, which is true of a vector page only). spec/016-Resources.md is outside the rf2-cudar dispatch fence, hence this item.

title: Epoch record-sub-run! files a late subscription run under whichever epoch settled last, so a run-step's sub runs appear on the next epoch
description:
RULED BY MIKE 2026-09-29 - option B (honest provenance). Dispatchable; the ruling and scope are in the notes.

Found by rf2-2tt74's worker (PR #10593, merged at trunk 9862875b7c) while fixing its item 5 (misfiled Xray rows). The cause is in core, outside that fence. It is a CLAIM; reproduce it first.

In `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/listeners.cljc`, `record-sub-run!` files a late subscription run under the epoch that settled LAST, not the epoch whose event caused it.

Reported reproduction: the run-step epoch shows sub runs `[]`, and the following increment-fx epoch shows `[:rf.runner/step]`. The misfiled rows come from the PRECEDING run-step, not the following one as rf2-2tt74 item 5 first said.

Fix it so a sub run is filed under the epoch that caused it, or, if that is not knowable, so the record is honest about where it came from. If the choice between those is a real design question, stop and report it rather than choosing.

A regression goes red at base. Xray's Epoch panel reads these rows, so check that no Xray test pins the misfiled shape. If one does, flip it in the same change and rename it: never loosen it.
notes:
== WORKER PASS 2026-09-29 (worker/epoch-03jei): REPRODUCED, then STOPPED as a design question. No fix landed; PR #10603 carries only rf2-03jei.

REPRODUCTION (trunk 71506fa86b, JVM, epoch artefact, plain-atom substrate):
- Setup: two layer-1 subs, ::step reading :step and ::count reading :count. Both are held and deref'd once.
- [::run-step 1] writes :step and returns :fx [[:dispatch [::inc]]]; ::inc bumps :count.
- dispatch-sync drains both events (epoch 2 = run-step, epoch 3 = inc) before anything derefs.
- The post-settle deref recomputes both subs with no cascade in flight, so capture routes both :rf.sub/run events to record-sub-run!, which files them under last-settled-epoch-id = 3.
- Ring rows as [sub-id value-changed? cause-event-id]:
  - epoch 2: :sub-runs []
  - epoch 3: [[::step true nil] [::count true nil]]
- ::step's value changed in epoch 2 and ::count's in epoch 3. This matches the reported Xray shape: the run-step epoch shows [], the increment epoch shows [:rf.runner/step].

WHY IT IS NOT KNOWABLE FROM WHAT THE EPOCH LAYER RECEIVES:
- A layer-1 :db reader depends on the whole app-db container, and both epochs changed it.
- Each sub recomputes ONCE, against epoch 3's db.
- :rf.sub/cause-event-id is omitted post-settle.
- The row carries only sub-id, query-v, prev-value, value and value-changed?.
- The two runs arrive carrying the same kind of information. Telling ::step (epoch 2) from ::count (epoch 3) needs what each BODY reads, and only running the body can tell that.
- Any rule over the dirty window files one of the two wrong:
  - last-settled (today) files ::step under 3;
  - first-epoch-since-last-run files ::count under 2.
- Coupling: state/resolve-render-epoch attributes a late render to the newest epoch carrying a value-changed sub-run in the view's read-set. So a view reading ::step follows the misfiled row, and any option must carry :renders along.

OPTIONS (not chosen):
A. RE-EVALUATE.
   - When a post-settle run has value-changed? true and its window spans more than one epoch, run the sub body against each window epoch's recorded :db-after, newest-first.
   - File the run under the newest epoch whose value differs from its predecessor's.
   - Exact for layer-1 subs. Layer-2 subs need their input subs' values per epoch, so the evaluation recurses.
   - Cost: it runs user sub code inside the debug capture path, with its traces suppressed. The window start is the epoch of the sub's previous run, read from the ring while it is retained.
B. HONEST PROVENANCE.
   - Keep filing under last-settled, but stamp the post-settle row and its trace with where it came from, e.g. a deferred flag plus the epoch window it reflects.
   - Xray would render it as "recomputed after epochs N..M".
   - This is a contract change: the :sub-runs row in Spec-Schemas :rf/epoch-record and :rf.sub/run in Spec 009 (both hot zones), plus the Xray consumer (tools/xray, held this tick).
C. FILE UNDER THE FIRST EPOCH OF THE WINDOW.
   - Fixes the runner case, and breaks the symmetric one (a child event that changes the sub's value).
   - Not recommended.
The worker's lean is B (no user code in tooling, and honest), but the choice is Mike's.

title: epoch attribution: three back-fill routes unexercised; two tests cannot reach their named fault
description:
Owner: rf2-98kzs.14 (found while pruning implementation/epoch/test; not fixed there).

Epoch attribution: three post-settle back-fill routes are never exercised, and two tests cannot reach the fault they name.

- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/capture.cljc` routes `render-ops` (`:rf.view/render`, `:rf.view/rendered`, `:rf.view/rendered-cap-reached`) and `sub-run-ops` (`:rf.sub/run`, `:rf.sub/skip`) to back-fill when no cascade is in flight. MEASURED: a search of `implementation/epoch/test` for these ops being emitted finds `:rf.view/render` and `:rf.sub/skip` only in prose. `:rf.view/rendered-cap-reached` is emitted only by `epoch_run_cause_test.clj`, which seeds the capture buffer directly and so never reaches the back-fill route. The ns header of `epoch_attribution_test.clj` and its INVARIANT 2 banner both say `:rf.view/render` is back-filled, but every render emit in that suite is `:rf.view/rendered`.
- `re-frame.epoch-attribution-test/qh13yf-back-fill-splices-target-by-id-not-stale-index` claims immunity to an append landing between back-fill's index lookup and its splice. The test is single-threaded, and it evicts before calling the back-fill. So an implementation that resolves the index on one deref and splices on a second would still pass. The race is reachable only through the concurrency stress test.
- `re-frame.epoch-attribution-test/inv-6c-bound-stranded-marker-cleared-by-terminal-path` half (b) claims the rejected-dispatch path clears a stranded marker. It drives the 1-arity `harvest-buffer-for-event!` (a nil settling id, which means a full clear). No production caller uses that arity: `settle!` passes the envelope id, and the 2-arity no-run-start branch keeps markers that carry a foreign id.

Fix shape: add one post-settle emit test each for `:rf.view/render`, `:rf.view/rendered-cap-reached` and `:rf.sub/skip`, drive inv-6c half (b) through the real settle path, and narrow the qh13yf docstring to what a single thread can show.

title: Fresco error-boundary: :on-error fires twice when a :reset-key change and the child throw land in the same render
description:
## Symptom (reported from reading the source while writing docs/api/re-frame.fresco.md's live cell, PR #10806; not yet pinned by a test)

`h/error-boundary` documents `:on-error` as fired **once per caught failure** (the props table in implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/boundary.cljs). The report describes a case that fires it TWICE: the `:reset-key` change and the child's throw happen in the SAME render.

1. The child throws under the new key, and React catches it: `getDerivedStateFromError`, then `componentDidCatch`, which fires `:on-error` (first report).
2. The boundary's update check then sees a `:reset-key` that differs from the previous props, and treats it as a retry. It clears the failure it has just caught and re-mounts the children.
3. The child throws again, which is a second catch and a second `:on-error`. This time the key is unchanged, so the fallback stays.

This is the pattern docs/api/re-frame.fresco.md's own static example teaches, `:reset-key (h/sub [:chart/query])`, whenever changing the query is what breaks the chart. A failure recorder then logs two failures for one, and the child renders an extra time.

## Want

`:on-error` fires once when a reset-key change and a throw land in the same render. A reset means "the key changed SINCE the failure was caught", so the reset check should compare against the key the failure was caught under, not against the previous props. Keep the change minimal and in the boundary's own vocabulary. The docstring's "Once per failure, and why that needs NO flag" section must stay true, or be corrected if the fix changes its reasoning.

## Verify

First add a DOM test beside `arm1_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test/the-boundary-reports-once-under-strictmode` that changes `:reset-key` and makes the child throw in the same update, and reads one `:on-error` record. It must go red on today's code before the fix. If it does not, the premise is false: close this bead with the measurement. Then fix it, and keep the existing boundary tests green.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #10807 (fix(fresco): report a failure once when a reset-key change and a throw share a render).

MECHANISM: React 19.3 commits a class in this order: componentDidUpdate first, then the componentDidCatch callback. So in the commit that caught, the boundary's reset check compared the new :reset-key against the previous props. It read the move as a retry, cleared the failure it had just caught, re-mounted the child, and reported the second throw as a second failure. FIX in implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/boundary.cljs: componentDidUpdate acts only while a failure is standing. A failure first seen in this commit (prevState carried no error) was caught under the current key, so the boundary adopts that key instead of comparing against it. Only a later move of the key clears the failure. The constructor's initial key still covers a failure caught at mount, because that commit runs no componentDidUpdate. The docstring's once-per-failure section now explains the reset half.

MEASURED in the browser lane: new row a-reset-key-move-and-a-throw-in-one-render-report-once in implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs, beside the StrictMode row. With the fix reverted, the scoped run exited 1, with 2 failures, both in the new row: one dispatch that moved the key and broke the child gave ["the child threw" "the child threw"], so the premise holds. With the fix restored (boundary.cljs blob hash matched HEAD), the scoped run exited 0 at 12 tests and 60 assertions. Full lane: baseline at merge base 263b576687 was 1118 tests / 6247 assertions; with the change it was 1119 / 6253, exit 0.

STALE CITATION corrected in the same PR: the docstring cited arm1_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test/the-boundary-reports-once-under-strictmode. That test is in bench/ and runs against the bench's donor copy of the class. The docstring now cites boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test/the-boundary-reports-once-per-failure-under-strictmode, which runs against the shipped class.

NOT DONE HERE: the bench copy (bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/fresco/arm1/boundary.cljs) has the same componentDidUpdate. docs/api/re-frame.fresco.md is left to the docs change.

title: resources SSR: Spec 016 says the blocking drain waits on ledger records, but it gates on entry status and its timeout settle leaves the work-ledger row :running
description:
## Spec 016 says the SSR drain waits on ledger records; the drain gates on entry status, and its timeout settle leaves the row :running

Found while checking rf2-ve6xq item 2 at source (trunk d3d70679d9).

**What the spec says, in two places that disagree.**
- Spec 016 §Frame work ledger, in the ledger's Read API row, names "SSR's blocking-drain wait point" as one of the ledger's readers. The ledger section also says "SSR *waits on* blocking ledger records server-side".
- Spec 016 §SSR and hydration (server route handling) says "drain until blocking resources for the current nav-token settle".

**What the code does.** `re-frame.resources.ssr/drain-blocking-resources!` loops on `blocking-settled?`, which is `entry-settled?` over each blocking entry: the entry `:status` is `:loaded` or `:error`. It never reads the work ledger. That matches §SSR and hydration, not §Frame work ledger.

**Where the two readings diverge.** On the ordinary reply paths the entry and its row settle in one write (`succeeded-handler` / `failed-handler`), so gating on either gives the same answer. They split on the timeout path. `settle-blocking-timeout` settles each unsettled blocking entry to a first-load failure through `entry-failed`, which clears `:current-work`. It never touches the work-ledger row. Measured on the JVM with a scratch test: a real `:rf.resource/ensure` on a `:server` frame, a blocking slot for its nav-token, then the drain with a no-op pump and a clock that jumps past a 50 ms deadline. Results: drain `{:settled? false}`; entry `:status :error`, `:current-work nil`; work-ledger row `:status :running`; host handle still present. The row stays live until a late reply is stale-suppressed or the frame is destroyed. The ledger has a terminal `:timed-out` status that this path never uses.

**Decision needed (one of):**
1. Reword the two §Frame work ledger sentences to say the drain gates on the blocking entries' settled status, as §SSR and hydration and the code do. Then decide separately whether the timeout settle should also mark the row terminal.
2. Keep the ledger wording, and make the timeout settle mark the row `:timed-out` and clear its host handle, so a released render leaves no live row on any path.

**Owners.** spec/016-Resources.md; implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/ssr.cljc (`settle-blocking-timeout`, `drain-blocking-resources!`). The test prose in `resources_ssr_cljs_test.cljc` §2c was corrected under rf2-ve6xq to describe the code as it is (gating on entry status).
notes:
== RULING (mayor, 2026-10-03 ~20:15 AUSEST): take BOTH halves; this is not either/or.

1. **Code.** `settle-blocking-timeout` marks each timed-out blocking entry's work-ledger row with the ledger's terminal `:timed-out` status and releases its host handle, in the same write as `entry-failed`. A released render then leaves no live row on any path. A late reply stays stale-suppressed as it is today. Add a JVM test beside the scratch measurement in this bead: after a timeout drain, the row is `:timed-out` and the handle is gone.
2. **Spec.** Reword the two spec/016 §Frame work ledger sentences to describe what the drain does. It gates on the blocking entries' settled status, which is what §SSR and hydration already says. Every path, timeout included, leaves the ledger row terminal. Drop "SSR's blocking-drain wait point" from the ledger's readers unless the code reads it.

Why both: the ledger already defines `:timed-out`, so a path that never uses it is the defect. Gating the drain on entry status is simpler than gating it on the ledger, and it is what the code and the other spec section say. One small PR.

FENCE: start after PR #10809 (rf2-ve6xq, resources-cluster) merges, because both touch resources_ssr_cljs_test.cljc.
== DONE (worker kqur5): PR #10813, both halves of the ruling

**Code (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/ssr.cljc).** `settle-blocking-timeout` now also returns `:timed-out-work`: the `:current-work` ids of the unsettled blocking entries it fails. `entry-failed` clears that pointer, so this return value is the only record of those ids. `drain-blocking-resources!` then makes one `swap-runtime-db!`. In it, the failed `:entries` are installed and each abandoned row is settled through the ledger's own transition, `rf.resources.work-ledger/settle-terminal`, with status `:timed-out` and outcome `{:reason :ssr-blocking-timeout :limit-ms <deadline>}` (it marks the row and prunes the terminal tail). After the swap, the drain calls `rf.resources.work-ledger/clear-handle!` for each one. That is the same settle-terminal plus clear-handle! pairing every reply handler uses. `opportunistic-abort!` was not used: the ruling keeps a late reply stale-suppressed as it is today, and the managed-HTTP artefact's own frame-destroy hook still aborts the in-flight request. No `#?(:cljs ...)` branch changed.

**Spec (spec/016-Resources.md, Frame work ledger).**
- The work-ledger Read API row, before: "Xray's live work-ledger table per frame, SSR's blocking-drain wait point, and the resource runtime's join/dedupe logic." After: "Xray's live work-ledger table per frame and the resource runtime's join/dedupe logic."
- The Cancellation paragraph, before: "SSR and tools observe the ledger projection, not host handles. SSR *waits on* blocking ledger records server-side, but the hydration payload serializes only ...". After: "Tools observe the ledger projection, not host handles. The SSR blocking drain does not read the ledger: it gates on the blocking entries' settled status (SSR and hydration), and every way out of it leaves those entries' ledger rows terminal. A reply settles an entry and its row in one write; the render-deadline timeout settles each abandoned attempt's row `:timed-out` in the same write that fails its entry, and clears its host handle. A released render therefore leaves no live work behind it. The hydration payload serializes only ...".

title: re-frame-migration: preserve existing completion handlers in the bridge recipe (GH #10829)
description:
skills/re-frame-migration/references/orchestrating-a-large-migration.md section 3 (near line 72) has the consuming worker register (rf/reg-event :config-loaded (fn [_ ev] {:fx [[:dispatch (into [:app/boot] [ev])]]})) in its own file, and migration/from-re-frame-v1/async-flow-fx-to-reg-machine.md (near line 141) repeats it. Registration keeps one handler per kind/id (events.cljc reg-event, registrar.cljc assoc-in), so a second registration replaces or collides with an existing substantive handler instead of composing with it. Make ownership explicit: when a real completion handler exists, its owning unit adds the addressed dispatch there, preserving body, interceptors and effect order, and publishes that in the coordination contract. A standalone forwarding registration is valid only for an ID that is genuinely unowned in the selected image. Keep child-actor completion routing as another option. Acceptance: both passages distinguish an unowned forwarding event from an existing completion handler. Give one worked example in which the existing handler's app-db update and effects still occur exactly once while the machine receives the payload, covering the several-consumer case without duplicate registrations. Shares async-flow-fx-to-reg-machine.md with GH #10832.

Filed from a consumer migration run. The full body (evidence links, suggested fix, acceptance line) is on the GitHub issue. Mayor triage 2026-10-04: valid, action it. The issue closes when its PR merges (PR body carries `Fixes #10829`). Posture: a proportionate correction in the existing voice and structure, not a rewrite. Trust the programmer, and don't litigate minutiae.

title: instruction_packet: a TAB- or space-numbered quote is refused when the quoted line begins with - | : . ) ] or the arrow
description:
Found while working rf2-6wnd0 (PR #10972). scripts/instruction_packet.py quote_matches() tolerates a line-number prefix on a quoted sentinel line, and its docstring names `37<TAB>text` as one of the tolerated forms. But a TAB- or space-separated prefix is REFUSED whenever the line itself begins with one of the separator characters in the prefix class [\t:|.)\]→-]. Markdown bullets ("- ...") and table rows ("| ...") are the common cases.

CAUSE. The pattern is `\s*{n}\s*(?:[\t:|.)\]→-]|\s)(.*)$`. In "304<TAB>- **Scope ...", the greedy `\s*` after the number consumes the TAB, and the class then consumes the line's own leading "-". re.match returns that first successful match without backtracking, so the captured text has lost its "-" and its hash misses.

MEASURED at the base of PR #10972 (line "- **Scope a plant to the NAMESPACE", n=304). The bare line is accepted. "304<TAB>- ...", "   304<TAB>- ..." (the cat -n shape of a numbered file view) and "304 - ..." are all REFUSED. "304: - ..." and "304→- ..." are accepted, and so is "304<TAB>plain text line" on a line that does not begin with a separator character.

EFFECT. A worker that faithfully copies a bullet or table sentinel out of a TAB-numbered view gets "quoted line(s) [N] do not match the packet: re-read it whole and quote again; if they still do not match, STOP and report". The same copy fails again, so this is the same harmless-reader-artefact-to-inline-redispatch class as GH #10971. PR #10972's UTF-8 read prints `N: text`, which the current pattern accepts for every line shape, so that route is unaffected.

LIKELY FIX (small). Accept the quote if either reading's remainder hashes right: the separator-class form `\s*{n}\s*[class](.*)$`, or the whitespace-only form `\s*{n}\s+(.*)$`. Add a self-test check that quotes a "- " line and a "| " line with a TAB prefix.
notes:
== RESULT (worker quotefix, PR #10974)
Reproduced at base through the real verify --quotes CLI on a scratch 400-line packet. A `- ` bullet (line 304) and a `| ` table row (line 12) were REFUSED under the N<TAB>, three-space-indented N<TAB>, cat -n and `N ` prefixes. Both were accepted bare, as `N: ` and as `N→`, and a plain line was accepted under all seven forms. After the fix, all 21 quotes are accepted.
OLD pattern: a single re.match of \s*{n}\s*(?:[\t:|.)\]→-]|\s)(.*)$
NEW pattern: two readings, each tried on its own, and the quote passes if either remainder hashes right. The separator reading is \s*{n}\s*[:|.)\]→-](.*)$ and the whitespace reading is \s*{n}\s+(.*)$. The line number is still matched literally under both. The docstring lists exactly these forms.
SELF-TEST: 27/27 (exit 0) at base, 32/32 (exit 0) after. The 5 new checks are TAB-, cat -n- and space-numbered acceptance of a bullet and a table row, wrong-text refusal under every prefix form, and right-text refusal under a wrong line number (n+1 and 10n). The two lines are tested one at a time, and the refusal must name only the wrong line.
PLANTS (each restored and verified by default-form blob hash against HEAD; none committed): the old pattern planted back scored 27/32 (exit 1), with all 5 new checks failing. A number-agnostic plant (\d+ for {n}) scored 31/32, with only the wrong-number check failing. A text-agnostic plant scored 31/32, with only the wrong-text check failing.

title: Test-suite pruning, third pass: every unit-test surface, cut to the smallest suite that catches the same bugs
description:
MIKE'S INSTRUCTIONS (2026-10-05)

This is the prompt as Mike pasted it. The paste was clipped at the right margin on about a dozen lines and stopped after "Prove it"; those line ends, the Report section and the closing paragraph are restored from the prompt he was given in the same session.

For each distinct unit test surface, create a bead for that surface which prunes the unit tests (do not change the code under test). LLMs tend to create too many unit tests.

Assume the suite has more tests than it needs. Many were generated in bulk, so several tests check the same behaviour, some check nothing the code could get wrong, and some pin implementation details and fail on harmless refactors. Every test costs CI time and reading time, and the redundant ones hide the tests that matter. I want the smallest suite that still catches every bug the current one catches.

Work in this order:
1. Run the suite and record the result: tests, assertions, failures.
2. Read the code under test and list the behaviours it promises its callers: normal results, each boundary, each promised failure, and any past bug the tests refer to.
3. Map every existing test to the behaviour it checks. Most of the pruning shows up in this map: behaviours with five tests, and tests with no behaviour.
4. Decide each test: keep, merge or delete.
5. Run the suite again and prove the pruned suite still catches bugs (see "Prove it").

Decide with one question: if this test were deleted, what bug could ship that no remaining test would catch? If you cannot name one, delete it.

Delete:
- A test another test implies. If A cannot pass while B fails, drop B.
- Extra examples of one behaviour that take the same path through the code.
- Tests of the language, a library or the framework: a constructor sets a field, a getter returns it, a map holds the key just put in it.
- Tests that pin how the code works instead of what it does: private helpers, call order, internal data shapes, greps of source text, and log or error wording that is not part of the contract.
- Tests whose expected value is computed by the same logic as the code under test.
- Assertions that a mock returned what it was told to return.
- Tests of code that has no logic in it.

Merge:
- Tests that vary one input become one table-driven test. Keep the boundary rows and drop the mid-range ones.
- One test per field of a result becomes one test asserting the whole result.
- Tests that repeat the same setup for one assertion each become one test.

Keep, however small:
- The only test of a behaviour.
- A test for a boundary that takes a different path: empty, one, many; zero; the limit and one past it.
- A test of a failure the caller is promised.
- A regression test for a bug that actually happened.
When a weak test and a strong test overlap, keep the strong one: the one that would fail on more bugs.

Do not:
- Weaken an assertion to make a merge easier.
- Delete a test because it fails, is slow or is flaky. Report it.
- Rewrite surviving tests for style. Rename one only when its name no longer says what it asserts, and first check that nothing matches on the name, such as a CI filter or a skip list.
- Leave unused helpers or fixtures behind.
- Add new tests. If you find a behaviour with no test, report it.
If anything pins test counts or names, such as a count floor or a roster, update it in the same change. Commit one file or module at a time, so each prune can be reviewed against its code.

Prove it:
- The suite passes before and after. Report both sets of counts.
- For each group of deletions, break the code in a place a deleted test used to guard and confirm a surviving test fails. Then restore the code. If nothing fails, you removed real coverage: put the test back.

Report:
- Before and after: tests, assertions, lines.
- Deleted tests, grouped by reason. For each, name the surviving test that covers it, or say why it guarded nothing.
- Merges: what went into what.
- Tests you considered deleting but kept, and why.
- Which breaks you planted and which test caught each.
- Gaps: behaviours with no test.

If you are unsure whether a behaviour is still covered, keep the test and say so. Losing coverage of a real behaviour is the one mistake that matters more than leaving an extra test in.

== HOW THIS PASS RUNS (worker session, 2026-10-05)

THIS IS THE THIRD PASS. The first ran under rf2-98kzs (implementation/), rf2-3h7v2 (tools/) and rf2-by74t (bench, skills, migration, scripts). The second ran under rf2-zbnoc and closed on 2026-10-04 with all 49 children done. Each cut roughly a tenth, and the second proved its removals with planted faults. Every child of this epic carries the second pass's close reason for its surface: its final counts are your likely baseline, and its plants are evidence you can reuse.

WHAT CHANGES FROM THE SECOND PASS. The second pass ran under "assume existing coverage is excellent" and protected whole categories by rule. This pass runs under "assume the suite has more tests than it needs", and its rule has no protected category. So:

- No keep-by-rule. Every test answers the deletion question, including the kinds the second pass kept by rule: tests pinning docs or spec wording, gate and ratchet self-tests, tests of documented error ids, security and privacy tests, and tests cited by name elsewhere. This is the worker session's reading of the 2026-10-05 instruction, and Mike may reverse it.
- Those kinds look weak and usually are not, because the bug they catch is not in the code under test. A guide-truth or terminology test catches prose drifting from the code. A gate self-test catches a gate that can no longer fail. A redaction test catches a leak. For these, "the code" you break in a plant is the thing they guard: the doc sentence, the gate, the redaction. The last test guarding one of them stays. A second test that goes red on the same plant may go.
- "Greps of source text" in the delete list means a test that reads the implementation's own source to pin how it is written. That goes when a behavioural test catches the same change. It does not mean a test that holds documentation or spec prose to the code.
- A keep recorded in an earlier pass is not binding by itself: decide it again with the question. A plant result recorded there (test X was the only red for fault Y) is evidence and stands.
- Expect less than the earlier passes found. If the map in step 3 shows nothing left to cut, close the child with no PR and say what you checked. That is a good result. Do not manufacture removals.

SCOPE. Unit tests only. Gate-shaped harnesses are out: e2e, acceptance, feature-matrix, live and integration harnesses, and the docs playground smoke. Three tiny surfaces have no child because two passes reviewed them and found nothing to change: the docs pilot tests, implementation/spec-resource (3 tests) and the skills/reagent-migration and skills/re-frame2 fixtures.

REPO MECHANICS (each measured or ruled in an earlier pass):
- Step 1 also confirms that a runner executes each file in scope, and which lane: JVM `clojure -M:test`, :node-test, :browser-test, a production gate, `node --test`, `bb`, or a Python `--self-test`. A file no runner executes cannot be pruned on evidence. Report it.
- A .cljc test that runs on both the JVM and ClojureScript is not a duplicate. Neither is a pair covering platform-specific code.
- Batches. Work in small batches by contract group. Before each, predict the change in test and assertion counts from the diff. After it, run the lane and confirm the counts moved by exactly that much. The quiet reporter does not list namespaces, so the count delta is how you know your tests ran.
- Names. Before a test name leaves, search the repo for it three ways: fixed-string, whitespace-collapsed and comment-stripped. A test cited by name in a spec, a doc, another test, a workflow or a roster stays unless the citation moves in the same change.
- Count floors. Some production gates carry a test-count floor (RF2_MIN_TESTS: core, routing, ssr, epoch). Prune on evidence, then as the branch's last commit set the floor to the lane's new observed count minus 35, in a commit of its own that gives the before and after counts. Never lower a floor without deletions beside it. If another in-flight child shares the floor file, tell the coordinator first.
- Hot zones. Do not edit implementation/deps.edn, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn or .github/workflows/* in a pruning PR. If test wiring must change, stop and report.
- The shadow-cljs lane. JVM lanes run freely. For CLJS counts, the PR's CI whole-lane :node-test delta against its base replaces a local lane window for anything CI compiles. A plant in CLJS-only code needs a local run: ask the coordinator for the lane and do all such plants in one window.
- Plants. Never commit or push a plant. After each, restore the file and confirm it matches the committed blob (`git diff --quiet HEAD -- <path>`).
- Parallel. Children run in parallel, because each owns one surface's test directory plus at most its own gate's floor line. A child that would touch another surface's tests stops and tells the coordinator.
- One worktree and one PR per child, babysat to green. Production code untouched. No .beads paths and no AI attribution in commits or the PR (CLAUDE.md).
- The report goes in the PR body and, as a summary, in the child's close reason: baseline to final per lane, per-batch predicted and measured deltas, each removal with its reason and cover, the plants and what each turned red, what you considered and kept, and gaps noticed. A gap or defect gets one line and is not filed.

ORDER. Largest suites first: tools/xray (four sub-areas), tools/story (four), implementation/core (five), then machines, fresco, implementation/scripts, re-frame2-pair-mcp, adapters, resources, machines-viz, bench/fresco, ssr, routing, http, epoch, schemas, mcp-base, story-mcp, ssr-ring, flows, ssr-node, mcp-conformance, and the small clusters the second pass also shipped as one PR each.
notes:
== RULING (mayor, 2026-10-05 09:20:04 AUSEST): citations in dated, commit-pinned findings snapshots do NOT keep a test.
The description's rule ("A test cited by name in a spec, a doc, another test, a workflow or a roster stays unless the citation moves in the same change") protects LIVE pointers - text a reader follows to the current tree, which a deletion would turn false. A findings document that pins a trunk commit in its header (for example spec/findings/resources-parity-2026-09/fable/evidence/scorecard-verification.md and its astra/evidence/sibling-review/round-1/ copy, pinned at bc371a9609) records what was true at that commit; its file:line citations still resolve there, so deleting the test makes no live text false. Earlier passes already removed tests that file names, and nothing outside spec/findings links to it. So such a citation is not a reason to keep a test, and spec/ stays outside the worker fence (no edit to the snapshot). Each child that deletes a test named only in such a snapshot lists the affected names in its PR body. A citation in a findings document that does NOT pin a commit, or that a live doc, spec page or roster links to as current, still binds under the description's rule.
close_reason:
All 38 children closed, each through merged work: 39 PRs (rf2-n6gq4.18, implementation/adapters, landed as two, #10905 and #10883). The last two to land were rf2-n6gq4.21 (bench/fresco, PR #10988, merged 2026-10-07T07:04:48Z) and rf2-n6gq4.4 (tools/xray filters, theme, settings, diff, palette and chart, PR #10989, merged 2026-10-07T07:54:19Z; trunk b58c5466ec). Each child's close reason carries its own baseline-to-final counts per lane, removals by reason with their surviving cover, and the planted faults that proved the cover. Those records are the epic's result; this note only marks the set complete.

Both final children ran without the local shadow-cljs lane, which a Dash8 watch held: CLJS counts and plants were graded by CI (PR CI for tools/xray, workflow_dispatch runs of expensive-tests.yml on the worker branch for bench/fresco), and every planted fault was removed by force-push and verified by blob hash before the PR was marked ready.

title: Test-suite pruning, fourth pass: implementation/resources
description:

title: SSR hydration ships machine :data collection tokens raw: [:data :items :token] redacts on traces, not in the payload
description:
## Bug

A machine that declares a sensitive field inside a collection, such as `:sensitive [[:data :items :token]]`, has that field redacted in every element on the trace and tool egress path, but not in the SSR hydration payload. The machine SSR projector matches declared paths exactly, so the indexed runtime value `[:items 0 :token]` never matches `[:items :token]`, and every visitor's page HTML carries the raw tokens. The same declaration gives two answers at two boundaries.

## Evidence

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/ssr.cljc:102` — `project-snapshot-data` redacts with `(update snapshot :data rf.classification/redact-with-paths s-paths [])`, the exact matcher (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:335-353`; `{:index-free? true}` is opt-in).
- The trace and egress side reads the same declarations through the durable walker (`re-frame.elision/elide-wire-value`), which treats a vector index as a collection coordinate.
- The namespace docstring (`ssr.cljc:22-27`) says each snapshot's `:data` "is run through the merged frame's merged `re-frame.projection/project-egress` policy under the `:rf.egress/ssr-hydration` profile". The code does not do that.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy.cljc:547-700` — `project-runtime-db` ships `:rf.runtime/machines` through this hook into `:rf/runtime-db`.

Repro (*probed* at trunk on the JVM, from `implementation/ssr` with the machines artefact):

```clojure
(rf/reg-machine :p/kid-type
  {:initial   :wait
   :data      {:token "SECRET-DEFAULT"
               :items [{:id 1 :token "SECRET-ITEM"} {:id 2 :token "SECRET-ITEM-2"}]}
   :sensitive [[:data :token] [:data :items :token]]
   :states    {:wait {}}})
(rf/reg-machine :p/parent2 {:initial :working :data {}
                            :states {:working {:spawn {:machine-id :p/kid-type}}}})
(rf/dispatch-sync [:p/parent2 [:rf.machine/start]])
```

| Projection of `:p/kid-type#1`'s `:data` | `:token` | `:items` |
|---|---|---|
| `frame-snapshot-classification` | `{:sensitive [[:data :token] [:data :items :token]]}` | — |
| Durable walker: `elide-wire-value` with the snapshot's absolute `:path` | `:rf/redacted` | `[{:id 1 :token :rf/redacted} {:id 2 :token :rf/redacted}]` |
| SSR projector: `project-runtime-db` | `:rf/redacted` | `[{:id 1 :token "SECRET-ITEM"} {:id 2 :token "SECRET-ITEM-2"}]` |

Contract: Spec 015 §SSR and hydration (`spec/015-Data-Classification.md:403`) says a sensitive child of a shipped slice is redacted under `:rf.egress/ssr-hydration` as defence in depth, and that the machine slices are "already projected against the registry server-side". The same declaration must mean the same thing at both boundaries.

## Expected

A machine's collection-element declaration redacts every element in the hydration payload, exactly as it does on the trace.

## Fix direction

Project snapshot `:data` through the same interpreter the trace uses, as the namespace docstring already claims:
- either `rf/project-egress` under `:rf.egress/ssr-hydration`;
- or `elide-wire-value` with `{:frame frame-id :path <snapshot path> :rf.egress/include-large? true}`. The hydration wire applies no size elision (ruled under the closed bead rf2-hjz4r).

The minimal alternative is `{:index-free? true}` on the existing `redact-with-paths` call. It closes the vector case but still disagrees with the trace on keyed collections.

Unifying the path grammar across every boundary is the larger design item in the Opus observability review. It is not needed here.

## Acceptance

- New regression in `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_machine_snapshot_projection_test.clj`: the machine above has both item tokens `:rf/redacted` in `project-runtime-db` output, with `:id` visible. The projected `:data` equals the durable walker's projection of the same snapshot. Fails today.
- The existing tests stay green: a large `:data` field rides whole, and an undeclared snapshot rides verbatim.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (08 §2), read; probed at trunk for this draft.
- Related:
  - rf2-mn2ht.48 is the HTTP-body instance of the same exact-matcher mismatch (a separate call site and fix);
  - rf2-mn2ht.51 (inline definitions in durable state) is the other machine-SSR leak, in a different file;
  - the conformance-security review's missing cross-boundary witness (one declared secret checked at every egress boundary) would have caught both.
- Hot-zone files: none.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/08-core-privacy-projection.md` §2; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/core-observability.md` §8 and Action 4 (Step 0); `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/machines.md` Action 1 (last bullet).
