title: conformance runner ignores unknown top-level fixture keys (:fixture/dispatchess passes; :fixture/compute-subs is inert)
description:
## Bug

The conformance spec says a harness that meets a top-level fixture key it does not implement must fail the run and name the key. The reference runner checks no top-level keys at all, only `:fixture/expect` keys. As a result:
- a misspelt setup key such as `:fixture/dispatchess` is silently dropped;
- `:fixture/compute-subs`, which a fixture the runner executes declares, is read by no code.

The scenario can therefore change, or an expectation can go unchecked, while the fixture still passes.

## Evidence

All file:line references are at trunk 475bdcaacf (unchanged at b375cd0e42).

- **Contract.**
  - `spec/conformance/README.md:42`: "A harness that meets a key it does not implement **fails the run naming the key** — it must not skip it silently … Ignoring a setup key silently changes the scenario; ignoring an expectation key lets a fixture pass having verified nothing."
  - `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4735` says the same.
  - `:fixture/compute-subs` is a documented expectation key (README `:62`; Spec-Schemas `:4701`).
- **Code** (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc`, *read*):
  - `unknown-expect-keys` (`:260-268`) inspects only `(keys (:fixture/expect fixture))`. `run-corpus` applies it (`:1846-1885`).
  - `run-fixture` (`:1533-1640`) reads setup keys by name, with empty defaults: `:fixture/frame-config` (`:1558`), `:fixture/frames` (`:1562`), `:fixture/dispatches` (`:1590`), `:fixture/calls` (`:1630`) and others.
  - Nothing inspects the fixture's top-level key set.
- **`:fixture/compute-subs` is inert.** A repo-wide search finds it only in `spec/` and in `spec/conformance/fixtures/error-sub-exception.edn:30`; no runner reads it. That fixture passes only because its `:sub-values` block happens to compute the same two subs.
- Repro (*probed*, JVM, `run-fixture` with the JVM leaf's own host map, `re-frame.conformance-test/host`):

  ```
  error-sub-exception.edn as shipped                                  passed?=true
  ... with :fixture/compute-subs REMOVED                              passed?=true
  ... with :fixture/compute-subs [[:no/such-sub]]                     passed?=true
  ... plus unknown top-level :fixture/dispatchess [[:x/y]]            passed?=true
  ... plus unknown top-level :fixture/setup-everything true           passed?=true
  (unknown-expect-keys <fixture + planted :fixture/expect key>)  => [:no-such-expect-key]
  (unknown-expect-keys <fixture + planted top-level key>)        => []
  ```

## Expected

A runnable fixture carrying a top-level key the runner does not implement fails on both hosts and names the key. `:fixture/compute-subs` either does what the README says or is not in the corpus.

## Fix direction

- **Top-level key set.** Add a set of top-level keys the runner implements, and check it beside `unknown-expect-keys` at the same point in `run-corpus`, after the capability gate. The set contains:
  - the keys `run-fixture` reads;
  - the metadata keys (`:fixture/id`, `:fixture/doc`, `:fixture/spec-version`, `:fixture/capabilities`);
  - `:fixture/dynamic-host-only?`, which a dynamic host implements by running the fixture;
  - keys owned by sibling runners, such as `:fixture/wire-order` and `:fixture/render-after-hydrate`, mirroring `sibling-owned-expect-keys`.
- **Check parsed keys.** Inspect the parsed map's keys, not text. The README warns that `:fixture/interceptor-fired` and similar are event ids, not top-level keys.
- **`:fixture/compute-subs`.** Implement it as "invoke each query before grading", which is a few lines on the same path `:sub-values` uses. That leaves `spec/` untouched. Deleting the key from the fixture instead would also need README and Spec-Schemas edits.
- **Scope.** This is the minimal fix. The review's wider proposal, one complete Malli `:rf/fixture-file` grammar validated at load, is a separate architectural change.

## Acceptance

- In the runner self-tests, an otherwise-passing fixture plus `:fixture/dispatchess` fails and names the key, on the JVM leaf and the CLJS leaf.
- `error-sub-exception.edn` with `:fixture/compute-subs [[:no/such-sub]]` fails.
- The whole corpus stays green on both hosts.
- Gates: `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/core`; `npm run test:cljs` (coordinator-granted shadow-cljs lane), or CI's `cljs` job.

## Notes

- **Origin:** Sol review (surface 32, insight 2), assimilated by the Opus conformance-security cross-review (decision 3, Insight 2).
- **Related:** rf2-9vbg3 (closed) documented the top-level key roster in the README but did not make the runner enforce it. rf2-7yth0 (closed) covered the Spec-Schemas op-map, not top-level keys.
- **Hot-zone files:** none if `:fixture/compute-subs` is implemented (runner plus test). Deleting it from the schema instead would touch `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`, which is hot-zone.
- **Supporting detail:** `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/conformance-security.md` decision 3 and Insight 2; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/32-conformance-security.md` §2.

title: CLAUDE.md instrument (z): take the test-delta baseline at the trunk after the final rebase, not an older merge base (matches loops.md)
description:
CLAUDE.md instrument hazard (z) tells a worker to compare its predicted test and assertion delta "against a baseline taken at your merge base". docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md §2 (Contention, the exclusive-gate bullet) says the opposite: take the base count "at the FIRST PARENT of the merge CI graded — the trunk as it stood at the push — never at the branch's merge base, or the delta silently absorbs whatever landed upstream in between", and records one measured case where a trunk move under a worker's branch added test namespaces of its own.

title: reagent-fresco-migration MIG-23: hydration needs frame-provider because frame-root renders nothing on its first pass, not because reacquiring reseeds state (GH #11130)
description:
From GitHub issue #11130 (filed by Mike, 2026-10-11): https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/issues/11130

The MIG-23 SSR guide in the reagent-fresco-migration skill gives the correct boot sequence but justifies its frame-provider choice with an incorrect state-loss claim. `skills/reagent-fresco-migration/references/ssr-hydrate.md` (~:102-107 at 4d20d6d1b9) says a frame-root ENSURE at commit would seed replacement state over the server state. A consumer can infer that reacquiring a live frame replays its initial events or overwrites hydrated app-db, which the engine explicitly preserves.

The actual reason, per the issue's static review at 4d20d6d1b9:
- the public Fresco render door (`implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco.cljc` ~:792-804): frame-root renders no descendant subtree on its first pass, while hydration needs the server's element shape on that first pass; frame-provider renders its children immediately;
- `acquire-frame-root!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/frame_boundary.cljs` ~:107-128) calls the unified make-frame constructor; reacquiring a seated id preserves durable state and does not replay initial-events;
- the frame-engine re-registration branch (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc` ~:3507-3541) refreshes config and generation on the existing record; setup events run only on the new-frame branch;
- the hydrating-frame-root refusal (`frame_boundary.cljs` ~:287-302) names that empty first render and tells the caller to create the frame, install the payload and scope it with frame-provider.

Fix: replace the guide's reseeding explanation with the first-render-shape and commit-time-boundary explanation the public door already gives. Keep the supported sequence: make-frame, ssr/hydrate!, frame-provider, adopting render. Documentation only; do not relax the hydration guard or change frame lifecycle behaviour.

Acceptance (from the issue):
- MIG-23 explains why hydration needs frame-provider without claiming that reuse of an existing frame overwrites app-db or replays initial-events.
- The wording agrees with the public render door, the adoption refusal and create-versus-refresh semantics.
- Nearby SSR migration summaries (the skill's procedure.md and catalogs carry related text) carry the same reason and preserve the supported boot order. The explanation applies to any consumer repository.

Close GitHub issue #11130 when this merges.

title: Error coordinates borrow the wrong generation inside a cross-frame with-frame scope
description:
Found while auditing merged PR #11136 (5d6e19ac1bc86e869db5104597afed85f49dd330). Follow-up to rf2-0vp6s; preserve that bead and its closure.

The own-scope? shortcut in error-emit/executed-coord treats a bound registrar/*generation* plus *current-frame* == failing frame as proof that the generation belongs to that frame. The public rf/with-frame macro only rebinds *current-frame* (core-reg-view-macro/expand-with-frame); it does not rebind the generation. Inside frame A's event handler, a lexical with-frame B therefore makes the test pass while A's generation is still bound.

REPRODUCED on the exact merged core source, with real image selection, subscriptions, dispatch and always-on error fan-out (JVM, no mocked lookup/emitter). Register :coord/cross-sub in coord.cross-a at line 60 and coord.cross-b at line 70, each throwing a namespace-specific message. A and B select their respective namespaces. A's event handler does (rf/with-frame :coord/cross-b @(rf/subscribe [:coord/cross-sub])). B's implementation actually throws: message is "thrown by coord.cross-b's sub", and the record frame is :coord/cross-b. But its :source-coord is coord.cross-a line 60. The otherwise identical explicit opts call @(rf/subscribe [:coord/cross-sub] {:frame :coord/cross-b}) reports B line 70 correctly.

Control before this PR: replacing only error_emit.cljc with its diff's old blob makes BOTH forms report B line 70. Both probe invocations exited 0; these are recorded observations, not a claim that the failing expectation passed. The merged file was restored byte-for-byte. Probe and logs: ai/pr-audit/11136-probe/ in worker pr-audit-sol-oct11; probe-pr-audit-sol-oct11-2.log is merged behavior, -3-before.log is the old-source control. Source coordinates are bound as the public registration macro expands them, as in the committed tests.

PROPOSED ACTION: distinguish the owner of the bound generation from the lexical default frame, or carry the actually executed descriptor into attribution. Keep the PR's no-flush behavior for a genuinely executing frame's generation; do not restore the original register-replacement-then-throw defect. No public API or general attribution framework is needed.

ACCEPTANCE: add the ordinary lexical with-frame B variant to the existing two-image regression. Both cross-frame forms must name B's throwing implementation, while the same-frame line-10 handler registering a line-20 replacement still reports 10 for the original throw and 20 on the next dispatch. Existing frozen-image, stale captured-op, no-macro and production-coordinate checks remain green.

title: Fresco forms: test prose says a revision bump is the only way a refusal shows; the late-async-acceptance row's settle-with-bump may discard a newer draft
description:
Two leftovers from the forms revision-prose correction. Both sit in files that correction edits, so this waits for it to merge.

1. Test prose still says a revision bump is the only way a refusal shows. The commit path removes the draft record in the same turn that dispatches :on-commit (implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/forms.cljs, the ::commit handler), and with no live record the field shows :value. So a synchronous rejection or rewrite is visible without a bump. The false claim survives in assertion messages and comments:
   - implementation/fresco/test/.../forms_cljs_test.cljs: a-refused-commit-still-ends-the-session, trap-same-value-blindness-the-model-half;
   - examples/forms/l0_cljs_test.cljs, about lines 155-159.
   Correct the prose only. Never change test behaviour.

2. docs/core/fresco/05-forms.md troubleshooting row "A late async acceptance overwrites newer work" prescribes settling value and revision together. A revision bump in the settle discards any draft begun while the request was pending, which is arguably the very overwrite the row describes. Read the code, decide what the row should prescribe (probably: settle the value only, and bump the revision only to supersede an ongoing session on purpose), and correct the row. If the row is right as written, say why in the close note and change nothing.

Evidence: the fresco-forms-revision worker's report on PR #11153 ("found, not mine").

Path correction: the l0 test lives at implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/examples/forms/l0_cljs_test.cljs, not examples/forms/.

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE. In forms.cljs, ::commit (lines 146-152) returns {:db (end-session db control)} together with the :on-commit dispatch, and the view renders (if (live? record revision) (:draft record) value) (line 239). A refusal therefore shows :value with no revision move.

1. TEST PROSE. Assertion messages and comments that called the bump necessary now say what the arrangement does.
- forms_cljs_test.cljs, a-refused-commit-still-ends-the-session. The revision message now reads: this caller advances the revision on every commit, and the refusal does not depend on it.
- forms_cljs_test.cljs, trap-same-value-blindness-the-model-half. The comment now says the commit ends the session, so the field shows :value. The old comment said "refuses", but this row's draft equals the committed title and is accepted. The message scopes the revision to replacing a live session from outside.
- examples/forms/l0_cljs_test.cljs, around line 156. The message drops "the only signal a refusal has". Ending the session moves subject-shown from the draft back to the committed subject. The bump repairs text the model never took, which flow-dom-cljs-test drives. The old message's "refusing branch of events/end-session" did not exist and is gone.
- Swept the fresco test tree for "only way", "only signal", "advance(s) the revision", "bump", "same-value" and "revision together". forms_dom_cljs_test.cljs already states the contract (lines 429-431 and the ns docstring), so it is unchanged.

2. TROUBLESHOOTING ROW "A late async acceptance overwrites newer work". The row was wrong as written: its prescription was one of the symptom's two causes.
- The revision does not fence settle writes. live? is revision equality only (forms.cljs:88-95), and a value written under an unchanged revision leaves a live draft in place (05-forms.md:168).
- A revision advance in the settle discards a draft begun while the request was pending. trap-commit-flicker-a-superseded-settle-changes-nothing pins that: "second" never reaches the caller.
- An older reply landing after a newer commit is mutation supersession's job: re-executing one instance suppresses the older reply's continuation (08-async-resources.md:195-197, 251-252).
New cause: an older reply settled after a newer commit, or the settle advanced the revision and discarded a draft begun while the request was pending.

title: Classification: a keyed collection before a declaration's first named slot still leaks (root :map-of HTTP decode, root-keyed invalid params, resources' anchor-stripped data walks)
description:
Filed by the delegated ruling on rf2-by79j (2026-10-10 AUSEST, HEAD 200a67df2d). That ruling makes index-free matching ride a map key once a declaration's first segment has matched (the durable walker's rule), and keeps the root guard. This bead is what the root guard leaves: a keyed collection that sits BEFORE a declaration's first named segment.

## Problem

`re-frame.classification/redact-with-paths` in `:index-free?` mode (after rf2-by79j) lets a candidate ride a map key only once it has matched at least one declared segment. The empty root candidate never rides, because otherwise `[:auth :password]` would float down to `[:tags :x :auth :password]` (the durable walker pins the same guard: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/elision_test.clj:237-245`). So wherever a keyed collection sits at the ROOT of the walk, no mark below it matches. Three shapes reach that:

1. **HTTP decode with a `:map-of` before any named slot.** `[:map-of :string [:map [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]]` gives the walker mark `[:token]`; `schema-has-opaque-child?` answers `false`, so the off-box disposition is `:classify`, and the body `{"a" {:token "SECRET-ROOT"}}` ships raw. Probed independently by both rf2-by79j reviews (exit 0): raw at HEAD, raw with the rf2-by79j fix, and raw under the durable walker too. The same holds for any keyed collection reached before the first named segment: `[:vector [:map-of ...]]`, a `:map-of` of `:map-of`, and transparent wrappers around those. An API that returns a bare id-keyed map is common.
2. **Resources invalid-params projection with a root-keyed `:params-schema`.** `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/classification.cljc` (~:651-664) reads the same walker marks with the same completeness check (`schema-has-opaque-child?`) and walks index-free, so a `:map-of`-rooted params schema leaks its marked slots in the thrown `:rf.error/resource-invalid-params` / `:rf.error/mutation-invalid-params` payload. UNPROBED: inferred from the shared matcher.
3. **Resources' index-free walks over ANCHOR-STRIPPED (data-relative) paths.** `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/trace_egress.cljc` re-roots data declarations under `data-roots` (`:1769-1781`): `:rf.resource/data [[]]`, `:rf.resource/previous-data [[]]`, `:rf.resource/pages [[]]`, plus the merged-items projection (`project-merged-items`, `:1923`, `:1933`) and the sub value projection (`:2010`). Key-component walks (`redact-key-declarations` `:227`, `recover-key` `:1890`) strip the component index the same way. A resource whose `:data` is keyed at its root (`{"u1" {:email "..."}}`, declared `:sensitive [[:data :email]]`) redacts on its durable entry (the walker matches `:data` as a named segment, then rides `"u1"`), but these walks start below `:data`, so `[:email]` meets `"u1"` with only the root candidate alive and the email rides raw. CLAIM, not probed end to end. The matcher-level evidence is the rf2-by79j ruling's probe: `(redact-with-paths {"a" {:token "SSR-SECRET"}} [[:token]] [] {:index-free? true})` stays raw with the fix, while `(redact-with-paths {:data {"a" {:token "SSR-SECRET"}}} [[:data :token]] [] {:index-free? true})` redacts. The `:rf/resource` sub (roots `[[:data] [:previous-data]]`) and `redact-continuation-reply` (re-roots to `[:value ...]`) keep an anchor and are covered by rf2-by79j. rf2-by79j fixes the machine SSR projector's instance of this shape (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/ssr.cljc` `project-snapshot-data`) by keeping its `:data` anchor.

## Fix direction

- **No named anchor exists (HTTP body root, params root): fail closed.** Add one clause to the walker's completeness answer: a mark reached through a keyed collection (`:map-of`) before the mark's first named segment (the walker descends a `:map-of` value while its base path is still empty) makes the schema incomplete. HTTP then stamps `:omit` (Spec 014 §Response-body classification rule 3), and the invalid-params projection redacts the whole `:params` slot (its existing fail-closed branch). If the clause lives in `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc`, both reach it through the existing `:schemas/schema-has-opaque-child?` late-bind hook with no HTTP or resources edit. A conjunct in `re-frame.http.privacy-body/introspectable-schema-decode?` is the alternative for HTTP alone. Note that schemas' own validation-failure redaction also consults opacity; failing closed there too is consistent.
- **A named anchor exists (resources data-relative walks): keep the anchor.** Walk with the `:data`-rooted declaration intact (for example over `{:data v}`, taking `:data` back), as rf2-by79j does for machines SSR, so each carrier and sub projection equals the durable entry's. Probe each site before changing it.
- **Do not** drop the root guard (it would turn declarations into name-matching at any depth, diverge from the durable walker, and contradict Spec 015's "classification covers exactly the paths ... you declare"), and do not add a matcher mode.
- **Coordinate with rf2-mn2ht.49** (open MIKE DECISION, qualified-keyword child): it may add another clause to the same completeness answer. Once it is ruled, co-dispatch or sequence; do not decide it here.
- **Spec.** Spec 014 rule 3's sub-bullet gains the keyed-collection-before-the-first-named-slot case. Spec 009's invalid-params rows are a HOT ZONE; touch them only if their wording needs it (they already state fail-closed and every-element redaction).

## Acceptance

- HTTP, through a real `:rf.http/managed` request: the root `:map-of` decode above is stamped `:omit` and no secret appears in the off-box projection; the app still receives the raw body. Controls stay `:classify`: `[:map [:accounts [:map-of :string [:map [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]]]]` (per-key redaction, from rf2-by79j) and `[:vector [:map [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]]` (index rides from the root).
- Invalid params: a `:map-of`-rooted `:params-schema` with a marked slot redacts the whole `:params` slot in both the resource and the mutation thrown payload.
- Resources: a resource with `:data` keyed at its root and `:sensitive [[:data :email]]` projects `:email` as `:rf/redacted` on every carrier and sub projection (`:rf.resource/data`, `:previous-data`, `:pages`, feed items), equal to the durable entry.
- Red at base, green with the fix, red again with the fix alone reverted. JVM lanes: http, resources, schemas (plus epoch if a projection it pins moves). CLJS via a granted lane or CI for any `.cljc` touched.

## Sequencing

Depends on rf2-by79j: the anchored part needs its key ride, and both edit Spec 014 rule text. No hot zone unless Spec 009 is touched.
notes:
== FENCE (mayor, 2026-10-11 00:28:15 AUSEST) ==
Waits for two merges: rf2-by79j (worktree classif-mapof-keyskip; this bead depends on it) and the http-rulings PR (rf2-mn2ht.12 and .49), which holds implementation/http and the schemas walker predicate this bead touches.
== WORKER RESULT (2026-10-11 01:55 AUSEST) - PR #11115, branch worker/keyed-root, head fd36e904a4 ==
All three shapes LEAKED at base 453d47d322. Shapes 2 and 3 were unprobed before; both are now probed and confirmed as leaks.

Shape 1, HTTP (real :rf.http/managed). [:map-of :string [:map [:id :int] [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]] and the same under a root :vector both stamped :classify, and SECRET rode off-box. FIX: new walker public re-frame.schemas.walker/schema-has-unanchored-map-of-mark? answers whether a :sensitive?/:large? mark sits below a :map-of the walk reaches while its base path is still empty: at the root, or behind :vector, :map-of, :maybe/:or, :orn/:multi. A :map slot or a pinned :tuple/:cat position anchors the mark, and a mark at the root path [] claims the whole value; both answer false. The :schemas/schema-has-opaque-child? HOOK binding in re-frame.schemas is now (or opaque-child unanchored-map-of-mark), so there is no new hook and no HTTP/resources behaviour edit. Now :omit, with no secret off-box and the raw body delivered. Controls stay :classify: [:map [:accounts [:map-of ...]]] redacts per key, and a root [:vector [:map ...]] redacts per element.

WHY NOT FOLD THE CLAUSE INTO schema-has-opaque-child? ITSELF (the premise the brief leaned on): that predicate also drives the registration nudge (:rf.warning/schema-walker-opaque, via storage/walker-introspectable?) and validation's (or sensitive? opaque?). Folding it in would warn on an ordinary id-keyed reg-app-schema, and would turn a large-only map-of validation failure into a sensitive redaction. Validation sees these marks anyway, because align-in-path drops :map-of keys. So the facade fn is unchanged, the same split rf2-mn2ht.49 made for schema-has-qualified-ref?.

Shape 2, invalid params. A :map-of-rooted :params-schema leaked the conforming marked :acct under every key, in BOTH the resource and the mutation thrown payload. FIXED by the same hook: walker-sees-every-mark? is false, so :params becomes :rf/redacted. Control: a :map-of under a named slot keeps per-slot redaction.

Shape 3, resources data-relative walks in trace_egress.cljc. These leaked: :rf.resource/data, :previous-data, :pages, both merged item lists (:rf.resource/items and :infinite-state :items, via project-merged-items' raw-pages walk and its no-accessor walk), :rf.mutation/result, redact-key-declarations and recover-key (a root-keyed params component). Already redacting (the controls): the durable entry (project-entry-data), :rf/resource :data/:previous-data, :rf/mutation :result and :infinite-state :pages. FIX: a private redact-anchored walks {slot v} with the declared slot (:data, or :params/:scope for a key component) as every path's first segment. Every carrier and sub projection now equals project-entry-data.

Red/green/red-again (scoped JVM namespaces; the fix files reverted from the prior commit and restored by blob hash):
- HTTP: 4 failures / 4 / 0 / 4
- invalid params: 2 / 0 / 2

title: INCOMPLETE reserved-slot refusal: SSR and Fresco disagree on canonical prop aliases
description:
At PR #10400 (edcf24321890811f06b43d8ddd20f6ab5e633334), ui_tree.cljc reject-reserved-attrs! uses the SSR standard-names dictionary through dom-attr-name. That dictionary omits dangerouslySetInnerHTML aliases; Fresco slot/prop-name performs kebab conversion. Exact-merge JVM probe proves :dangerously-set-inner-HTML becomes dangerouslySetInnerHTML under the actual Fresco slot rule but SSR emits
. Literal :dangerouslySetInnerHTML is refused and ordinary :data-ref emits, both controls passed. Correction: align reserved-slot detection with the actual authored-key-to-React-slot rule, then reject keys resolving to a reserved slot through ui-tree-malformed with the authored key/path. Preserve data/aria attributes, ordinary-case spellings and hiccup policy; use the existing canonicalization boundary rather than enumerating a growing alias list. Include the real uppercase-acronym alias in cross-host regression coverage. Important correction to rf2-wt2wy item 1: the same probe shows lowercase :dangerously-set-inner-html resolves to dangerouslySetInnerHtml, NOT dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Do not justify its treatment by claiming the current Fresco resolver maps it to the reserved slot. Any intended policy for that distinct spelling must be explicit. Evidence: ai/probe-reserved-alias-audit-sep23-monitor-1.log/.exit, exit 0 is the defect witness with positive refusal/ordinary-attribute controls, correct worker root. No full suite rerun. The corresponding implementation is already in rf2-wt2wy, currently in_progress. This separate OPEN finding tracks the exact correction under the audit policy; coordinate that implementation, do not duplicate edits. Existing status/closure fields remain unchanged.

Both actionable findings are separately open/ready, dependencies and source pointers appended, with all source statuses/closure metadata preserved. Actionable findings: rf2-qtpzl. Existing finding updates: rf2-kgtn0. == WORKER VERDICT (ssrgate-empi3, 2026-09-25) — FIXED in PR #10410 == Reproduced at trunk 5c32f2f141: emit-ui-tree emitted `

# Senior review: skills/reagent-migration

Reviewer persona: senior migration-tooling reviewer; treats the skill as instructions an agent executes verbatim, and checks every replacement name, option, id and command it teaches against the Fresco source, the codemod source and spec/API.md on the frozen tree.
Tree: skills-review-sep21 worktree, trunk b60a20abca

No skill-specific drift gate names this skill; everything it teaches is ungated.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. The trigger description, both packaging descriptions, the docs index and the docs mirror were never re-synced after the L2 and MIG-28 rewrites: they still draw the publication gap and the reserved `:&` merge the skill's own evals grade as failures  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: self-contract] [size: S]
- Where: skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:12 (front-matter description: "Fresco is pre-publication with no released Maven coordinate"); package.json:5 and .claude-plugin/plugin.json:4 ("the Reagent adapter is first-class and Fresco is pre-publication"); docs/skills/index.md:42 ("and Fresco is pre-publication"); docs/skills/reagent-migration.md:11 ("**Fresco is PRE-PUBLICATION.** … If yours has no path to that, there is nothing to migrate onto yet"), :23 ("computed props through the reserved `:&` merge"), :26 ("the draft guide teaches several forms that do not exist").

- Evidence: `VERSION` reads `0.0.1.alpha` and `git tag -l 'v*' | wc -l` is 0, so NOTHING is published — `day8/re-frame2-reagent` no more than Fresco — and `.github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh:139` lists `fresco` in the same 14-entry ARTEFACTS array as `reagent`. spec/design.md:91-99 (L2): "The honesty obligation is not to draw the asymmetry 'swap to the adapter now, wait for Fresco', which is false." evals.json:26 (eval 15) FAILS "an answer that … gives Fresco a publication status the adapter does not share"; evals.json:110 (eval 22) FAILS an answer that emits "a reserved :& key"; catalog-judgment.md:370 (MIG-28): "there is no reserved merge key and no spread form". The skill's own README.md:15 and SKILL.md:162 carry the corrected wording ("same release set … no separate publication gap"; "don't invent a publication gap either"), and inputs.md:86 records the installation-page fix as rf2-esrp (2026-09-13) — the sweep reached the body and README but not these five. Control: the mirror's :7-9 and :46-48 match README.md:11-16 and :29 nearly verbatim, so it was mirrored once and left. No gate compares the mirror: `grep -rl 'docs/skills' scripts/` returns nothing (control: 11 scripts name `docs/core`); `.github/workflows/docs.yml:29-31` only builds `docs/**`; mkdocs.yml:472 publishes the page in nav.
- Action: (a) respell the three descriptions and index.md:42 length-neutrally — the description sits at 1005/1026 chars — e.g. replace "and Fresco is pre-publication with no released Maven coordinate" with "and Fresco resolves like every other re-frame2 artefact"; (b) re-mirror docs/skills/reagent-migration.md:9-12 from README.md:13-16, replace :23's "through the reserved `:&` merge" with "via a plain `merge` with the owned keys last", and :26's "the draft guide" with "guide pages". One PR, no spec change; add one line to README.md §Layout naming docs/skills/reagent-migration.md as the mirror so the next rewrite carries it.

### 2. The "exactly-one-props-map law" overstates its call-site half: a bare `[view]` head is legal, the codec supplies `{}`, and it is the door's own idiom  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: teaching-drift] [size: S]
- Where: skills/reagent-migration/references/gotchas.md:113-117 ("Call sites match: `[status-pill {}]`, never `[status-pill]`. Reagent's habit of zero-arg components is the most common mechanical miss in a first pass"); references/catalog-mechanical.md:37-38 ("A view that reads no props declares `[_]`, and its call sites pass `{}`"); SKILL.md:142 (routes to it as "the exactly-one-props-map law").
- What: the leaf tells the agent that a prop-less mount without a map is a defect to hunt, when the runtime accepts it and the door's own docstrings mount that way.
- Evidence: implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/codec.cljs:1398-1400, `boundary-element`: `has-props? (props-map? argv 1)`, `props (if has-props? (nth argv 1) {})` — an absent map is supplied as `{}` and children begin at index 1; `props-map?` (codec.cljs:1071-1075) is `(map? (nth argv i nil))`, nothing refuses. The door itself mounts prop-less heads: fresco.cljc:564 `[root-view]` (frame-root docstring), :695 `[counter]` (render! docstring), substrate.cljs:146 `[app]`. Control for the other half: the HEADER rule is right — `defview` expands to `(fn ~argv ~@body)` (fresco.cljc:273) invoked with the one body-props map, so `[_]` is the correct header for a view reading no props, and eval 16 (evals.json:36) pins exactly that.
- Action: soften both leaves to "a view takes ONE props map; a call site passes it only when there are props — `[status-pill]` mounts with `{}` supplied — and the header is `[_]` or a destructure. Never a positional argument." Delete the "most common mechanical miss" sentence. This also honours L10's "smallest correct diff": as written, the rule spends the author's diff adding `{}` to every zero-prop mount, and would "repair" the door's own examples on sight.

### 3. Two leaves name `h/dispatch`, a var the door does not export, in the one sentence that describes what a frameless subtree loses  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: teaching-drift] [size: S]
- Where: skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-mechanical.md:338 ("every bare `h/sub` / `h/dispatch` beneath loses what it resolved against"); references/catalog-reject.md:61 ("every bare `h/sub` and `h/dispatch` beneath it resolves against that frame instead").

The door sentence the leaf paraphrased, fresco.cljc:724-725, reads "every bare `dispatch` / `subscribe` beneath it loses the frame" — core's unqualified verbs, not `h/`.
- Action: respell both as "every `h/sub` read and every intent lowered beneath it". Two lines.

### 4. The first command the skill runs prints a stderr WARNING no leaf mentions, and the only explanation lives in a file the agent never opens  [PLAUSIBLE] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics] [size: S]
- Where: skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:70-84 (the reporter command, "Run it from the consumer's own project"); references/procedure.md:34-51 (Step 0) and :275-285 (Step 6).
- What: the pinned coordinate loads a codemod whose deps.edn deliberately puts a path outside its project root on `:paths`, which the Clojure CLI reports as `Use of :paths external to the project has been deprecated`; an agent told to "read the report first" meets a warning first and nothing in the skill says it is expected.

What would confirm: run the documented command from a scratch consumer directory and read stderr — not done here, because a `:git/sha` dep clones into `~/.gitlibs`, which the review rules class as an install. The pin itself is sound: `8b17cc53d5` exists, the codemod README and 20-migration.md pin the same sha (rf2-kiwa), and `git log 8b17cc53d5..HEAD -- migration/reagent-to-fresco/codemod` is one commit touching one README line, so the pinned tool is the tool the leaves describe.
- Action: one sentence beside the command in SKILL.md and procedure.md Step 0: "Expect one stderr line, `Use of :paths external to the project has been deprecated` — the shared slot rule on the tool's classpath, deliberate (codemod deps.edn:67-77); not a failure." If a newer CLI ever IGNORES external dep paths instead of warning, the run fails at `re-frame.fresco.impl.slot` load and that is the codemod's bead, not this skill's.

title: story: compile-time guards skip every :plays entry after the first and every check body; an unknown :checks id compiles and passes forever
description:
Discovered by the senior-developer review rf2-wd2t (2026-09-13, trunk 1c9ff9697b). Verified at source by the mayor.

WHERE: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc:1407-1414: reject-unknown-assertions! and reject-malformed-causal-opts! receive (script-assertion-atoms script*) (the primary play only) while scripts* (1396-1398) carries every play; plan.cljc:1306-1310: checks is reduced from bodies with no lookup; plan.cljc:1174-1188: expand-checks maps an unregistered id to [] and "never throws". assertions.cljc:44-49 promises "an unrecognised id never reaches a handler".

EVIDENCE: source as cited; rg -c ':checks' tools/story/test shows 59 lines and a search for unknown/unregistered beside :checks reads 0 (control: story-unknown-assertion pinned 3 times for the two guarded positions).

WHY IT MATTERS: [:assert [:rf.assert/typo]] in a second named play reaches the runner; :checks [:check/no-runtime-erors] compiles and, with the checks-never-execute defect filed from the same review, is a double vacuous pass.

SMALLEST CHANGE: feed (mapcat (comp script-assertion-atoms :script) scripts*) to both rejecters; resolve each :checks id through chk-lookup and fail! :rf.error/story-check-unknown (mirror of story-compose-unknown). LAND WITH the checks-never-execute bead from the same review, one PR.

GATE: jvm-tools-story.

ALREADY-COVERED CHECK: rf2-m0cge5 (closed) fixed the same one-play blind spot for :required-runner only.
notes:
VERDICT (vacpass-a, PR #9717, branch worker/vacpass-a; landed together with rf2-b2mt as one PR): FIXED.

Cause, verified at source on trunk 5b89378c45, all in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc compile-body:
- reject-unknown-assertions! and reject-malformed-causal-opts! received (script-assertion-atoms script*), which is the primary play only.
- The checks vector was reduced from the bodies with no lookup, and expand-checks mapped an unregistered id to [].
- No guard read a check body's atoms.

Fix, all in compile-body:
- Every :checks id (own, inherited or composed) resolves through chk-lookup. An unresolved id fails :rf.error/story-check-unknown with ex-data {:variant/id :check/id}. This mirrors :rf.error/story-compose-unknown, and the message tells the author to register the check or fix its spelling.
- Both assertion guards now receive play-atoms (the in-script checkpoints of EVERY play in scripts*) and expect-atoms (the terminal :assertions plus every resolved check body's atoms).
- The expand-checks docstring now notes that its tolerance of an unknown id is reachable only through a hand-built plan.

Evidence: the same JVM probe, run on trunk and then on the branch.
- Unknown :checks id. Before: :pass. After: :error :rf.error/story-check-unknown.
- Typo'd assertion id in a SECOND play. Before: :pass. After: :error :rf.error/story-unknown-assertion.
- Typo'd id inside a registered check body. Before: :pass, check :pass over 0 records. After: :error :rf.error/story-unknown-assertion.
- Control, the same typo in the FIRST play: :error :rf.error/story-unknown-assertion on both sides.

New tests, in tools/story/test/re_frame/story/inline_plan_test.clj:
- unknown-check-id-fails-plan-construction. Inline, plus an inherited unknown id read through variant-plan's ex-data.
- assertion-guards-cover-every-play-and-check-body. A second-play typo, a check-body typo, and a malformed causal opt in a second play.

Four existing tests named checks that were never registered, and now thread or register the check bodies (that is the only change to them):
- plan_test.cljc: checks-inherit-through-extends.
- compose_test.cljc: compose-mixes-fragments-and-checks-in-declared-order and parent-check-inherits.
- story_authoring_surface_test.clj: extends-compiler-authority-through-default-side-table.

Gate: jvm-tools-story. The branch ran 1918 tests, 7072 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, exit 0. The planted fault was three single-line plants in the changed lines, each anchor matching exactly once:
- B1: an unknown check resolves to {}.
- B2: the guards walk the first play only.
- B3: the check-body atoms are dropped from the guards.

Result: exit 1, still 1918/7072, and 10 failures, each attributable to exactly one plant: B1 hit the inline and inherited unknown-id cases, B2 the second-play typo and second-play causal cases, B3 the check-body typo. The restore was verified by blob hash against HEAD.

Sequencing note: rf2-exlh renames plan_test.cljc and compose_test.cljc to *_cljs_test.cljc. This PR touches three small deftest hunks in those two files, so whichever lands second rebases over a rename plus a small hunk.
close_reason: Fix in PR #9717 (vacpass-a, one PR with rf2-b2mt). compile-body resolves every :checks id (own, inherited, composed) through the check lookup and fails :rf.error/story-check-unknown on a miss (mirror of story-compose-unknown); both assertion guards now walk every named play and every resolved check body. Probe before/after: unknown :checks id, a typo in a second play, and a typo inside a check body each read :pass and now read :error; the first-play typo control reads :error on both sides. Gate jvm-tools-story on the rebased tip: 1918 tests, 7072 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0; three single-line planted faults turned exactly the 10 new jjhy assertions red, each attributable to one plant. Four existing deftests that named unregistered checks now thread the bodies. Spec 017 wording gap filed as a follow-up. Full verdict in the notes.

description:

## Problem

Teaching and migration prose still spells derived subs with `:<-` and the two-fn tail: docs 62 code-block registrations in 21 files and 110 `:<-` mentions in 35 files at HEAD (less the four pages `.2` rewrites); skills 42 registrations in 16 files and 62 mentions in 20 files (less `fundamentals/subs.md`); `skills/re-frame2/evals/evals.json` (2 expected-output strings naming "the `:<-` chain"); the migration README advertises the static `:<-` forms as preserved (`migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:25`, `:3148`, `:3153`) and M-71 (:767-831) documents the two-fn form as the v2 target. A v1 codebase now needs one more mechanical rule.

## Target API

Rewrite every code block by the `.1` migration rule (docs code blocks are hand-edited; each is a fenced sample, so neither link gate inspects them — the worker verifies by reading). Prose: "`:<-` chain" → "`:inputs` declaration"; "one arrow delivers a bare value…" sentences deleted.

**Migration README:**
- **M-71** (:767-831) shrinks: the v1 signal fn becomes `{:inputs (fn [query-v] …)}` in the metadata slot (not a positional first fn); cases 1–4 keep their classification (Type B for map-returning and app-db-reading signal fns); case 3's body is already `[item]` and now needs no special mention.
- **New M-75** (README:25 says rules run M-0 through M-74; verify at tip and take the next free number), **Type A** (mechanical): `(reg-sub id ?meta :<- q1 … :<- qn f)` → `(reg-sub id (assoc meta :inputs [q1 … qn]) f)`; when n = 1 and `f` is a literal `(fn [p q] …)`, `p` → `[p]`; when `f` is a reference, wrap `(fn [[v] q] (f v q))`; a missed site fails loudly at ns-load with `:rf.error/reg-sub-bad-args` naming `:inputs`. Add it to the Type A roster (the list beside the Type B roster at :1777) and to the migration report's rule surfacing. Correct :25 / :3148 / :3153 ("static `:<-` forms preserved" → "`:<-` is retired; M-75").
- The v1 codemod (`migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/`, rewrite-clj, implements M-73/M-70 only — no `reg-sub` handling at HEAD) is NOT extended here: a hand-applied Type A rule satisfies Vision C1 exactly as every other Type A rule does. File a follow-on only if v1 pilot demand shows.

**Migration skill** (`skills/re-frame-migration/references/`): `auto-call-site-rewrites.md:298-340` §reg-sub flat-sub sugar removed — the `:->` / `:=>` desugaring REWRITE targets become `{:inputs [...]}` + `(fn [[in] _] (f in))` for one upstream (the SEARCH blocks keep the v1 spellings — they are what the agent greps for); `guided-interceptors-subs.md` (5 sites), `breaking-changes.md` (3), `silent-runtime-failures.md` (2); `inventory-and-plan.md` if it inventories `:<-`.

Two-reviewer; the prose half of the ruled change. Counts re-measured at HEAD with `rg -c -F ':<-'`.

Every `:<-` token under `docs/` (except `docs/design/**`), `skills/`, and `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` outside M-75's v1 SEARCH block; every two-fn `reg-sub` tail in those trees.

## The decision in one sentence

The first managed-HTTP example a reader meets spends 127 of its 420 lines on a Start long / Cancel pair that writes a fabricated handle into `re-frame.http.registry` — a namespace Spec 014 marks test-only, saying application code SHOULD route through `:rf.http/managed` — and hand-spells the framework's cancellation envelope; keep it as the documented controlled seam (A), delete it and leave cancellation to the guide and the framework tests (B), or replace it with the two-line public shape, `:request-id` on the live +1 request plus `[:rf.http/managed-abort id]`, and let the reader throttle the network to watch it cancel (C, mine).

## The problem, carefully

**What the example is sold as.** `examples/README.md:88` calls it "the compact complement to RealWorld for Spec 014" covering "success, 4xx failure, retry-recover, and abort"; `docs/async/http.md:327` says it "demonstrates the manual-abort path end-to-end"; `docs/async/examples.md:10` lists "manual abort"; the skill `skills/re-frame2/patterns/managed-http.md:150` says it covers "`:request-id` cancellation via `:rf.http/managed-abort`"; `skills/re-frame2/examples-map.md:38` says "the abort-token wiring". Four tracked files (`git ls-files examples/core/managed_http_counter`): `core.cljs` (420 lines), `README.md` (60), `index.html`, `api/inc.json`.

**What Start long / Cancel actually do** (`examples/core/managed_http_counter/core.cljs`):

- The ns requires the registry namespace and says why: "The write seam (`record-in-flight!`) isn't on the public facade, so we reach for the registry ns directly" (`core.cljs:46-50`).
- `:http-counter/start-long` (`:295-322`) fires a demo-only fx `:http-counter/seed-long-request` (`:233-293`), which calls `rf.http.registry/record-in-flight!` (`:250`) with a fabricated handle `{:url "api/long" :frame frame :abort-fn …}`. Nothing is fetched; `long-pending-url` exists "purely so it reads naturally in the abort trace" (`:227-231`).
- The handle's `:abort-fn` (`:269-292`) does the framework's two jobs by hand: `rf.http.registry/clear-in-flight-in-frame!` (`:276`) and a dispatch of a hand-built reply `{:status :cancelled :cancelled? true :rf.reply/cancel-reason reason :error {:kind :rf.http/aborted …}}` (`:285-292`), with a comment that it is "the exact shape the live transport's abort path emits (see `re-frame.http.reply/failure-reply`)".
- `:http-counter/cancel` (`:324-333`) is the one genuinely public line: `:fx [[:rf.http/managed-abort long-request-id]]`.

**What the public cancellation surface is.** Spec 014 §Aborts, `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:644-663`: put any `=`-comparable value under `:request-id` on the request; "A subsequent `:rf.http/managed-abort` fx with the same id … cancels the in-flight request, dispatching `:on-failure` with `:kind :rf.http/aborted`", e.g. `{:fx [[:rf.http/managed-abort :article/load]]}` (`:662`). A manual abort "DOES dispatch `:on-failure` with `:reason :user`" (`:666`); the id is frame-local (`:668-691`). Worked example E, "Aborting a stale search", is the whole shape in ten lines (`:1005-1020`). `spec/API.md:420` lists `:rf.http/managed-abort` as a v1 fx ("abort the in-flight request with the given `:request-id`"); `:507` and `:804` are the other two mentions. In code, `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:482-514` (`managed-abort-handler`) resolves the frame stamp and calls `registry/abort-in-flight-in-frame!` (`registry.cljc:456-470`), which does nothing but fire the handle's `:abort-fn` (`fire-abort!`, `:421-431`). The live transport records its own handles at `transport.cljc:1247` and `:1866`, and their `:abort-fn` is where `AbortController` and finalisation live (`AbortController` reads 4 in `transport.cljc`, 2 in `transport_cljs.cljc`, 3 in `registry.cljc`). With a fabricated handle none of that runs — the example supplies both halves of the contract itself, which its own docstring concedes: "This covers the framework path, but not `AbortController` or network cancellation" (`core.cljs:33`).

**What the spec says about the seam — one premise of the bead is wrong, in the direction that strengthens the finding.** The bead (and PR #10174's body) record `record-in-flight!` at 0 hits in `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md`. It has 2: `:1102`, the row for `seed-in-flight-for-test!` ("Registers a fabricated in-flight handle through the SAME `record-in-flight!` path production uses"), and `:1104`: "These are **test-only** surfaces — not part of the user-facing API for production code paths. Application code SHOULD route through `:rf.http/managed` and the dispatch-shape replies". `spec/API.md` is genuinely 0 (control: `managed-abort` 3 hits there). So the example is not merely off the public facade; it is application-shaped code doing what the owning spec says application code should not. `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/managed.cljc:133-143` re-exports `seed-in-flight-for-test!` and `clear-all-in-flight!` but neither `record-in-flight!` nor `clear-in-flight-in-frame!`, "because direct mutation would bypass the by-identity cleanup invariant" (`:137-138`).

**Who else reaches in.** Repo-wide (Grep, `.beads` and `ai/` excluded), `record-in-flight!` callers outside `implementation/http/` are exactly two files: this example and `tools/xray/testbeds/managed_http/core.cljs` (`:223`, `:328`), whose require comment makes the same apology (`:79-85`). **Nothing is hidden.** README `:5-8` ("The last two are controlled seams rather than live transport: this example does not run a retry policy or cancel a network request"), `:22` (the full bullet), `:28-30`; `core.cljs:14-36`; and `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1663-1667`, whose comment says the Cancel button exercises "the canned-stub seam" — which is not what it does (it is the registry seam), a stale comment in a hot-zone file. The bead is right that the whole cost is pedagogical.

**What the seam has cost so far** (`git log --oneline -- examples/core/managed_http_counter/`, 24 commits): three repairs to this one demo — `c6165855b0` (2026-07-11) fixed the hand-spelled envelope's retired `:cancel/reason` key and added the 128-line pin `implementation/core/test/re_frame/managed_http_counter_cljs_test.cljs`; `94852fed61` stamped `:frame` on the seeded handle; `5c01850a80` (2026-09-05) fixed the abort closure's any-frame `clear-in-flight!` and added the 95-line `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_demo_frame_isolation_cljs_test.cljs`. Of the 143 lines the pair occupies (`:19-20`, `:27-33`, `:46-50`, `:207-333`, `:371-372`), 45 are code and the rest comment — comment explaining registry internals: frame stamping, the any-frame sweep, the namespaced reason key.

## Make it tangible

**What the reader copies today (A), condensed from `core.cljs:233-292`:**

```clojure
(rf/reg-fx :http-counter/seed-long-request
  (fn [frame-ctx {:keys [request-id]}]
    (let [frame (:frame frame-ctx)]
      (rf.http.registry/record-in-flight!            ;; not on any public surface
        request-id nil
        {:url "api/long" :frame frame
         :abort-fn (fn [reason]
                     (rf.http.registry/clear-in-flight-in-frame! frame request-id)
                     (rf/dispatch [:http-counter/start-long
                                   {:status :cancelled :cancelled? true
                                    :rf.reply/cancel-reason reason         ;; hand-spelled
                                    :error {:kind :rf.http/aborted …}}]
                                  {:frame frame}))}))))
```

On screen: click **Start long**, status reads `loading`; click **Cancel**, status reads `idle` and "Error kind: :rf.http/aborted". Deterministic, clickable, and the three names the reader learns — `record-in-flight!`, `clear-in-flight-in-frame!`, the envelope's field spellings — are the three they must never use.

**What the public shape is** (Spec 014 example E, `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:1008-1017`, and the tutorial at `docs/async/tutorial.md:182`): a `:request-id` on the request, and `[:rf.http/managed-abort id]` from any handler in the same frame. The framework builds the envelope, clears the slot, and fires `AbortController`.

**What C would put in the file** (about ten lines net, replacing 143):

```clojure
;; :http-counter/+1 — initiation arm gains one key, and one reply arm is added
(nil? reply)
{:db (assoc db :http-counter/status :loading :http-counter/error nil)
 :fx [[:rf.http/managed {:request    {:method :get :url "api/inc.json"}
                         :decode     :json
                         :request-id :http-counter/+1      ;; the cancel handle
                         :reply-to   [:http-counter/+1]}]]}

(some-> reply :status (= :cancelled))                     ;; the abort reply lands here
{:db (assoc db :http-counter/status :idle :http-counter/error (:error reply))}

(rf/reg-event :http-counter/cancel
  (fn [{:keys [db]} _]
    {:db db :fx [[:rf.http/managed-abort :http-counter/+1]]}))
```

On screen: click **+1**, the count moves. Click **Cancel** afterwards and nothing visible happens — the reply landed first, the lookup misses, and the abort is the documented no-op (`registry.cljc:465-467`; the example's own comment already says this at `core.cljs:331-332`; `:436-437`: "cancellation is opportunistic"). Open DevTools, throttle the network (Slow 3G), click **+1** then **Cancel** inside the second or two the GET now takes: status `idle`, "Error kind: :rf.http/aborted" — from the framework's own envelope, through `AbortController`, which is the half the current demo says it leaves out. No fixture, no timer, no seam.

**What each option leaves on the page and in the docs:**

| | Buttons | Cancel is | Reader learns | Prose that must change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 5 | live fx on a fabricated handle | registry internals + the envelope's spelling | none (the `shadow-cljs.edn:1666` comment stays stale) |
| B | 3 | absent | nothing about cancel here; pointed at the guide | 7 surfaces: README, docstring, `examples/README.md:88`, `docs/async/http.md:327`, `docs/async/examples.md:10`, skill `:150`, examples-map `:38` |
| C | 4 | live fx on a live request | exactly Spec 014 example E | README and docstring only — the other five become true as written |

**Recommend B: remove Start long / Cancel and their synthetic request fixture from this introductory counter; retain a short explanation of public cancellation in its README.** This is a recommendation for Mike's decision, not a ruling or permission to implement it. The useful application pattern is already small: put `:request-id` on a `:rf.http/managed` request, then return `[:rf.http/managed-abort id]` from an event in the same frame. The framework owns the handle and cancellation reply. This follows [Spec 014](../../spec/014-HTTPRequests.md), lines 648-689, and the actual effect in `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:508-514`. That effect delegates to the frame-scoped registry lookup; `registry.cljc:421-430,456-470` only invokes the registered callback. In this example, the callback itself clears the slot and constructs and dispatches the reply (`examples/core/managed_http_counter/core.cljs:250-292`). Consequently, the demo demonstrates real lookup and callback invocation, but its cleanup and reply production are example-owned substitutes for transport lifecycle code. Removing it loses a deterministic clickable cancellation illustration, not a live Fetch cancellation demonstration.

Two premises need correcting. First, literal `record-in-flight!` occurs **zero times in `spec/API.md`, but twice in Spec 014**, at lines 1102 and 1104; searching the same texts finds the positive control `:rf.http/managed-abort` four and fifteen times respectively. This is a teaching and maintenance judgment, not distrust of programmers or a claim that the current comments conceal anything. However, the counter's central lesson is a pure handler describing a request and consuming its reply; implementing the framework's registry and reply responsibilities in the same lesson makes that pattern harder to copy cleanly. A delayed canned success is also not equivalent: the actual `:after-ms` implementation schedules `:dispatch-later` and re-fires the canned effect (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc:336-387`); that path does not register a managed request for abort-by-id. **stated root naming the tree**, and **the change merged**. `xrcov-onaxh` satisfied two of them and was
reaped anyway. **The mayor did that without recording the exception at the time**, and the §5 method reread
— which asks whether the rules being ENFORCED match what is actually being done — is what surfaced it.

**What was and was not present.** The change was merged (PR #10090, `799dea9c18`). The worktree was verified
at **0 porcelain lines** and local == remote. But there is no done-sentence, because the worker was killed
by a weekly rate limit and its final message is a PROGRESS line — "Bead closed … Worktree clean. Now cleanup
and the PR check status" — not a completion statement. A progress line is precisely what the done-sentence
conjunct exists to exclude.

**Why the exception was nevertheless sound, stated so it can be judged rather than trusted.** The conjunct
protects against reaping a tree a worker is still using. Two independent facts discharge that here: the
agent was TERMINATED, not merely quiet — a harness stop event, which the method itself ranks above every
clock — and the worker had CLOSED its own bead with an 8,175-character reason carrying the decisive
measurement inline, which is a completion statement in the durable record even though it is not in the final
message. The mayor also read that close reason and confirmed the deliverable (the red control) BEFORE acting.

when ALL of: the agent is confirmed TERMINATED by a harness stop event rather than inferred dead from
silence; the bead carries the worker's own close reason with its measurement; the change is merged; and the
tree is clean with local == remote. **Silence is not termination**, and a worker inside a long gate looks
identical to a dead one on every clock — the method says so at length. Absent a stop event, wait.

**What should have happened at the time: this note, before the removal rather than after it.** The act was
right; the record was late, and a right act with no record is indistinguishable from an unexamined one the
next time somebody reads the hygiene log.

on the dead worker's behalf, for the same reason and on the same evidence. The two exceptions share one
justification and should be read together.

description:
Found and MEASURED by `routewit-a` while correcting the Static inventory under rf2-k97c.3 (PR #9650).
It deliberately did not widen into this, and reported it for filing instead — the right call, since
the Dynamic surface belongs to slices that have not run yet.

## THE GAP

The same two pages that carried a stale STATIC inventory also carry a DYNAMIC panel table, and that
table is stale for SIX of its TEN rows and correct for the other four:

    docs/xray/api/reference.md
    tools/xray/spec/API.md

STALE — these are now Fresco boundaries, not `reg-view`s:
    app-db-diff · reactive-panel · resources · derivation-graph · module-view

STALE IN A DIFFERENT WAY — `routing/Panel` is a BRIDGE over a private `PanelView`, so the row is
wrong about what the exported name IS, not merely about its kind. That is the #9578 spelling, which
rf2-k97c.3 RULING 1 says converges onto the #9581 spelling at step 3 — so whoever fixes this row
should expect it to move AGAIN, and should say in the PR body that it will.

CORRECT AS WRITTEN — the remaining four rows. Do not touch them.

## WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE BEAD RATHER THAN A WIDENING OF THE STATIC FIX

`routewit-a` corrected the STATIC inventory WHOLE rather than one row of five, and its reasoning is
worth keeping: correcting a single row of a shared table makes the corrected entry read as the odd
one out, which is worse than leaving the table uniformly stale. The same argument does NOT carry
across to the Dynamic table, because those panels' migrations have not landed and their spellings are
still moving — a correction now would be re-stale within a slice or two.

SO THE TRIGGER IS SEQUENCING, NOT PRIORITY: fix the Dynamic table when the Dynamic panel migrations
have settled, and take the shape from the tree at that point rather than from this bead.

## RE-MEASURE BEFORE ACTING; THIS IS A DATED SNAPSHOT

The six/four split was measured at trunk around 606ba24a19. Panel migrations are landing steadily, so
re-derive which rows are stale at your tip. Read `panels.cljs`'s `render-panel!` call sites for the
authority on what each mount actually passes — a `Panel-bridge` argument is the #9581 spelling and a
bare `Panel` may be either an unmigrated view OR a #9578-style bridge, and the two are not
distinguishable from the mount line alone.

## GATES

`scripts/check_doc_slugs.py --verbose` covers both paths (`docs/` and `tools/*/spec` are both inside
its roots) and runs unguarded in `test.yml`'s `verify-readme-links` job. It validates link targets and
heading anchors ONLY — nothing grades prose, tables or rendering, and it does not look inside fenced
code blocks at all. So check table column counts and anchors by hand and say so in the PR body.

## Problem

Four normative statements contradict the tree or each other, and readers act on them (a migrator following the skill will address a boot singleton by `:system-id`, which the pattern spec forbids). Independently, `make-machine-handler` is still presented as a registration door in two API tables and in 005 §Registration's lead, while the framework's registration entry point is `reg-machine` / `defmachine` + `reg-machine`; two sites still use the door composition. All are ruling-free; each is fixed where it stands. (If @machines.2 is ruled "delete" before this dispatches, items 1 and 3 collapse into that deletion — drop them from this bead and say so.)

## Evidence (tip `6445d0611b`)

1. `spec/Conventions.md:441` — the `:rf.machine/dispatch-to-system` row ends "The fx counterpart to the `dispatch-to-system` fn (`re-frame.core`)". That fn was deleted (rf2-c6xkmn; `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1082-1085,1650-1653` record it; `docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:17` and `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2957` already say "there is no `dispatch-to-system` var").
2. `spec/Conventions.md:439` — the `:rf.machine/spawn` row says "record its id into the parent's `:data` via `:on-spawn`". `:on-spawn`'s return is dropped (`transition.cljc:2320-2380`; 005:2984 "a callback like `(assoc data :pending id)` is a no-op"); the pure reducer binds the id under `:rf/spawned` (`transition.cljc:533-562`; 005:2986-2990). The row names the one mechanism that does NOT record the id.
3. `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2138` — the `:rf.warning/on-spawn-return-ignored` row's remedy is "dispatch `:rf.machine/update-snapshot` against the spawned `:system-id`", and the emitted `:remedy` payload agrees (`transition.cljc:2374` `:remedy [:system-id …]`), while 005:2986-2999 ranks `:rf/spawned` first and `update-snapshot` fourth ("only when you need it under a domain-specific name"). The warning's own text and the spec disagree about how to work around a hook nobody uses.
4. `skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md:124` — "A singleton boot-machine needs an explicit start + address … eager-start it in the boot fn and address it by `:system-id`", linking `spec/Pattern-Boot.md` §Worked example, whose :215-231 says the opposite: "A singleton — addressed by its registered id, NOT `:spawn` / `:system-id` … the id IS the address". The O-16 companion `migration/from-re-frame-v1/async-flow-fx-to-reg-machine.md` carries no `:system-id` claim (measured) — the skill line is the only source of the contradiction.
5. Manifest tiering: `spec/api-manifest.edn:259` `dispatch-to-system-fx` is `:tier :advanced` beside its siblings `spawn-fx` (:274) and `destroy-machine-fx` (:258) at `:implementation`; it is an fx HANDLER app code never calls (it emits the tuple; `docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:364` already says "implementation tier"). Source: `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1658`.
6. `make-machine-handler` as a registration door: 2 sites — `testbeds/deliberate_throw/core.cljs:134` and `tools/story/testbeds/login_form/events.cljs:57`, both `(rf/reg-event id [opts] (rf.machines/make-machine-handler spec))`, exactly the composition `examples/capabilities/machines/state_machine_walkthrough/core.cljc:208-212` says the 3-arity `reg-machine` makes unnecessary. Tables and leads that present it as the door: `spec/API.md:33` (artefact table: "`reg-machine`, `make-machine-handler`, …"), `spec/API.md:941` (its row: bare "`(make-machine-handler spec)` → event-handler fn", tier `advanced`), `spec/005-StateMachines.md:13` ("Machines are registered as event handlers via `reg-event + make-machine-handler`"), :24, :133, §Registration :857-870 (the lead example is the `reg-event` composition), :903 (hot-reload text). Its surviving rationale is real and stays: 005:945-955 "`make-machine-handler` is a pure factory" — Level-2 testing (69 impl-test mentions) and the spawn path's construction. `reg-machine*` stays (Story's provenance case, `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/loaders.cljc:195`); `reg-machine` / `defmachine` verified fine — no change.

## Target

- Conventions:441 — delete the "fx counterpart to the `dispatch-to-system` fn" clause.
- Conventions:439 — "Spawn a dynamic actor; the transition reducer binds the child's id into the parent's `:data` under `:rf/spawned` (005 §Recording the spawned id)".
- 009:2138 + `transition.cljc:2367-2376` — remedy names `:rf/spawned` first (read `(get-in data [:rf/spawned <invoke-id>])`), `update-snapshot` as the domain-key option; the emitted `:remedy` vector changes with it, and whichever test pins that vector (`grep -rn ':remedy' implementation/machines/test`) is updated. SPLIT OUT OF rf2-85og2 when its ground-1 re-test landed in PR #8595 (worker/budgetgates-85og2, 2026-08-21). This is the EDIT-SHAPED, LOUD-BOX-SAFE half — it needs NO window and can be dispatched beside anything.

WHAT PR #8589 GAVE US, and why it is not enough. rf2-xa8wo landed an interaction-to-paint clock on the slice app: slice_echo_clock_app.cljs requires re-frame.hicasso.examples.slice.{events,routes,views}, mounts through h/mount!, and its window! runs t0 -> real DOM event -> requestAnimationFrame -> setTimeout 0 -> t-paint. That instrument satisfies section 9.4's 'package-resident' test, which turns on what the instrument is POINTED AT rather than on jar residence, and it clears rf2-85og2's ground 1 for rows U1 and U2.

WHAT IT DOES NOT REACH, measured rather than assumed. The driver's OWN DOCSTRING states U3 and U4 are not served. Its four rows are a floor, two Hicasso interactions and a positive control — there is NO DONOR ARM, so C3 and C4 have nothing to compare against. The blocker for those four rows has therefore MOVED: it is no longer 'no instrument exists', it is 'this instrument's arms do not span the comparison'.

WHAT IS WANTED: a SECOND DRIVER plus a DONOR ARM, so U3, U4, C3 and C4 become reachable. Build the instrument; do not run a window. Sizing, arm choice and which donor is the honest comparator are all open and should be settled at source rather than from this text.

VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING. Re-read the driver's docstring at the tip and confirm U3/U4 are still unserved — rf2-85og2 is a bead whose refusals have already been overtaken once by a merge, which is exactly how this bead came to exist. If a donor arm has landed meanwhile, say so and close.

THE PROHIBITION THAT OUTRANKS THE TASK, carried over from rf2-85og2 and not negotiable: DO NOT WIDEN A BAND OR GUESS A THRESHOLD to make a row reachable. That programme has refused four times rather than do that, and each refusal carried more information than a pass would have. And note section 7: it routes every distributional row to pinned evidence runs on P-DEV-1 and FORBIDS converting one into a PR threshold, with check_budget_ledger.py enforcing it — so building a GATE here is out even where building an INSTRUMENT is in. That distinction is what a previous dispatch got wrong.

MOVE NO LEDGER CELL. The ledger stands at 49 rows / 31 MET / 5 BREACH / 3 UNRESOLVED / 10 UNPINNED.

SURFACE: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/. Not docs/design/hicasso/product/budgets.md, which rf2-85og2 owns.

WHAT LANDED. Two new files, pure additions, no existing file edited.
  slice_broad_clock_app.cljs  the second driver, on the slice FEED route, timing two broad
                              operations through the SAME window! the first driver publishes

SO U3, C3 AND C4 NOW HAVE AN INSTRUMENT ON THE GOVERNED POPULATION. They keep UNPINNED: an
instrument is not a verdict, and a verdict needs a quiet-box window.

THREE REFUSALS, EACH SOURCE-LOCATED.
1. NO NAVIGATION ROW, and this is mechanical. Two of the three broad operations the first
   driver names (a route change, a save reply) CANNOT be bracketed by this window at all:
   routing/activate-link! ends at router/dispatch!, the ASYNC door, so the click returns with
   the operation merely enqueued and the router drains it on a next-turn task. A window that
   stops at the first paint after the click stops BEFORE THE OPERATION HAS BEGUN. The slice's
   own flow_dom_cljs_test.cljs states the split. Those operations need a DIFFERENT window,
   bounded by the drain and its paint. Not built.
2. U4 IS NOT REACHABLE ON THE SLICE. It is registered over dragging/animation and the slice
   publishes neither -- every interaction it has is discrete. A per-frame estimator over a
   scripted repetition of a discrete interaction would be the same class of error the first
   driver exists to have stopped making, and adding a drag would move the population.
3. ONE DONOR DOES NOT SETTLE C3'S 'best relevant adapter'. UIx was chosen because the process
   carries one adapter and because this lane's re-taken HD-008 rows make direct UIx the faster
   donor (the conservative direction). A Reagent-on-subs donor needs a second adapter phase and
   therefore a second page.

WHAT THIS BEAD STILL OWES, and why it stays OPEN.
  (a) U4's INSTRUMENT, which is a THIRD DRIVER ON A THIRD PAGE. examples/ledger publishes a
      virtualized 10,000-row list over a real scroll viewport (see its virtualized_dom_cljs_test,
