title: nightly_failure_alert.py counts a run with an unfinished job as green (ignores every in_progress job, not only its own); a hung nightly advanced #11459 to greens=2
description:
## Problem

.github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py counted a hung, cancelled nightly as GREEN.

Run 39278093794 (2026-10-19) ended `cancelled`. Its browser job hit the 60-minute job cap at 16:27:34, but the Actions API still reported that job as `status=in_progress, conclusion=null` when the "Nightly result -> tracking issue" job ran at 16:27:52. The script logged `nightly-alert: run=39278093794 failing-steps=0 action=hold notifies=no` and wrote `greens=2` into #11459's state comment (`<!-- nightly-alert:v1 signature=10e682471f1e reds=2 greens=2 -->`).

The cause is the rule pinned by the self-test "an in-progress job (this script's own) is ignored" (around line 531; the rule's docstring is near line 132). It ignores EVERY in-progress job, not only the script's own. A job that is still running, or is reported running after a timeout, is therefore read as passing.

The hazard is concrete. One more such "green" closes #11459 automatically while the nightly is actually red, and the hang behind tonight's run is filed separately but is not yet fixed. The next scheduled nightly is ~2026-10-20 15:23 UTC.

## Change

- Ignore only the script's OWN job, identified exactly: by job name or by the current job id, using whatever the Actions environment provides. Read the code to choose.
- Treat any other job that is not completed as not green. Either make it red, naming the job as unfinished, or hold WITHOUT advancing the green counter. Choose whichever fits the script's existing action vocabulary with the least new surface, and say which in the PR.
- A run whose own conclusion is `cancelled` must never count as green, whatever its jobs report.
- Add self-test cases: another job in_progress gives no green; a cancelled run gives no green; the script's own in_progress job is still ignored.
- Do NOT edit #11459 or its state comment by hand. The next real run re-derives the state. Say in the PR body what tonight's false green left behind (greens=2) and what the next run will do with it.

## Acceptance

`python3 .github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py --self-test --verbose` passes with the new cases, and the new cases fail against the current rule (shown red first). Replaying run 39278093794 (the script has a replay/what-would mode near line 429) no longer reports it as green.
notes:
== DISPATCH (mayor), 2026-10-20 03:43:50 AUSEST: worker nightly-alert-green (branch worker/nightly-alert-green), dispatched from nightly run 39278093794. Must land before the 2026-10-20 ~15:23 UTC nightly.
== WORKER (nightly-alert-green), 2026-10-20 03:58 AUSEST: done; PR #11554 (draft until CI green)

Change, in .github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py only (no workflow edit):
- Own job identified exactly by is_own_job: the unfinished job of THIS run (GITHUB_RUN_ID == --run-id) whose runner_name equals RUNNER_NAME. A runner executes one job at a time. Both variables come from the runner, so expensive-tests.yml is untouched.
- Every OTHER unfinished job is RED. It contributes "<job> -> (job <status>, no verdict)", the same vocabulary as aborted jobs, and decide() is unchanged. Red was chosen over a non-advancing hold because a hold would need a new branch in decide().
- A run concluded cancelled or startup_failure is never green. It adds "(run) -> (run <conclusion>, no verdict)", only when the jobs read green. The run has no conclusion while the alert job runs, so this bites under --replay and on --run-id of a finished run. --replay now requests conclusion.
- The live log prints "own job, not graded: <name> (runner <r>)", or the no-match line.

Evidence:
- Self-test before the rule change (tests and parameters already in): exit 1, 7 failed / 39 passed. One failure reproduces the incident: ('hold', greens 2).
- Self-test after: exit 0, 46 passed.
- As-seen replay of run 39278093794 (the API's 12 jobs, with the browser job and the alert job set back to in_progress, and the own runner "GitHub Actions 1000974120"): old rule gives action=hold greens=2; new rule gives action=change greens=0 with "Browser, bundle, examples, Story/Xray gates -> (job in_progress, no verdict)".
- --replay 3 does NOT discriminate now. The API record caught up (the browser job reads completed/cancelled), so both old and new code print RED change for 2026-10-19.
- Fast-PR spine: exit 0. report-changed-surfaces arms nothing for this path (a declared file-level hole); no PR CI lane runs the script.

Residuals for the mayor:
(1) #11459 still carries reds=2 greens=2. A wholly green next nightly makes greens=3 and CLOSES it, with the hung night counted in the streak. A red next nightly resets greens to 0. Not edited here (outside the fence).
(2) The RUNNER_NAME == jobs-API runner_name equivalence on hosted runners is not provable before tonight's nightly. If it fails, the run goes red naming "Nightly result -> tracking issue -> (job in_progress, no verdict)" and logs the no-match line. That failure is closed and loud, not open. The fallback is one workflow env line passing job.check_run_id, which is outside this fence.
close_reason:
Merged in PR #11554 (rebase, commit 5506e56140, merge 21bbd8ed47). Only .github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py changed.

- The script ignores only its OWN job: the unfinished job of this run (GITHUB_RUN_ID == --run-id) whose runner_name equals RUNNER_NAME. A runner runs one job at a time, so exactly one job can match. The live log names the job skipped as its own, or says none matched.
- Every other unfinished job is red, reported as "<job> -> (job <status>, no verdict)", the same wording cancelled jobs get. Red rather than hold, because it needs no new branch in decide().
- A run concluded cancelled or startup_failure is never green, reported as "(run) -> (run <conclusion>, no verdict)". This applies under --replay and to a finished --run-id; --replay now requests the run conclusion.

Evidence: the self-test went red first against the old rule (exit 1, 7 failed / 39 passed, one case reproducing the incident's ('hold' ... greens 2)) and passes after (exit 0, 46 passed). A reconstruction of run 39278093794 as the alert job saw it (browser and alert jobs in_progress, the alert job's own runner name) gives action=hold greens=2 under the old rule and action=change greens=0 under the new, red on the browser job. The fast-PR spine exited 0. CI: 59 checks (19 passed, 40 skipped). The count is a legitimate narrowing, because a .github/scripts-only change arms none of the 20 dynamic JVM implementation-matrix entries; the mayor diffed the check names against #11553 to confirm.

Unverifiable before the first live run: the fix assumes RUNNER_NAME matches the jobs API's runner_name on GitHub-hosted runners. If it does not, the run goes LOUD red naming "Nightly result -> tracking issue -> (job in_progress, no verdict)" and logs the no-match line, never a false green. The fallback is one env line in expensive-tests.yml passing job.check_run_id.

Left for Mike: #11459's state marker still reads reds=2 greens=2, and one of those greens is the hung 2026-10-19 run. A fully green next nightly would close the issue on that count.

title: Nightly red: Xray feature gate 'managed http and effects rows' misses its :rf.http/timeout trace, then the gate hangs to the 60-min job cap
description:
## Problem

The nightly `expensive tests` run 39278093794 (2026-10-19, head ca993b1f5c) was cancelled. The job "Browser, bundle, examples, Story/Xray gates" (`browser-bundle-and-story-gates`, timeout-minutes 60) hit its cap. The last two nightlies finished it in 27 and 38 minutes. The last green nightly ran at 83a2a42d8e.

Two defects, both in the Xray feature gate step (`npm run test:xray-feature-gate`, i.e. `implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-xray-feature-gate.cjs`, nightly-full sweep of 16 scenarios over 11 surfaces):

1. A real failure. Scenario "managed http and effects rows" (`runHttpToggle`, tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs:1552) failed at 15:47:57 with `waitForValue: expected :rf.http/timeout :rf.http/* trace within 10000ms` (examples/scripts/spec-helpers.cjs:119). The app itself reached the timeout outcome: the trace dump shows `:http-toggle.core/set-outcome :rf.http/timeout` and a sub value of `:rf.http/timeout`. What the scenario waits for is an `:rf.http/*` trace carrying the timeout. The browser console also logged one 404. Among the merges since 83a2a42d8e, #11547 (rf2-beau9) removed `[:tags :category]` from traces and moved the error category to `:rf.error/id`, and #11538 changed machine snapshots. Treat these as SUSPECTS to check, not the cause.
2. A hang. After that failure the gate printed its diagnostics and then produced no output for 40 minutes, until the job cap killed it at 16:27:34. The orphans terminated were npm, sh, MainThread, http-server and chrome-headless-shell. A failing gate must exit non-zero promptly. The step also has no per-step timeout, unlike the other capped steps in .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml.

## Change

- Reproduce the scenario failure locally at trunk and find the cause. Bisect between 83a2a42d8e and trunk if needed. Fix the defect where it lives: if the trace contract changed by ruling (#11547), update the scenario's expectation; if a trace stopped being emitted, fix the emitter.
- Make serve-and-run-xray-feature-gate.cjs exit non-zero promptly after a scenario failure, closing the browser and the server. Pin this with a planted failure.
- Give the xray-feature-gate step in expensive-tests.yml a per-step timeout-minutes in line with its neighbours. A hang should become a named red, not a job-cap cancellation.
- Report why the per-PR "Story/Xray browser gates (PR-smoke)" did not catch this. Do not widen the PR-smoke set unless the change is a one-line, near-free addition.

## Acceptance

`npm run test:xray-feature-gate` (nightly-full) passes at the PR head. A planted scenario failure makes the gate exit non-zero within a minute or two, not hang. The step carries a per-step cap. A manual `workflow_dispatch` of expensive-tests.yml on the branch is NOT required: CI is the final gate, and the mayor re-runs the nightly after merge.
notes:
== DISPATCH (mayor), 2026-10-20 03:43:50 AUSEST: worker nightly-xray-gate (branch worker/nightly-xray-gate), dispatched from nightly run 39278093794. Must land before the 2026-10-20 ~15:23 UTC nightly.
== WORKER (nightly-xray-gate), PR #11555: two regressions plus a gate that could not fail

1. "managed http and effects rows": the cause is NOT #11547 or #11538. It is a race in testbeds/http_toggle, introduced by 36872c3915 (rf2-r1awf, the move to stub transports). Go called dispatch-sync for a failure outcome inside a with-transport scope and chose its branch from the outcome the view last rendered. The select dispatches asynchronously, so a Go clicked about 2 ms after the selection ran ahead of the queued ::set-outcome. In nightly run 39278093794 the :rf.http/timeout click issued api/5xx a second time (trace ids 1074 to 1084), and only then did set-outcome :rf.http/timeout run. The same race sent the 4xx click out on the live network, which is where the console 404 came from. Fix: selecting an outcome installs the matching backend as the frame's transport (an fx on ::set-outcome and ::initialise), and Go is a plain dispatch.

2. The 40-minute hang was a SECOND regression. Nothing went wrong after the http failure itself: the gate moved on to the next scenarios, and the routes-epochs scenario wedged its page's main thread. A bisect of 83a2a42d8e..ca993b1f5c, with a probe that pings the page's main thread, names 3c2550942e (#11535, Reagent views resolve their frame from the component tree first). Mechanism: epoch capture notifies :epoch listeners while it records a view render. The testbed runner's listener calls day8.re-frame2-xray.focus/focus! from there, and focus! wrapped its dispatches in (with-frame :rf/xray ...), which the tree-first rule overrides during a render. Every :rf.xray/* event therefore ran in the host frame :rf/default. At the wedge, epoch 152 of :rf/default carried Xray's own app-db keys, :epoch-history included. Its epoch history was nothing but :rf.xray/focus-after-frame, focus-epoch, select-frame and set-frame, so the redaction walk (re-frame.elision/walk-tree) never finished. Fix: every focus! dispatch now names {:frame :rf/xray}. A new test in focus_host_frame_async_cljs_test points :adapter/current-frame at the host frame for the length of the call. It is red against the pre-fix focus.cljc (1 failure, "focus drain never settled") and green after the fix.

3. serve-and-run-xray-feature-gate.cjs bounds the diagnostics' page.evaluate, context.close, browser.close, newContext/newPage and the harness cleanup (TEARDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS = 20 s), and exits non-zero. The nightly step gets timeout-minutes: 10, about three times the sweep's roughly three-minute length.

4. PR-smoke did not catch either regression because neither culprit PR opened the job: report-changed-surfaces.sh gives story_xray_browser=false for testbeds/http_toggle/core.cljs and for implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs, against a control of true for tools/xray/src/.../focus.cljc. Neither scenario is smoke-tagged, and widening the smoke set would not help without also widening the classifier, which is a hot zone. Reported, not widened.

Evidence, all at the PR head: the nightly-full xray gate exits 0 (16 scenarios, 0 failures). A planted throw exits 1, 27 s after its FAIL line. A planted main-thread wedge exits 1: 93 s from serve to FAIL (the 45 s scenario bound, then two 20 s teardown bounds), then 24 s from FAIL to exit. test:cljs exits 0 (6198 tests, 17509 assertions). The Xray JVM lane exits 0 (593 tests, 1583 assertions).

Finding for a separate item: since #11535, any (with-frame :x (dispatch ...)) reached from inside a Reagent render resolves to the tree's frame instead of :x. focus! was the case the gate hit; there may be others.
close_reason:
Merged in PR #11555 (rebase, merge 822228d6fc). Two regressions, neither of them the suspects the bead named (#11547, #11538):

1. The http failure was a race in testbeds/http_toggle, introduced by 36872c3915 (rf2-r1awf). Go used dispatch-sync and chose its branch from the outcome the view had last rendered, so a click about 2 ms after a selection overtook the queued ::set-outcome (in the nightly trace, ids 1074-1084, the timeout click re-issued api/5xx). Selecting an outcome now installs its backend as the frame's transport through an fx, and Go is a plain dispatch.
2. The hang bisects (83a2a42d8e..ca993b1f5c) to 3c2550942e (#11535: Reagent views resolve their frame from the component tree first). Epoch capture notifies :epoch listeners during a view render; the testbed runner's listener calls focus!, and focus!'s (with-frame :rf/xray (dispatch ...)) resolved to the HOST frame. Xray events piled into the host app-db until a redaction walk never finished. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/focus.cljc now names {:frame :rf/xray} on every dispatch; focus_host_frame_async_cljs_test fails against the old focus.cljc and passes. The general rule is filed and ruled as rf2-fwbix (an inner with-frame decides).

Also: serve-and-run-xray-feature-gate.cjs bounds every teardown and diagnostics await (20 s each), so a failing scenario exits instead of hanging. The nightly step has timeout-minutes: 10, about three times the roughly 3-minute sweep.

Evidence: the nightly-full gate at head exited 0 (16 scenarios, 0 failures, 157 s), and both failures reproduced at trunk. A planted thrown failure exited 1, 27 s after its FAIL line. A planted main-thread wedge exited 1, 24 s after FAIL; before the fix it was still hung when killed at 420 s. test:cljs 6198/17509, the Xray JVM lane 593/1583, check_readme_links --ci and the fast-PR spine all exited 0. CI was green: 85 checks (83 passed, 2 skipped).

PR-smoke did not catch either regression: the changed-surfaces classifier arms story_xray_browser for neither testbeds/http_toggle/core.cljs nor implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs, and neither scenario is smoke-tagged. Reported, not widened, because widening means the classifier hot zone. Noted and not tracked: routes-epochs logs boot-time :rf.error/frame-destroyed console errors (focus! runs before Xray's frame exists). They are console noise only and do not fail the gate.

title: Resources: a mutation's {:from-db} consequence targets resolve against the issuance context, so a reply never lands in another viewer's cache
description:
## Ruling

Mike ruled on 2026-10-20 that every write a mutation causes has one context, the one in force when the mutation was issued. An explicit `{:from-db <resolver>}` in a consequence target resolves against the app-db at issuance, not at settle. The spelling stays.

The alternative was to remove `{:from-db}` from post-write consequence targets, and route a deliberate current-viewer write through a `:reply-to` event. That is the fallback if issuance resolution proves heavier, as described under Change.

## Problem

Measured at trunk cb9cb3c074, under `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/`.

A mutation's execution scope is resolved and stored at execute: `cscope` in `mutation_events.cljc:856`, written on the instance (`empty-instance`, `mutation_runtime.cljc:69-89`) and carried on the reply payload (`:902`). The `:before-request` invalidation plan and the optimistic targets also resolve at execute (`:874-875`, `:918-927`).

The success-phase consequences resolve `{:from-db}` against the reply event's app-db instead:
- **Exact targets:** `resolve-exact-target-scope` (`:84-101`) is called from `apply-patches` (`:117`), `apply-populates` (`:148`) and `apply-removes` (`:210`). `succeeded-handler` runs them at `:1177-1183`, with the db from the reply event (`:1153`).
- **Invalidation descriptors:** `resolve-descriptor-scope` (`:550-563`), via `invalidation-plan`, at `:1193` and, in `failed-handler`, at `:1387`.

So if the viewer changes while a mutation is in flight, the response is written into the new viewer's cache as fresh data. The test `map-form-from-db-targets-resolve-at-settle` (`implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_populate_exact_target_cljs_test.cljc:101`) pins exactly this: zed issues, yan logs in, and zed's reply populates and patches yan's feed and profile. Generation checks do not catch it, because the mutation instance is still current.

## Change

**One constraint shapes the mechanism.** Consequence plans are `(fn [params result])` (Spec 016 §Cache-consequence callback signatures). Which resolvers a mutation references is therefore known only once the result arrives, at settle.

- **Recommended:** at execute, resolve every registered scope resolver with the pure, untraced resolution (`resolve-scope*-pure`, `scope_registry.cljc`). Carry the resulting `{resolver-id → scope}` map where `:scope` already rides. At settle, look `{:from-db r}` up in that map. Emit `:rf.resource/scope-resolved` only for the resolvers a consequence actually used.
- **If that proves heavier** than holding the issuance app-db value host-side for the instance's lifetime, do that instead. App-db values are immutable, so this is resolution against the issuance db by construction. Restored pending instances already reconcile to dangling, so host-side state lost on restore costs nothing.
- **Unchanged:**
  - a `{:from-db}` that resolves nil still drops the target fail-closed;
  - `:rf.scope/same` still means the execution scope;
  - the direct `:rf.resource/invalidate-tags` event still resolves at its own execution;
  - passive reads, ensures and route entries resolve as they do today.
- **Classification:** the carried scopes follow the classification of the existing `[:scope …]` carriers (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:96`, `:350-360`).

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/016-Resources.md:1032` and `:1062`, which say a descriptor's `{:from-db}` resolves "at settle time"; §Map-form exact resource targets (`:1094-1118`) gains the timing; Phase order step 1 (`:999`).
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2968-2994` (`MutationInstance`), if the instance gains a field. **Hot zone.**
- `skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources-mutations.md:104`.
- The docstrings at `mutation_events.cljc:84-88`, `:550-555` and `:565-570`.

## Acceptance

- `map-form-from-db-targets-resolve-at-settle` is flipped and renamed: with zed at issuance and yan at settle, the reply populates and patches zed's entries and leaves yan's untouched.
- `from-db-descriptor-resolved-at-settle-time` (`resources_invalidation_descriptors_cljs_test.cljc:159`) is flipped the same way for invalidation.
- A new test covers `:removes`, which has no settle-time test today.
- The nil fail-closed tests still pass (`resources_populate_exact_target_cljs_test.cljc:194`, `resources_invalidation_descriptors_cljs_test.cljc:175`, `resources_optimistic_validation` `:241`).
- JVM and `npm run test:cljs` green.
notes:
== DISPATCH (mayor), 2026-10-20 15:58:21 AUSEST: dispatched to worktree resources-mutation-context (branch worker/resources-mutation-context), cut from origin/main at cb9cb3c074. P1. The worker holds spec/016 and spec/Spec-Schemas.md for this wave.
== WORKER (resources-mutation-context), 2026-10-20 17:07:19 AUSEST: implemented on branch worker/resources-mutation-context, draft PR #11574.

Mechanism: the recommended route. At execute, scope_registry/resolve-all-pure resolves every registered resolver against the execute app-db (no trace) into {resolver-id -> scope-or-nil}; it rides the mutation reply payload as :from-db-scopes beside :scope. Every consequence resolution (optimistic exact + tag targets, :before-request plan, :patches/:populates/:removes, success and failure invalidation plans) reads that map through scope_registry/resolve-from-db-scopes, which emits :rf.resource/scope-resolved only for the resolver a consequence names (issuance scope, no :input-values) and throws :rf.error/resource-scope-not-registered for a resolver not registered at issuance. The settle handlers no longer read the reply event's app-db. resolve-exact-target-scope / resolve-descriptor-scope take the map in place of a db. Off-box, each carried scope takes the standing scope rule (trace_egress project-embedded-keys), as the payload :scope does. MutationInstance unchanged (map rides the payload, not the instance), so Spec-Schemas changed only ScopePolicy's comment.

Not taken: the host-side issuance-db fallback. Pure data on the payload keeps replay deterministic and needs no host-side release. Consequence: a resolver that throws now fails the execute before any write, rather than the settle after the server committed.

Tests: map-form-from-db-targets-resolve-at-settle flipped+renamed -at-issuance (also pins :from-db-scopes on the payload); from-db-descriptor-resolved-at-settle-time flipped+renamed from-db-descriptor-resolved-at-issuance; new map-form-from-db-removes-resolve-at-issuance, from-db-descriptor-on-failure-resolved-at-issuance, settle-traces-only-the-resolvers-its-consequences-name, a-mutation-payloads-issuance-scopes-agree-with-its-scope. Red at trunk before the fix: three namespaces, exit 1, 11 failures (yan's cache received zed's reply). Nil fail-closed tests unchanged and green.

Premise correction: the bead cites implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:96 and :350-360 for the [:scope ...] carriers; those lines are in implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/classification.cljc. No classification change was needed.

Outside the fence, not edited: examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/README.md:139 still says the mutation's scopes are "each resolved at settle time against the frame's db".

Gates (captured exits): red at trunk 1 (11 failures); targeted namespaces 0; resources JVM 0 (562 tests); test-jvm-implementation.sh 0 (19 artefacts); npm run test:cljs 0 (6220 tests); check_doc_slugs 0 (planted anchor fault -> 1, restored by blob hash); mkdocs --strict 0; test-fast-pr.sh 0. PR CI green on 46a86a22bc (All required checks passed). Disposition: done. Leave closing to the mayor on merge.
Merged-PR audit #11574: follow-up rf2-gaao1 — RealWorld resources README: explain mutation scopes at issuance. This is a separate open finding; the source status and ruling are preserved.
close_reason: Merged as PR #11574 (rebase, 9cdb8d4953). A mutation's consequences now resolve {:from-db ...} against its issuance context: at :rf.mutation/execute the runtime resolves every registered resolver against that event's app-db, untraced (scope_registry/resolve-all-pure), and carries the {resolver-id scope} map on the reply payload as :from-db-scopes beside :scope. Optimistic exact/tag targets, the :before-request plan, :patches/:populates/:removes and the success and failure invalidation plans all read that map through resolve-from-db-scopes; settle handlers no longer read the reply event's app-db. :rf.resource/scope-resolved is emitted only for resolvers a consequence uses, carrying the issuance scope and no :input-values. Off-box, each carried scope is tokenised by the payload :scope rule (trace_egress.cljc). title: Fresco test kit: ht/tree returns normalised Hiccup instead of the 004B v1 node vocabulary
description:
## Ruling

Mike ruled on 2026-10-20 that the Fresco L2 test kit's `ht/tree` returns normalised Hiccup instead of the 004B v1 node vocabulary. Tests then make their assertions in the language views are written in, so a programmer, or the AI writing the test, needs no second tree vocabulary.

The one-body boundary stays: `ht/tree` runs one body and does not mount.

## Problem

Measured at trunk cb9cb3c074.

**What `ht/tree` emits today.** `ht/tree` (`implementation/fresco/test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/test.cljs:1297-1472`) runs one body through `collector/render-body` and returns the 004B v1 tree, stamped `:rf.ui/tree-version 1` (`:1467-1470`):
- elements: `:tag :ns :attrs :events :key :children`;
- fragments;
- view boundaries: `:view-id :props :children`;
- the opaque marker `{:rf.ui/opaque :fn}`.

The node builders are at `:1019-1180`. The projections `find-all`, `find`, `attrs`, `text` and `intents` (`:1512-1590`) and the `markup-*` readers (`:1720-1910`) read that vocabulary.

**Spec 004B has two halves** (`spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md`, 667 lines):
- **The tree:** node schema, attribute normalisation, canonical children, versioning, projections and the semantic normalisation `N`, at roughly `:58-443`. `ht/tree` is its only producer, and the kit's own assertions its only consumer (`:21-29`).
- **The DOM conversion table** (`:444-602`). This half is live elsewhere: the SSR hiccup emitter cites it 13 times (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc`), and `spec/011-SSR.md:281`, `:285` and `:364` link it.

## Change

1. **Start with one consumer.** Convert `implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/examples/forms/l2_cljs_test.cljs` (10 calls; its docstring cites 004B) to assert on the normalised Hiccup. If the smaller form reads worse there, stop and say so on this bead.
2. **The new output.** `ht/tree` returns normalised Hiccup: `[tag attrs & children]` with
   - attributes normalised as today;
   - children canonicalised (no nils, flattened seqs);
   - intents left as data in their `on-*` attrs.

   A view boundary appears as its rendered body, or as a `[:rf.ui/view {:view-id …} …]` element if the boundary must stay visible. Take the smaller option that the existing tests can live with. The opaque marker stays a value.
3. **Port the rest.** Port the projections and the `markup-*` readers to the Hiccup form, then the remaining callers:
   - `test_kit_cljs_test` (24 calls), `examples/slice/a11y_cljs_test` (9) and `test_kit_dogfood` (2);
   - `test_kit_runtime_parity` (2) and the single calls in `combobox_keyboard_dom`, `erasure_sentinels`, `examples/ledger/a11y`, `examples/navigation/conduct_dom`, `forms_cljs_test`, `overlay_dom` and `test_kit_a11y`.
4. **Spec 004B.** Its tree half shrinks to the normalised-Hiccup contract, or moves into Fresco's test-kit docs if nothing outside the kit reads it. The conversion table stays where the SSR emitter and Spec 011 cite it.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md` (the tree half), `spec/Ownership.md:39`, `spec/README.md:70` and `spec/008-Testing.md:636`.
- **Hot zones:**
  - `spec/Conventions.md:104` (the `:rf.ui/*` member groups);
  - `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2338` and `:2440` (`:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` and the kit's ids).
- `docs/core/fresco/15-testing.md` §L2 (`:144-258`), `22-accessibility.md` and `api-reference.md`.
- `codec.cljs:1730` and `:1799` (`head-kind`, `child-kind`), shared with the kit.

## Acceptance

- `ht/tree` returns Hiccup, and every listed caller asserts on it.
- The forms L2 test is the first converted file in the PR.
- No `:rf.ui/tree-version` remains unless 004B keeps a versioned contract.
- `npm run test:cljs`, the Fresco gates, `mkdocs build --strict` and `check_doc_slugs.py` green.

The forms L2 test converted first in its own commit; every other caller ported; deletion census finds no code reference to a removed name. Spec 004B's tree half shrank to the Hiccup contract (667 -> 356 lines), conversion table kept, the two anchors Conventions and 009 link to kept; 011, Ownership, spec README and the Fresco guide pages follow. title: Preserve shared schema diagnostics in resource and mutation parameter errors
description:
Merged-PR audit of #11588 at 5f9ea8b3d26a3139847b2ac5936cbfd4e82d79bb.

Concrete behavior: resources/params.cljc:25-36 calls :schemas/check! in tags-only mode, then passes only (:explain (:tags failure)) to build-invalid-error. Both registry.cljc:494-512 and mutation_registry.cljc:264-284 therefore throw their domain invalid-params error with :params and raw :error only. The seam has already built a redacted :explain-humanized in development, but neither caller exposes it. When the validator throws, the seam returns :rf.error/malformed-schema with structural tags and no value; the pipeline discards that diagnosis too, yielding an ordinary invalid-params exception with :error nil and no malformed-schema trace.

Why this matters: rf2-1kdo2 explicitly includes resource and mutation params among the throwing sites that must report the shared failure shape. Spec 010, Humanize-hook (line 306 at this merge), promises :explain-humanized in the failure data a resource param check throws. Its malformed-schema contract (line 203) distinguishes a broken schema from a rejected input. The current exceptions leave a programmer or tool with the old port-specific explanation, or no explanation and an incorrect input-conformance diagnosis for a schema defect. The PR body acknowledges the malformed-params limitation; this is a separately trackable remaining part of the ruling.

Evidence: focused JVM probe ai/pr-audit/probe-pr-audit-sol-oct11-11588-1.clj, .log and .exit (exit 0), using source verified identical to the merge before and after. With [:map [:n :int]], {:n 1} conforms for both families; {:n \"x\"} makes check! return the installed humanizer's {:n [\"HUMANIZED\"]}, while both thrown ex-data maps contain no :explain-humanized anywhere. With a throwing validator, check! reports malformed-schema, while both public validate+canonicalize-params functions throw their ordinary invalid-params id with :error nil and emit no malformed-schema trace. No shadow-cljs lane was entered.

Small correction: carry the shared failure diagnosis through the one params pipeline and both error factories instead of reducing it to :explain. Preserve the existing domain error ids, throwing recovery and per-slot params redaction; expose the seam's already-redacted humanized explanation, and retain/report the malformed-schema distinction without reattaching an undecided raw value. Add focused assertions for resource and mutation ordinary failures and validator throws.

In both families :explain-humanized was nil. On a throwing validator :reason was the "do not conform" sentence, no :rf.error/malformed-schema trace fired, and the undecided {:n "SECRET-N"} rode RAW in :params, because per-slot redaction finds no marks on [:map [:n :int]]. title: A JVM-only check proves each documented coordinate set resolves every documented require exactly once
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 one JVM-only check of what an external consumer resolves. It resolves each documented coordinate set against the built jars and POMs (`clojure -Spath` plus a lookup) and asserts that each documented require resolves to exactly one classpath file. It runs no shadow-cljs.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e.

- **No gate sees a consumer's classpath.** The aggregate `implementation/deps.edn` (`:28-50`) puts every artefact on one classpath by `:local/root`. Each artefact's `:test` alias adds siblings its published `:deps` lack:
  - `implementation/ssr/deps.edn` ships core alone (`:42`) but tests with schemas, flows, routing and machines (`:57-60`);
  - `implementation/http/deps.edn` tests with schemas, flows, routing, ssr, machines and epoch (`:55-66`).
  So a require that resolves only through a sibling stays green in every suite.
- **The preflights check POMs, not resolution.** `.github/scripts/preflight-{story,xray,tool}-package.sh` parse the generated POM for complete, lockstep coordinates. None runs `-Spath` or `-Stree` (zero hits in `.github/scripts/`; `ElementTree` hits all three). They run only in `release-story.yml` (`:384`, `:443`, `:519`) and `release-xray.yml` (`:280`). The framework's `release.yml` runs none.
- **The documented sets exist in the repo:**
  - the template's `_reagent/deps.edn:8-9` and `_uix/deps.edn:10-11` (under `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/`);
  - the static feature table, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/features.cljc:90-127`: eight `:maven` coordinates, each with the `:require` it documents;
  - `docs/core/how-to/use-uix.md:58-60`, and Fresco alone at `docs/core/fresco/00-installation.md:38` (a `:local/root` until a release), with its requires at `:106-108`.

## Change

- Add one script that, for each publishable artefact:
  - takes the set from the `:clein/build` aliases, the authority `implementation/scripts/lib/publishable-runtimes.cjs` and `verify-version-lockstep.sh` already read;
  - applies the `:local/root` → `:mvn/version` rewrite to a scratch copy (`.github/scripts/rewrite-local-root-coord.sh`);
  - builds its jar and POM with clein into a scratch Maven local repo, as `release.yml` does.
- For each documented coordinate set, write a scratch `deps.edn` naming only that set, with `:mvn/local-repo` at the scratch repo. Run `clojure -Srepro -Spath`. Then look up each documented require (`re-frame.adapter.reagent`, `re-frame.http.managed`, …) as `.clj`/`.cljc`/`.cljs` across the classpath entries.
- It fails on zero matches (a hole) and on more than one (two jars shipping one namespace).
- Read the sets from the files above rather than a roster in the script, so the coordinate rename needs no edit here.
- Run it in the `release.yml` pre-release `test` job (`:192-305`, which `deploy-core` needs), and nightly in `expensive-tests.yml`, so the release candidate's run carries it.
- It loads nothing: a namespace's transitive requires and every CLJS compile stay with `rf2-59bgn` and the tag's one-off cold-repo proof.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` and `.github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml`. **Hot zone.**
- `TESTING.md`: a matrix row for the check.
- `docs/release-process.md` §Pre-flight checklist (`:192-201`): one line for the check.

## Acceptance

- Every documented set resolves, and every documented require hits exactly one file.
- Removing `day8/re-frame2` from `implementation/fresco/deps.edn`'s `:deps` (`:86`) in a scratch copy turns the check red: the Fresco page's `re-frame.core` require (`00-installation.md:106`) no longer resolves (planted-fault control).
- Adding a scratch jar that also ships `re_frame/schemas.cljc` turns it red on the duplicate.
- The script exits non-zero on its own failure, and its log names the set and the require.

## Sequencing

- Related: `rf2-59bgn` (the post-publish cold-repo install gate; this is its pre-publish half) and `rf2-fo4ng` (the coordinate rename, which this check must survive unedited).
- **Recommendation: this blocks `rf2-kmqx3`, the first tag.** Clojars has no yank, and this is the only check of what a consumer resolves that runs before anything publishes. It can land before or after `rf2-fo4ng`; if before, the rename PR carries it.
notes:
== DISPATCHED (mayor), 2026-10-21 17:03:01 AUSEST: worktree consumer-classpath-check, branch worker/consumer-classpath-check, solo. The bead recommends it block rf2-kmqx3 (the first tag, held for Mike); that dependency is not added yet. RE-DISPATCH FENCE: do not put a second worker on this bead or branch until that worker reports. Wave 1 of the adversarial-review beads: six workers, each holding a disjoint set of hot-zone files. resources-transport-prev (rf2-nwcpt) holds spec/Spec-Schemas.md and spec/009; fx-overrides-test-support (rf2-re4ed) holds spec/API.md with its two manifests and migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md; integration-tests-fresco (rf2-n73oq) holds spec/Conventions.md, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn and the classifier pair; substrate-dispose-spec006 (rf2-c3792, rf2-ds7oe) holds spec/006; consumer-classpath-check (rf2-j2nso) holds .github/workflows/release.yml and expensive-tests.yml; subs-per-node-step (rf2-s8zl1) holds no hot zone.
== WORKER (consumer-classpath-check), 2026-10-21 17:59:12 AUSEST: DONE in PR #11604, not merged yet

What landed:
- .github/scripts/check-consumer-classpath.sh (driver) + check-consumer-classpath.clj (structural helper, read-only EDN/Clojure reading, loads nothing). It builds all 13 publishable artefacts (the publishable-runtimes.cjs :clein/build authority) the way release.yml does: scratch copy, rewrite-local-root-coord.sh, `clein jar` + `clein pom`, jar + POM installed into a scratch Maven repo. It then resolves each documented set with `clojure -Srepro -Spath` and requires each documented require to be shipped by exactly one classpath entry. Exit 1 on a hole, a duplicate, or a set that does not resolve; exit 2 on input it cannot classify.
- Documented sets are read from files, with no coordinate spelled in the script: the template's _reagent and _uix deps.edn files (requires = what core.cljs reaches through the app namespaces; stories.cljs is excluded because Story rides the :dev alias), the 8 entries of core's feature-registry (set = core + :maven, require = :require), and the first deps.edn block plus the first following ns form on docs/core/how-to/use-uix.md and docs/core/fresco/00-installation.md. A publishable lib resolves at VERSION whatever the page writes for it (<latest>, {{rf2-version}}, a :local/root checkout).
- Wired into release.yml's pre-release `test` job (before npm install) and a new nightly expensive-tests.yml job `consumer-classpath`, which is also in nightly-result's needs. One TESTING.md Kinds-of-tests row, one docs/release-process.md pre-flight line.
- scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn gains `".github" 0`. The helper is the first tracked Clojure file under .github/, and the dialect ratchet requires every surface holding one to be named; floor 0, :min-edges held.

Evidence (local, Windows Git Bash):
- Full run exit 0: 13 artefacts built, 12 documented sets, 18 requires, each shipped by exactly one entry. uix.core ships .clj and .cljs in one jar and counts once, which is why the count is per classpath entry rather than per file.
- Planted fault, hole: dropping BOTH day8/re-frame2 and day8/re-frame2-ssr from a scratch copy of Fresco's :deps gives exit 1, with "docs/core/fresco/00-installation.md:36: require re-frame.core resolves to NO classpath file".
- Planted fault, duplicate: a scratch artefact shipping re_frame/schemas.cljc, made a dependency of schemas in the copy, gives exit 1, with ":schemas: require re-frame.schemas resolves to 2 classpath entries: re-frame2-schemas-0.0.1.alpha.jar, dupe-schemas-0.0.1.alpha.jar". Both plants ran in one copy, and the run reported exactly those 2 findings across 12 sets.
- Build-step failures propagate: a failed rewrite exited 3, a failed clein build exited 1.

PREMISE THAT DID NOT HOLD: the Acceptance plant "remove day8/re-frame2 from Fresco's :deps turns the check red" stays GREEN (scratch-copy run, exit 0). Fresco also publishes day8/re-frame2-ssr, and ssr's POM carries day8/re-frame2, so re-frame.core still reaches a Fresco consumer transitively through re-frame2-0.0.1.alpha.jar. That is correct consumer behaviour, not a missed hole. The red control has to cut both in-repo edges, as above.
Citation drift at tip: Fresco's deps map opens at 00-installation.md:38 and its coordinate sits on :39. Every other citation held.

Changed-surface classifier: the two new .github/scripts paths and release.yml classify to zero outputs. So do preflight-story-package.sh, rewrite-local-root-coord.sh, verify-version-lockstep.sh and release-story.yml. No PR lane runs this check, so there is nothing for an arm to schedule, and none was requested. The PR still arms every surface through expensive-tests.yml and TESTING.md.

Linux: the script has run only under Git Bash on Windows. Its first Linux run is the first nightly after merge, which comes before rf2-kmqx3.

Sequencing recommendation (mayor to record): this blocks rf2-kmqx3, the first tag.

title: The portable conformance corpus grades only public contract; internal-shape ops move to reference tests
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 that the portable corpus in `spec/conformance/` grades only the public contract and the normative trace shapes. The call ops and expectations that bind internal shapes move to reference-only tests, so an internal refactor is not a port obligation:

- `:derivation-graph`, a shape Spec-Schemas says has no public accessor;
- `:assemble-image`, whose descriptor pools are keyed by `:rf.provenance/ns` strings;
- the `:epoch-records` and `:error-emit-records` record-shape expectations.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e. The corpus holds 242 fixtures.

**What binds internals.**
- `:derivation-graph` (grammar `spec/conformance/fixture-file.edn:707-729`): `derivation-graph-algebra.edn` and `derivation-graph-algebra-full.edn`. Spec-Schemas says "no public authoring or accessor primitive ships" (`spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3152`; `spec/Derivations.md:312`).
- `:assemble-image` (`fixture-file.edn:403-445`): the nine `image-*.edn` fixtures. The op drives `re-frame.image-assembly`'s explicit-pool assembler and reads descriptor coordinates (`spec/conformance/README.md:276-297`).
- `:epoch-records` (`fixture-file.edn:279-284`): eight fixtures. `:rf/epoch-record` is Layer: Runtime, dev-tier (`Spec-Schemas.md:4257-4262`).
- `:error-emit-records` (`fixture-file.edn:273-278`): three fixtures. The error-emit registry is "for framework-internal consumers" (`spec/API.md:618`).

**Two kinds of fixture.**
- **Wholly about an internal shape (15 fixtures):** the two derivation fixtures, the nine image fixtures, and `epoch-record-shape`, `epoch-ring-multi-dispatch` and `replay-with-interceptor-override`. Besides `:epoch-records`, those three assert only `:final-app-db`, or a trace incidental to the record. The 15th is `data-classification-epoch-export-projects-no-storage-mutation`, which pins the stored epoch record; its paired t1 redaction is also pinned portably by `data-classification-frame-sensitive-app-db-redacts.edn`.
- **A public contract with one internal key (7 fixtures):** `cross-spec-machine-action-throws`, `drain-depth-limit`, `error-handler-exception` and `machine-internal-event-boundary` (`:epoch-records`); `effect-map-shape-bad-fx-value`, `effect-map-shape-bad-top-level-key` and `flow-eval-exception` (`:error-emit-records`). Each also grades `:final-app-db` and `:trace-emissions` or `:effects-routed`.

**The harness.**
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc`:
  - claims `:core/image` and the two `:derivation/*` tags (`:135`, `:188-190`);
  - grades the two keys (`:828-835`);
  - lists `:derivation/algebra-graph` as dev-posture (`:878-883`);
  - implements both ops (`:1267-1333`, contributors at `:1023`).
- `conformance_test.clj` pins those ops and keys (`:158`, `:225-240`, `:396-400`, `:510-520`), and `conformance_submap_test.clj` pins the `:error-emit-records` matcher.
- The flows family runner grades `:error-emit-records` too (`implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_conformance_test.clj:12`, `:263`).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/conformance.cljc` has nothing op-specific.

## Change

- **Grammar.** Remove from `fixture-file.edn`: the `:derivation-graph` and `:assemble-image` call entries, the `:epoch-records` and `:error-emit-records` expectation keys, and the `:core/image`, `:derivation/algebra-graph` and `:derivation/algebra-graph-subs-machines` capability tags (`:107-109`).
- **Move whole** the 15 fixtures to a reference-only home that the same runner grades. One way: a reference fixture directory under `implementation/core/test/`, plus a small reference grammar that adds the four removed entries back for that directory only. Derivation cases may instead go to the existing reference-only tier, `implementation/derivation-conformance/`.
- **Strip** the one internal key from the 7 public fixtures, which stay portable. Carry each stripped assertion in a reference-only test: epoch ones beside `implementation/epoch/test/`, error-record ones beside core's error-emit tests and the flows runner.
- **Harness.** The portable runner stops claiming and grading what moved, and the reference runner keeps it. `conformance_test.clj`'s guards follow the ops they pin.
- **Stays:** every public-contract expectation, the moved fixtures' assertions (now reference-only), and the standing rulings that an expected `nil` matches nil or absent (rf2-nbgqz) and that `:fixture/spec-version` stays (rf2-s0tzq, rf2-myknb).

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/conformance/README.md`:
  - `:178` (the `:derivation-graph` paragraph);
  - `:180` ("The set is additive"): say ops that bind internals leave the portable set;
  - `:276-297` (the `:assemble-image` section);
  - `:305` and `:312` (the `:core/image` and `:derivation/*` capability rows).
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4262`, the `:rf/epoch-record` Conformance line. **Hot zone.**
- `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:547` (the epoch-export fixture row).
- `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md:564` (the `:derivation/*` row) and `spec/Derivations.md:312` ("which Xray and the conformance fixtures consume").
- `tools/xray/spec/025-Derivation-Graph-Panel.md:349-352`.
- `spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md:131` keeps its link, because that fixture stays portable.

## Acceptance

- `git grep` for `:assemble-image`, `:derivation-graph`, `:epoch-records` and `:error-emit-records` under `spec/conformance/` reads 0, with a control search for `:trace-emissions` that still hits.
- The reference implementation still grades every moved assertion: the moved fixtures pass under the reference runner, and the stripped keys pass in their reference tests.
- `conformance_grammar_test.clj` green, so every portable fixture parses under the slimmer grammar.
- The JVM core suite, `npm run test:cljs`, the flows, machines and epoch JVM suites, the derivation-conformance tier, `scripts/check_conformance_fixture_edn.py`, `mkdocs build --strict` and `check_doc_slugs.py` green.

Citations had drifted only by line (Spec-Schemas :rf/epoch-record Conformance line now :4254, Implementor-Checklist derivation row :587).

What moved. The portable grammar (spec/conformance/fixture-file.edn) drops the :assemble-image and :derivation-graph call arms, the :epoch-records and :error-emit-records expect keys, the :core/image and two :derivation/* tags, and the :positional / :member / :non-member laws only those entries named (26 call arms, 22 expect keys, 8 laws remain). title: A frame's descriptor-pool provenance lives on its record; the pool atom and construction hand-off go
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 that a frame's descriptor-pool provenance lives on its frame record, beside the generation, and the public 2-arity `(make-frame opts descriptors)` stays.

- nil means the live store. Pool and generation are read and restored together, from one record snapshot.
- Delete the separate `frame-generation-pool` atom with its publication, rollback and release paths, and the one-shot construction hand-off (`call-with-frame-construction-claim!`) that exists for that write. Re-derive the provisional row's visibility.
- Keep the admission and clean-rollback guarantees. Descriptor pools stay transient and unserialised.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e. Paths are under `implementation/core/src/re_frame/` unless stated.

**A second id-keyed store holds the pool:** `frame-generation-pool` (`live_frame.cljc:842-864`), its record, restore and release fns (`:866-918`), and a destroy hook published at ns load (`:953`). The section runs `:717-962`.

**Generation and pool are read apart.** `reproject-live-frame!` takes token and generation from the record, then the pool from the atom (`:1536-1540`). The atom is written before the engine commit, so during a re-construction the outgoing generation can meet the incoming pool (`:830-840`).

**The hand-off exists for this write.** `make-frame` runs the write, commit and rollback inside `call-with-frame-construction-claim!` (`live_frame.cljc:1244-1256`; `frame.cljc:337-369`). Its machinery has no other `src/` caller: `*frame-construction-handoff*` (`frame.cljc:219`), the hand-off fns (`:301-335`), and the `handoff?` argument of `call-with-frame-transaction!` (`:371-386`). The claim also covers the `displaced-record` read behind the subscription refresh (`live_frame.cljc:1236-1250`).

**The record already carries the siblings.** `:generation` and `:live-store?` arrive as reserved config keys (`live_frame.cljc:1171-1172`). They are seated on the record (`frame.cljc:2433`, `:2441`, `:3620-3622`) and stripped from `:config` (`:2491`, `:3548`, `:3604`). `restore-provisional-frame!` rolls the generation back (`:3149-3180`).

**Provisional visibility:** a first construction's row is visible only to its owner (`frame.cljc:1333-1352`).

## Change

- **Record slot.** The pool travels as a reserved key beside `:rf.frame/generation`. The engine seats it beside `:generation`, strips it from `:config`, and stages and restores it with the generation under the same identity check (`frame.cljc:3175-3176`). Reprojection leaves it alone.
- **One snapshot:** `reproject-live-frame!` reads token, generation and pool from one record.
- **Delete** the atom and its three fns, plus the `:live-frame/on-frame-destroyed!` hook. Its directory entry (`late_bind/directory.cljc:821-831`), destroy step (`frame.cljc:4749-4771`), docstring line (`:4475-4481`) and comments (`live_frame.cljc:68`, `:717-840`, `:2008-2030`) go too.
- **Delete the hand-off**: `call-with-frame-construction-claim!`, the hand-off fns and var, and `handoff?`. `upsert-frame!` claims for itself and hands out the displaced record through its existing out-channel (`frame.cljc:3286-3291`), so that read stays inside the reservation.
- **Visibility.** Re-derive the provisional-row rule. The owner check still holds without the hand-off, because `upsert-frame!` binds its own owner. Keep owner-only visibility as far as its stated reason needs (no unrelated caller sees a pre-setup row, `:1359-1362`).
- **Stays:**
  - the public 2-arity;
  - the same-id refusal `:rf.error/frame-construction-in-progress`;
  - a failed creation leaves nothing, and a failed re-construction keeps the prior generation and pool;
  - the pool is not serialised and appears in no `frame-meta`, Tool-Pair or Xray read;
  - the sealed generation keeps its shape.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/002-Frames.md:820-823`: step 6 drops the provenance row. **Hot zone.**
- No public API change: `spec/API.md:87` and `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:912` stand.

## Acceptance

- Keep `initial-events-cascade-does-not-reproject-onto-the-previous-pool` (`make_frame_generation_pool_window_jvm_test.clj`), reading the record slot instead of the private atom.
- In `make_frame_generation_pool_contention_jvm_test.clj`:
  - keep `rejected-same-id-attempt-neither-publishes-nor-clobbers`, re-pointed the same way;
  - delete `provenance-write-and-rollback-both-hold-the-id-reservation` (no separate write);
  - delete `rollback-restores-a-recorded-nil-row-rather-than-removing-it` (absent and nil no longer differ);
  - delete `a-handed-off-reservation-is-adopted-and-a-spent-one-is-not`.
- Delete `a-construction-handoff-permits-exactly-one-engine-entry` (`frame_construction_transaction_cljs_test.cljc:93`).
- Delete `frame_destroy_generation_provenance_cljs_test.cljc` and `live_frame_teardown_hook_reload_jvm_test.clj`, because the pool now leaves with the record at dissoc.
- Keep both pool tests in `live_frame_reload_cljs_test.cljc` (`:303`, `:318`).
- New: a failed re-construction interleaved with a reprojection leaves generation and pool paired; `frame-meta` carries no pool.
- Green: `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`, `npm run test:cljs`, `late_bind_drift_test.clj`.

## Sequencing

Goes before the lifecycle-registry bead, which would otherwise convert the hook this deletes; both edit Spec 002 §Destroy. It shares two test files with the frame-config validator bead, which replaces their `:on-create` failure trigger. Whichever lands second rebases.
notes:
== DISPATCHED (mayor), 2026-10-22 00:01:40 AUSEST: worktree frame-pool-on-record, branch worker/frame-pool-on-record, alone, holding spec/002-Frames.md; rf2-zp0ne (lifecycle registry) follows it on the same surface RE-DISPATCH FENCE: do not put a second worker on this bead or branch until that worker reports.
== WORKER (frame-pool-on-record), 2026-10-22 00:54:53 AUSEST: DONE, draft PR #11633 (branch worker/frame-pool-on-record, commit a0e3a8b9a8 on trunk 450663ee5e)
- Record slot: make-frame threads :rf.frame/descriptor-pool beside :rf.frame/generation; the engine seats :descriptor-pool (nil = live store), strips it from :config via one construction-input-keys list (also the created/re-registered traces), stages it with the generation on re-registration, and restore-provisional-frame! restores both under the generation's identity check (a reprojection that landed in the staged window keeps both). reproject-live-frame! reads token/generation/pool from ONE rf.frame/frame record.
- Deleted: frame-generation-pool atom + record/restore/release fns, the :live-frame/on-frame-destroyed! publication, directory row, destroy step-6 call + docstring entry + comments; the construction hand-off (call-with-frame-construction-claim!, call-with-frame-construction-handoff!, consume-/unspent- fns, *frame-construction-handoff*) and call-with-frame-transaction!'s handoff? arg (its only caller passed join-current-owner? false, so that dead branch went too). upsert-frame! claims for itself; its out-channel now carries {:token :displaced} (deliver-construction-outcome!), :displaced = the exact pre-stage record from swap-vals!.
- Provisional visibility re-derived: unchanged predicate (owner is the dynamic transaction owner AND still holds id on this host thread). Reason: only upsert-frame!'s own transaction binds *frame-transaction-owner*, and the hand-off never bound a different owner; the host-thread half excludes a JVM-conveyed binding. Docstring now states the derivation.
- Spec 002: Destroy step 6 drops the provenance row; the line-674 'one-shot handoff' sentence now says only the engine holds the claim.
- New test failed-re-construction-keeps-generation-and-pool-paired (cljc): RED on trunk exactly as predicted [true ::live-v2 <diff> ::pool]; green after. frame-meta carries no pool (asserted).

title: M73 codemod: an explicitly named non-Clojure PATH crashes the whole run with a reader error that names no file (directories are filtered, files are not)
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 2a6fd908a6.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md, "M-73 — one event-registration form" (the codemod CLI, lines 533-546), and the codemod it runs: migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/reg_event_codemod.clj (`expand-paths`, lines 1650-1660; `scan-paths` and `rewrite-paths!`).

## What it says

Line 533: "Run it from the project's own root as a Clojure git dependency, pointing `PATH` at the project's source dirs". Line 541: `-M -m re-frame.migration.reg-event-codemod PATH ...`. Nothing says that a PATH which names a FILE is parsed whatever its extension.

## What happened (generic)

A migration that scopes the codemod to one unit's files (for example the output of `git diff --name-only` for a unit, or a planned file list) passes file paths rather than directories. When that list contains a non-Clojure file (package.json, a .md, a .yml), the codemod parses it as Clojure, throws a reader error that names no file, and exits 1. Because the scan is all-or-nothing, the findings for every good file in the same run are lost too. Observed on a ~170-file app when a unit's changed-file list included package.json.

## Evidence

* Source: `expand-paths` filters a DIRECTORY through `clj-source-file?` (.clj/.cljc/.cljs), but passes a FILE through unfiltered: `(.isFile f) [f]`. `scan-string` / `rewrite-string` call `z/of-string` with no try/catch, so the rewrite-clj reader error propagates with no :file.
* Reproduced at origin/main (codemod via :local/root, in an empty scratch dir), with an a.cljs holding one `rf/reg-event-fx` and a 4-line package.json:
  * `... reg-event-codemod a.cljs package.json` exits 1 and prints only `Execution error (ExceptionInfo) ... [line 2, col 11] A single colon is not a valid keyword.` The a.cljs finding is not printed.
  * Control: `... a.cljs` exits 0 and prints `a.cljs:2:1 reg-event-fx rename ...`. The directory form `... .` exits 0 and prints the same finding (package.json skipped by the extension filter).
* The same expand-paths code is present at the pinned sha 0d4cf2e537 the leaf prints.
* Not confirmed: the friction note also named a per-unit "codemod rescan" gate in orchestrating-a-large-migration.md. No such gate exists at this tip (`git grep -n -i "rescan"` over skills/re-frame-migration finds only the codemod's own Type-B rescan note at auto-call-site-rewrites.md:593). That part of the gate was the downstream project's own, so it is not part of this report.

## Suggested change

1. Codemod: apply the same .clj/.cljc/.cljs filter to explicitly named files (skip, and report each skipped path on stderr), and wrap each file's parse so a reader error names the file and the scan continues with the other files (non-zero exit at the end if any file failed).
2. Leaf, line 533 or 544: one sentence that PATH may be directories or files, that only Clojure sources are read, and (until 1 ships) that a file list must be filtered to *.clj/*.cljc/*.cljs first, for example a unit's changed-file list.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): M-42 item 4 says to wrap the producer's value in unsafe-html but never shows the prop form; the natural {:__html (r/unsafe-html s)} is deleted as silently as the untagged map
description: Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626. Priority 2: the natural reading of the instruction produces a site that compiles, passes the floor-gate grep, and silently renders an empty element. That is the very loss M-42 item 4 exists to prevent. ## Skill file and section - skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-handlers-state.md §M-42, "Apply, symbol by symbol", item 4 "Raw-HTML producers" (line 212). - The same instruction in the corpus: migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md §M-42, Migration agent action step 5 (line 1885). - Follows the closed rf2-vpd7m, which added item 4 but gave no hiccup before/after. ## What it says - guided-handlers-state.md:212: "wrap a producer's value in `reagent.core/unsafe-html` only where the code shows its string escaped, sanitized or application-owned, and change nothing else". - README.md:1885: "Wrap each producer whose string the code shows to be escaped, sanitized or application-owned in `reagent.core/unsafe-html`". - README.md:1875 is the only place the shape can be inferred: "keeps that prop only when its value is tagged" and the `.cljc` form `#?(:clj {:__html s} :cljs (r/unsafe-html s))`. No page in skills/re-frame-migration writes the hiccup before/after. The only literal example in skills/ is in a different skill (reagent-fresco-migration catalog-mechanical.md:458). ## What happened (generic) Both texts say to wrap the producer's value or string. A v1 site reads `[:div {:dangerouslySetInnerHTML {:__html s}}]`, and the string there is `s`. The natural edit is therefore `{:dangerouslySetInnerHTML {:__html (r/unsafe-html s)}}`, which wraps the string and keeps the map. Stock Reagent 2.0.1 deletes that prop. The tag has to replace the whole `{:__html …}` map: `{:dangerouslySetInnerHTML (r/unsafe-html s)}`. The wrong form reports nothing: no compile error, no warning, no `:rf.error/*` trace, just an empty element. It also defeats the Identify step. floor-gate.md Check 3's grep (`dangerouslySetInnerHTML|__html|unsafe-html`, floor-gate.md:68) now finds `unsafe-html` on the line, so the site looks done. This was observed on a ~170-file app. ## Evidence - Stock Reagent 2.0.1, reagent/impl/template.cljs:131-135 (`convert-props`): `(when-let [d (and js-props (.-dangerouslySetInnerHTML js-props))] (if (instance? UnsafeHTML d) (set! … #js {:__html (.-s d)}) (js-delete js-props "dangerouslySetInnerHTML")))`. - Only a prop value that is itself an `UnsafeHTML` instance survives. - A map holding a tagged value is converted to a plain JS object and deleted. - reagent/core.cljs:374-382: `unsafe-html` returns `(tmpl/UnsafeHTML. s)`, "a tagged value for use with :dangerouslySetInnerHTML". - In-repo witness of the correct shape: implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/reagent_codemod_contract_donor_cljs_test.cljs:112-118. It uses `:dangerouslySetInnerHTML (r/unsafe-html "x")`, with the tag as the whole prop value, and shows the untagged `{:__html …}` deleted. ## Suggested change In guided-handlers-state.md §M-42 item 4, and in the corpus step 5, add the before/after line and one sentence: v1: [:div {:dangerouslySetInnerHTML {:__html s}}] v2: [:div {:dangerouslySetInnerHTML (r/unsafe-html s)}] "The tag replaces the whole `{:__html …}` map. `{:__html (r/unsafe-html s)}` is deleted as silently as the untagged map." Optionally, have the Check 3 / M-42 grep flag `__html` and `unsafe-html` appearing in one form as a likely misreading.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): causal-world-inputs source triage sends every in-handler subscribe read to the :db coeffect, but machine snapshots live in runtime-db and the O-16 producer guard requires subscribe-once [:rf/machine id]
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626. Priority 2: two pages contradict each other, and following the triage turns the O-16 producer guard into a read that can never succeed (a silent stall).

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/causal-world-inputs.md: the Scope note (line 7) and §Triage — split an in-handler ambient read by source (line 19).
- The same routing is repeated at breaking-changes.md:288 (the "What stays the same" `subscribe` carve-out) and guided-views-m11.md:242.
- The conflicting page: migration/from-re-frame-v1/async-flow-fx-to-reg-machine.md §Deliver only to a live, awaiting run (line 147) and its worked example (line 169).

## What it says

- causal-world-inputs :7: "An in-handler read whose value is derived from app-db — an `@(rf/subscribe …)` deref, or any recompute of derived state inside the handler body — … read it from the `:db` coeffect the handler already holds. db is a coeffect."
- causal-world-inputs :19: "DB-derived — an `@(rf/subscribe …)` deref … read the slice / recompute the derived value from `:db`."
- Companion :147: "The handler reads each awaiting machine's snapshot with `(rf/subscribe-once [:rf/machine <machine-id>])` — the one-shot read for handler bodies".

## What happened (generic)

The O-16 recipe adds a subscribe read inside a producer handler. A worker who then applies the triage to that handler is told to replace the read with a `:db` read. But machine snapshots live in runtime-db (`[:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots <id>]`), a partition "the handler never holds" (spec/002-Frames.md:447). The rewritten guard never sees the awaiting tag, never forwards, and the converted boot hangs on its first await with no error. That is the companion's "#1 silent-failure mode".

The triage's own premise ("db-derived") does not hold for `[:rf/machine …]`, but no page says so, and the triage is cited from three places as the rule for every in-handler subscribe.

## Evidence

- spec/002-Frames.md:405 (two partitions; machine snapshots in runtime-db) and :447 ("runtime-db is a partition the handler never holds").
- spec/API.md:197 (`subscribe-once`: "one-shot, non-reactive read for handler bodies").
- Observed on a ~170-file app's boot design unit, where the two instructions collided.

## Suggested change

Add a carve-out to the triage (and one clause each at breaking-changes.md:288 and guided-views-m11.md:242): "A read of framework runtime state — `[:rf/machine <id>]`, or any other sub backed by runtime-db — is not db-derived. It stays an `rf/subscribe-once` in the handler, as the O-16 companion's producer guard requires." Link the companion's §Deliver only to a live, awaiting run.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
New evidence from a later retrospective pass (verified at origin/main 0783705626). It bears on this item's premise and on its suggested fix.

- A handler DOES hold runtime-db. implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:352-382 (`assemble-initial-ctx`) stages `:rf.db/runtime` in every handler's coeffects, beside `:db`. spec/002-Frames.md:447 ("runtime-db is a partition the handler never holds") is about the `:db` EFFECT not replacing runtime-db, not about what the handler can read.
- The ruled read is `compute-sub` against that partition. rf2-qzfrn (closed, ruled 2026-10-20) has handlers read framework state with `(rf/compute-sub [:rf/machine id] (:rf.db/runtime cofx))`. The compute-sub docstring gives the same example (implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:2428-2433).

So the carve-out could name `(rf/compute-sub [:rf/machine <id>] (:rf.db/runtime cofx))` as the in-handler read, beside the O-16 companion's `subscribe-once`. Or the companion could say why it prefers `subscribe-once`. Either way the triage, the companion and the ruling should agree.

The same retrospective also reports two further gaps in the triage bullet, filed separately: rf2-xtfib (a path-focused `:db` read) and rf2-6kxq9 (the missing compute-sub / shared-helper / interceptor-body routes).

title: docs(xray): the layout-host recipe uses an un-namespaced .app-shell class, has no variant for an app that already scrolls an inner pane, and ships no print rule
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/xray-replaces-10x.md §"The layout host (true-inline default)" (lines 116-142).
- The same snippet appears in docs/xray/01-installation.md §"Reserve the host" (lines 48-80), tools/xray/README.md:126-134, tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md:45-90, and the console host hint that Xray prints (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/config.cljc:261-283).

## What it says

- xray-replaces-10x.md:123 gives the host markup as `<div class="app-shell">`, and :131 gives the CSS as `.app-shell { display: flex; width: fit-content; min-width: 100%; min-height: 100vh; }`. The host is `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh`.
- docs/xray/01-installation.md:78 and spec 011:85: "Keep the window as the app's scroller. Routing's scroll-to-top and Back restoration act on the window". The migration leaf does not carry this sentence.

## What happened (generic)

A migration pastes the host recipe into an existing v1 app's HTML and CSS. Three things are unaddressed:

1. **Un-namespaced class.** `app-shell` is a common application class name. An app that already styles `.app-shell`, or a CSS framework that does, either restyles Xray's wrapper or has its own element restyled by the pasted rule. Every other Xray surface is namespaced (`data-rf-xray-host`, `--rf-xray-inline-width`, `--rf-xray-accent`). The wrapper alone is not.
2. **Window scrolling is required but unstated in the migration leaf.** Many v1 apps, dashboards especially, pin `html, body, #app` to `height: 100%` and scroll an inner pane. The wrapper sets only `min-height: 100vh`, which gives its children no definite height. So an inner `height: 100%` chain that used to stop at the viewport now grows to content height.
   - Spec 011's reason for window scrolling is re-frame2 routing's scroll restoration. A v1 app being migrated does not use that routing.
   - The migration leaf neither states the requirement nor offers a full-height variant for an app that already owns an internal scroller.
3. **No print rule.** Nothing in tools/xray ships `@media print` (a grep over tools/xray finds 0, against 6 hits for `app-shell` with the same grep). Printing a page from a dev build prints a 560px Xray column beside the app.

This was observed on a ~170-file app that mounted Xray into its existing shell.

## Evidence

- The quotes above.
- `rg '@media print|app-shell|rf-xray-layout' tools/xray` finds only `app-shell` (README.md:126/:134, config.cljc:261/:269, spec 011:45/:58). It finds no print rule and no namespaced wrapper class.
- A tracker description search for `app-shell` and `@media print` finds 0 items; the control `data-rf-xray-host` finds 8.

## Suggested change

- Rename the wrapper to a namespaced class (for example `rf-xray-layout`) in every copy, including the console hint in config.cljc, so the pasted rule cannot meet an app's own class.
- In xray-replaces-10x.md, carry the window-scroller requirement and its reason. Then add a short variant for an app that already scrolls an inner element: wrapper `height: 100%` (or `100vh`) instead of `min-height`, with the host at `height: 100%`. State when spec 011's routing reason does not apply.
  (This variant and the min-height analysis in point 2 are read from the CSS, not measured in a browser.)
- Ship or document `@media print { [data-rf-xray-host] { display: none; } .rf-xray-layout { display: block; } }`.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): M-51 sweep pattern 1 misses a unary reg-fx behind a ; comment line and still matches an already-binary (fn [_ [x y]]) handler it says drops out
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 2a6fd908a6.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md, "Effect-handler arity (M-51)", sweep pattern 1 and its rationale (lines 421-428).

## What it says

Line 421: "`\s+` spans the newlines, `(\S+\s+)?` admits a named `(fn h [x]` ... and the parameter class admits a destructured `(fn [{:keys [url]}]` ... while excluding `_`, so an already-rewritten `(fn [_ request]` drops out."

Line 424: `rg -U -n 'reg-fx\s+\S+\s+(\(fn\s+(\S+\s+)?\[[^]\s_]|#\()' .`

Line 428 lists the known false positives as a named first parameter `(fn [m request]` and a `#(…)` that reads `%2`.

## What happened (generic)

Two defects in pattern 1, both silent:

1. **False negative.** `\s+` cannot step over a `;` comment line, so a unary handler with a comment between `reg-fx`, the id and the `(fn` is not found. On a ~170-file app, the worker's parsed census reported 6 real unary sites missed this way (that count is the worker's claim; the mechanism is reproduced below). The REPL cross-check on line 428 is the only backstop, and it needs a booted app, which a mid-sweep tree does not have.
2. **False positive the text says cannot happen.** The optional name group `(\S+\s+)?` also matches `[_` followed by a space, so an already-binary handler whose second parameter is destructured, `(fn [_ [ws url]]`, still matches. Line 421 says an already-rewritten handler "drops out", and line 428's skip list does not name this shape. So a re-run on a partly migrated tree reports an already-converted handler as unary, and a mechanical `_`-prepend would make it `(fn [_ _ [ws url]]`, a silent wrong rewrite.

## Evidence

rg 14.1.1 at origin/main's exact pattern, over four 2-4 line files:
* a: `(rf/reg-fx :plain (fn [x] ...))` gives a HIT (control, correct).
* b: `(rf/reg-fx` / `:commented` / `;; a comment line ...` / `(fn [x] ...))` gives NO hit (false negative).
* c: `(rf/reg-fx :converted (fn [_ [ws url]] ...))` gives a HIT (false positive).
* d: `(rf/reg-fx :converted-plain (fn [_ request] ...))` gives no hit (control, correct).

The suggested pattern below gives a and b as hits, with c and d excluded:
`rg -U -n 'reg-fx(\s|;[^\n]*\n)+\S+(\s|;[^\n]*\n)+(\(fn(\s|;[^\n]*\n)+([^\s\[]\S*\s+)?\[[^]\s_]|#\()' .`

## Suggested change

Replace pattern 1 with the comment-aware form above: each gap becomes `(\s|;[^\n]*\n)+`, and the name group becomes `([^\s\[]\S*\s+)?`, so a name cannot start with `[`. Keep pattern 2 unchanged. Correct line 421's rationale to match. Also say that the REPL cross-check (line 428) can run only once the tree compiles, so before that a zero from the regex is not a proven zero. Either a parsed census (rewrite-clj, which skips comments and `#_`) or a deferred cross-check after the consolidated compile is needed.

Priority 2: the leaf's own description of its pattern ("an already-rewritten ... drops out") is contradicted by the pattern, and the false positive leads to a wrong rewrite.
