close_reason: Fixed in PR #11663 (auto-call-site-rewrites.md, Effect-handler arity (M-51)). Every gap in both sweeps is now (\s|;[^\n]*\n)+, so it steps over a ; comment line. The fn-name group is ([^\s\[]\S*\s+)?, so it cannot start with [. The var-handler sweep (pattern 2) had the same comment-line miss and got the same gap. This goes beyond the item's 'keep pattern 2 unchanged'. Control: ripgrep 14.1.1 and Python re were run over 16 fixture shapes. Trunk's patterns misclassified 7, the item's two counter-examples among them: the comment-line unary was MISSED and (fn [_ [ws url]]) was MATCHED. The new patterns misclassified 0, with both engines agreeing. The REPL cross-check is now split by when an app boots. First, a v1 census before M-0: (keys (:fx @re-frame.registrar/kind->id->handler)). re-frame 1.4.3 do-fx calls (effect-fn effect-value), one argument. Then the v2 rf/registrations check once the migrated tree compiles. Gate plant: narrowing the parameter class to exclude { turned check_skill_migration_contract_drift --verbose --ci red (exit 1, two M51-SWEEP-BLIND lines). The restore matched the committed blob hash. That gate's fixture lacks both new shapes, so it passed the old pattern as well; growing the fixture is follow-up rf2-edonr (the script was fenced).

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
Related prior fix (found in a de-dup pass after filing): the closed rf2-0tur replaced this sweep (it had matched 1 of 4 unary shapes) and added a drift gate, `m51_sweep_problems()` in scripts/check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py. That gate runs the leaf's own pattern over a fixture. At origin/main 2a6fd908a6 the fixture (lines 1445-1455) holds four comment-free unary shapes (newline or same-line `fn`, bare or `{:keys}` param) and one binary control, `(fn [_ request]`. So the gate passes the current pattern while both defects reported here stand. This is a new gap beside rf2-0tur, not a regression of it.

Suggested gate change, alongside the pattern fix: add a unary shape with a `;; comment` line between the id and the `(fn`, and add `(fn [_ [ws url]] ...)` to the binary controls the sweep must not match.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
Supporting evidence for this item's "the REPL cross-check (line 428) can run only once the tree compiles" point, re-verified at origin/main 0783705626 (a later retro pass). The skill schedules M-51 at exactly the moment when no booted v2 REPL exists:

- orchestrating-a-large-migration.md:38 puts M-51 in the Wave 0.5 mechanical pre-pass.
- sequencing.md:58-60 carries the compile-silent rules on the up-front grep, "applied whether or not the compile failed".
- orchestrating §5 (:97): mid-sweep "there is no clean per-file compile".

So `(rf/registrations {:kind :fx})` (auto-call-site-rewrites.md:428) has no app to run against when the sweep runs.

A generic fallback the fix could name: run the cross-check against the **v1** app before M-0, while it still boots. Use `(keys (:fx @re-frame.registrar/kind->id->handler))` (v1's registrar atom, re-frame 1.4.3 `registrar.cljc`:15), filtered to the app's namespaces by grepping the registering forms. This gives the same "proven zero" before anything changes, and the v2 `rf/registrations` check is kept as the post-gate confirmation.

title: spec(conventions): Reserved fx-ids says a reg-fx of a reserved id is a collision the registrar warns about; nothing warns, and a reg-fx of :dispatch is never consulted
description:
spec/Conventions.md §Reserved fx-ids says: "User code MUST NOT register a `reg-fx` handler for these ids; doing so is a collision the registrar warns about." Nothing warns.

## Verified at source

- `reg-fx` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc) validates only that a handler fn is given (`validate-fx-handler!`), then registers through `register-with-classification!`. No path in fx.cljc or the registrar checks the id against the reserved table; `reserved-fx-handlers` is read only inside `handle-one-fx`.
- `handle-one-fx` runs a reserved body (`:dispatch`, `:dispatch-later`) BEFORE any registry lookup, unless a fn-valued `:fx-overrides` entry names the id. So `(rf/reg-fx :dispatch (fn [_ ev] ...))` registers without complaint and is never consulted. A v1 test that captured dispatches this way passes its "nothing was dispatched" assertions vacuously after migration.
- The other reserved ids in the table (`:rf.machine/*`, `:rf.nav/*`, `:rf.route/with-nav-token`) are ordinary framework `reg-fx` registrations, so a user re-registration of one competes as a duplicate registration rather than being silently ignored.

The skill now tells test authors to use `:fx-overrides` for `:dispatch` / `:dispatch-later` (re-frame2 testing.md §HTTP and other side-effecting fx; the migration skill's test-layer table).

## Decide

Either make `reg-fx` refuse or warn on a reserved table id (a reserved body id at least), or reword the Conventions sentence to say what happens: the registration succeeds and the reserved body still runs. Trust-the-programmer stance suggests the reword unless a loud refusal is cheap; `reg-event` already refuses its reserved ids (`:rf.error/reserved-event-id`), which is a precedent for a refusal.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): test-layer table has no row for the v1 test-body double (re-registering a product id or :dispatch, get-handler save/restore); a reserved fx-id re-registration is silently never consulted
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md §Test-layer v1 API to v2 mapping (table at lines 275-280).
- skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing.md §HTTP and other side-effecting fx (line 255).
- skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing-doubles.md §Mocks under explicit images (line 57).

## What it says

- auto-call-site-rewrites.md:273 introduces "The four surfaces and their v2 destinations, gathered here in one place". Those four rows are the day8.re-frame.test require, make-restore-fn, reg-event-db in a fixture, and post-event callbacks. No row covers a test-body double.
- auto-call-site-rewrites.md:105 (M-1 caveat) sorts a `get-handler` result into two classes only: "introspected (a key read off it, handed to a tool) → the mechanical swap above; invoked → flag for the author".
- testing.md:255: "For arbitrary fx on the reset fixture's ambient frame, override the registered handler from inside the test — that frame resolves the live registrar, and the fixture rolls the registration back on the way out. A frame the test makes resolves an image instead, where re-registering a product's id never wins".
- testing-doubles.md:57: "A mock registered in the test body reaches the reset fixture's ambient frame, which resolves the live registrar, and a frame made without `:images` while no other loaded namespace registers the mock's id. ... a frame made without `:images`, whenever it was made, finds the id ambiguous and raises `:rf.error/ambiguous-registration` where it uses it."

## What happened (generic)

The commonest v1 test double has no row in the test-layer table. It works like this: the test saves the product handler with `re-frame.registrar/get-handler`, calls `reg-fx` / `reg-sub` / `reg-event-*` on a product id (or on `:dispatch`, to capture dispatches), and restores the saved handler afterwards. A migrating agent has to assemble the v2 route from three leaves. M-1's caveat does not classify the save-and-restore use: the result is neither read nor called, it is re-registered.

Two v2 behaviours make this shape a trap.

1. A re-registered reserved fx-id never runs. `:dispatch` and `:dispatch-later` run their reserved body before any registry lookup (fx.cljc:578, `(if-let [reserved-body (and (not fn-value-override?) (get reserved-fx-handlers fx-id))]`). `reg-fx` makes no reserved-id check (fx.cljc:76-97, then registrar `register!`). So `(rf/reg-fx :dispatch (fn [_ ev] (swap! seen conj ev)))` registers without complaint and the mock is never called. Tests asserting "nothing was dispatched" then pass vacuously. spec/Conventions.md:435 says "doing so is a collision the registrar warns about", but no such warning exists at this tip. That is a spec/implementation drift worth a separate look. The only route that works is a fn-valued `:fx-overrides` / `ts/with-fx-overrides`; spec/002 §Reserved fx-ids take overrides too.
2. A body re-registration is a test-only exception that depends on how the frame was built. spec/008-Testing.md:233 states it exactly: "The fixture frame is the test-only exception: the latest registration wins there ... `(rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default})` resolves like any other frame `make-frame` builds". A migrated suite that boots the app (or calls `make-frame` on `:rf/default`) in `:init-fn` or in the test body turns the ambient frame into a live-store frame, and the double then raises `:rf.error/ambiguous-registration`. Neither testing.md:255 nor testing-doubles.md:57 says that re-making `:rf/default` loses the exception.

Two independent workers on one migration misread testing.md:255 / testing-doubles.md:57 as "the ambient frame finds a test-body double ambiguous". Part of the cause is terminology. "resolves the live registrar" (the fixture frame, latest registration wins) and "resolves the registration store live" (a `make-frame {}` frame, ambiguous) differ by word order, and they describe opposite outcomes. testing.md:255 also still says a frame the test makes "resolves an image", which is pre-live-default wording for a `make-frame {}` frame.

## Evidence

- Source: the fixture seats `:rf/default` through `ensure-default-frame!` (test_support.cljc:413), which `upsert-frame!`s a record with no `:rf.frame/live-store?`. frame.cljc:2394-2399: "False for every other frame without a generation (the test fixture's ambient frame), which resolves the registrar's latest registration". live_frame.cljc:118-121 says the same, and `call-with-record-resolution` binds nothing for such a record, so `registrar/lookup` takes `latest-descriptor`.
- Tests that pin it: implementation/core/test/re_frame/app_ns_fixture_cljs_test.cljc:45 and registrar_query_source_cljs_test.cljc:149.
- Reserved body first: fx.cljc:578-585. `reserved-fx-handlers` is read only there; it is never read at registration.
- Observed on a ~170-file app: 15 test re-registrations of production ids among the 19 duplicate (kind, id) pairs its census found (see rf2-soqmk).

## Suggested change

- Add a fifth row to the test-layer table. v1 surface: a test-body `reg-fx` / `reg-sub` / `reg-event-*` of a product id (optionally bracketed by `get-handler` save / re-register restore). v2: on the reset fixture's ambient frame, the body registration wins and the fixture rolls it back, so drop the save/restore. On any frame `make-frame` builds (including a re-made `:rf/default`), use fn-valued `:fx-overrides` / `ts/with-fx-overrides` for fx, `:rf.cofx` for a recordable cofx value, and a final mock image for events and subs (testing-doubles.md). For a reserved fx-id (`:dispatch`, `:dispatch-later`), always use `:fx-overrides`, because re-registration is silently never consulted.
- Extend M-1's `get-handler` classification with a third class, "saved and re-registered (a test double's restore)" → delete it; the fixture restores registrations.
- In testing.md:255 and testing-doubles.md:57, say "takes each id's latest registration" for the fixture frame in place of "resolves the live registrar". Add that re-making `:rf/default` with `make-frame` (app boot in `:init-fn`) removes the exception. Replace "resolves an image instead" with the live-store / ambiguity wording testing-doubles.md:57 already uses.
- Optional, outside the skill: either add the reserved-fx-id registration warning spec/Conventions.md:435 promises, or drop the claim.

Related: rf2-3t84p (the make-restore-fn row in the same table), rf2-aunc0 (production `get-handler`), rf2-soqmk (the duplicate-registration census that counts these test re-registrations).

comments.text:
From a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (pass 7). This is a suggestion, not a work order. Verified at origin/main bafbe4028e.

A second v1 double belongs in the fifth row this item asks for: a test that stubs dispatch with `(with-redefs [rf/dispatch (fn [ev] (swap! seen conj ev))] …)`. Observed on a ~170-file app's test-fixture unit.

What the skill already covers:
- auto-call-site-rewrites.md:194 (M-52, "Three v1 test-double habits"): "`with-redefs` on `rf/dispatch` or `rf/dispatch-sync`. In call position these are v2 macros, so the redef compiles and intercepts nothing while the real event runs."
- testing-doubles.md:37-53 gives the replacement seam: a recorder interceptor on the frame's `:interceptors`.

So the mechanism is covered. The gap is the same as this item's: the table at :273-280 says it gathers the test layer "in one place", and it has no row for this double either.

Two further points for that row:

1. It also holds for code that M-11 moved onto `capture-frame`. The captured `:dispatch` op routes through the internal `dispatch-impl` seam (implementation/core/src/re_frame/capture_frame.cljc:145-151 and :195), not the `rf/dispatch` var. testing-doubles.md:39 says a redef "does reach code that reads a function as a value". A reader can take that to include a captured op, but it does not. Saying so in the row closes that reading.

2. The recorder fires at a different time from the v1 stub. The v1 stub recorded synchronously at the call, and the real event never ran. The v2 recorder interceptor records when the router RUNS the event, in queue order, and the real handler runs too. As a result:
   - after a plain `dispatch` in the code under test, the recorder is empty until something drains;
   - a test that asserts the order of recorded dispatches against synchronous callback effects sees queue order, not call order.
   A rewrite that keeps a synchronous recorder hides real ordering bugs. Suggested wording: "Record through the frame's queue (the interceptor recorder, or on the fixture frame `rf/clear` plus a `reg-event` recorder when the real handler must not run). Drive callback steps through the frame's queue too, and settle with `dispatch-sync`, which drains both lanes (see rf2-h7vhf)." The check that found no existing wording for this: grep -n -i "queue|drain|interleav" over testing-doubles.md found 0 hits. The control: "dispatch-sync" has 6 hits in the same file.

Related: rf2-ja1t7 (the :163 vs :194 contradiction on redefining `rf/subscribe`) and rf2-h7vhf (v1 `run-test-sync` made dispatch synchronous).
